symbols.name: CONSOLE
symbols.desc:
A pseudoplayer table that can be used in place of a regular player for automated server actions.
 This table implements a subset of the Player metatable methods to allow it to be used where
 a player object is expected, such as for bans, kicks, or admin commands initiated by the server.

 Note: while this table can be used in place of a regular player, it will fail for most
 regular player operations that require an actual entity (e.g., GetPos(), Spawn(), etc.).

 Example usage:
 ```lua
 CONSOLE:Name() -- Returns "Console"
 cityrp.bans.DoBan(CONSOLE, steamid, nick, 0, reason)
 cityrp.acommands.adminDo(CONSOLE, "Server action performed", icon, flags)
 ```

symbols.name: CONSOLE.Announce
symbols.desc:
Announce an automated server message in every player's chat, attributed to the console.
 Rendered through the Discord relay's stand-in player table, so the line carries the console
 rank's icon and colour rather than the bare "Console: " the engine's `say` produces. The
 relay owns that table on both realms, so without it there is nothing clientside to receive
 the announcement and this falls back to `say`.

symbols.name: CPPI
symbols.desc:
CPPI (Common Prop Protection Interface), implemented by Simple Prop Protection.
See: ~https~ ://ulyssesmod.net/archive/CPPI_v1-3.pdf

symbols.name: CPPI.GetInterfaceVersion
symbols.desc:
CPPI: version of the CPPI standard this interface implements. Required.
 2.0 is a CityRP-local extension of the standard - there's no published 2.0 spec,
 this just means "CPPI 1.3 plus our own additions" (see OwnerSID on Entity, and any
 other CityRP-specific behaviour documented alongside it).

symbols.name: CPPI.GetName
symbols.desc: CPPI: name of the active prop protection. Required.

symbols.name: CPPI.GetNameFromSID
symbols.desc:
CPPI: resolves a player's name from their SteamID64/CommunityID, checking online
 players first, then (server-only) an in-memory cache warmed by online players, then
 (server-only, rate-limited) a DB lookup. This replaces GetNameFromUID - Player:
 UniqueID() is deprecated by GMod and not guaranteed unique, so this codebase keys
 everything by SteamID64/CommunityID instead. Not part of the CPPI 1.3 standard
 (which specifies a UID-based GetNameFromUID); a CPPI 2.0 (CityRP-local) addition.

params.name: sid
params.desc: A SteamID64/CommunityID - NOT a classic SteamID32 (STEAM_0:...).

returns.desc: nil if no match, CPPI_DEFER if a lookup is pending/unsupported.

warns: On the client, this only works for online players.

symbols.name: CPPI.GetVersion
symbols.desc: CPPI: version of the active prop protection. Required.

symbols.name: CPPI.Logger
symbols.desc: A namespaced, level-filterable logger. Obtain instances via cityrp.logging.GetLogger rather than constructing directly.

symbols.name: CPPI.LookupNameFromSID
symbols.desc:
Resolves an offline player's name from CPPI.NameCache, or (rate-limited) issues a
 DB lookup and returns CPPI_DEFER while it's pending.

returns.desc: nil if sid isn't well-formed, CPPI_DEFER if pending.

symbols.name: CPPI.NameCache
symbols.desc:
In-memory cache backing CPPI.LookupNameFromSID, keyed by SteamID64/CommunityID.
 Each entry is {name = string|nil, lastHit = number, lastQuery = number|nil}, where
 name is nil until a DB lookup resolves it, and lastQuery rate-limits re-querying
 the same SID.

symbols.name: CPPI.NameCacheSettings
symbols.desc: Tuning for CPPI.NameCache's query rate-limit and cleanup timer.

symbols.name: GAMEMODE.CPPIFriendsChanged

symbols.name: DB.QueryParams
symbols.desc:
Run a query with positional parameters using ? placeholders.
 Each parameter will be escaped and quoted automatically unless it's a table with `_raw` field.
 WARNING: The _raw field feature allows bypassing escaping - use with extreme caution!
 Only use _raw for trusted, non-user-controlled SQL fragments like column names or operators.
 Example: DB:QueryParams("INSERT INTO t (a,b) VALUES (?, ?)", {val1, val2}, cb)

symbols.name: DB.RunChecked

Run a query and report success explicitly to the callback.

params.name: cb

symbols.name: ITEM.AutoFunction
symbols.desc:
Creates an automatically named setter function.
 It also returns a single param function, which sets a default value and returns the item.
 ```lua
 local setDefault = ITEM:AutoFunction("SpecialValue", "internal_flag")
 -- This creates a function, ITEM:SetSpecialValue().
 -- Calling this function sets a value on ITEM.internal_flag.
 -- Calling setDefault, sets the value now, returning the item. This is useful for chaining.
 ITEM:AutoFunction("SomeValue", "this_defaults_to_false")(false)
 ```

returns.desc: Sets the value immediately and returns the item, for chaining.

 If autoStore is true, model and skin will be pushed to the store model.

```lua
model:
    | true
```

params.name: model
params.desc: Model path, or `true` to pull from the store model.

params.name: autoStore
params.desc: Whether this should also automatically set the store models.

returns.desc: The item, for chaining.

symbols.name: ITEM.SetName
symbols.desc:
Sets the name of an item.
 If plural is undefined, defaults to "<name>s".
 If plural is true, it's set to "<name>".

```lua
plural:
    | false
```

params.name: plural
params.desc: The plural form. Defaults to "<name>s" if omitted, or "<name>" if `true`.

returns.desc: The item, for chaining.

modules.name: Migrations
modules.description:
Database schema migrations runner.
Runs ordered SQL migrations against DB_MAIN exactly once per database, tracked via a
`schema_migrations` table created on demand. Migration files live in gamemode/core/migrations/,
named `NNNN_description.lua`, each returning a table with `up(done)` and `down(done)` functions.

symbols.name: Migrations.EnsureTable
symbols.desc: Ensure the schema_migrations tracking table exists.

params.name: cb
params.desc: Called once the table has been created (or already existed).

symbols.name: Migrations.GetApplied
symbols.desc: Get applied migrations, keyed by id.

params.name: cb
params.desc: Called with the read result; applied maps id to {id=, name=, applied_at=}.

symbols.name: Migrations.Load
symbols.desc: Load all migration files from core/migrations, keyed by id.

symbols.name: Migrations.Redo
symbols.desc: Down then up a single migration id (or the latest applied id if omitted).

params.name: id
params.desc: Migration id to redo; defaults to the latest applied id.

symbols.name: Migrations.RunDown
symbols.desc:
Revert the last `count` applied migrations (default 1), most-recent first. Each migration's
 down(done) callback must call done(ok) itself; a failed revert stops the run and leaves its
 schema_migrations row in place.

params.name: count
params.desc: How many migrations to revert. Defaults to 1.

symbols.name: Migrations.RunPending
symbols.desc:
Run all pending migrations in ascending id order. Each migration's up(done) callback must
 call done(ok) itself; a migration that fails is not recorded as applied and stops the run.

symbols.name: Migrations.RunSequence
symbols.desc:
Run a sequence of raw SQL statements in order.
 Stops on the first failed statement and does not call done(true).

params.name: done
params.desc: Called with the result. Legacy callers that ignore the argument still work when ok is true.

symbols.name: Migrations.Status
symbols.desc: Get a status snapshot of applied and pending migrations.

params.name: cb
params.desc: Called with {applied = {...}, pending = {...}}, or {applied = {}, pending = {}, error = true} on read failure.

modules.name: SPropProtection
modules.description:
Simple Prop Protection - server-side ownership tracking and permission engine.
Originally by Spacetech (code.google.com/p/simplepropprotection).

symbols.name: SPropProtection
symbols.desc:
Simple Prop Protection - client-side HUD and Q-menu panels.
 Originally by Spacetech (code.google.com/p/simplepropprotection).

symbols.name: SPropProtection.AdminPanel
symbols.desc:
Populates the Q-menu "Admin" panel with spp_* settings and per-player/global
 cleanup buttons. No-ops for non-admins.

symbols.name: SPropProtection.AdminReload
symbols.desc: Pushes the current spp_* admin settings to every connected player.

symbols.name: SPropProtection.AdminReloadPlayer
symbols.desc: Pushes the current spp_* admin settings to a single player's client convars.

symbols.name: SPropProtection.ApplyFriends
symbols.desc:
Console command (spp_applyfriends): applies the caller's spp_friend_* convar
 selections to their (session-only, unpersisted) friends list and fires
 CPPIFriendsChanged if it changed.

symbols.name: SPropProtection.ApplySettings
symbols.desc:
Console command (spp_apply): persists an admin's spp_* setting convars to the local
 SQLite settings table and pushes the new config to every player.

params.name: ply
params.desc: The invoking player (must be an admin).

symbols.name: SPropProtection.CanTool
symbols.desc:
Generic tool-use ownership check. CityRP-specific carve-outs (submaterial-on-player
 Assistant/EventMgr override, vehicle-weld REP/Mechanic override, vehicle MaterialURL
 staff-only override, vehicle-submaterial REP/Mechanic override) are NOT handled here -
 they live in GM:CanTool (gamemode/init.lua), which consults this function for
 anything not already decided by those carve-outs.

params.name: tr
params.desc: The tool trace (as passed to GM:CanTool).

returns.desc: nil abstains.

symbols.name: SPropProtection.CanToolGeneric
symbols.desc:
Generic tool-use gate: ownership plus the mapper-set spp_cantool keyvalue override.
 Shared by SPropProtection.CanTool (the toolgun hook, which also runs trace-dependent
 checks for "nail"/WeirdTraces modes that need real trace geometry) and
 Entity:CPPICanTool (which only receives a tool mode, no trace, so can't run those).

symbols.name: SPropProtection.CDP
symbols.desc:
Console command (spp_cdp): removes every owned entity whose owner (by OwnerSID) is
 no longer connected. Entities are collected before any are removed, per the same
 ents.Iterator() caveat noted on DRemove.

params.name: ply
params.desc: The invoking player, or nil/invalid from server console.

symbols.name: SPropProtection.CheckConstraints
symbols.desc:
Checks whether ply may touch every entity constrained to ent (used to gate the
 "remover" tool so it can't indirectly delete someone else's constrained props).

params.name: ent
params.desc: The entity whose constrained set is checked.

symbols.name: SPropProtection.CheckKeyvalue
symbols.desc:
Reads mapper-set spp_cantouch/spp_canuse/spp_cantool keyvalues so map-placed entities
 can override the default protection behaviour.

symbols.name: SPropProtection.CleanupPlayerProps
symbols.desc:
Removes every entity currently owned by ply (by OwnerSID). Entities are collected
 before any are removed, per the same ents.Iterator() caveat noted on DRemove.

params.name: ply
params.desc: The player whose props are removed.

symbols.name: SPropProtection.CleanupProps
symbols.desc:
Console command (spp_cleanupprops): with no argument, cleans up the caller's own
 props; with an entity index argument, staff can clean up another player's props.

params.name: ply
params.desc: The invoking player, or nil/invalid from server console.

params.name: args
params.desc: args[1], optionally an EntIndex to target another player.

symbols.name: SPropProtection.ClearFriends
symbols.desc:

symbols.name: SPropProtection.PlayerUse
symbols.desc:
function SPropProtection.EntityTakeDamage(ent, inflictor, attacker, amount, dmginfo)
	if(tonumber(SPropProtection.Config["edmg"]) == 0) then
		return
	end
    if(!ent:IsValid() or ent:IsPlayer() or !attacker:IsPlayer()) then
		return
	end
	if(!SPropProtection.PlayerCanTouch(attacker, ent)) then
		dmginfo:SetDamage(0)
		timer.Simple(0.1, SPropProtection.EntityTakeDamageFireCheck, ent)
	end
end
hook.Add("EntityTakeDamage", "SPropProtection.EntityTakeDamage", SPropProtection.EntityTakeDamage)

 Don't need damage protection
 Ownership check for the "use" (+use) event.

returns.desc: nil abstains.

symbols.name: SPropProtection.RelinkOwnerObj

Re-points OwnerObj (a direct Entity reference) at ply's new Player object for every
 entity ply still owns by OwnerSID. OwnerObj goes stale across a disconnect/reconnect
 - the old Player object was removed on disconnect, so it becomes an invalid entity
 reference - even though OwnerSID/Owner stay correct the whole time. CPPIGetOwner and
 several first-party consumers (sh_contextmenu.lua, sv_access.lua, propsave, etc.)

symbols.desc:
Bone the hip slots hang from. The chest attachment sits at the top of the
 spine, so a hip measured down from it is out by however long the torso of the
 player model happens to be, and drifts off the body the moment an animation
 moves the chest. The pelvis sits between the hip joints on every ValveBiped
 model and travels with the legs, which is what a belt holster does.

symbols.name: bwep.offsets
symbols.desc:
Slots 1-5 are local to the chest attachment and 6-7 to the pelvis, but both
 frames are player aligned: -X is behind the body, +Y is the player's left, -Z
 is down. See bwep.getSlotAnchor.

 Angles read the same way in either. Yaw 270 with roll 0 lays a gun flat
 against the back with its right flank facing out, and the pitch then swings
 the muzzle from the player's right (0) round to straight down (90) without
 lifting it off the body -- that is the family slots 4 and 5 sit in, shallow
 across the kidneys and steep across the shoulder blades respectively. Slots
 6-7 hang a pistol muzzle down beside the leg, canted a few degrees so the grip
 leads the way a belt holster does.

 Only slots 1-3 pose differently depending on what the player is holding.
 4-7 declare Normal alone and drawPlayerWeapons falls back to it.

modules.name: cityrp.imageHosts
modules.description:
Central allowlist of image hosts that are trusted for remote content.

Anything that loads a player-supplied image off the internet (billboards, the Material URL
tool, 3D signs) validates against this one list. Adding or retiring a host here updates every
consumer at once, including the host names shown in their UIs - there is deliberately nowhere
else in the codebase that a host name should be written down.

Host matching is exact and case-insensitive against the URL's hostname. Subdomains are not
implied: "i.ibb.co" does not permit "evil.i.ibb.co", so every host that should work must be
listed in full.

Both http and https are accepted. Plain http means the image bytes can be tampered with in
transit by anything between us and the host, but the host itself is still allowlisted and the
result is only ever decoded as an image, which is an accepted trade-off here rather than an
oversight - a good few of these links come in as http and rejecting them broke more than it
protected. A URL with no scheme is assumed to be https.

Extract the hostname from a URL.
 Userinfo ("user@host") and explicit ports are rejected rather than parsed, so a crafted

symbols.name: cityrp.item.applyAppearance
symbols.desc:
Applies an item's colour and material override to the model panel drawing
 it, so an icon or preview shows what the item will actually look like on
 the ground.

 The colour goes on the panel rather than the entity: DModelPanel's paint
 pass calls render.SetColorModulation with its own colour every frame,
 which overrides anything Entity:SetColor put there. The material has no
 such equivalent and stays on the entity.

 Both are set unconditionally rather than only when the item declares them:
 these panels are reused across the items they show, so an item that
 declares neither has to clear what the last one left behind.

 A plain function rather than an ITEM method on purpose. cityrp.item.new
 points a new item's __index at its *base item*, not at ITEM, so a stored
 item is only as good as whatever its base chain happens to expose - the
 weed pot, for one, reaches none of ITEM's methods.

params.name: panel
params.desc: The DModelPanel drawing the item's model.

 A parent entry (e.g. "Clothing") grants every sub-category under it; a sub-category
 entry (e.g. "Clothing - Government Clothing") grants only that exact category.

symbols.name: cityrp.item.canUseItem
symbols.desc: Checks every non-cooldown, non-context gate on using/equipping itm -- Clothing's fireCanUse ban and membership requirement, the PlayerCanUseItem hook, reps, membershiplevel, and canUse. Pure, never notifies -- a nil reason means the PlayerCanUseItem hook blocked it and already notified the player itself (e.g. uniforms' cooldown), so callers shouldn't show a fallback for that case; every other false result carries a real reason string.

True if itemCat is exactly `selected`, or itemCat's parent category is `selected`.
 Also true if itemCat has no sub-category of its own (e.g. "Mixtures") and `selected`
 is that same parent's "Other" bucket (e.g. "Mixtures - Other") -- uncategorized items
 fall back into their parent's Other bucket once the parent has real sub-categories.
 Used both for shop/tab filtering and for team category-permission checks, so the

modules.name: cityrp.network
modules.description:
Clientside receiving, handshake, pull-on-visible resync and `:ClientOwned()` sends for the CityRP
networking library.
Storing values directly on the entity (`sh_store.lua`) retires the plugin this library replaces'
worst clientside bug for free: `PLUGIN.NSVars[entIndex]`, keyed by raw index, was never cleared on
disconnect, so a recycled edict inherited whatever the previous occupant left behind. GMod hands a
newly-created entity a fresh Lua table regardless of which index it reuses, so `ent.__netvars` simply
does not exist yet for it -- there is nothing to clean up, and nothing here needs to try.

The one real gap that storage model leaves is timing: a value can arrive (via Update or Resync)
referencing an entity this client hasn't networked yet. Those are buffered by raw index in `pending`
until `OnEntityCreated` actually produces the entity, and swept on a TTL in case it never does (e.g.
the entity never entered this client's PVS at all).

symbols.desc: Applies a value and, if `ApplyValue`'s delta guard says it changed, sends it.

returns.desc: Whether the value changed, and therefore whether an update was sent.

symbols.name: cityrp.network.ApplyIndexed
symbols.desc:
Applies a decoded entity-scoped value (Entity/Player/Vehicle/Weapon), buffering it if the entity
 hasn't appeared yet.

symbols.desc: Applies a decoded no-index value: Global goes to the global table, LocalPlayer to `LocalPlayer()`.

symbols.name: cityrp.network.ApplyValue
symbols.desc:
Validates (if the var has an `:Enum()`-set `validate` function), applies a value to storage, and
 fires the var's `:SetHook()` hook if the value changed. Shared by the server's own
 `SetNetVar`/`SetGlobal` (`sv_send.lua`) -- so the server's own copy of a value updates immediately
 regardless of who receives the resulting net message, and so the delta guard that decides whether
 to bother networking at all lives in exactly one place -- and the client's receive path
 (`cl_receive.lua`), once an update has actually been decoded.
 for a client-side local apply the server has not confirmed, from either a `:Predictable()` or a
 `:ClientOwned()` var's client setter. See `GenerateAccessor` below.

params.name: ent
params.desc: The entity to store on. Ignored (may be nil) for Global scope.

params.name: predicted
params.desc: Passed through to the `:SetHook()` hook as its 5th argument -- true only

returns.desc: Whether the value actually changed (false for a redundant re-set or a rejected invalid one).

Sets a `:ClientOwned()` var on the local player: applies it locally, then asks the server to

 The generated `Set<Name>()` calls this; use it directly for a var registered without

symbols.desc:
Meta codec: the value's shape is written to the wire as a per-value tag instead of being fixed
 by the manifest. Never chosen by `GetValueCodec` as a nested `Auto`/`Table` entry's tag.

symbols.name: cityrp.network.CODEC_BIT
symbols.desc:
Raw single bit via `net.WriteBit`/`net.ReadBit`, returning `0`/`1` rather than a real boolean.
 Declared-only, like `Integer`/`UInteger` -- `Auto` already covers booleans via `CODEC_BOOL`.

symbols.name: cityrp.network.CODEC_BITS
symbols.desc: Bits used to write a `NetCodecId` value.

symbols.name: cityrp.network.CODEC_BSTRING
symbols.desc:
Length-prefixed string, bounded to the `maxLen` its `:String(maxLen)` registration declared.
 Declared-only: `Auto` has no `maxLen` to infer, which is also why this sits above `AUTO_TAG_MAX`.

symbols.name: cityrp.network.CODEC_CUSTOM
symbols.desc:
User-supplied `:Write(fn, opt)` / `:Read(fn, opt)`. Cannot be described by the manifest, so vars
 using it are sent one per message rather than batched -- see `sv_send.lua`.

symbols.name: cityrp.network.CODEC_INTEGER
symbols.desc:
Explicit bit-width signed integer, 1-32 bits. Declared-only; `Auto` always prefers the fixed
 Nibble/Byte/Short/Int tiers instead, so a var must call `:Integer(bits)` to get this codec.

symbols.name: cityrp.network.CODEC_PLAYER
symbols.desc:
Narrower counterpart to `CODEC_ENTITY` for a value known to be a player: `net.WritePlayer`/
 `net.ReadPlayer` size the index off `MAX_PLAYER_BITS` (the engine's own player-slot-count bound)
 instead of the wider `MAX_EDICT_BITS` every other entity needs. `GetValueCodec` picks this over
 `CODEC_ENTITY` automatically whenever the value actually is a player.

symbols.name: cityrp.network.codecs
symbols.desc:
Codec definitions, indexed by `NetCodecId`. Each entry is `{name, write, read, batchable}`.
 `write(value, arg)` / `read(arg)` -- `arg` is the codec argument from the `NetVar` (bit width for
 `Integer`/`UInteger`, byte length for `Data`), ignored by fixed-shape codecs. `batchable = false`
 (currently only `Custom`) marks a codec that can't safely share a batched message, since an
 undecodable value must not corrupt any entry after it -- see `sv_send.lua`.

 A `read` may return a second value, `false`, to declare the byte stream unsalvageable from there
 on -- only `BoundedString` does, on a length prefix above its registered maximum. `DecodeEntry`
 checks it with `== false`, since every other codec's second return is `nil`.

symbols.name: cityrp.network.CollectSendableVars
symbols.desc:
Collects this entity's currently-set entity-scoped vars (`IsEntityScope`) that `ply` is allowed
 to see. Global and LocalPlayer-scoped vars never go through resync -- Global is broadcast
 independently of any entity's visibility, and LocalPlayer is always pushed straight to its one
 owner.

symbols.name: cityrp.network.CountInbound
symbols.desc:
Counts one inbound message against `ply`'s budget and says whether to process it. Deliberately
 crude -- `:Debounce()` is what actually makes client-owned vars safe, so this only ever fires for
 a client sending orders of magnitude more than a real one.

returns.desc: False if the message should be ignored.

symbols.name: cityrp.network.DebounceSet
symbols.desc:
Routes one server-side set through this var's debounce window. Called from
 `cityrp.network.Dispatch` (`sv_send.lua`) for any var that declared `:Debounce()`.

symbols.name: cityrp.network.DecodeEntry
symbols.desc:
Reads one var entry written by `WriteVarEntry`. On any decode failure the byte length of what
 follows is unknowable, so callers must stop reading rather than continue -- safe because a
 non-batchable entry is never batched with anything else.

returns.desc: nil on failure.
False if the rest of this message must be discarded.

symbols.name: cityrp.network.DequeueEntity
symbols.desc: Removes `ent` from `ply`'s resync queue, clearing `ply` from `pendingPlayers` if that empties it.

symbols.name: cityrp.network.Dispatch
symbols.desc:
The single seam every server-side set goes through, so `:Debounce()` is one branch rather than a
 condition duplicated in `SetNetVar` and `SetGlobal`.

symbols.name: cityrp.network.DrainOnePlayer
symbols.desc: Drains up to `take` entities from `ply`'s resync queue and sends whatever they're owed.

returns.desc: How many queue entries were consumed (valid or not).

symbols.name: cityrp.network.DrainPending
symbols.desc: Applies any values buffered for `ent`, now that it actually exists.

symbols.name: cityrp.network.DrainPendingDebounces
symbols.desc:
Applies any pending values whose windows have closed. On `Think` rather than a `timer.Simple` per
 pair, which would be a timer per player per var, each needing to re-validate its entity inside the
 callback (AGENTS.md footgun #2) for a routine mid-window disconnect.

symbols.name: cityrp.network.DrainResyncQueues
symbols.desc:
Drains every player's resync queue, round-robin, within the configured per-frame budgets.
 The cursor persists across frames (`drainCursorPly`) so a player who was last in line this frame
 is first in line next frame -- with enough players queued to exceed the per-frame budget, this is
 what guarantees everyone is eventually served instead of the same players always winning the race.
 If the previous cursor's queue emptied out between frames, the round-robin simply restarts from
 the first candidate rather than trying to preserve a "position" a table with unstable iteration
 order can't actually promise -- a minor, self-correcting fairness wrinkle.

symbols.name: cityrp.network.EnqueueAllEntitiesForResync
symbols.desc:
Queues every currently-known networked entity for resync to `ply`. Used for the join bootstrap --
 reusing the resync path means a large join gets the same per-frame rate limiting as any other
 resync, rather than a separate one-off bulk-send path to reason about and maintain.

symbols.name: cityrp.network.ENTITY_INDEX_BITS
symbols.desc:
Bits used to write/read an entity index on the wire for Entity/Player-scoped vars. `MAX_EDICT_BITS`
 is the engine's own answer to "how many bits does any entity index need" (what `net.WriteEntity`
 itself is sized on), so this is guaranteed correct for whatever the server's actual edict limit
 is, rather than a separately-guessed "safely large" literal that could drift from the real limit.

symbols.name: cityrp.network.ENTITY_LIKE_SCOPES
symbols.desc:
Scopes whose value is stored on an entity and travels with an entity index on the wire, as
 opposed to Global (no entity at all) or LocalPlayer (never carries an index -- the recipient
 is implicit). `SetVehicle()`/`SetWeapon()` behave exactly like `SetEntity()` here; the only
 thing they change is `:Accessor()`'s target metatable. Consulted via `IsEntityScope` below
 rather than repeating this set as an ad hoc `or`-chain at every call site that cares -- adding a
 future metatable-specific scope (NPC, NextBot, ...) then only ever needs one line changed here.

symbols.name: cityrp.network.FindVar
symbols.desc:
Looks up a registered var by name, logging (once per call, not once per name) if it isn't one.
 Shared by every public getter/setter so "unregistered name" fails the same way everywhere.

params.name: name
params.desc: The var name to look up.

returns.desc: The registered var, or nil (and a logged error) if `name` isn't registered.

symbols.name: cityrp.network.FlushClientSets
symbols.desc:
Sends everything buffered while the manifest was outstanding. Called from the manifest receiver
 above, once `byId`/`idBits` are populated.

 The queue is swapped out before iterating: each apply runs the var's `:SetHook()`, which may call
 `ClientSet` again, and adding a key mid-`pairs` is undefined in Lua.

symbols.name: cityrp.network.FlushResyncRequests
symbols.desc: Sends one batched resync request for every entity queued since the last flush.

symbols.name: cityrp.network.GenerateAccessor
symbols.desc:
Defines `Get<Name>()` (both realms) and `Set<Name>()` for a var registered with `:Accessor(name)`,
 on the metatable `ACCESSOR_METATABLE` maps its scope to (Entity for Global/Entity scope, Player
 for Player/LocalPlayer, Vehicle/Weapon for those). A no-op for a var with no accessor name set.
 Idempotent -- safe to call more than once for the same var.

 `Set<Name>()` is server-only -- `SetNetVar`/`SetGlobal` live in the server-only `sv_send.lua` --
 unless the var opted into a client-side form:

 - `:ClientOwned()` applies locally and sends. Already vetted at seal by `ValidateClientOwned`, so a
   var that failed has had the flag cleared and simply gets no setter here.
 - `:Predictable()` applies locally only. Coherent for `:SetLocalPlayer()` alone, so a scope
   mismatch is a logged error rather than a silently-generated footgun.

 Both pass `predicted = true` -- the client is holding a value the server has not confirmed either
 way. Client-owned wins if a var chained both; `ValidateClientOwned` has already warned.

params.name: netvar
params.desc: The var to generate accessors for.

symbols.name: cityrp.network.GenerateAccessors
symbols.desc:
Generates accessors for every currently-registered var. Called once from `Seal()`, after which
 new registrations no longer occur -- see `sh_registry.lua`.

symbols.name: cityrp.network.GetDebounceReport
symbols.desc:
Every (owner, var) pair the debouncer is tracking, for `cityrp_network_dump`. Includes settled
 pairs: without them the dump cannot tell a var that has never been set from one that has, which
 is exactly the question worth asking of a client-owned var that is not arriving.

returns.type: { owner: Entity?, netvar: NetVar, interval: number, pending: boolean, dispatches: integer }[]

symbols.name: cityrp.network.GetGlobal
symbols.desc: Reads a Global-scoped networked value.

params.name: default
params.desc: Returned if the value has never been set, or on any error path.

symbols.name: cityrp.network.GetQueue
symbols.desc:
Gets (creating if needed) a player's resync queue.
 A queue is a plain weak-keyed set of entities, not an ordered array. Photon's original resync
 queue is an array plus a drain cursor needing periodic "backlog reclamation" to stop the backing
 array growing forever; a weak-keyed set has no backing array to grow, and dropping an entity from
 it is an ordinary key removal. The trade-off is that iteration order (`pairs`) is unspecified
 rather than FIFO, which is fine -- fairness across players already comes from the round-robin in
 `DrainResyncQueues`, not per-player ordering.

symbols.name: cityrp.network.GetSignedBits
symbols.desc:
Number of bits required to write `value` with `net.WriteInt`, clamped to 1-32. Always reserves a
 sign-headroom bit -- without it, an exact power of two (e.g. 4, needing 3 unsigned bits) would
 not fit the signed range those same 3 bits provide (-4..3), silently truncating.

params.name: value
params.desc: The (integral) value that will be written.

returns.desc: Bits required, 1-32.

symbols.name: cityrp.network.GetUnsignedBits
symbols.desc:
Number of bits required to write `value` with `net.WriteUInt`, clamped to 1-32. Unlike
 `GetSignedBits`, no sign-headroom bit is reserved -- callers must already know `value` is
 non-negative.

params.name: value
params.desc: The (integral, non-negative) value that will be written.

returns.desc: Bits required, 1-32.

symbols.name: cityrp.network.GetValueCodec
symbols.desc:
Determines which codec `Auto` should tag a value as. Mirrors the closed set bounded by
 `AUTO_TAG_MAX` -- every branch here must return an ID whose codec table entry actually exists
 and is self-contained (no extra argument required to read it back).

returns.desc: The codec ID to tag and write it with.

symbols.name: cityrp.network.globals
symbols.desc:
Global-scoped values, by name. Entity/Player/LocalPlayer-scoped values live on the entity itself
 instead -- see the `Entity.__netvars` field below.

symbols.name: cityrp.network.IsEntityScope
symbols.desc: Whether `scope` stores on an entity and uses entity-index wire framing.

params.name: scope
params.desc: Where a `NetVar`'s value lives and who it is sent to by default.

symbols.name: cityrp.network.IsFloatValue
symbols.desc:
Whether a Lua number is non-integral. Written without GMod's `math.floor(value, 0)` two-arg
 form this codebase's predecessor relied on -- the second argument is silently ignored either way.

returns.desc: True if flooring `value` would change it.

symbols.name: cityrp.network.IsNormalVector
symbols.desc:
Whether a vector's components are all small enough to use the compact `Normal` wire encoding.
 Checks magnitude, not raw value -- a component of -1000 must not qualify just for being < 1.

returns.desc: True if every component's magnitude is at most 1.

symbols.name: cityrp.network.IsRecipientsEmpty
symbols.desc: Whether a resolved recipient value (from `:Filter()`/`:SendOmit()`) contains no one.

params.name: recipients
params.desc: The player metatable, with CityRP's own additions to Garry's Mod's `Player`.

symbols.name: cityrp.network.MANIFEST_COUNT_BITS
symbols.desc: Bits used to write the manifest's entry count.

symbols.name: cityrp.network.MANIFEST_IDBITS_FIELD
symbols.desc:
Fixed-width wire format constants shared between `sv_send.lua` and `cl_receive.lua`. Defined once
 here, rather than as literals repeated on both realms, so the two can never drift apart --
 see AGENTS.md footgun #11 (client/server-paired literals must be edited together).
 Bits used to write `cityrp.network.idBits` itself in the manifest header.

symbols.name: cityrp.network.MarkReady
symbols.desc:
Completes a player's handshake: sends the manifest and initial bootstrap, marks them ready, and
 runs anything queued by `WaitForPlayer`. Idempotent -- a client that re-announces before receiving
 anything back is a safe no-op.
 `__netReady` does not gate live `Update`/`Resync` sends (see `SendUpdate`'s own comment for why);
 it gates the *server's* willingness to accept a resync request from this player and to count them
 as a resync candidate, both of which would be meaningless before their manifest exists.

symbols.name: cityrp.network.NETVAR
symbols.desc:
A registered network variable, mid-configuration or sealed.
 Every field below is set through the chained builder methods; construct with
 `cityrp.network.Register`, never with `setmetatable` directly.

symbols.name: cityrp.network.PassesRecipientCheck
symbols.desc:
Whether `ply` should receive this var's current value, for resync and bootstrap purposes.
 PVS/PAS are treated as bandwidth filters, not secrecy boundaries: they always pass here, because
 resync/bootstrap only ever consider a var for a player who is (or is about to be) in a position to
 receive it anyway. Only `:Filter()` can actually withhold a value from a specific player -- this is
 also why `:Filter()`'s callback doubles as the authorization check, rather than needing a second,
 separately-maintained predicate that could drift out of sync with the one used for live sends.

symbols.name: cityrp.network.QueueEntity
symbols.desc: Adds `ent` to `ply`'s resync queue and marks `ply` as having pending work.

symbols.name: cityrp.network.ReadAutoValue
symbols.desc: Reads a value written by `WriteAutoValue`.

returns.desc: The decoded value, or nil if the tag was Nil.

symbols.name: cityrp.network.ReadIndexHeader
symbols.desc:
Reads an index header written by `WriteIndexHeader` in sv_send.lua: whether an entity index
 follows, and the index itself if so. Shared by the Update and Resync receivers below so this
 wire shape is decoded in exactly one place -- see the matching `WriteIndexHeader` for why
 (AGENTS.md footgun #11: paired literals, or paired shapes, drift when edited independently).

symbols.name: cityrp.network.ReadSignedComponent
symbols.desc: Reads one component written by `WriteSignedComponent`.

returns.desc: The decoded component.

symbols.name: cityrp.network.RecipientsContain
symbols.desc: Whether `ply` is a member of a resolved recipient value.

params.name: recipients
params.desc: The player metatable, with CityRP's own additions to Garry's Mod's `Player`.

symbols.name: cityrp.network.Register
symbols.desc:
Registers a new network variable, or returns the existing one if `name` is already registered.
 Must be called before the registry seals (on `Initialize`) -- see `Seal` below.

params.name: name
params.desc: The variable's name. Must be unique.

returns.desc: The (possibly just-created) `NetVar`, ready for chained configuration.

symbols.name: cityrp.network.registry
symbols.desc: Registered vars by name. Populated by `cityrp.network.Register`, consumed by `Seal`.

symbols.name: cityrp.network.RequestResync
symbols.desc:
Queues `ent` for resync, debounced to at most one request per frame regardless of how many
 entities become visible in that frame.

symbols.name: cityrp.network.RESYNC_COUNT_BITS
symbols.desc: Bits used to write how many entity indices a resync request contains.

symbols.name: cityrp.network.RESYNC_GROUP_OVERHEAD_BITS
symbols.desc:
Approximate extra bits a mapped-index `:Enum()` (`CODEC_CUSTOM`) costs per resync versus a
 batchable one, assuming worst case: its own `WriteIndexHeader` plus the group/var/end framing
 bools `SendGroups` adds around a non-batchable entry -- see `sv_send.lua`. Deliberately a little
 above the literal ~20-bit tally, so a marginal bit saving isn't enough to justify losing
 batchability (see `:Enum()`).

symbols.name: cityrp.network.resyncQueues
symbols.desc:
Per-player resync queues: `ply -> {[Entity] = true}`. Both axes are weak so a disconnect or an
 entity removal cleans itself up even if the explicit `PlayerDisconnected`/`EntityRemoved` hooks
 below somehow miss it (which, per AGENTS.md footgun #3, a third-party `hook.Add` on the same event
 returning non-nil first genuinely could) -- see `GetQueue`'s note for why this is a plain
 weak-keyed set rather than an ordered array.

symbols.name: cityrp.network.SCOPE_BITS
symbols.desc: Bits used to write a `NetScope` value.

symbols.name: cityrp.network.SCOPE_GLOBAL
symbols.desc: Stored in the library, not on any entity; has no owning entity at all.

symbols.name: cityrp.network.SCOPE_LOCALPLAYER
symbols.desc: Stored on the owning player; sent only to that player, never broadcast.

symbols.name: cityrp.network.SCOPE_VEHICLE
symbols.desc:
Storage and wire format identical to `SCOPE_ENTITY` -- only `:Accessor()`'s generated methods
 differ, attaching to `FindMetaTable("Vehicle")` instead of `FindMetaTable("Entity")`.

symbols.name: cityrp.network.Seal
symbols.desc:
Seals the registry: assigns every var a stable numeric ID and locks out further registration.
 Only the server actually assigns IDs, by sorting registered names -- the client waits for the
 server's manifest to populate `byId` by name instead, so the two realms never need to agree on
 sort order or registration order. Safe to call more than once; later calls are no-ops.

symbols.name: cityrp.network.sealed
symbols.desc: Whether the registry has sealed. `Register` after this point is an error.

symbols.name: cityrp.network.SendGlobalsAndLocal
symbols.desc:
Sends every current Global value and `ply`'s own LocalPlayer-scoped values in one no-index group.
 Part of the join bootstrap; Global/LocalPlayer vars aren't entity-visibility-driven so they don't
 go through the resync queue the way entity-scoped vars do. Global values still run through
 `PassesRecipientCheck` here -- a Global var has no owning entity to gate resync eligibility on
 `IsValid`/PVS, so without this check a `:Filter()`-restricted Global value would reach every new
 or reconnecting player regardless of the filter, the moment they join.

symbols.name: cityrp.network.SendGroups
symbols.desc:
Sends a batch of `{ent, vars = {{netvar, value}, ...}}` groups to one player as one or more
 `cityrp.network.Resync` messages, splitting on the byte threshold between groups.
 A non-batchable (custom-codec) var is never shared with any other entry -- it is always flushed
 into, and sent as, a message of its own -- so an undecodable custom value can only ever corrupt
 that one message, not a whole batch of unrelated vars riding alongside it.

params.name: groups
params.type: { ent: Entity?, vars: { netvar: NetVar, value: any }[] }[]

symbols.name: cityrp.network.SendManifest
symbols.desc:
Sends the sealed registry as `id -> name/scope/codec/arg`. Sent once per player, on their first
 `cityrp.network.Sync` announce -- see `MarkReady` below. The ID width travels in the header so the
 two realms can never disagree about it, which is what keeps a load-order difference between them
 from corrupting every value the way it could in the plugin this library replaces.
 A Custom-coded var's real `codecArg` (the `opt` passed to its `:Write()`/`:Read()`) is whatever the
 registering plugin's own shared code chose -- not necessarily numeric, and not something the
 receiving client needs from the wire anyway, since decoding it already requires that client to
 have run the same local `:Read(fn, opt)` call. A placeholder `0` goes out instead of the real
 value so a non-numeric `opt` can never break `net.WriteUInt` here.

symbols.name: cityrp.network.SendUpdate
symbols.desc:
Sends a single var change. Resolves recipients before `net.Start` so an empty `:Filter()` result
 skips networking entirely instead of leaving a started message with nowhere to send.
 Reaches every currently-connected player for Broadcast/PVS/PAS/Omit, including ones who haven't
 finished their handshake yet -- deliberately: filtering the recipient list down to "ready" players
 would mean reimplementing PVS/PAS membership in Lua just to exclude a few joining players from an
 engine call that already does that natively. Instead `cl_receive.lua` discards any Update/Resync
 payload before its own manifest has arrived, which costs that player nothing: `MarkReady` sends a
 full bootstrap right after the manifest, so a live update missed during the join race is already
 reflected in the state that bootstrap sends moments later.

symbols.name: cityrp.network.SetGlobal
symbols.desc: Sets a Global-scoped networked value and, if it changed, broadcasts it (subject to `:Filter()`).

symbols.name: cityrp.network.sortedIds
symbols.desc:
Every assigned ID, in order. Populated once by `Seal` (server only -- the client never assigns its
 own IDs) so repeat consumers like `SendManifest` and `cityrp_network_dump` don't each rebuild and
 sort this from `byId` on every call to a value that cannot change after sealing.

symbols.name: cityrp.network.ValidateClientOwned
symbols.desc:
Checks a `:ClientOwned()` var's constraints and clears the flag if it fails any, so the client
 setter is never generated rather than a var being writable in a shape nobody vetted.

 Runs at seal, not inside `:ClientOwned()`: a chain sets its fields in whatever order it was
 written, so `:ClientOwned():Bool():SetPlayer():Debounce(1)` would see a default scope, a default
 codec and no debounce. `:Predictable()` defers its scope check for the same reason.

params.name: netvar
params.desc: The var to check. A no-op unless it called `:ClientOwned()`.

symbols.name: cityrp.network.WaitForPlayer
symbols.desc: Runs `fn(ply)` once `ply`'s handshake has completed, or immediately if it already has.

symbols.name: cityrp.network.waitQueue
symbols.desc:
Callbacks waiting on a player's handshake to finish. `WaitForPlayer` queues here; cleared (and
 run) once that player's manifest and bootstrap have been sent.

symbols.name: cityrp.network.WriteAutoValue
symbols.desc:
Writes a value self-describingly: a codec tag, then the value via that codec.
 This is what backs both the `Auto` codec and every key/value inside a `Table`.

params.name: value
params.desc: The value to write. `nil` writes only the tag.

symbols.name: cityrp.network.WriteIndexHeader
symbols.desc:
Writes an index header: whether an entity index follows, and the index itself if so. Shared by
 every send path that needs this exact shape (`SendGroups`'s per-group header and `SendUpdate`'s
 per-message header) so the wire format for "does this carry an index" is defined once -- see the
 matching `ReadIndexHeader` in `cl_receive.lua` (AGENTS.md footgun #11).

 A player entity's index is always within the engine's player-slot range, so `MAX_PLAYER_BITS` is
 enough to encode it -- narrower than the general `ENTITY_INDEX_BITS` (`MAX_EDICT_BITS`) every
 non-player entity needs. Which width applies can't be inferred from `netvar.scope` alone -- a
 Player-scoped and an Entity-scoped var can share the same group/index header when they target the
 same physical player entity (`SendGroups` groups by entity, not scope) -- so the leading
 `isPlayer` bool is checked against the entity itself, and travels on the wire since the reader
 doesn't have `ent` yet; it's what this index will construct.

params.name: ent
params.desc: Required (and used) only when `hasIndex` is true.

symbols.name: cityrp.network.WriteSignedComponent
symbols.desc:
Writes one signed vector/angle component, choosing between a raw float and a compact signed
 integer depending on which the value actually needs. Emits its own leading flag bit. Values
 outside the 32-bit signed integer range are forced onto the float path -- `GetSignedBits` clamps
 to 32, which would otherwise silently truncate a huge whole-number component.

symbols.name: cityrp.network.WriteVarEntry
symbols.desc:
Writes one var entry: `[id][isNil][value?]`. Used by the server's live Update and grouped Resync
 paths (`sv_send.lua`) and by the client's `ClientSet` send (`cl_receive.lua`).

symbols.name: NetCodecId
symbols.desc:
Numeric codec IDs. Freely renumberable -- unlike the manifest-assigned `NetVar` IDs in
 `sh_registry.lua` (which travel between realms and must never desync), these are never sent or
 persisted; both realms assign them identically from this shared file at every boot. `Player` is
 inserted in the self-contained/fixed-argument block rather than appended so `AUTO_TAG_MAX` stays a
 simple contiguous bound.

symbols.name: NetRecipientMode
symbols.desc: How a `NetVar`'s updates choose their recipients.

symbols.name: NetScope
symbols.desc: Where a `NetVar`'s value lives and who it is sent to by default.

symbols.name: NETTYPE_BYTE
symbols.desc: Signed 8 bit.

symbols.name: NETTYPE_FLOAT
symbols.desc: 32 bit floating point value.

symbols.name: NETTYPE_INT
symbols.desc: Signed 32 bit.

symbols.name: NETTYPE_LONG
symbols.desc: Signed 64 bit.

symbols.name: NETTYPE_MAX
symbols.desc: Increment this value if you add additional types.

symbols.name: NETTYPE_NIBBLE
symbols.desc: Signed 4 bit.

symbols.name: NETTYPE_SHORT
symbols.desc: Signed 16 bit.

symbols.name: NETTYPE_UBYTE
symbols.desc: Unsigned 8 bit.

symbols.name: NETTYPE_UINT
symbols.desc: Unsigned 32 bit.

symbols.name: NETTYPE_ULONG
symbols.desc: Unsigned 64 bit.

symbols.name: NETTYPE_UNIBBLE
symbols.desc: Unsigned 4 bit.

symbols.name: NETTYPE_USHORT
symbols.desc: Unsigned 16 bit.

symbols.name: NETTYPE_UXLONG
symbols.desc: Unsigned 128 bit.

symbols.name: NETTYPE_XLONG
symbols.desc: Signed 128 bit.

symbols.name: NetVar
symbols.desc:
A registered network variable, mid-configuration or sealed.
 Every field below is set through the chained builder methods; construct with
 `cityrp.network.Register`, never with `setmetatable` directly.

symbols.name: NetVar.__index
symbols.desc:
A registered network variable, mid-configuration or sealed.
 Every field below is set through the chained builder methods; construct with
 `cityrp.network.Register`, never with `setmetatable` directly.

symbols.name: NetVar.Accessor
symbols.desc:
Generates `Get<name>()` (both realms) and `Set<name>()` (server only), attaching to the metatable
 that best matches this var's scope -- `FindMetaTable("Player")` for `:SetPlayer()`/
 `:SetLocalPlayer()`, `FindMetaTable("Vehicle")`/`FindMetaTable("Weapon")` for those, and
 `FindMetaTable("Entity")` otherwise -- see `sh_store.lua`'s `GenerateAccessor` for why that
 distinction exists.

params.name: name
params.desc: Suffix for the generated method names.

returns.desc: For chaining.

symbols.name: NetVar.accessorName
symbols.desc: If set, generates `Get<Name>()`/`Set<Name>()` (setter server-only unless `predictable`) on the metatable `:Accessor()`'s scope maps to -- see `sh_store.lua`'s `GenerateAccessor`.

symbols.name: NetVar.Auto
symbols.desc: Explicitly requests the self-describing codec (the default when no codec method is called).

symbols.name: NetVar.AutoHook
symbols.desc:
Shorthand for `:SetHook()` that derives the hook name from the var's own name, for the common
 case of not caring what it's called -- `"CityRP.Network." .. name .. ".Changed"`, matching this
 codebase's existing `CityRP.<Module>.<Event>` hook naming (`CityRP.DayNight.PeriodChanged`,
 `CityRP.Networking.Register`, etc).

returns.desc: For chaining.

symbols.name: NetVar.Broadcast
symbols.desc:
Sends updates to every player (the default for every scope except LocalPlayer, which is always
 owner-only regardless of this setting).

returns.desc: For chaining.

symbols.name: NetVar.clientOwned
symbols.desc: If true, `:Accessor()` generates a client-side `Set<Name>()` that applies locally *and* sends to the server -- see `:ClientOwned()`. Cleared at seal if the var fails `ValidateClientOwned`.

symbols.name: NetVar.ClientOwned
symbols.desc:
Lets a client set this var on its own player: `Set<Name>()` appears on the client, applying
 locally then sending, and the server applies it through the ordinary `SetNetVar` path so recipient
 rules and the `:Enum()` validator still hold. `cityrp.network.ClientSet` is the same without an
 accessor.

 What arrives is a claim, never a fact -- never gate permissions, economy or anti-cheat on one. See
 `docs/networking.md`.

 Constraints are checked at seal, not here: a builder chain sets its fields in any order, so none of
 them exist yet. See `ValidateClientOwned`.

returns.desc: For chaining.

symbols.name: NetVar.codec
symbols.desc: The wire codec. `CODEC_AUTO` unless a codec constructor was called.

symbols.name: NetVar.codecArg
symbols.desc: Codec-specific argument (bit width for Integer/UInteger, byte length for Data).

symbols.name: NetVar.customRead
symbols.desc: Set by `:Read()`; used when `codec == CODEC_CUSTOM`.

symbols.name: NetVar.customWrite
symbols.desc: Set by `:Write()`; used when `codec == CODEC_CUSTOM`.

symbols.name: NetVar.Data
symbols.desc:
Fixed-length byte string. Pads short values with `\0` to exactly `maxLen` and costs that much
 regardless; for text use `:String(maxLen)` above.

params.name: maxLen
params.desc: Byte length. Both realms must agree on this value; it also travels in the manifest.

returns.desc: For chaining.

symbols.name: NetVar.Debounce
symbols.desc:
Coalesces sets to at most one change per `seconds`: a set in a quiet period dispatches
 immediately, one inside the window overwrites a single pending slot. The apply is debounced too,
 so server-side reads lag by up to `seconds`. `ceiling` reserves the shape for adaptive backoff
 without enabling it -- omitted, it equals `seconds` and the interval never moves. Required by
 `:ClientOwned()`. See `docs/networking.md`.

params.name: seconds
params.desc: Minimum seconds between dispatches. Must be positive.

params.name: ceiling
params.desc: Upper bound for adaptive backoff. Defaults to `seconds`, i.e. no escalation.

returns.desc: For chaining.

symbols.name: NetVar.debounceCeiling
symbols.desc: Upper bound for adaptive backoff. Equal to `debounceInterval` unless `:Debounce()` was given a second argument, in which case escalation is enabled.

symbols.name: NetVar.debounceInterval
symbols.desc: Minimum seconds between dispatches, and the floor an adaptive interval resets to -- see `:Debounce()`.

symbols.name: NetVar.default
symbols.desc: The value `Entity:GetNetVar` returns before anything has been set.

symbols.name: NetVar.Double
symbols.desc: 64-bit IEEE double via `net.WriteDouble`. Also the target for `:Long()` -- see below.

symbols.name: NetVar.Enum
symbols.desc:
Declares this var as an enum over `list`, a sequential (`ipairs`-ordered) array of its legal
 values. Picks between two wire strategies by comparing their actual bit cost:

 - **Direct value** (batchable): `list` is entirely integers. The value itself goes on the wire,
   sized to its min/max via `:Integer`/`:UInteger` -- signed only if `min` is negative. No offset
   from `min` is applied even when every value shares a large common magnitude (e.g. `{100,101}`)
   -- an offset would itself need a `CODEC_CUSTOM` closure, exactly the cost this path avoids.
 - **Mapped index** (not batchable): the value's index in `list` goes on the wire instead, via an
   auto-generated `:Write()`/`:Read()` pair sized to `#list`. Cheaper for a small set of
   large-magnitude or widely-spread values, at the cost of `CODEC_CUSTOM` -- never sharing a
   resync message with sibling vars on the same entity.

 For an all-integer `list`, the mapped index is used only if it beats the direct-value encoding by
 more than `RESYNC_GROUP_OVERHEAD_BITS`. A `list` containing anything non-integer always uses the
 mapped index; there is no numeric value to size a direct encoding from.

 Either way, `Set`ting a value not present in `list` is rejected -- logged, not stored/sent -- by
 `ApplyValue`'s `validate` check. `nil` (clearing the var) always bypasses this check.

params.name: list
params.desc: The enum's legal values, in wire-assignment order. Must be non-empty; a mapped-index list must also have no duplicates.

returns.desc: For chaining.

symbols.name: NetVar.enumList
symbols.desc: The list passed to `:Enum()`, kept for introspection (`cityrp_network_dump`).

symbols.name: NetVar.Filter
symbols.desc:
Sends updates only to whoever `fn` returns, and doubles as the authorization check used by
 resync and late-join sync -- see `sv_send.lua`. Keep `fn` cheap and side-effect free: it can run
 once per update and again per resync candidate.

returns.desc: For chaining.

symbols.name: NetVar.hasDefault
symbols.desc: Whether `:SetDefault()` was called.

symbols.name: NetVar.hookName
symbols.desc: Hook run on change, both realms: `hook.Run(hookName, ent, newValue, oldValue, predicted)`.

symbols.name: NetVar.id
symbols.desc: Assigned at seal. `nil` before the registry seals.

symbols.name: NetVar.Integer
symbols.desc:
`net.WriteInt`/`net.WriteUInt` only accept 1-32 bits -- the plugin this library replaces declared
 64- and 128-bit integer types that could never actually be written. `:Long()` below is the
 closest working replacement for those call sites, not a wider integer.

returns.desc: For chaining.

symbols.name: NetVar.Long
symbols.desc:
Widest integer GLua numbers can actually represent exactly (2^53). An alias of `:Double()` --
 there is no true 64-bit integer codec, because a Lua number cannot hold one losslessly regardless
 of how it is framed on the wire.

returns.desc: For chaining.

symbols.name: NetVar.name
symbols.desc: The registered name. Unique; this is what travels in the manifest.

symbols.name: NetVar.Normal
symbols.desc:
Compact vector codec for components known to stay within +/-1 (e.g. a direction). A component
 outside that range still encodes correctly, just without the compact path's benefit.

symbols.name: NetVar.noSync
symbols.desc: If true, excluded from join sync and resync -- push-only.

symbols.name: NetVar.Player
symbols.desc:
Narrower than `:Entity()` for a value known to always be a player: sizes the index off
 `MAX_PLAYER_BITS` instead of the wider `MAX_EDICT_BITS` every other entity needs. `:Auto()`
 already picks this over `:Entity()` on its own whenever the value actually is a player, so this
 constructor is for declaring the narrower shape explicitly up front, not required for the saving.

symbols.name: NetVar.predictable
symbols.desc: If true, `:Accessor()` also generates a client-side `Set<Name>()` that applies locally (storage + hook only, no network send) instead of being server-only -- see `:Predictable()`.

symbols.name: NetVar.Predictable
symbols.desc:
Allows client-side prediction: `:Accessor()`'s generated `Set<Name>()` becomes available on the
 CLIENT too, applying locally (storage + `:SetHook()` only -- never a network send, the client has
 no authority to send) instead of being server-only. A later confirmed value -- whether that same
 client's predicted action being confirmed, or an unrelated server-side change -- arrives through
 the normal decode path and overwrites the locally-applied one, correcting any drift.

 Only meaningful for `:SetLocalPlayer()` -- a client predicting some other entity's state isn't
 coherent, so `:Accessor()` logs an error and skips generating the client setter on a scope
 mismatch rather than silently letting a broadcast/entity-scoped var be mutated client-side with
 nothing to correct it.

returns.desc: For chaining.

symbols.name: NetVar.Read
symbols.desc: Sets a custom deserializer to pair with `:Write()`.

params.name: readFn
params.desc: Called with `opt` to read the value back.

params.name: opt
params.desc: Passed through as `arg`; typically the same value given to `:Write()`.

returns.desc: For chaining.

symbols.name: NetVar.recipientFn
symbols.desc: Backing function for `:SendOmit()`/`:Filter()`.

symbols.name: NetVar.recipientMode
symbols.desc: How a `NetVar`'s updates choose their recipients.

symbols.name: NetVar.scope
symbols.desc: Where the value is stored and who receives it by default.

symbols.name: NetVar.SendOmit
symbols.desc: Sends updates to everyone except whoever `fn` returns (`net.SendOmit`).

returns.desc: For chaining.

symbols.name: NetVar.SendPAS
symbols.desc:
Sends updates only to players who can potentially hear the entity's position (`net.SendPAS`).
 Same bandwidth-not-secrecy caveat as `:SendPVS()`.

returns.desc: For chaining.

symbols.name: NetVar.SendPVS
symbols.desc:
Sends updates only to players who can potentially see the entity's position (`net.SendPVS`).
 Treated as a bandwidth filter, not a secrecy boundary: resync always includes a PVS var, because
 the client is asking precisely because the entity just entered its PVS. Use `:Filter()` for
 anything that must not reach a player at all.

returns.desc: For chaining.

symbols.name: NetVar.SetDefault
symbols.desc: Sets the value `Entity:GetNetVar`/`cityrp.network.GetGlobal` returns before anything is set.

returns.desc: For chaining.

symbols.name: NetVar.SetEntity
symbols.desc: Scopes this var to a single entity (the default scope).

returns.desc: For chaining.

symbols.name: NetVar.SetGlobal
symbols.desc:
Scopes this var globally -- one value, no owning entity. Use `cityrp.network.SetGlobal`/`GetGlobal`
 rather than an entity method.

returns.desc: For chaining.

symbols.name: NetVar.SetHook
symbols.desc:
Runs `hook.Run(hookName, ent, newValue, oldValue, predicted)` on both realms whenever this var
 changes. `predicted` is `true` only for a client-side local apply from a `:Predictable()` var's
 client `Set<Name>()`; every other trigger (a normal server `Set`, or either realm decoding a
 confirmed value off the wire) passes `nil`.

returns.desc: For chaining.

symbols.name: NetVar.SetLocalPlayer
symbols.desc:
Scopes this var to a single owning player's private state. Never broadcast: sent only to the
 owner via `net.Send(ply)`, regardless of any `:Filter()`/`:SendPVS()` call. Like `:SetPlayer()`,
 `:Accessor()` attaches to `FindMetaTable("Player")`.

returns.desc: For chaining.

symbols.name: NetVar.SetNoSync
symbols.desc:
Excludes this var from join sync and resync -- it is only ever pushed on change. Use for
 fire-and-forget events rather than durable state; a client that was out of PVS during the push
 will never receive it.

returns.desc: For chaining.

symbols.name: NetVar.SetPlayer
symbols.desc:
Scopes this var to a player. Storage/wire format are identical to `:SetEntity()` -- a player is an
 entity -- but `:Accessor()` attaches to `FindMetaTable("Player")` rather than Entity's, so a
 same-named method Player's own metatable already defines natively can't shadow it.

returns.desc: For chaining.

symbols.name: NetVar.SetVehicle
symbols.desc:
Scopes this var to a vehicle. Storage/wire format identical to `:SetEntity()`; only
 `:Accessor()`'s target metatable (`FindMetaTable("Vehicle")`) differs -- see `:SetPlayer()`.

returns.desc: For chaining.

symbols.name: NetVar.SetWeapon
symbols.desc:
Scopes this var to a weapon. Same rationale as `:SetVehicle()`, targeting
 `FindMetaTable("Weapon")` instead.

returns.desc: For chaining.

symbols.name: NetVar.String
symbols.desc:
Text. With no argument, `net.WriteString`/`net.ReadString` -- null-terminated, so the writer picks
 the length. With `maxLen`, a length prefix sized to `maxLen` then exactly that many bytes: no
 padding, and the read length comes from this registration rather than the wire, which is why it is
 the only string form `:ClientOwned()` accepts. Over-length is logged either way, never silently
 dropped (`sh_codecs.lua`). `maxLen` counts bytes, so truncation can split a character.

params.name: maxLen
params.desc: Maximum byte length, 1 to `(2 ^ CODEC_ARG_BITS) - 1`. Omit for the unbounded form.

returns.desc: For chaining.

symbols.name: NetVar.UInteger
symbols.desc: Unsigned counterpart to `:Integer(bits)`. Same 1-32 bit range and the same fallback on misuse.

returns.desc: For chaining.

symbols.name: NetVar.validate
symbols.desc: Optional value validator, set by `:Enum()`. Checked by

symbols.name: NetVar.Write
symbols.desc:
Sets a custom serializer, bypassing the built-in codec table. Because the manifest cannot
 describe an arbitrary function, vars using this are sent one per message rather than batched --
 see `sv_send.lua`.

params.name: writeFn
params.desc: Called with the value (and `opt`) to write it.

params.name: opt
params.desc: Passed through to `writeFn`/the matching `:Read()` call as `arg`.

returns.desc: For chaining.

Internal function, for the batched spawn bootstrap of every player's NSVars.

symbols.name: cityrp.pcasino.AutoExcludeTiers
symbols.desc:
Ascending tiers that trigger automatic, escalating self-exclusion.
 A tier is reached when *either* tally passes its own threshold. `duration` is
 played-time seconds the exclusion lasts. Neither tally is reset when a tier
 fires, so a player who keeps playing once an exclusion lifts escalates straight
 to the next tier rather than restarting.

symbols.desc:

 Already definition-locked prizes (M3, Ninja, Dragon's Breath, Golden Vape) are omitted.
 Trabbi is intentionally left tradable as the joke prize.

symbols.desc: Build the odds browser.

symbols.desc: [SteamID64] = index into AutoExcludeTiers already applied.

symbols.desc: [SteamID64] = net cash position at the casino this sitting (negative while down).

symbols.name: cityrp.pcasino.SessionWagered
symbols.desc: [SteamID64] = total cash staked at the casino this sitting.

symbols.name: cityrp.pcasino.SessionWarnedTier
symbols.desc: [SteamID64] = index into WarningTiers already notified for.

symbols.name: cityrp.pcasino.WarningTiers
symbols.desc:
Ascending tiers that trigger an in-game reminder only, once per tier per session.
 A tier is reached when *either* tally passes its own threshold. The loss side is
 floored well above a single top-tier spin (advanced_high stakes $25,000) so one
 unlucky bet never reads as a loss pattern: tier 1 needs 4 full losses back to back.
 The wagered side is set at 20x the matching loss tier: roughly where an
 average-luck player at the published 95% RTP would be down the loss figure.

symbols.name: cityrp.plugin.Discover

Discovers every plugin under `core/plugins`, resolving folder and file plugins into one key space.
 A folder plugin is a folder of `sv_init.lua`/`cl_init.lua`/`sh_init.lua`; a file plugin is a single
 `sv_<key>.lua`, `cl_<key>.lua` or `sh_<key>.lua` sitting directly in `core/plugins`. Folders outrank
 files, and among files `sh_` outranks `sv_`, which outranks `cl_`. Conflicts and unrecognised Lua
 files are logged on the server and are never fatal. Every candidate is returned regardless of its
 own metadata - `cityrp.plugin.Resolve` reads `.meta.lua` and decides afterwards.

 "Area Manager", `licenseplates` as "Licence Plates").

symbols.name: cityrp.plugin.register
symbols.desc:
Registers a new plugin.
 The plugin is stored under its key, taken from the loader; its display name is recorded as an
 alias so existing `cityrp.plugin.get("Display Name")` call sites keep resolving.

symbols.name: cityrp.plugin.Resolve
symbols.desc:
Discovers every plugin, reads its metadata and resolves a deterministic load order.
 Plugins declare dependencies in an optional `.meta.lua` beside them; a missing required
 dependency or a required cycle stops the plugins involved from loading, and is logged rather
 than raised. A plugin whose metadata declares `disabled = true`, or whose `servers`/`maps`
 conditions exclude it here, takes no part in resolution - it is absent from the returned order,
 contributes no sub-resources, and is reported to any dependent as disabled rather than not
 installed; it reaches `cityrp.plugin.registry` with status `"excluded"` only for diagnostics.
 Everything else discovered is returned even on failure, so a caller can still send a failed
 plugin's files to the client - only inclusion is gated, on `status`.

returns.desc: Every discovered, available plugin, in load order.

symbols.name: cityrp.plugin.SendsSubResourcesToClient
symbols.desc:
Whether any of one plugin's sub-resources will be sent to the client.

 The loader `AddCSLuaFile`s sub-resources *after* the plugin loop in `sh_init.lua` has already
 decided whether to send the plugin's `.meta.lua`, so a plugin with no `cl_init.lua`/`sh_init.lua`
 of its own can still materialise its folder clientside through them - `breathalyser` is exactly
 that shape. Left alone, the client discovers such a plugin with no metadata at all and resolves
 it with its dependencies and availability conditions never evaluated.

 This deliberately mirrors what `includeSubResourceFiles` and `LoadSubResourceItems`/`Derma`
 actually send rather than merely testing whether the folders exist: sending the sidecar for a
 plugin that sends nothing else would materialise the folder clientside on its own, which is the
 opposite failure and the reason the `sendsToClient` gate exists in the first place.

returns.desc: Whether the client will receive any file from this plugin's sub-resources.

modules.name: cityrp.ui
modules.description:
Primary UI Scaling Library for CityRP 2
Provides resolution-aware scaling for all Derma panels and HUD elements.
This library ensures consistent UI sizing across different screen resolutions
and respects user-defined HUD scale preferences (cl_llhud_scale ConVar).

symbols.name: cityrp.ui.AddTitleBarCloseButton
symbols.desc:
Adds a text-only close button to a frame title bar, matching the cooking stove UI.
 The stock DFrame close control is hidden by the cityrp.ui chrome; this draws
 a plain centred X on the dark header rather than a coloured box.

params.name: frame
params.desc: The menu frame. Must already be sized for layout to settle.

params.name: titleBarHeight
params.desc: Title bar height from the styled frame.

returns.desc: The close button.

symbols.name: cityrp.ui.CreateScaledFont
symbols.desc:
Creates a resolution-aware font that scales with the UI scale factor.
 The font size is automatically calculated based on the current scale factor
 and rounded to the nearest integer for crisp rendering.

 ```lua
 cityrp.ui.CreateScaledFont("MyFont", "Open Sans", 14) -- Creates 14px font that scales
 cityrp.ui.CreateScaledFont("BoldTitle", "Open Sans", 24, 700) -- Creates bold 24px font
 ```

params.name: baseSize
params.desc: Base font size in pixels at 1920x1080 reference resolution

params.name: weight
params.desc: Font weight (100-900, default: 500 for normal weight)

returns.desc: The name of the created font (same as input name parameter)

symbols.name: cityrp.ui.GetScaleFactor
symbols.desc:
Gets the current UI scale factor for resolution-aware rendering.
 Combines automatic resolution-based scaling with user-adjustable HUD scale.
 The scale factor is calculated as: (baseScale * autoScale), where:
 - baseScale = cl_llhud_scale ConVar value (0.5 to 2.0, default 1.0)
 - autoScale = max(0.75, screenWidth / 1920)

 ```lua
 local scale = cityrp.ui.GetScaleFactor() -- Returns 2.67 on 5120x1440 with default settings
 ```

returns.desc: The total scale factor to apply to UI elements (typically 0.75 to 5.0+)

symbols.name: cityrp.ui.OnScaleChanged
symbols.desc:
Runs `callback` whenever the UI scale changes.

 The entire UI, not just the HUD. cl_llhud_scale is named for the HUD because
 that is where it started, but it is the user-scale input to GetScaleFactor,
 which every consumer of this library reads -- menus, entity panels and the
 HUD alike. Both of that function's inputs can move while the player is in
 game, so both are watched here: the ConVar, and the screen resolution behind
 the automatic component. Menus that watched only the ConVar kept the font
 sizes they were built with when the resolution changed under them.

 Debounced, because dragging the HUD scale slider fires the ConVar callback
 every tick, and a resolution change can fire alongside one.

 ```lua
 cityrp.ui.OnScaleChanged("door", createDoorMenuFonts)
 ```

params.name: id
params.desc: Unique identifier, used to name the callback, hook and timer.

params.name: callback
params.desc: Called once the scale has settled.

symbols.name: cityrp.ui.Scale
symbols.desc:
Scales a single value based on the current UI scale factor.
 This is the primary function for scaling individual dimensions, margins, positions, etc.

 Rounded to a whole pixel. The raw product is almost always fractional, and
 fractional pixel geometry misbehaves: panels land on half pixels and render
 soft, adjacent elements sized from the same base can differ by one, and
 anything fed into a moving effect such as a screen bounce jitters as the
 fraction rounds differently frame to frame.

 Use GetScaleFactor directly if you genuinely need the unrounded factor --
 for a value that is not a pixel measurement, or where you intend to do the
 arithmetic first and round once at the end.

 ```lua
 local scaledWidth = cityrp.ui.Scale(128) -- Returns 341 on 5120x1440 with 1.0x user scale
 local scaledMargin = cityrp.ui.Scale(8) -- Scales margin consistently with screen size
 ```

params.name: value
params.desc: The base value to scale (in pixels at 1920x1080 reference resolution)

returns.desc: The value multiplied by the current scale factor, to the nearest pixel

symbols.name: cityrp.ui.ScaleCheckBox
symbols.desc:
Applies a scaled font to a DCheckBoxLabel and grows its tick box to match.
 DCheckBoxLabel lays the box out at a fixed size, so setting a scaled font on
 one leaves a small box beside large text. This takes over the checkbox's
 layout so the two stay in proportion.

 Guarded: if the panel's internals are not where we expect, the font is still
 applied and the stock layout is left alone rather than erroring.

 ```lua
 cityrp.ui.ScaleCheckBox(self.lockdoors, "DoorMenuDefault")
 ```

params.name: font

symbols.name: cityrp.ui.Shade
symbols.desc:
Lightens or darkens a colour, preserving its alpha.
 Returns a new colour rather than mutating the one passed in, which matters
 because the shared COL_* enumerations are the usual input.

 Allocates. Cache the result -- work out a panel's hover and pressed shades
 once when you style it, not inside its Paint, or you are building a colour
 every frame the cursor rests on it.

 ```lua
 local hover = cityrp.ui.Shade(COL_BRAND, 25) -- once, at style time
 ```

params.name: amount
params.desc: Positive to lighten, negative to darken.

returns.desc: The shifted colour.

symbols.name: cityrp.vehicledamage
symbols.desc: Main table for vehicle contact damage rules.

symbols.name: cityrp.vehicledamage.scaleSlowContact
symbols.desc:
Replace contact damage below `Minimum Run Over Speed`, scaling from zero at rest up to
 `Maximum Contact Damage`. Replaced rather than scaled because a parked vehicle's physics
 resolving against a player reports impulses past a lethal value, so the incoming number says
 nothing about how hard they were hit.

 Callers must skip run over handling when this returns true, and both damage hooks must call it:
 the `EntityTakeDamage` one bails out beforehand on build servers and for godmoded, knocked out
 or seated victims.

params.name: damageInfo
params.desc: The damage being dealt. Rewritten when the vehicle is too slow.

params.name: vehicle
params.desc: Vehicle behind the damage, saving a lookup when the caller has it.

returns.desc: Whether the damage was replaced with a slow contact value.

symbols.desc:

symbols.name: cityrp.vehicleparams.MPH_TO_HU
symbols.desc:
Hammer units per second per mile-per-hour.
 Inverse of Entity:LLSpeed / Photon_AdjustedSpeed: HU/s * (3600 / 63360) = MPH.
 GetVehicleParams returns engine speeds in HU/s. Since 2021, SetVehicleParams
 uses the same units (not MPH). Vehicle .txt scripts still store MPH.

symbols.name: cityrp.vehicleparams.ParseKeyValues
symbols.desc:
Parse a Valve KeyValues document into an ordered node tree.
 Nodes are `{key = string, value = string}` or `{key = string, children = node[]}`.
 Order, duplicate keys and blocks the schema knows nothing about are all preserved,
 so a parse/serialize round trip only reformats — it never drops content.

returns.desc: Ordered root nodes, or nil when the document is malformed.

symbols.name: cityrp.vehicleparams.RegisterModifier
symbols.desc:
Register a named runtime modifier used by item meta / future mod plugins.
 Re-registering the same id replaces the previous definition (hot-reload safe).

symbols.name: cityrp.vehicleparams.ResolveModifiers
symbols.desc: Build an ordered modifier list from registered ids with optional per-instance data.

params.name: entries
params.type: { id: string, data: any, priority: number }[]

returns.type: { id: string, priority: number, data: any, apply: function }[]

symbols.name: cityrp.vehicleparams.RestoreBaseline
symbols.desc: Restore params from a previously captured baseline.

returns.desc: Whether the baseline was restored.

symbols.name: cityrp.vehicleparams.SerializeKeyValues
symbols.desc:
Serialize editable (MPH) params into a Valve KeyValues vehicle script.
 With `sourceScript`, the original document is reformatted and only schema-owned
 keys are rewritten: `"Vehicle_Sounds"`, wheel materials, `DustCloud` and any other
 key the editor does not model keep their original values. Without it (or when the
 source will not parse) only the `"Vehicle"` physics block can be emitted.

params.name: sourceScript
params.desc: Contents of the vehicle's original script file.

returns.desc: Whether `sourceScript` was parsed and carried through.

symbols.desc:
----------------------------------
 Adds an achievement to the storage.

symbols.desc:
----------------------------------
 Awards a player with achievements.

symbols.name: meska.achievements.create
symbols.desc:
----------------------------------
 Creates all given achievements in the database.

params.name: achievements
params.desc: Initial achievements table. @func[opt] cb Callback Function with the insert ids as return value.

symbols.name: meska.achievements.get
symbols.desc:
----------------------------------
 Either gets all or filtered achievements.

returns.desc: The achievements.

symbols.name: meska.achievements.getBy
symbols.desc:
----------------------------------
 Get achievements by key and value.

returns.desc: The achievements.

symbols.name: meska.achievements.iterator
symbols.desc:
----------------------------------
 Creates all given achievements in the database.

returns.desc: An exhausted iterator, kept for backwards-compatibility.

symbols.name: meska.achievements.load
symbols.desc:
----------------------------------
 Loads all achievements from DB.
 @func[opt] cb Callback Function.
----------------------------------

symbols.name: meska.achievements.loadFor
symbols.desc:
----------------------------------
 Loads the achievements of a player.

symbols.name: meska.achievements.meetsRequirements
symbols.desc:
----------------------------------
 Calls the requirements hook.

symbols.name: meska.achievements.producer
symbols.desc:
----------------------------------
 Creates the achievements one after another while respecting the
 underlying asynchronous DB code-flow. The next achievement is only
 created once its predecessor finished, which prevents race-conditions.
 The callback receives the collected insert ids once the chain is done.
 Note the chain walks the table backwards, so the collected ids come back
 in reverse order relative to the given achievements.

params.name: curIdx
params.desc: The current table index. @func[opt] cb Callback Function with the insert ids as return value. @param[opt] dbIdsMatrix The accumulated insert ids, passed along the chain.

symbols.name: meska.achievements.runAnnounceQueue
symbols.desc:
----------------------------------
 Display delayed announcements.

symbols.name: meska.achievements.tpl
symbols.desc:
----------------------------------
 The template for achievements

returns.desc: The template.

Bone Animations Library

Because I wanted custom, dynamic animations.
Give credit or reference if used in your creations.

symbols.name: INTERP_COSINE
symbols.desc: Best compatability / quality balance.

symbols.name: INTERP_CUBIC
symbols.desc: Overall best quality blending but may cause animation frames to go 'over the top'.

symbols.name: INTERP_LINEAR
symbols.desc: Straight linear interp.

symbols.name: TYPE_GESTURE
symbols.desc: Gestures are keyframed animations that use the current position and angles of the bones. They play once and then stop automatically.

symbols.name: TYPE_POSTURE
symbols.desc: Postures are static animations that use the current position and angles of the bones. They stay that way until manually stopped. Use TimeToArrive if you want to have a posture lerp.

symbols.name: TYPE_SEQUENCE
symbols.desc: Sequences are keyframed animations that use the reference pose. They play forever until manually stopped. Use RestartFrame to specify a frame to go to if the animation ends (instead of frame 1).

symbols.name: TYPE_STANCE
symbols.desc: Stances are keyframed animations that use the current position and angles of the bones. They play forever until manually stopped. Use RestartFrame to specify a frame to go to if the animation ends (instead of frame 1).

never sees, so their volume can only be lowered where the sound is defined. The
`State` blocks in `scripts/vehicles/` therefore name the sound scripts below
instead of a raw `.wav`, and this file registers them at `ENGINE_VOLUME` of the
volume they used to play at.

Sounds a vehicle addon or the base game already defines (`ATV_engine_idle` and
friends) are re-registered with their existing properties and a scaled volume
instead.

Generated by `src/vehicle-engine-sounds.py` - regenerate it rather than editing
the tables below by hand.
