| EDGE-6 | Stale invite to a deleted clan is accepted | Rejected; stale row deleted as a defensive fallback | integration |

---

## 4. Identity validation

### Length boundaries

| Field | Counted in | Reject | Accept min | Accept max | Reject |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Name | characters | 2 | 3 | 32 | 33 |
| Abbreviation | characters | 1 | 2 | 7 | 8 |
| Motto | characters | — | 0 | 80 | 81 |
| Description | **bytes** | — | 0 | 500 | 501 |
| MOTD | **bytes** | — | 0 | 2000 | 2001 |

All pure-fn, BLOCKING. There are **no** line-count or per-line caps.

| ID | Given | Then | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| ID-1 | Name `"O'Brien's Crew"` | Rejected — no quotes or apostrophes | pure-fn |
| ID-2 | Name `"---"` | Rejected — no alphanumeric remains | pure-fn |
| ID-3 | `"THE REAPERS"` when `"The Reapers"` exists | Rejected — case-insensitive collision | integration |
| ID-4 | Name `"  The   Reapers  "` | Stored as `"The Reapers"` — trimmed and collapsed, not rejected | pure-fn |
| ID-5 | Abbreviation `"A-B"` | Rejected — `[%a%d]` only, stricter than Name | pure-fn |
| ID-6 | Abbreviation `"abc"` | Stored as `"ABC"` | pure-fn |
| ID-7 | Motto with an embedded newline and a chat colour code | Stored single-line, both stripped | pure-fn |
| ID-8 | Description of 500 four-byte emoji (2000 bytes) | **Rejected** — Description is byte-counted; 2000 > 500 | pure-fn |
| ID-9 | Name of 32 four-byte emoji (128 bytes) | Accepted — Name is character-counted, and 128 is exactly the ceiling | pure-fn |
| ID-10 | A Name rejected at creation is submitted via the **edit** path | Rejected identically. "A rule applied at intake and skipped at update is not a rule" | integration |
| ID-11 | A Description containing an apostrophe is saved and reloaded | Round-trips intact, no SQL error — behavioural proxy for `QueryParams` use | integration |

### Word filter matrix

| ID | Field | reserved | slur | profanity |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| WF-1..3 | Name | reject | reject | reject |
| WF-4..6 | Abbreviation | reject | reject | reject |
| WF-7..9 | Motto | **allow** | reject | reject |
| WF-10..12 | Description | **allow** | reject | **allow** |
| WF-13..15 | MOTD | **allow** | reject | **allow** |

WF-12 is the highest-value row — the one most likely to be over-blocked by an
implementation that does not vary the category set per field.

| ID | Given | Then |
|---|---|---|
| WF-N1 | Abbreviation `"4DM1N"` | Normalises to ADMIN, rejected |
| WF-N2 | Abbreviation `"A-D-M-I-N"` | Separators stripped, rejected |
| WF-N3 | Homoglyph substitution (Cyrillic а for Latin a) | Belongs to `cityrp.wordfilter`'s own test suite. Clans criteria confirm the library is **invoked correctly per field**, not that its internals work |

---

## 5. Bank

### Amount validation

One `validateBankAmount`, called by deposit **and** withdrawal. All pure-fn, BLOCKING.

| ID | Amount | Then |
|---|---|---|
| BV-1 | `nil` / non-numeric | Reject |
| BV-2 | NaN | Reject |
| BV-3 | `math.huge` (`tonumber("1e400")`) | Reject |
| BV-4 | `100.50` | Reject — non-integer |
| BV-5 | `0` | Reject |
| BV-6 | `-100` | Reject |
| BV-7 | `> MAX_TRANSACTION` ($100,000,000) | Reject |
| BV-8 | `100` | Accept — proves no over-rejection |
| BV-9 | `-500` on the **deposit** path | Rejected identically. A negative deposit is an unauthenticated withdrawal; deposit must not be exempt |
| BV-10 | `> per_withdrawal_cap` on withdrawal | Rejected in Lua — the cap is global config, not in SQL |

### Atomic ledger append

| ID | Given | Then | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| BA-1 | Balance 100 | Withdrawing 101 inserts 0 rows | db-script |
| BA-2 | Actor demoted between request and execution | 0 rows — permission is a predicate inside the statement, not an earlier check | db-script |
| BA-3 | A rank with **no stored row**, relying on the module default | Still permitted — `LEFT JOIN` + `COALESCE(p.value, ?)`. An inner `JOIN` would wrongly deny | db-script |
| BA-4 | Two writers race, computing the same `seq` | Exactly one inserts; the other gets a duplicate-key error on `(clan, seq)` and **retries**. Never a user-facing failure | db-script, two connections |
| BA-5 | Clan with no ledger rows | First deposit yields `seq = 1`, `balance_after` = amount. Withdrawal against empty fails `HAVING` | db-script |
| BA-6 | A successful append | The fire-and-forget cache update follows; **if it fails, the operation still succeeded** | integration |
| BA-7 | Cache and `SUM(delta)` disagree | Ledger wins; cache rebuilt; logged at Error | integration |

### Caps, gate and latch

| ID | Given | Then | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| BC-1 | Clan rolling 24h withdrawals at 70,000 of 75,000 | A further 10,000 is rejected in full | pure-fn |
| BC-2 | Clan has withdrawn 75,000 today via other officers; a freshly promoted officer has withdrawn 0 | Rejected — the cap tracks the **clan**, closing promote→withdraw→demote cycling | db-script |
| BC-3 | Clan 2 days old, 5 members | Bank locked — age not met | pure-fn |
| BC-4 | Clan 10 days old, 2 members | Bank locked — member count not met | pure-fn |
| BC-5 | Clan 3+ days, 3+ members | Unlocked | pure-fn |
| BC-6 | **An unlocked clan drops to 2 members** | **Stays unlocked.** The latch is stored, never recomputed. Funds are never trapped and kicking cannot freeze the bank | pure-fn + integration |
| BC-7 | Player performs any bank action | A second action within 10s is rejected; the cooldown is shared across deposit, withdraw and reclaim | integration |
| BC-8 | A sequence-collision retry occurs | **Not** subject to the cooldown — it is not an entry-route invocation | integration |

### Self-reclaim

| ID | Given | Then | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| BR-1 | 1000 deposited 100s ago (window 600s) | Reclaim allowed | pure-fn |
| BR-2 | Same, 601s ago | Rejected regardless of balance | pure-fn |
| BR-3 | 1000 deposited; balance now 700 | Receives 700 — lesser of unreclaimed remainder and current balance | pure-fn |
| BR-4 | Recruit with no `bank.withdraw` | Reclaim allowed — not gated by withdraw permission | integration |
| BR-5 | Clan rolling cap exhausted | Reclaim still allowed — exempt, closing reclaim-starvation | integration |
| BR-6 | 1000 deposited; 400 reclaimed; 700 more attempted in window | Capped to the 600 remainder, not rejected outright | pure-fn |

### Consent

| ID | Given | Then | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| BCO-1 | Never deposited to this clan | Prompt shown before the deposit completes | pure-fn |
| BCO-2 | Last deposit or withdrawal 31 days ago (limit 30) | Prompt shown again | pure-fn |
| BCO-3 | Last deposit 10 days ago | No prompt | pure-fn |
| BCO-4 | Only viewed the balance/ledger for 40 days | **Prompt shown** — passive activity is not a bank interaction | pure-fn |
| BCO-5 | Consented in Clan A | First deposit to Clan B prompts independently — consent is per `(steamid, clan)` | integration |
| BCO-6 | Prompt displayed | States all four facts, including whether **this player** holds withdraw permission | manual |

### Dissolution

Fixture — balance 900. A (member): +1000/−200 → net 800. B (member): +500/−700 → net −200. C (kicked): +300 → net 300. Claims = 1100.

| ID | Then | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| BD-1 | A receives `floor(900×800/1100)` = **654**; B receives **0**; C, an ex-member, receives `floor(900×300/1100)` = **245**; the 1 remainder is discarded | pure-fn |
| BD-2 | Negative net clamps to zero — B never owes anything | pure-fn |
| BD-3 | Total claims zero → equal split among zero-net depositors, else all to the leader, **and an Error is logged** — the branch should be unreachable under event sourcing | pure-fn |
| BD-4 | A deposit of 500 with a 200 reclaim yields net 300 — reclaims count as withdrawals for net purposes while remaining tagged `reclaim` | pure-fn |
| BD-5 | After deletion, ledger rows still exist — the audit record outlives the clan | integration |
| BD-6 | Deletion is **immediate**: no hold, no countdown, no cancellation window | integration |
| BD-7 | Confirmation states the balance and the distribution, and requires the clan name typed | manual |
| BD-8 | Online recipients get `GiveMoney` then `SaveData` | integration |
| BD-9 | Offline recipients get a `remote` row that returns **without** `done()` until they connect | integration |
| BD-10 | On a `noSave` server (build/beta/beta2/event) the row returns without `done()`, deferring to a real server | integration |
| BD-11 | Two servers poll the same payout row | Exactly one claims it via `UPDATE ... SET done=1 WHERE id=? AND done=0`; the other affects 0 rows and does not grant | db-script |

### Undo

| ID | Given | Then | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| BU-1 | Undo within 300s of creation | Full 50,000 refunded; no distribution logic invoked | integration |
| BU-2 | Balance is nonzero, however that arose | `/clan undo` rejected, directing to `/clan delete`. A defensive guard that must hold independently of the unlock gate | pure-fn |

---

## 6. Regression — the twelve defects

Each must **fail** against the current implementation.

| ID | Defect | Then | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| REG-1 | 1 — unchecked accept | A player already in Clan A accepting a Clan B invite is rejected outright; success is never reported unless the write affected a row | integration |
| REG-2 | 2 — return from inside async callback | A kicked or promoted online member's live state updates in the same session, no relog | integration |
| REG-3 | 3 — `results`/`result` typo | State recovery repopulates clans; never net-clears | integration |
| REG-4 | 4 — string/number mismatch, missing `done()` | `deleteclan` reaches a terminal state; never retries forever | db-script |
| REG-5 | 5 — hardcoded server list | One row per server from **configuration**; `v4b1_fl2` receives its row. Not `server='all'`, which only the first poller consumes | db-script |
| REG-6 | 6 — ranks by reference | Same test as INV-9 — write once | pure-fn |
| REG-7 | 7 — permissions that gate nothing | Every permission with a config surface actually gates its claimed action | integration |
| REG-8 | 8 — `clan_member` typo | Leadership transfer to an **offline** target succeeds. Note the underlying charset mismatch must also be fixed | db-script |
| REG-9 | 9 — shared timer name | `/clan model` is not a registered command; no `cityrp.model.register` call for clan models; models unreachable via the normal flow (fail-closed) | integration |
| REG-10 | 10 — unguarded nil index | A player with no clan invoking clan-info gets a clean message, no server error | integration |
| REG-11 | 11 — missing `return` after `done()` | `reloadclan`/`deleteclan` with `cityrp.clans` absent return cleanly, no nil index | integration |
| REG-12 | 12 — `model.remove` no-op | `cityrp.model.remove` actually deregisters; `conds` does not grow across reloads | pure-fn |

---

## 7. Concurrency — how to actually test it

GMod Lua is single-threaded and cooperative, so two Lua calls in one process
cannot race. **The real contention is between database writers** — this server,
another server, a future admin tool — and what protects against it is the
`UNIQUE (clan, seq)` constraint, not anything in Lua.

**Two simultaneous withdrawals.** Seed a balance of 30,000. Open two MySQL
connections. Fire the real generated `INSERT` for 25,000 from each with minimal
delay, or widen the window with held-open transactions. Assert exactly one
succeeds, the other hits the duplicate key and retries, and the final balance is
exactly 5,000 — never negative, never double-deducted.

*Cheaper secondary check*: count database round-trips per attempt using the
callback-queuing mock in `lua/tests/cityrp2/libraries/sv_achievements.lua`. A
read-then-write implementation issues two queries where the correct one issues
one — detectable without any real race.

**Kick during withdrawal.** Do not chase true simultaneity. Test both orderings
deterministically, since correctness under either *is* the property: kick commits
first → withdrawal inserts 0 rows, balance unchanged; withdrawal commits first →
it succeeds and the kick still succeeds after. Assert the outcome is always one
of those two, never a third.

**Simultaneous promotion** needs no harness at all — see EDGE-1.

---

## Open items

| # | Item |
|---|---|
| 1 | Confirm `lua/tests/` infrastructure and CI wiring before assuming any framework is available |
| 2 | Whether a `core.invite`-only holder sees the pending invite list ([ui.md](ui.md)) |

topics.title: Clans — Bank Module
topics.body:
# Clans — Bank Module

Module 2. Shared clan funds: deposits, rank-gated withdrawals, and an audit
ledger.

> **Status**: In Design. Depends on [core.md](core.md) for ranks and permissions.
> See [design.md](design.md) for the module framework.

## Source

Issue #1418 (*Clan/Business Account*) asks for a clan wallet the owner and
officers can deposit to and withdraw from, motivated by *"business-oriented
clans that wish to have a clan account to place funds into for business
expenses, which may include real estate, equipment, salaries."*

Issue #1600 separately proposes clan group accounts with leader-configured
access, and **interest** on stored balances as a deposit incentive.

## Economic stance

**Deposit and withdrawal are neutral transfers.** Wallet to bank, 1:1. They
become a sink or a faucet only if a fee or interest is attached — and that is the
actual decision, not something inherent to having a bank.

### No interest

Interest is money created from nothing, uncapped, on every balance, forever.
The game already runs a 10% income tax (`cityrp.configuration["Default Tax"]`)
specifically to manage money supply on *earned* income; adding an ungated faucet
that rewards parking cash more reliably than working is inconsistent with that
stance.

If #1600's underlying goal — give players a reason to bank rather than hoard —
still matters, the sink-safe forms are a fee-funded redistribution pool, or a
non-monetary prestige incentive. Both are larger scope and neither is proposed
for v1.

### No deposit or withdrawal fee

**Decided: no fee mechanism is built.** This is not a configurable rate defaulted
to zero — there is no fee code path, and none needs testing.

A percentage haircut punishes the legitimate case #1418 describes (a business
clan saving for real estate) and is a rounding error to anyone moving duped or
stolen money — they do not care about efficiency loss on money they did not
earn. Taxing the transaction type does not distinguish good actors from bad; it
just taxes the honest ones harder, because they are the ones who notice and
change behaviour.

If a fee is ever proposed, it needs fresh justification rather than a config
change: the analysis above concluded fees are the wrong lever for the problem
they are usually reached for, so re-adding one means the reasoning changed.

### The laundering question, honestly framed

Deposit-by-A / withdraw-by-B is an untaxed player-to-player transfer. But this
is **not a new capability** — `/salary add` already does a raw
`GiveMoney(-x)` / `GiveMoney(x)` with no fee and no persistent audit trail
([employee_salary/sv_init.lua:131](../../../gamemodes/cityrp_2_by_limelightgaming/gamemode/core/plugins/employee_salary/sv_init.lua)).

The bank changes the *shape* of an existing route in three ways that matter:

1. **Pooling breaks attribution** — a withdrawal does not reveal whose deposit it was.
2. **Lump sum, not metered** — salary drips per payday; a withdrawal is instant.
3. **Cheap containers** — $50,000 is trivial against amounts worth laundering.

What closes it is **throttling and attribution, not taxation**: per-transaction
and rolling caps limit blast radius and force multiple logged steps; a small,
named withdrawer set shrinks the suspect pool; and a queryable ledger makes it
investigable. On a human-moderated server, staff investigation is the real
enforcement layer — the ledger is the control, and it is **not optional scope**.

> Worth checking separately: if `/salary` remains unlogged, the bank must not
> become the *softer* target purely by having better logging than the
> alternative. Flagged in [plan.md](plan.md) as an adjacent gap.

## Tuning knobs

| Variable | Type | Default | Safe range | Breaks if too low | Breaks if too high |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ~~`deposit_fee_pct`~~ | — | **not implemented** | — | — | No fee. Not a knob defaulted to zero — the mechanism is not built |
| ~~`withdrawal_fee_pct`~~ | — | **not implemented** | — | — | As above |
| ~~`interest_rate`~~ | — | **not implemented** | — | — | Any nonzero value is an uncapped faucet with no offsetting sink |
| `per_withdrawal_cap` | currency | **$25,000** | $10k–$100k | Legitimate large purchases need many repeated withdrawals; players route around the bank via `/salary` | Stops constraining anything at the $50k creation-cost scale; one action empties a treasury |
| `rolling_withdrawal_cap` | currency / 24h, **clan-scoped** | **$75,000** | 3–6× per-transaction cap | Blocks legitimate high-tempo operations | Above ~10× it stops throttling at all |
| `bank_capacity_ceiling` | currency | **`BIGINT` column ceiling** | — | — | Not unbounded. `clans.bank` is currently `int DEFAULT 0 NULL` — a signed 32-bit ceiling of 2,147,483,647, and NULL-able, so `SET bank = bank + ?` against a NULL row yields NULL and the deposit vanishes. Migrate to `BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` before the Bank module ships |
| `creation_cost_seeds_bank` | bool | **false** | — | — | Seeding creates arbitrage between creation cost, deposits and the refund paths |
| `balance_on_delete` | enum | **pro-rata by net contribution** | — | — | `forfeit` destroys money members contributed in good faith; `refund-leader` is a direct exit-scam vector |
| `self_reclaim_window` | seconds | **600** | 120–1800 | Too short to catch a mistake or a pressured deposit | Long enough to use the bank as a personal stash, and widens the window where a legitimate clan spend is undone underneath it |
| `consent_reprompt_days` | days | **30** | 7–90 | Prompt fatigue; players click through without reading | The warning goes stale — leadership may have changed entirely since they last agreed |
| `unlock_min_age` | days | **3** | 1–7 | Negligible friction against a same-day mule clan | Locks out the small business clan #1418 describes for over a week |
| `unlock_min_members` | count | **3** | 2–5 | At 2, the cheapest collusion pair clears it trivially | At 5 it excludes #1418's stated use case |

Two of these are load-bearing rather than ordinary knobs:

- **The rolling cap must be clan-scoped, not per-person.** If each promoted
  withdrawer got a fresh allowance, the promote → withdraw → demote cycle
  bypasses it by rotating accounts. One clock, shared.
- **`unlock_min_age` = 3 days is what actually closes the deposit-then-undo
  scam**, not a special case in the undo path. Three days ≫ the 300-second undo
  window, so a bank cannot hold deposits while undo is available. Treat that as
  a primary reason for the gate, not a coincidence.

### The unlock is a one-way latch

Once a clan meets the gate, **it never relocks**, even if membership later falls
below `unlock_min_members`.

This must be implemented as a **stored flag** — `clans.bank_unlocked_at`, set
once when the conditions are first met. Do **not** evaluate
`age >= N AND members >= M` on each action: that is the obvious implementation
and it relocks automatically as a side effect.

Relocking would be actively harmful:

- **It traps funds.** Members would be unable to withdraw money they are entitled
  to, for a reason unrelated to their own conduct.
- **It is a griefing vector.** A leader could kick members specifically to freeze
  the bank.
- **It does not serve the gate's purpose.** The gate exists to stop disposable
  mule clans, which is a creation-time concern. A clan that has demonstrably
  existed for three days with three members has satisfied it permanently;
  shrinking later does not make it retroactively disposable.

The latch also simplifies dissolution: a clan that never unlocked has a zero
balance by construction, so there is nothing to distribute.

`unlock_min_members` = 3 is deliberately lighter than the 5-member gate proposed
for clan inventory in #1624 — money access has lower per-unit abuse potential
than concrete item storage. That differential is a judgement call worth
confirming.

## Rank gating

Withdrawal is not "acting on another rank", it is "acting on the treasury", so it
does not use the threshold shape.

| Permission | Kind | Leader | Officer | Lieutenant | Private | Recruit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `bank.deposit` | boolean | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| `bank.withdraw` | boolean | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ |

- **Deposit open to all.** Depositing cannot hurt the depositor beyond what they
  willingly hand over; gating it only frustrates "I want to chip in".
- **Withdraw = Leader and Officer**, matching #1418's explicit "owner/officers".

> No `bank.configure_limits` permission. The tuning knobs (`per_withdrawal_cap`,
> `rolling_withdrawal_cap`, `unlock_min_age`, `unlock_min_members`,
> `self_reclaim_window`, `consent_reprompt_days`) are server operator config,
> not per-clan settings — no in-game surface edits them, so there is nothing
> for a permission to gate. A permission with no connected feature was a
> specification gap, not a real capability; removed rather than defined after
> the fact.

**There is no per-rank withdrawal cap.** `per_withdrawal_cap` is a single global
value applying to every withdraw-capable rank, so `bank.withdraw` is a plain
boolean rather than a `NUMERIC_LIMIT`.

This simplifies the atomic statement materially. A *per-rank* cap is racy — the
rank can change between check and write, which is why it had to live inside the
statement. A *global* cap is a configuration constant that cannot change
underneath a request, so it is validated in Lua alongside `MAX_TRANSACTION` and
never appears in SQL at all.

> Note: `NUMERIC_LIMIT` now has no consumer. It is retained in
> [core.md](core.md#permission-model) as a general-purpose kind, but nothing
> currently uses it — worth revisiting if no module claims it by the time Core
> ships.

The clan-scoped rolling cap and the unlock gate are **not** rank permissions
either. They are aggregate constraints evaluated after the permission check
passes, and live in this module's own logic.

## Informed deposit

Deposits are open to every rank, but withdrawal is not — so a member without
withdraw permission is handing over money they cannot themselves retrieve. That
must be a choice, not a surprise.

**A consent prompt is shown before the deposit completes when either:**

- this is the player's first deposit to this clan, or
- more than `consent_reprompt_days` have passed since their last bank
  interaction with this clan.

**A bank interaction is an explicit deposit or withdrawal** — a reclaim counts,
since the ledger already treats it as a withdrawal. Passive activity does not:
opening the bank tab, viewing the balance or reading the ledger leave the clock
running. The prompt exists because the player has not *moved money* recently
enough to be confident the arrangement still holds.

Otherwise no prompt appears. Consent is stored per `(steamid, clan)`, not
globally — agreeing in one clan says nothing about trusting another, and clan
leadership changes over time, which is what the staleness re-prompt exists for.

The prompt must state plainly:

1. Deposited funds become clan property.
2. Only ranks holding `bank.withdraw` can take money out — and it names whether
   the player currently holds it.
3. Deposits can be reclaimed by the depositor for `self_reclaim_window` after
   the deposit, and not after.
4. If the clan is dissolved, remaining funds are distributed by net contribution.

## Self-reclaim

A depositor may reclaim **their own** recent deposit without holding
`bank.withdraw`.

| Property | Rule |
|---|---|
| Eligibility | Per deposit, within `self_reclaim_window` of that deposit |
| Amount | The lesser of the unreclaimed remainder of that deposit and the current balance |
| Permission | None required — this is not a withdrawal |
| Rolling cap | **Does not count** against `rolling_withdrawal_cap` |
| Ledger | Recorded as a distinct `reclaim` action, but counts as a withdrawal for net-contribution purposes |
| Atomicity | Same conditional `UPDATE` pattern as withdrawal |

Exempting reclaims from the rolling cap is deliberate. If they counted, a
malicious leader could deliberately exhaust the clan's daily cap to block a
member from recovering their own money.

Reclaim is not a general withdrawal route: it is capped at what you put in, it
expires, and it cannot touch anyone else's contribution.

## Correctness and security requirements

### The ledger is authoritative — event sourcing

`clan_bank_transactions` is an **append-only event stream** and the sole source
of truth. Balance is not stored data; it is a **projection** — a fold over the
stream. `clans.bank` is a materialised view of that projection and is
authoritative for nothing.

Consequences that follow from the model rather than from policy:

- **Every balance change is an event.** Deposits, withdrawals, reclaims and
  dissolution payouts are all entries, distinguished by action type.
- **State is always reconstructable** by replaying the stream. The cache can be
  discarded and rebuilt at any time.
- **Nothing is ever edited or deleted.** A correction is a compensating entry
  with its own reason, so the history of the correction is itself auditable.
- **The ledger outlives the clan.** It is not deleted on dissolution; it is both
  the audit record and the input to the distribution calculation.
- Any invariant expressible over the stream — such as "balance equals the sum of
  deltas" — is checkable rather than assumed.

`clans.bank` is **display only**. It is read for UI and for cheap
non-authoritative eligibility hints, and nothing else depends on it.

**Rules that follow:**

- The **ledger insert is the authoritative write**. It happens first, and it is
  what authorises and records the mutation.
- The cache update is a **fire-and-forget mutation issued after the ledger
  callback returns**. If it fails, nothing is lost — the value is derived, and
  reconciliation or the next write corrects it. Do not retry it, do not block on
  it, and do not fail the transaction because of it.
- **On any disagreement, the ledger wins.** Rebuild the cache from the stream.
- **Dissolution distribution reads the ledger, never the cache.**
- Reconciliation on clan load and periodically: assert `clans.bank == SUM(delta)`.
  Log a mismatch at Error, rebuild, and surface it to staff — but treat it as an
  observability signal, not a fault.

This removes the `db.lua` transaction gap entirely. With the ledger written first
and the cache derived, there is no window in which money moves without an audit
record — the failure mode inverts from "unrecoverable" to "cosmetic".

### Consequence: the cache was also the lock

The cache `UPDATE` was doing a second job — a conditional update against a single
`clans` row takes a row lock, and that is what serialised concurrent withdrawals
across server processes. Taking it off the critical path removes that, and
summing the ledger in a subquery serialises nothing: two withdrawals can both
read the same total and both pass.

**Replace it with a per-clan sequence number**, which is the standard optimistic
concurrency control for an event stream:

- The ledger carries `seq`, with **`UNIQUE (clan, seq)`**.
- Each write computes `seq = COALESCE(MAX(seq), 0) + 1` for that clan inside the
  same `INSERT ... SELECT`.
- Concurrent writers compute the same `seq`; the unique constraint rejects the
  loser with a duplicate-key error.
- The loser **retries** — recomputing balance and sequence against the now-current
  stream. Bank operations are low-frequency, so contention is rare and a small
  retry budget is sufficient.

Also store `balance_after` on each row, computed in the same statement. It makes
the current balance a single-row read rather than a full fold, and makes cache
rebuilds and audits cheap.

**A duplicate-key rejection is not a user-facing error.** It means "someone else
wrote first" — retry, and only surface a failure if the retry budget is
exhausted.

### Withdrawals must be a single atomic statement

The balance check, the permission check and the ledger append are one statement.
Never read the balance in Lua, decide, then write.

```sql
INSERT INTO clan_bank_ledger
    (clan, seq, steamid, action, delta, balance_after, created_at)
SELECT ?,                                    -- clan
       COALESCE(MAX(l.seq), 0) + 1,          -- next sequence
       ?,                                    -- actor
       'withdraw',
       -?,                                   -- amount
       COALESCE(SUM(l.delta), 0) - ?,        -- amount
       UNIX_TIMESTAMP()
FROM clan_bank_ledger l
WHERE l.clan = ?
  AND EXISTS (
      SELECT 1
      FROM clan_members m
      LEFT JOIN clan_rank_permissions p
             ON p.clan = m.clan AND p.rankid = m.rank
            AND p.permission_id = 'bank.withdraw'
      WHERE m.clan = ? AND m.steamid = ?
        AND COALESCE(p.value, ?) = 1         -- ? = registered default
  )
HAVING COALESCE(SUM(l.delta), 0) >= ?        -- amount
```

`COALESCE(p.value, ?)` is still required even for a boolean: Core resolves module
defaults at read time and never materialises them, so an inner `JOIN` would find
no row for a rank relying on the default and wrongly **deny** it. The `LEFT JOIN`
plus the default bound as a parameter applies the same resolution order as
`hasPermission`.

The per-transaction cap does **not** appear here — it is global configuration,
checked in `validateBankAmount`.

Then branch on the outcome:

| Result | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 1 row inserted | Accepted. Issue the fire-and-forget cache update. |
| 0 rows | Rejected — insufficient balance, or permission absent or too low. |
| Duplicate-key error on `(clan, seq)` | Lost a race. **Retry**, do not report failure. |

A clan with no ledger rows still returns one aggregate row of `NULL`s, so the
`COALESCE` calls yield `seq = 1` and `balance = 0` — a first deposit works
(subject to the unlock gate below), and a withdrawal against an empty bank
correctly fails the `HAVING`.

**The `LEFT JOIN` and `COALESCE` are both load-bearing** — an earlier draft of
this statement checked only a boolean permission flag, which was wrong twice
over:

1. It never compared the requested amount against the rank's `NUMERIC_LIMIT`
   cap, so the cap would have to be checked in Lua *before* the statement —
   reopening precisely the rank-change-then-withdraw ordering race this pattern
   exists to close.
2. An inner `JOIN` against `clan_rank_permissions` only matches **materialised**
   rows. Core resolves module defaults at read time and never materialises them,
   so a rank relying on the declared default would have no row and be wrongly
   **denied**.

### Deposits are gated by the unlock latch too

**Decided:** deposits are blocked until the clan's bank has unlocked, not only
withdrawals. An earlier pass left this implicit — "the deposit-then-undo scam
cannot arise because the bank does not exist yet" — without ever writing the
statement that makes it true. That is a real gap: nothing upstream of the
ledger actually stops a deposit into a locked bank on its own. Fixed here by
giving deposits the same rigor as withdrawal's statement, not by relying on it
following from prose elsewhere in this document.

```sql
INSERT INTO clan_bank_ledger
    (clan, seq, steamid, action, delta, balance_after, created_at)
SELECT ?,                                    -- clan
       COALESCE(MAX(l.seq), 0) + 1,          -- next sequence
       ?,                                    -- actor
       'deposit',
       ?,                                    -- amount
       COALESCE(SUM(l.delta), 0) + ?,        -- amount
       UNIX_TIMESTAMP()
FROM clan_bank_ledger l
WHERE l.clan = ?
  AND EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM clans c
      WHERE c.id = ? AND c.bank_unlocked_at IS NOT NULL
  )
```

No permission predicate — `bank.deposit` is universal — so the `EXISTS` clause
carries only the unlock check, which is why this statement is otherwise
simpler than withdrawal's. Same result branching: 1 row inserted is accepted,
0 rows means the bank has not unlocked yet (there is no other rejection reason
for a deposit once `validateBankAmount` has already passed in Lua).

This closes the deposit-then-undo scam by construction rather than by
implication: a bank that has not unlocked cannot accept a deposit, full stop,
independent of the `unlock_min_age` vs. `self_reclaim_window`/undo-window
arithmetic argued above. The arithmetic argument still holds and is worth
keeping as the *reason* `unlock_min_age` is sized the way it is, but the
deposit statement — not the arithmetic — is what actually enforces it.

`COALESCE(p.value, ?)` resolves this: Lua reads the registered default from the
permission registry and binds it as a parameter, so the SQL applies the same
resolution order as `hasPermission` without the defaults ever being written to
the table. A `NULL` default coalesces to `NULL`, and `NULL >= x` is not true, so
"no permission" still fails closed.

The same shape applies to any module permission gating a racing mutation.

This single pattern closes three separate attacks at once:

- **Lost update / double spend** — two withdrawals racing cannot both read the
  same starting balance, because there is no separate read.
- **Rank-change-then-withdraw ordering** — a demotion cannot land in a gap
  between the permission check and the money movement, because there is no gap.
- **Replay** — combined with a request row keyed on `status = 'pending'`,
  resubmitting a processed request finds no matching row and is a guaranteed
  no-op.

> **Prerequisite.** `DB:RunChecked` and `DB:QueryParamsChecked`
> ([db.lua:164, 257](../../../gamemodes/cityrp_2_by_limelightgaming/gamemode/db.lua))
> currently discard the affected-row count for non-`INSERT` queries. This pattern
> needs it — a small addition to both functions, to be agreed with the lead
> programmer before implementation.

**Cross-process note.** Multiple game servers and the web app share one MySQL
database. An in-process Lua lock protects nothing against a second server
process. The atomic conditional `UPDATE` is the only real serialisation point,
because the database is the only thing all writers share.

### Amount validation

One `validateBankAmount(amount)` function, called by **both** deposit and
withdrawal. Do not write two.

```lua
if amount == nil then                     -- non-numeric
elseif amount ~= amount then              -- NaN
elseif amount == math.huge then           -- non-finite ("1e400" parses to inf)
elseif amount ~= math.floor(amount) then  -- non-integer; money is whole units
elseif amount <= 0 then                   -- zero and negative both rejected
elseif amount > MAX_TRANSACTION then      -- also guards precision loss above 2^53
```

**`MAX_TRANSACTION` is not the withdrawal cap.** The two are unrelated and were
previously easy to confuse:

| | `MAX_TRANSACTION` | `per_withdrawal_cap` |
|---|---|---|
| Job | Safety rail against absurd input, precision loss above 2^53, and the column ceiling | Policy: how much a rank may take at once |
| Applies to | Deposits **and** withdrawals | Withdrawals only |
| Enforced in | `validateBankAmount`, before any other check | The `bank.withdraw` permission value |
| Varies by rank | No — it is a global constant | Yes |

**Proposed value: $100,000,000.** Two thousand times the clan creation cost, far
above any plausible legitimate single transfer, and small enough that even
repeated maximum deposits stay many orders of magnitude below the `BIGINT`
ceiling. Lua numbers are doubles, so this also sits comfortably under the 2^53
integer-precision limit.

A negative "deposit" that escapes this is functionally an unauthenticated
withdrawal — asymmetric validation between the two paths is itself the
vulnerability. This check is UX only; the atomic `UPDATE` is the enforcement.

### Audit ledger

Two logs, two purposes — do not conflate them.

- `cityrp.logs.add()` for the admin-visible trail. Note it buffers in memory and
  flushes every 20 seconds, so a crash inside that window loses the entry.
  Acceptable for chat logs; **not acceptable as the sole record of money**.
- A dedicated `clan_bank_transactions` row, written in the same callback as the
  atomic `UPDATE`, before notifying the player. This is the audit of record.
  Minimum fields: clan, request ID, actor SteamID and name, action, amount,
  resulting balance, timestamp, originating surface.

### Rate limiting

**A 10-second cooldown per player, shared across all bank entry routes** —
deposit, withdraw and reclaim draw on one clock, so alternating between them
cannot bypass it. That is six actions per minute, comfortably above any real
usage pattern and well below anything worth automating.

Enforced **server-side at the entry route**. A client-side cooldown is a
usability affordance, never the control.

**The internal sequence-collision retry is exempt.** It is not an entry-route
invocation — it is machinery responding to contention that the player did not
cause and cannot see. Subjecting it to the cooldown would convert a routine race
into a ten-second stall or a spurious failure. Retries are bounded by the retry
budget, not by the rate limit.

## Degenerate strategies

| Exploit | Mechanism | Closing rule |
|---|---|---|
| Throwaway mule clan | Create, invite, deposit, withdraw, abandon | Age and member gates delay it; caps force multiple logged actions; ledger makes it traceable |
| Promote → withdraw → demote cycling | Rotate allies through Officer to reset a per-person cap | Clan-scoped rolling cap — everyone draws against one clock |
| Bank-drain-before-leaving | An Officer withdraws heavily then leaves | **Not mechanically preventable** while withdrawal is instant. The control is attribution: a small, named, logged withdrawer set makes it attributable and bannable. State this plainly — it is a trust control, not a hard block |
| **Deposit-to-join scam** | A leader tells a recruit to deposit to "prove commitment", withdraws it, then kicks them. Requires no exploit — it is the permission model working as specified | Consent prompt makes the risk explicit before the first deposit; self-reclaim gives a `self_reclaim_window` escape; pro-rata dissolution returns a share even to kicked members; the ledger makes the rest investigable |
| Reclaim-cap starvation | A leader exhausts the clan rolling cap specifically to block a member reclaiming their own deposit | Reclaims are exempt from the rolling cap |
| Kick-before-dissolve | A leader kicks members before deleting, to keep their contributions | Distribution includes everyone in the ledger, not only current members |
| Deposit-then-undo arbitrage | Mark deposits during the 300s undo window; creator undoes | Closed by construction via the 3-day unlock gate. **Defensive guard regardless**: if `bank != 0`, block `/clan undo` and require `/clan delete` |
| Self-serving drain-then-delete | A withdraw-capable member withdraws, then immediately deletes the clan, profiting from pro-rata dilution — see [Why there is no deletion hold](#why-there-is-no-deletion-hold) | **Not mechanically preventable** — same class as bank-drain-before-leaving. Attribution via the ledger; ongoing pattern monitoring is a community-management call, not an engineering one |

## Undo and delete

**`/clan undo`** (300s grace, full $50,000 refund): with the 3-day unlock gate,
and deposits themselves blocked until the gate is met (see
[Deposits are gated by the unlock latch too](#deposits-are-gated-by-the-unlock-latch-too)),
the scenario cannot arise — a clan within its 300s undo window is nowhere near
`unlock_min_age`, so its bank cannot hold a deposit yet. Add the guard anyway
so this stays true if the gate is ever loosened. No new bank logic is needed in
the common case.

*If the age gate is rejected*, the fallback is: refund the creator's $50,000 as
today, and separately refund each depositor their own logged deposits to their
own wallet — never crediting bank contents to the creator. If per-depositor
refund is not buildable for v1, the safe minimum is to disallow undo outright
whenever the balance is nonzero.

**`/clan delete`** (leader only, confirmation code, $25,000 refund) with a
nonzero balance:

- The $25,000 refund to the leader is unchanged — it compensates the creation
  cost and is independent of the bank.
- The balance is **distributed pro-rata by net contribution**, computed from the
  ledger. It is neither forfeited nor paid to the leader.
- The confirmation prompt must state the current balance and that it will be
  distributed this way, so the leader is not destroying or redirecting other
  members' money unknowingly.
- **Deletion is immediate.** There is no hold or countdown; distribution runs as
  part of the deletion, and members learn of it from their payout.

### Why there is no deletion hold

An earlier draft had a 300-second broadcast-and-hold. It existed because the
balance was originally **forfeited** — a last chance for withdraw-capable members
to rescue funds before they were destroyed. Pro-rata distribution removed that
justification entirely: contributors receive their share automatically.

Left in place, it would have actively **created an arbitrage**. Because negative
nets are clamped to zero, total claims are always at least the balance, so a
pro-rata share is *diluted* relative to net contribution — while a withdrawal
converts at 1:1:

> Balance 900. A net +800, B net −200, C net +300; total claims 1100.
> A's share is `900 × 800/1100` = **654**.
> If A first withdraws 200: balance 700, A net +600, claims 900.
> A's share is `700 × 600/900` = 466, plus the 200 already taken = **666**.

A profits by draining first, and only members already holding `bank.withdraw`
can do it.

**Removing the hold narrows this risk to its irreducible case; it does not
close it.** What a hold specifically enables is a **third party** reacting to
an *announced, pending* distribution — that is the window a broadcast-and-hold
opens, and that is what dropping the hold removes. It does not touch the actor
who unilaterally controls the timing of deletion itself: a Leader (or an
Officer, who can also withdraw) can always withdraw first and delete
immediately after, with no broadcast, no hold, and no window for anyone to
react to. Nothing in this module — with or without a hold — stops that,
because the actor's own decision to delete *is* the trigger; there is nothing
to race.

This is the same class of risk as **bank-drain-before-leaving**, above: not
mechanically preventable while withdrawal is instant and the withdrawer
controls their own timing. The control is the same, too — attribution.
A small, named, logged withdrawer set (the ledger) makes the drain-then-delete
sequence investigable and bannable after the fact, even though nothing stops
it beforehand. **This residual risk is a moderation/community-management
concern, not an engineering one** — ongoing monitoring for the pattern (a
withdrawal immediately followed by deletion) is a call for whoever owns
community management, not something this module's design can close by adding
more mechanism.

**Do not reintroduce a hold to try to close it.** A hold does not touch the
self-serving case above — the actor doesn't need the broadcast window, since
they already know deletion is coming — and it reopens the third-party-reacts
arbitrage this section exists to avoid. Any window between confirmation and
distribution reopens that arbitrage unless the bank is frozen for its
duration, which is the trade the earlier draft made and this design rejects.

The remaining safeguard against the third-party case is the type-the-clan-name
confirmation, which is the standard pattern for irreversible destructive
actions and does not have this problem.

### Distribution formula

For every SteamID appearing in this clan's ledger:

```
net_i        = Σ(deposits_i) − Σ(withdrawals_i + reclaims_i)
claim_i      = max(net_i, 0)
total_claims = Σ(claim_i)
share_i      = floor(balance × claim_i / total_claims)
```

| Symbol | Type | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `net_i` | int | unbounded | Net contribution; may be negative for a net withdrawer |
| `claim_i` | int | ≥ 0 | Net contribution clamped at zero |
| `total_claims` | int | ≥ 0 | Sum of all positive claims |
| `balance` | int | ≥ 0 | Funds remaining at dissolution |
| `share_i` | int | ≥ 0 | Amount paid to this SteamID |

Rules that must be explicit or two implementations will differ:

- **Negative net is clamped to zero.** A member who withdrew more than they
  deposited receives nothing, and never owes anything.
- **If `total_claims` is zero**, fall back to equal distribution among everyone
  with at least one deposit entry and a net of zero. If no such participant
  exists, the entire balance goes to the leader.

  **This branch should be unreachable.** Under event sourcing the balance *is*
  the sum of all deltas, so if every net is at most zero the balance is also at
  most zero and there is nothing to distribute. Reaching it means the ledger and
  the cached balance have diverged, or funds entered outside the ledger.
  Therefore: **log at Error and alarm before applying the fallback**, and
  reconcile from the ledger first in case the balance itself is wrong. Treat the
  rule as damage limitation, not routine behaviour. It also avoids a division by
  zero.
- **Shares are floored; the remainder is discarded.** It is at most one unit per
  claimant and not worth the complexity of a distribution rule.
- **Everyone in the ledger is included, not only current members.** Someone who
  deposited and later left or was kicked still contributed the money. This also
  removes the incentive to kick members before dissolving. Worth confirming — see
  open question 6.
- **The ledger is not deleted with the clan.** It is the audit record and the
  input to this calculation; deleting it would make the distribution
  unverifiable.

### Payout delivery

| Recipient | Mechanism |
|---|---|
| Online | `GiveMoney` directly, followed by `SaveData` |
| Offline | Insert a `remote` row of a **new** type — see below |

**A new remote type is required.** The existing `pmoney` type is
moneypack-specific: it grants `50000 × qty` plus trading cards and stickers and
announces publicly. It cannot be reused.

The new handler should follow `pmoney`'s structure, which already implements the
behaviour needed:

- Return **without** calling `done()` when the player is offline, so the row
  stays `done = 0` and is retried until they connect. This is the offline
  delivery mechanism.
- Return without `done()` on `cityrp.remote.noSave` servers (`build`, `beta`,
  `beta2`, `event`) so a real server picks the row up instead.
- Require `IsValid(ply)` **and** `ply._Initialized` before granting.
- Call `SaveData()` after `GiveMoney` so the payout persists.
- Target `server = 'all'`. Do not hardcode server IDs — that is defect 5.

**Claim the row before granting**, not after: `UPDATE remote SET done = 1 WHERE
id = ? AND done = 0` and proceed only if one row was affected. The existing
grant-then-mark ordering leaves a window in which two pollers could both pay out.

## Open questions

| # | Question | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| ~~1~~ | ~~Does economy telemetry justify any fee?~~ | **Resolved — no fee.** Not a zero default awaiting evidence; the fee mechanism is not built. See [No deposit or withdrawal fee](#no-deposit-or-withdrawal-fee) |
| ~~2~~ | ~~Are 3 days / 3 members the right unlock gate?~~ | **Confirmed.** The unlock is a one-way latch and never relocks — see [The unlock is a one-way latch](#the-unlock-is-a-one-way-latch) |
| ~~3~~ | ~~No return path for a non-privileged depositor~~ | **Resolved** — three layers: a consent prompt on first deposit and after `consent_reprompt_days` of inactivity; a `self_reclaim_window` on your own deposits; and pro-rata distribution at dissolution |
| ~~4~~ | ~~Should per-rank withdrawal caps differ?~~ | **Resolved — no per-rank cap.** `per_withdrawal_cap` is global and `bank.withdraw` is a boolean, which takes the cap check out of SQL entirely |
| ~~5~~ | ~~Does `/salary`'s lack of an audit log need fixing alongside?~~ | **Tracked separately** as [#3004](https://github.com/limelight-development/cityrp2/issues/3004). Not blocking this module |
| ~~6~~ | ~~Pay out to former members at dissolution?~~ | **Resolved — everyone in the ledger.** Fairer, and it removes the incentive to kick members before dissolving |

topics.title: Clans — Core Module
topics.body:
# Clans — Core Module

Module 1. Owns clan identity, membership, the rank ladder, permissions, radio
and MOTD, and exposes the registration API every other module builds on.

> **Status**: In Design. See [design.md](design.md) for the module framework and
> [plan.md](plan.md) for rollout.

## Scope

Core is deliberately close to the existing feature set. It is *"your clan radio,
your rank system, general membership administration"* — the value of this module
is the framework and the correctness, not new mechanics.

In scope: identity (name, abbreviation, motto, description), MOTD, membership
lifecycle, ranks and permissions, clan radio, administration.
Out of scope: bank (Module 2), inventory, vehicles.
Retired: clan models — see [design.md](design.md#retiring-clan-models).

## Permission model

### Decision: hybrid capability registry

Permissions are declared by modules and stored per rank in a single generic
table. Each permission has a **kind** that determines how its value is
interpreted.

| Kind | Value domain | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `BOOLEAN` | `true` / `false` | Flat capability, not targeted at another member |
| `THRESHOLD` | `NULL` or a `rankid` | May act on any member at or below the referenced rank; `NULL` = no permission |
| `NUMERIC_LIMIT` | `NULL`, `-1`, or a non-negative number | Amount-gated capability; `-1` = unlimited, `NULL` = no permission |

`NUMERIC_LIMIT` is retained as a general-purpose utility kind, not to avoid a
migration — migrations are cheap here, so that would not be a reason. It earns
its place because "you may do this, up to N" is a recurring shape a future
inventory or vehicle module wanting per-rank quotas could use, rather than
reinventing it. Its `-1` sentinel is an in-band magic value in the same column
as real amounts; that is a known wart, tolerated because `NULL` already carries
the "no permission" case cleanly.

> `bank.withdraw` does **not** use this kind — see
> [bank.md](bank.md#rank-gating): the per-transaction cap is a single global
> config value, not a per-rank quota, so `bank.withdraw` is `BOOLEAN`.
> `NUMERIC_LIMIT` currently has no consumer; revisit if nothing claims it by
> the time Core ships.

This keeps the genuinely good idea in the legacy model — seniority-scoped
authority, "you may only act on people below you" — while generalising it so any
module can use it for any targeted action, rather than it existing only for the
two actions someone hardcoded columns for.

`NULL` is the single "no permission" sentinel across all three kinds. This
resolves the legacy defect where `0` meant both "no permission" and, numerically,
"the most senior possible rank" — forcing an inconsistent special case at every
call site.

> **Decided.** The alternative considered was plain boolean capabilities plus a
> separate seniority ordinal and an explicit `is_leader` flag — simpler to reason
> about, but a boolean cannot express "kick, but only people junior to me"
> without a second mechanism bolted alongside it, and it cannot satisfy the hard
> requirement that a module declare its own permissions without a schema
> migration. Module extensibility is the point of the rebuild, so the hybrid
> wins. The rejected model's other recommendations — atomic leadership transfer,
> re-checking permission at commit time — are adopted and were compatible with
> either choice.

### Schema: `rankid` vs `rank_order`

The legacy `rankid` column conflates stable identity with seniority position.
Split it:

| Column | Stability | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `rankid` | Immutable, never reused | Foreign-key identity. Allocated from a per-clan monotonic counter (`clans.next_rankid`), never from array position |
| `rank_order` | Mutable, renumbered on structural change | Contiguous `1..N`, `1` = most senior. **The only column ever used for seniority comparison** |

`clan_ranks(clan, rankid, rank_order, rankname, ...)`,
PRIMARY KEY `(clan, rankid)`, **UNIQUE `(clan, rank_order)`**.

This makes the non-contiguous rank IDs already present in live data (`8`, `170`)
harmless: they are opaque identity and are never compared.

`THRESHOLD` stores a **rankid**, not a raw ordinal — so "may kick Lieutenant and
below" keeps meaning what the leader configured even if a new rank is later
inserted above Lieutenant.

Ranks are a **strict ladder** — one rank per position, no ties. Co-equal ranks
were considered and rejected: no clan has ever had them, the migration cannot
produce them (rankids are already distinct per clan, so backfilling `rank_order`
yields no ties), and they would have shipped with no users, an awkward two-part
invariant, and a documented expressiveness hole in threshold configuration.

Relaxing this later is one migration in the easy direction — dropping a unique
constraint — so nothing is foreclosed.

### Permission value column

`clan_rank_permissions.value` is **`INT NULL`**. This is not incidental.

`DB:QueryParams` binds every parameter as a **quoted string literal**
(`db.lua:239`) — there is no numeric binding path. Against an `INT` column MySQL
coerces the literal and comparisons stay numeric. Against a `VARCHAR` column
they become **lexicographic**, and `'9' > '10'` is true. Live clans already have
28 ranks, so ordinals above 9 are reachable today — a `VARCHAR` value column
would silently invert the threshold check for exactly the clans with the most
complex ladders.

All three kinds fit an integer: `BOOLEAN` as 0/1, `THRESHOLD` as a rankid,
`NUMERIC_LIMIT` as the amount. Do not use `VARCHAR` or JSON.

### Join rank

Each clan stores an explicit `clans.join_rankid` rather than deriving the join
rank from the ladder.

This removes the legacy defect where the join rank was whichever rank row
happened to be loaded last — a value derived from iteration order rather than
intent, which is how live data ended up with join ranks of `8` and `170`.
Deleting the designated join rank requires nominating a replacement, in the same
operation.

### Declaration format

A module registers each permission once at load time. Example shown with
`NUMERIC_LIMIT` since that kind's shape is the least obvious of the three —
`inventory.take_items` is hypothetical (inventory is a deferred future module,
not part of this rebuild), used here only to illustrate the kind, not because
it is being built:

```lua
{
    id      = "inventory.take_items", -- unique, "<module>.<name>"
    module  = "inventory",            -- must match the registering module
    label   = "Take items from clan inventory",
    kind    = NUMERIC_LIMIT,
    default = nil,                    -- fallback when no stored value exists
    unit    = "items_per_transaction",
}
```

`default` is resolved at read time, never materialised — this is what lets a
module installed after a clan already exists apply to every existing rank with
no migration.

**Resolution order** for any permission check:

1. Look up `(clan, rankid, permission_id)` in `clan_rank_permissions`.
2. If present, use it (type-checked against the declared `kind`).
3. Otherwise use the module's declared `default`.
4. If the permission is not registered by any loaded module, treat as `NULL` and
   log a warning via `cityrp.logging`. **Fail closed** — a disabled or renamed
   module must never result in a silent grant.

### Core permission set

| Permission | Kind | Gates | Leader | Officer | Lieutenant | Private | Recruit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `core.invite` | boolean | Invite a non-member | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ |
| `core.manage_invites` | boolean | Cancel pending invites | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ |
| `core.kick` | threshold | Remove a member | Officer | Lieutenant | Private | — | — |
| `core.setrank` | threshold | Change a member's rank | Officer | Lieutenant | — | — | — |
| `core.motd_edit` | boolean | Edit clan MOTD | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ |
| `core.edit_identity` | boolean | Edit name / abbreviation / motto / description | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ |
| `core.manage_ranks` | boolean | Create, rename, reorder, delete ranks; edit stored permission values | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ |
| `core.delete_clan` | boolean | Permanently delete the clan | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ |

`core.kick` and `core.setrank` are independent axes, not bundled — a Lieutenant
may remove a Private without being able to re-rank one.

**Intrinsic actions**, not stored permissions: *leadership transfer* is always
and only "whoever currently holds `rank_order = 1`". Storing it as configurable
data would allow a misconfiguration to hand leadership transfer to a non-leader.

### Inalienable permission

**Rank 1 permanently holds `core.manage_ranks`.** It cannot be revoked, and the
write path rejects any attempt to set it false on rank 1 regardless of who is
asking.

Without this, a leader can remove `core.manage_ranks` from their own rank and
lock the clan out of its own configuration permanently — recoverable only by
staff intervention.

`core.manage_ranks` is the **only** permission that needs this treatment. A
weaker rule such as "at least one rank must hold it" is insufficient, because
that rank may have no members — the invariant would hold while nobody could
actually use it, and guarding every membership change instead gets expensive.
Pinning it to rank 1 piggybacks on invariant 1, which already guarantees exactly
one member holds that rank.

Nothing else needs protecting, because `core.manage_ranks` is sufficient to
restore anything: a leader who removes `core.delete_clan` or
`core.edit_identity` from their own rank can grant it back. Those stay freely
editable.

Modules must not assume more than this. Core guarantees only that rank 1 can
always reach the permission editor; a module that can lock itself out through
its own permissions is a bug in that module.

> ⚠️ `core.manage_ranks` also gates editing a rank's *own* permission values,
> including `core.delete_clan`. Granting it to a non-Leader rank is effectively
> granting clan co-ownership. This is intentional, but the UI must warn the
> leader when enabling it for anyone else.

### Permission check formulas

**Threshold**

```
allowed = defined ∧ (ord_target ≥ ord_thresh) ∧ (ord_target > ord_actor)
```

| Symbol | Type | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `defined` | bool | — | Acting rank has a non-`NULL` value for this permission |
| `ord_actor` | int | 1..N | `rank_order` of the acting member's rank |
| `ord_target` | int | 1..N | `rank_order` of the target member's rank |
| `ord_thresh` | int | 1..N | `rank_order` of the rank referenced by the stored threshold |

Worked example — ladder Leader(1)/Officer(2)/Lieutenant(3)/Private(4)/Recruit(5),
Officer's `core.kick` = Lieutenant (ord 3):

- Officer kicks Private (4): `4≥3` ✓, `4>2` ✓ → **allowed**
- Officer kicks Lieutenant (3): `3≥3` ✓, `3>2` ✓ → **allowed** (boundary)
- Officer kicks another Officer (2): `2≥3` ✗ → **denied**
- Officer kicks Leader (1): `1≥3` ✗ → **denied**

Rank 1 needs no special case — its protection falls out of the ordering. Clause
three (`ord_target > ord_actor`) is what forbids acting on your own rank, and it
holds independently of how the threshold is configured.

**Numeric limit**

```
effective_cap = (L == -1) ? ∞ : L
allowed       = (L ≠ NULL) ∧ (A ≤ effective_cap)
```

Where `L` is the stored limit for the actor's rank and `A` is the requested
amount. The request is accepted or rejected whole — never silently clamped down
to the cap.

## In-game menu

The menu is the only clan management surface. See [ui.md](ui.md).

Accepting an invite from the no-clan screen re-validates at accept time: the clan
must still exist and the player must still be unaffiliated.

## Membership lifecycle

| Current state | Action | Actor requirement | Resulting state |
|---|---|---|---|
| None | Invite sent | `core.invite`; target holds no other membership | Invited |
| Invited | Cancelled or TTL expired | `core.manage_invites`, or system | None |
| Invited | Clan deleted | System (cascade) | None |
| Invited | Accepted | Self; re-validated: clan active **and** target still unaffiliated | Member (join rank) |
| Member | Promoted / demoted | `core.setrank`; both current and new rank must satisfy the threshold | Member (new rank) |
| Member | Kicked | `core.kick`; target rank must satisfy the threshold | None |
| Member (not sole leader) | Leaves | Self — no permission gate | None |
| Leader, others remain | Attempts to leave | Self | **Rejected** — must transfer leadership first |
| Leader + target member | Leadership transferred | Self, must hold `rank_order = 1` | Atomic swap of the two ranks |
| Leader, sole member | Leaves | Self | None, **and** clan deleted |
| Clan active | Deleted | `core.delete_clan` | Clan deleted; all members and invites cascade to None |

Leadership transfer must be a **single atomic statement**, not a demote followed
by a promote — two statements reopen a race window where a clan has zero or two
leaders.

## Edge cases

- **If the sole leader attempts to leave while members remain**: reject with
  "Transfer leadership before leaving". No auto-succession — it introduces a tie
  problem between same-rank members for no real benefit.
- **If someone attempts to demote the leader**: structurally unreachable. Rank 1
  has the minimum ordinal, and every threshold must reference a rank strictly
  junior to its owner, so no actor can satisfy `ord_target > ord_actor` against
  it. The only path to a new leader is leadership transfer.
- **If two officers simultaneously promote each other**: both rejected
  independently. An Officer's `setrank` threshold requires the *new* rank to also
  satisfy the threshold, and Officer is senior to that threshold — so no Officer
  can ever assign Officer or above. Structurally impossible, not a race to be
  locked against.
- **If a member is kicked while a bank withdrawal from them is in flight**: the
  withdrawal handler re-checks membership and permission **at commit time**,
  inside the same critical section as the ledger write. If the kick landed
  first, the withdrawal aborts and no funds move.
- **If a rank is deleted while members hold it**: rejected by default, reporting
  the holder count. Optionally accepts a `migrate_to` rankid, reassigning holders
  atomically before removal. `migrate_to` may not be rank 1.
- **If a permission references a deleted rank as its threshold target**: reset to
  `NULL`. Fail closed — never auto-widen to a neighbouring rank.
- **If rank IDs are non-contiguous**: harmless. `rankid` is opaque; only
  `rank_order` is compared, and it is contiguous by invariant.
- **If a player is invited while already in a clan**: rejected at send time, before
  any invite row is created. Re-checked again at accept time to close the race.
- **If a player accepts a stale invite to a deleted clan**: accept re-validates
  the clan is active, rejects, and deletes the stale row. Deletion should already
  cascade invites proactively; this is the defensive fallback.

## Invariants

| # | Invariant | Checkable condition | On violation in live data |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Exactly one leader per active clan | Exactly one member holds `rank_order = 1`, where `member_count > 0` | Flag for manual review. Do not auto-resolve silently; if unattended, keep oldest join timestamp and log every change |
| 2 | `rank_order` contiguous, unique, ≥2 ranks | `COUNT(*) = MAX(rank_order)` and `MAX ≥ 2` | Renumber by sorting on legacy `rankid`; synthesise a second rank if fewer than 2 survive |
| 2a | The join rank exists and is a real rank of this clan | `clans.join_rankid` resolves to a row in `clan_ranks` for the same clan | Backfill to the rank at `MAX(rank_order)`; log the choice |
| 2b | Permission values are integers and compared numerically | `clan_rank_permissions.value` is `INT NULL`; no comparison is ever performed on a string column | Fail the migration rather than proceeding — see [Permission value column](#permission-value-column) |
| 3 | One active membership per player | DB uniqueness on `clan_members.steamid` **plus** an application pre-check | Constraint already exists; only the pre-check is new |
| 4 | No threshold resolves to a rank at or above its owner | Resolve target `rank_order` > owner `rank_order` on every write and in a periodic sweep | Clamp to `owner_order + 1` and log |
| 4a | Rank 1 always holds `core.manage_ranks` | The stored value for `(clan, rank 1, 'core.manage_ranks')` is never false | Restore it and log — a clan in this state is locked out of its own configuration |
| 5 | Every stored permission key is registered and type-matched | Boot-time sweep after all modules register | Exclude orphans from checks (fail closed) and report — do not delete; the module may return |
| 6 | `rankid` unique and never reused per clan | Allocation from `clans.next_rankid` | Seed `next_rankid = MAX(rankid) + 1` per clan |
| 7 | No active clan has zero members | `COUNT(members) ≥ 1 OR state ≠ active` | Soft-delete zombie clans |
| 8 | Rank and member counts bounded | `2 ≤ rank_count ≤ 50`, `member_count ≤ 100` | Live maxima are 28 ranks and 18 members, so no clan is currently over cap. Grandfather any that appear; never truncate live rosters |
| 9 | Rank seed data never shared by reference | Code property — deep copy the seed template at clan creation | Covered by a unit test creating two clans and mutating one |

Invariant 9 is the fix for the legacy defect where all clans created in one
server session shared a single mutable ranks table.

## Identity field validation

Enforced identically at **every** entry point — creation, edit, game and web.
A rule applied at intake and skipped at update is not a rule.

| Field | Limit | Counted in | Charset | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Name | 3–32 | **characters** (128-byte ceiling) | Letters, digits, space, hyphen. No quotes or apostrophes | Trim and collapse whitespace; reject if no alphanumeric remains; reject case-insensitive collision with an existing clan |
| Abbreviation | 2–7 | **characters** (28-byte ceiling) | `[%a%d]` only | Renders inline on every member's name. Uppercase-normalise. Requires **both** reserved-word and prohibited-content screening — see below. **No column exists yet** |
| Motto | 0–80 | **characters** (320-byte ceiling) | Name charset plus `. , ! ? -` | Single line; strip newlines and chat colour codes |
| Description | 0–500 | **bytes** | Broad printable, multi-line | Total length only — no line-count or per-line cap |
| MOTD | 0–2000 | **bytes** | As Description | Total length only. If images are ever permitted, URLs **must** go through `cityrp.imageHosts` — there is exactly one allowlist |

**Short identity fields are character-counted; long-form fields are
byte-counted.** This split is deliberate, not an inconsistency:

- Name, abbreviation and motto are rendered inline in chat, on the scoreboard and
  above players' heads, so their *visible* length must be predictable. Counted
  via `utf8.len`, backed by a byte ceiling of 4× the character limit — the
  `utf8mb4` worst case — as defence in depth.
- Description and MOTD are long-form panel text where exact character counts
  matter far less than bounding storage and network payload predictably.

**Known consequence:** a byte-counted field gives less content in non-Latin
scripts — 500 bytes is roughly 250 Cyrillic or 166 CJK characters, and about 125
emoji. Acceptable for a predominantly English-speaking server, but it is a real
asymmetry and should be a deliberate choice rather than a discovered one.

Truncation must never split a codepoint. Validate and reject rather than
silently trimming.

**Because Description and MOTD have no line-structure limits, the renderer must
hard-wrap.** A single unbroken 2000-byte token with no whitespace is valid input,
so wrapping cannot rely on word boundaries — it must break on character
boundaries when no break opportunity exists, and the panel must clip or scroll
rather than expand. Responsibility for layout safety moves from validation to
rendering; it does not disappear.

Storage uses `DB_MAIN:QueryParams` exclusively — never concatenated `Run`.
Web rendering HTML-escapes at output time regardless of write-time validation,
because output encoding is what protects against data that entered by another
path.

### Schema is not a constraint

Gamemode migrations are cheap and routine here, so **design the schema the system
needs and migrate to it**. Do not contort the design to fit the existing tables,
and do not preserve a legacy column merely because it exists.

Concretely, this means: add `abbreviation varchar(7)` rather than repurposing
`short` (`varchar(2000)`, selected by `loadclan` but never used); drop
`clan_ranks.invite` / `kick` / `setrank` / `motd` / `forum` once
`clan_rank_permissions` replaces them; drop the dead `clan`, `clan_has_players`
and `clan_has_invite` tables; and size `name`, `motto` and `description` to the
limits below rather than inheriting `varchar(40)` / `varchar(70)`.

The one thing worth checking before dropping anything is whether it holds live
data worth keeping — `clans.short` in particular. That is a data-preservation
question at migration time, not a design constraint.

Similarly, `clan_members` should be keyed `(clan, steamid)` with a separate
unique constraint on `steamid` if one-clan-per-player is retained. The current
`PRIMARY KEY (steamid)` expresses the rule as a side effect of the key rather
than as an explicit constraint, which is why violations surface as duplicate-key
errors instead of clean rejections.

### Charset

Join keys and text fields need different charsets, and the split must be
deliberate.

| Column class | Charset | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Join keys — `clan_members.steamid`, `clan_invites.steamid`, ledger SteamIDs | **`latin1`, matching `players._SteamID`** | SteamIDs are ASCII. These columns are joined against `players` constantly, and a cross-charset comparison forces an implicit conversion that prevents index use and can raise `Illegal mix of collations` |
| Player-authored text — clan name, motto, description, MOTD | **`utf8mb4`** | Must accept non-ASCII names, and the character-count limits assume it |

**The clan tables migrate to match `players`, not the reverse.** `players` is
central and widely joined; migrating it is the larger, riskier change, and the
clan tables are small.

Note this makes fixing defect 8 insufficient on its own: `setleader`'s offline
path joins `players._SteamID` (`latin1`) to `clan_members.steamid` (`utf8`).
Correcting the `clan_member` → `clan_members` typo leaves a cross-charset join
behind it.

### Two different things called `_Clan`

`self._Clan` is the **numeric clan ID** set by the clans plugin
(`sv_player.lua:583` compares `self._Clan > 0`). `self.cityrp._Clan` is an
unrelated **free-text `latin1` string** defaulted from
`cityrp.configuration["Default Clan"]` and compared against `"none"`
(`sv_player.lua:1480`, `:1536`).

Two concepts, one name, distinguished only by whether the access goes through
`.cityrp`. Core's public API must not expose the raw `_Clan` field at all — use
named accessors, and treat any bare `_Clan` in existing code as ambiguous until
read in context.

### Prohibited content

Screening is provided by a shared library, `cityrp.wordfilter`, with **multiple
named categories** rather than one flat list. Categories differ in what they
protect against, who curates them, and which fields they apply to — merging them
makes all three worse.

| Category | Protects against | Example entries |
|---|---|---|
| `reserved` | Impersonating staff or the server | `admin`, `mod`, `staff`, `owner`, `limelight` |
| `slur` | Hate speech and targeted abuse | — curated by moderation |
| `profanity` | General swearing | — curated by moderation |

The set is extensible; other features will want categories clans does not.

**Category-to-field policy.** Each field declares which categories it rejects.
The distinction that matters is **consent**: a clan name and abbreviation are
broadcast to every player constantly and non-consensually, whereas a description
or MOTD is only seen by someone who opens it.

| Field | `reserved` | `slur` | `profanity` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Clan name | reject | reject | reject |
| Abbreviation | reject | reject | reject |
| Motto | — | reject | reject |
| Description | — | reject | allow |
| MOTD | — | reject | allow |

**Ownership is split.** Product owns this matrix — which categories gate which
fields is a policy call. Moderation owns the contents of each list. Neither
should be hardcoded by engineering.

The `reserved` category is load-bearing precisely because the abbreviation limit
moved to 7 characters: at 4 only `MOD` fitted, whereas `ADMIN`, `STAFF` and
`OWNER` all fit in 7.

Screening is necessary rather than sufficient, and should be specified honestly:

- **Normalise before matching**, or it is bypassed in seconds: casefold, strip
  separators and punctuation, fold leetspeak digits (`4`→`a`, `3`→`e`, `0`→`o`,
  `1`→`i`/`l`) and common homoglyphs. An unnormalised list stops nobody.
- **Match whole-field for the abbreviation**, substring for the longer free-text
  fields. Substring matching on short fields produces false positives — the
  classic case being innocuous words that contain a blocked substring — and a
  2–7 character field has too little context to disambiguate.
- **No list is complete.** The real backstop is player reporting plus staff
  action, which requires a **staff force-rename / force-retag tool**. A clan that
  slips through must be fixable without deleting it and refunding it. This tool
  is a hard requirement of shipping the feature, not a nice-to-have.

**`cityrp.wordfilter` is a gamemode library, not part of the clans module.** No
profanity or slur filter currently exists anywhere in the gamemode, so this is
the first — which makes it the moment to centralise. Clan names, abbreviations,
mottos, descriptions and MOTDs all need it, and so will the next feature that
accepts player-authored text. This codebase already has a documented incident
where the same allowlist was independently copied into four places and drifted
apart; one library consumed by clans avoids repeating it.

Clans is its first consumer, so the library ships in Phase 1 — but it should be
designed for the gamemode, not for clans.

## Open decisions

| # | Decision | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|
| ~~1~~ | ~~Hybrid capability registry vs. plain booleans~~ | **Resolved — hybrid.** See [Permission model](#permission-model) |
| ~~2~~ | ~~`MAX_RANKS` and `MAX_MEMBERS` values~~ | **Resolved — 50 ranks, 100 members.** Live maxima are 28 and 18; these are abuse backstops with headroom, not design targets |
| ~~3~~ | ~~Whether `core.manage_ranks` should be delegable~~ | **Resolved — keep delegable**, with a UI warning when a leader grants it to another rank |
| ~~4~~ | ~~Reserved abbreviation list~~ | **Resolved — two separate screens**: reserved words for staff impersonation, prohibited terms for slurs, both via a shared library. See [Prohibited content](#prohibited-content) |
| ~~5~~ | ~~How the UI presents tiers containing several ranks~~ | **Moot** — co-equal ranks were scrapped, so a plain ordered list is correct. The menu route is in [ui.md](ui.md) |
| ~~6~~ | ~~What `clans.short` actually holds~~ | **Resolved as a design question — migrations are cheap, so design the schema needed.** Remains a data-preservation check at migration time only |
| ~~7~~ | ~~Curation of the word lists~~ | **Resolved — split ownership.** Product owns the category-to-field matrix; moderation owns list contents. See [Prohibited content](#prohibited-content) |
