topics.body:
# Clans

Clans are player-formed groups with a shared identity, a rank ladder, and
group-scoped features. This document specifies the **modular architecture** the
system is being rebuilt onto, and indexes the per-module design documents.

> **Status**: In Design — not yet implemented.
> The system described here replaces the legacy implementation in
> `core/plugins/clans/`. See [plan.md](plan.md) for migration and rollout.

## Design principle: modules, not a monolith

The legacy system put membership, ranks, radio, models and administration into a
single 700-line server file with a companion PHP website writing to the same
tables. Every new clan feature was added by extending that file, and the two
surfaces drifted apart.

The rebuild inverts this. A small **core** owns clan identity, membership and
ranks, and exposes a registration API. Everything else — bank, inventory,
vehicles — is a **module** that registers against the core and owns its own
tables, permissions, UI tab and commands.

The organising unit is the *activity a clan does together*, not the code that
happens to implement it.

### Why

- Modules ship independently. Core can go live before the bank is designed.
- A module's failure is contained; a broken bank must not prevent clan chat.
- Permissions, UI and persistence follow one declared pattern per module rather
  than being reinvented each time.
- Horizon features (inventory, vehicles) get a defined seam to land against
  instead of requiring core surgery.

## Module registry

| Module | Scope | Status | Design |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Core** | Identity, membership, ranks, radio, MOTD, administration | In design | [core.md](core.md) |
| **Bank** | Shared clan funds — deposits, rank-gated withdrawals, audit ledger | In design | [bank.md](bank.md) |

The in-game menu, the only management surface, is specified in [ui.md](ui.md).
| Inventory | Shared item storage (ammunition, weapons, food) | Deferred | — |
| Vehicles | Shared vehicles, callsigns, rank-gated access | Deferred | — |
| ~~Models~~ | Clan-restricted player models | **Retired** — see below | — |

Deferred modules are **not** designed here. They are listed so the framework can
be validated against their known requirements.

### Retiring clan models

`/clan model` is removed rather than ported. Clan activity is currently minimal,
the model files remain as game content and can be spawned manually if needed, and
the feature carries two of the legacy defects on its own (the shared
`clanskinchanger` timer name and an unguarded nil index).

**Retirement is fail-closed.** Two independent paths exist today:

- `/clan model` calls `player:SetModel()` directly, bypassing validation entirely
  and relying on its own lookup.
- `loadclan` calls `cityrp.model.register(path, fn)` so clan models also appear
  in the normal model-change flow.

`cityrp.model` is an allowlist whose `access()` returns `false` by default, and
the consumer rejects any model absent from the registry
(`metatables/sv_player.lua:1292`). Removing the registration therefore makes
clan models *unavailable*, not *unrestricted* — there is no risk of leaking
clan-exclusive models to all players.

Retiring also moots the "grants access to `/clan model`" element of `/clan
shift` (#1327), which is separately deferred.

## Framework contract

A module declares itself to Core at load time. Core validates the declaration
and owns all shared state; modules own only their own tables.

### Registration validation

| Rule | Why |
|---|---|
| Permission keys must be prefixed with the module's own id (`bank.withdraw`, never `can_kick`) | Prevents a module silently overwriting a Core permission while adding its own |
| Declared tables must be prefixed (`clan_bank_*`) and checked for collision at registration | Same, for persistence |
| A second registration of the same module id is rejected or no-ops | Duplicate registration on hot reload is a documented recurring bug class in this codebase |
| Each module's init runs inside `pcall` | On failure the module is marked inert and logged via `cityrp.logging`; Core and sibling modules continue |

The `pcall` rule is what makes "a broken bank must not prevent clan chat" true
rather than aspirational.

### State access

Modules read membership, rank and permission state **only** through Core
accessors — never by indexing Core's tables or querying `clan_members` /
`clan_ranks` directly. Only Core writes those tables.

**Accessors must return copies or read-only views, never live references.** This
is not hypothetical: the legacy code already assigns `ranks =
cityrp.clans.defaultranks` by reference (defect 6 below), so every clan created in
a session shares one mutable table. In a modular system that same mistake becomes
a cross-module privilege bug — a module mutating what it believes is its own copy
would corrupt Core's live permission state for every clan at once.

**No caching of permission results.** Modules call `hasPermission` fresh per
action. A cached "this player may withdraw" survives a demotion and reopens the
ordering attack the atomic-write pattern exists to close. Bank-action volume is
low enough that this costs nothing. If a future module genuinely needs caching,
Core must expose a synchronous `onRankChanged` hook and subscription must be
mandatory, not optional.

### Honest limit

Lua modules cannot be sandboxed from each other at runtime — any module has full
VM access and could bypass all of the above. These rules are API discipline
backed by review, not enforcement. A mechanical grep for `DB_MAIN` queries
against `clan_members` / `clan_ranks` outside Core is a cheap review check, and
belongs in CI rather than in a reviewer's head.

### Correctness rules for every module

**Re-validate players inside async callbacks, never before.** Every operation
here is an async database round trip followed by a player notification, and the
player can disconnect in between. Check `IsValid(ply)` **and** `ply._Initialized`
*inside* the callback. This is the exact misunderstanding behind defect 2, and it
is the defect most likely to recur, because it is a language-level trap rather
than a clan-specific bug.

Critically: **the state mutation, the ledger write and any `remote` row happen
regardless of player validity.** Only the notification is conditional. Money must
not fail to move because the actor closed the game between the statement and the
message.

**Explain rejections with a separate diagnostic read.** The conditional statement
returns only an affected-row count, so "rejected" carries no reason. Do not
surface that to players — today they get *"You do not have the ability to kick a
player with that rank"*, and losing it is a real supportability regression for
them and for staff. On a zero-row result, run a **non-authoritative diagnostic
`SELECT`** purely to produce the message. The `UPDATE` remains the only thing
that grants; the `SELECT` only explains, and runs on the failure path only.

There is nothing confidential to protect here — clan members can read the entire
rank ladder in the UI.

**Hot reload: declarations replace, side effects guard.** Re-registering a module
must replace its permission declarations, so new code takes effect during
development. Anything with a side effect — timers, hooks, net strings, commands —
must guard against double registration instead. "Rejected or no-ops" is not a
specification; these two halves need opposite behaviour.

## Surfaces

The in-game menu is the only surface in scope. **The companion web app is out of
scope and its repository is disabled** — it is neither being rebuilt nor
maintained as part of this work, and the `?dev=true` escalation it carried is not
reachable while it is offline.

The rest of this section records the constraints that apply *if* a web surface
returns. It is deliberately retained rather than deleted, because the conclusions
were expensive to reach and the failure modes recur.

### Constraint: there is no in-game API to call

A Garry's Mod server can make outbound HTTP requests but cannot host an inbound
listener. The web app therefore **cannot call into the game server**, and clan
modification cannot be funnelled through a single Lua implementation. The web
app must implement its own write path against the database.

This means the authorisation logic exists **twice**, in two languages. That is
not ideal and cannot be designed away — but it can be managed, and drift between
the two copies is precisely what produced the `?dev=true` escalation and the
dead `motd` / `forum` permission columns.

### The authorisation boundary is the SQL statement

Rather than a single *implementation*, the design uses a single *statement*.
Every mutating action is expressed as one parameterised conditional `UPDATE`
whose `WHERE` clause carries the entire permission check. Both surfaces issue
the same statement; neither can grant more than the statement permits, because
neither evaluates the permission in its host language at all.

The threshold formula is fully expressible as SQL predicates — the actor's rank,
the target's rank and the stored threshold are three joins and two comparisons.
See [core.md](core.md#permission-check-formulas) for the formulas and
[bank.md](bank.md#withdrawals-must-be-a-single-atomic-statement) for the worked
withdrawal case.

Consequences:

- **The canonical statements are a specification artifact.** They belong in this
  documentation and, ideally, in a shared `.sql` file both surfaces load rather
  than two hand-copied strings. Duplicated string literals across a
  language boundary are a known recurring defect class in this codebase.
- **Affected-row count is the only success signal.** Zero rows means rejected,
  for any reason. Neither surface reports *which* reason.
- **Stored procedures are the stronger form** — one definition in the database,
  called by both. Recommended if the team is willing to take on the deployment
  and migration overhead; the shared-statement approach is the fallback if not.

### Rules that still hold on both surfaces

- **Identity** comes only from what the transport authenticated — the server-side
  `Player` object in game, the Steam OpenID session on web. Never a SteamID or
  rank read from a request body or query string.
- **No "already authorised" assertion is ever accepted** from a client. This is
  the general form of the `?dev=true` bug and must not recur on either surface.
- **No permission bypass flag may exist at all** — no debug mode, no sudo
  parameter, no environment toggle that skips a check. If a developer override is
  genuinely needed, it belongs behind the existing staff admin system, not a
  parallel one.
- **Rendered UI is not authorisation.** Disabling a control in the page is a
  usability affordance; the statement is the control.

### Keeping the two implementations honest

- **Permission declarations are data, not code.** The registry (id, kind,
  default) lives in the database so both surfaces read the same definitions
  rather than each hardcoding a list. Adding a module's permissions must not
  require a PHP change.
- **A shared conformance fixture set** — a rank ladder, stored permission values,
  and a table of (actor rank, action, target rank) → expected allow/deny — that
  both implementations are tested against. This is the practical anti-drift
  control; without it, the two copies will diverge again.

### In-memory state remains game-authoritative

The game server caches clan state in memory. Any web write must therefore
notify the affected servers to reload — see
[Replacing the `remote` channel](#replacing-the-remote-channel). Today that
notification is broken in three separate ways (defects 3, 4 and 5), which is why
web edits appear not to take effect until a map change.

## Current state

This section records what exists today and why it is being replaced. It is
evidence for the rebuild, not a specification.

### What is implemented

- `core/plugins/clans/sv_init.lua` — chat commands `/clan
  create|undo|delete|invite|uninvite|accept|decline|kick|setrank|setleader|leave|info|model`
  and `/cradio`, plus the `!updateclans` staff command.
- `core/derma/cl_clans.lua` — the in-game clan panel. It renders a background
  image and the text `"Coming soon..."`. There is no in-game clan UI.
- An external PHP site (`services/clan`) providing Clan Info, Commands, Rank
  Manager, User Management and Invites. It writes directly to the shared MySQL
  database and signals game servers by inserting rows into the `remote` table.

### Confirmed defects

These are root causes, each verified against code and, where noted, against an
open issue.

| # | Defect | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `clan_members` is `PRIMARY KEY (steamid)`; `/clan accept` does not check existing membership, and the failed `INSERT` is not error-checked — the code sets `_Clan` and announces success regardless | A player already in a clan appears to join a new one, then reverts to the old clan on reconnect. **Root cause of issues #464, #336, #713** |
| 2 | `cityrp.clans.kick` and `.setrank` `return` from inside the async DB callback, so they always return `nil` to their caller | The `if(kick)` / `if(setrank)` follow-up blocks never execute; a kicked or promoted player's live state is never updated |
| 3 | `!updateclans` names its callback parameter `results` but reads `result` | The command clears `cityrp.clans.clans` and reloads nothing — the documented recovery path wipes state |
| 4 | `deleteclan` remote handler compares `row.value1` (string) against `_Clan` (number), and `return`s without calling `done()` when the actor is offline | Clears no members; the row is retried every 60s indefinitely |
| 5 | In-game `/clan delete` inserts `deleteclan` rows hardcoded for `v2d`, `v33x`, `v4b1`. Live is **`v4b1_fl2`**, a distinct `LLServer` value, and `cityrp.remote.check()` matches on exact string equality | Live has **never** received a `deleteclan` notification. `v4b1` ≠ `v4b1_fl2` |
| 6 | New clans assign `ranks = cityrp.clans.defaultranks` **by reference** | All clans created in one server session share one mutable ranks table |
| 7 | `loadclan` selects only `rankid, rankname, invite, kick, setrank` | The `motd` and `forum` permission columns are editable on the web but gate nothing in game |
| 8 | `setleader` for an offline target queries `INNER JOIN clan_member` (table is `clan_members`) | The offline path always fails with a SQL error |
| 9 | `timer.Create("clanskinchanger", ...)` uses a fixed global timer name | Two players changing models concurrently collide; the second cancels the first |
| 10 | `/clan info` and `/clan model` index `cityrp.clans.clans[player._Clan]` without a nil guard | Runtime error for players not in a clan, or for unloaded clans |
| 11 | `reloadclan` and `deleteclan` both open `if not cityrp.clans then done() end` — **no `return`**. Execution falls through and immediately indexes `cityrp.clans.lastreload` | The guard marks the row done and then errors on the next line. In `sv_remote.lua`, so it survives the rebuild — Phase 0 work, not throwaway |
| 12 | `cityrp.model.register` appends a new condition closure on every `loadclan`, growing `conds` unboundedly across reloads; `cityrp.model.remove` calls `table.RemoveByValue` on a key-indexed table and is a silent no-op | Model retirement moots the clans half, but the `remove` bug affects every other consumer, and the append is the same duplicate-registration class the framework guards against |

### Web app security

The companion site derives its `devmode` flag from `$_GET["dev"]`, and `devmode`
is the bypass condition on the leader-only rank manager, the kick permission
check and the rank-ceiling check. Any authenticated member can obtain full clan
leader authority by appending `?dev=true`.

This is being tracked and fixed independently of the rebuild — it must not wait
on this design. See [plan.md](plan.md).

### Dormant schema

Present in the database with no implementation. Listed because the rebuild
should either use or drop each one, not inherit them silently.

- `clans.bank` — adopted by the Bank module.
- `clans.motto`, `clan.description`, `clan.abb` — adopted by Core identity.
- `clans._Inventory` — reserved for the deferred Inventory module.
- `clan_vehicles` — full table, reserved for the deferred Vehicles module.
- `clan_ranks.forum` — web-only permission; the web app is out of scope.
- `clan_models` and `clans.model` — become dead once `/clan model` is retired.
- `clan` (singular), `clan_has_players`, `clan_has_invite` — dead duplicates of
  `clans`, `clan_members`, `clan_invites`. Candidates for removal.

## Player fantasy

[To be designed.]

## Ranks and permissions

Specified in [core.md](core.md#permission-model).

## Membership lifecycle

Specified in [core.md](core.md#membership-lifecycle).

## Security model

Trust boundaries are in [Surfaces](#surfaces); module isolation is in
[Framework contract](#framework-contract). Per-module controls are in
[core.md](core.md) and [bank.md](bank.md#correctness-and-security-requirements).

### Replacing the `remote` channel

`remote` is currently an **unauthenticated command channel**. `cityrp.remote.check()`
polls every 60 seconds and executes whatever row it finds — `kick`, `deleteclan`,
`money_give`, and `announceupdate` (which reaches the server console). Anything
with `INSERT` rights on that table can command every game server it targets, and
a game server cannot distinguish a real web-app row from any other writer's.

With the web app out of scope, `remote` is **not needed as a command channel for
clans at all**. Its only remaining clan job is cache invalidation between game
servers, which share one database and each cache clan state in memory: "clan N
changed, reload it."

Narrow it accordingly:

- Clan use of `remote` reduces to a single idempotent, side-effect-free type
  (`reloadclan`). Reloading a clan the caller has no authority over leaks nothing
  and changes nothing, so the unauthenticated-channel risk largely evaporates for
  this use.
- **Do not** add clan mutation types (`kickmember`, `setrank`, …) to `remote`.
  A row that performs a privileged action on behalf of an unauthenticated writer
  is the exact shape of the existing problem.
- The dangerous existing types (`kick`, `money_give`, `deleteclan`) are outside
  this rebuild's scope but should be tracked separately — a compromised or
  over-granted DB account can still drive them.
- Fix the hardcoded server list (defect 5) and the missing `done()` / string-vs-
  number comparison in the handler (defect 4), or reload notifications will keep
  silently failing.

**One row per server, from configuration — not `server = 'all'`.** This is
counter-intuitive and worth stating precisely, because the obvious fix is wrong.

`cityrp.remote.check()` selects `WHERE done = 0 AND (server = 'all' OR server =
<this server>)`, and `checkRow` hands the handler a `done` closure that runs
`UPDATE remote SET done = 1 WHERE id = <id>` — marking the single row done for
everyone. A `server = 'all'` row is therefore consumed by **whichever server
polls first**, and no other server ever sees it. That is correct for a
*filtered* action targeting one server, and wrong for *fan-out* — and cache
invalidation is fan-out.

The legacy `/clan delete` writing one row per server was structurally right. Its
defect is that the list is three literals (`v2d`, `v33x`, `v4b1`) while live runs
as `v4b1_fl2`, matched by exact string equality, so live never matched any of
them.

Write one row per server, with the server list **derived from configuration**.
Never from literals in a command handler.

## Data model

[To be designed — tables retained, retired, and migrations required.]

## Edge cases

[To be designed.]

## Dependencies

[To be designed.]

## Tuning knobs

[To be designed.]

## Acceptance criteria

See [acceptance-criteria.md](acceptance-criteria.md) — permission formulas,
invariants, membership lifecycle, identity validation, the bank module, and
regression criteria for all twelve defects.

## Open questions

| # | Question | Owner | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| ~~1~~ | ~~Are clan models still wanted?~~ | — | **Resolved — retire the command.** Model files stay as game content and can be spawned manually. Clan activity is minimal, so player impact is low. See [Retiring clan models](#retiring-clan-models) |
| 2 | Should the module framework support third-party/addon modules, or core-only? | — | Affects how defensive the registration API must be |
| 3 | Player suggestions were referenced in planning but not yet reviewed | — | A set of clan suggestions exists that has not been passed through; they may add requirements |
| ~~4~~ | ~~Does `/clan shift` (#1327) belong to Core or its own module?~~ | — | **Resolved — out of scope.** Comes later as a Core rework. It is essentially an additional gate on command execution, so it retrofits cleanly and does not need a seam reserved for it now |
| 5 | ~~Should the one-clan-per-player rule be enforced in logic rather than by primary key?~~ | — | **Resolved**: enforce in application logic before the write, at both invite-send and invite-accept; keep the primary key as defence in depth. See [core.md](core.md#invariants) invariant 3 |
| 6 | ~~Permission model: hybrid capability registry, or plain booleans plus a seniority ordinal?~~ | — | **Resolved**: hybrid capability registry, for module extensibility. See [core.md](core.md#permission-model) |
| ~~7~~ | ~~How should UI present a tier containing several co-equal ranks?~~ | — | **Moot — co-equal ranks were scrapped.** Ranks are a strict ladder, so a plain ordered list is correct |
| ~~8~~ | ~~Concrete values missing for byte ceilings, rate limit and line caps~~ | — | **Resolved.** Byte ceilings are 4× the character limit; Description and MOTD are byte-counted with no line caps; bank cooldown is 10s per player; `MAX_TRANSACTION` proposed at $100,000,000 |
| ~~9~~ | ~~Does the ledger write share a transaction with the balance mutation?~~ | — | **Moot.** The ledger insert is now the authoritative write and the cache is a fire-and-forget derived value, so no transaction is needed. See [bank.md](bank.md#the-ledger-is-authoritative--event-sourcing) |

## References

- Issue #1418 — Clan/Business Account (source suggestion for the Bank module)
- Issue #1541 — In-game F1 Clan Menu (player demand for an in-game surface)
- Issue #1624 — Clan Inventory (deferred module requirements)
- Issue #1327 — `/clan shift`
- Issue #1318 — Team/Clan/Private Radio Overhaul (affects Core radio)
- Issues #464, #336, #713 — membership persistence failures (defect 1 above)
- Issue #1892 — Clan System (tracking issue, currently empty)

topics.title: Clans Overhaul — Plan
topics.body:
# Clans Overhaul — Plan

Delivery plan for the modular clans rebuild specified in [design.md](design.md).

Phase numbers match module numbers: Phase 1 delivers Module 1 (Core), Phase 2
delivers Module 2 (Bank).

> **Status**: Draft. Phase 0 is independent of the rebuild and should not wait on it.

## Scope boundary

The companion web app is **out of scope** — its repository is disabled. Nothing
in this plan depends on it, and no phase includes work on it. See
[Deferred](#deferred) for what that leaves unresolved.

## Phase 0 — Hotfixes (do not wait on this design)

Live defects, all game-side. Listed here for traceability but they should ship as
ordinary fixes as soon as they are reviewed.

| Priority | Fix | Where |
|---|---|---|
| **High** | `/clan accept` does not reject players already in a clan, and does not check the `INSERT` result before declaring success. The insert fails on the `clan_members` primary key, but in-memory state is set and success is announced anyway — so the player reverts to their old clan on reconnect | `clans/sv_init.lua` |
| **High** | `!updateclans` reads `result` from a callback parameter named `results`, wiping clan state and reloading nothing — the documented recovery path is broken | `clans/sv_init.lua` |
| **High** | `cityrp.clans.kick` and `.setrank` return from inside the async DB callback, so they always return `nil`; the permission-dependent follow-up never runs and live state is not updated | `clans/sv_init.lua` |
| Medium | `deleteclan` rows are hardcoded to `v2d`/`v33x`/`v4b1`. Live is `v4b1_fl2`, matched by exact string equality, so live never receives them | `clans/sv_init.lua` |
| Medium | `deleteclan` handler compares `row.value1` (string) to `_Clan` (number) and can return without calling `done()`, causing infinite 60s retries | `libraries/sv_remote.lua` |
| Medium | `reloadclan` and `deleteclan` both open `if not cityrp.clans then done() end` with **no `return`** — the guard marks the row done, then errors on the next line | `libraries/sv_remote.lua` |
| Low | `cityrp.model.remove` calls `table.RemoveByValue` on a key-indexed table and silently does nothing; affects every model consumer, not just clans | `libraries/sv_model.lua` |

The two `sv_remote.lua` fixes and the `sv_model.lua` fix are **not throwaway** —
those files survive the rebuild. The `clans/sv_init.lua` fixes are throwaway,
since that file is being replaced.
| Medium | `setleader` offline path joins `clan_member` instead of `clan_members` | `clans/sv_init.lua` |
| Low | `/clan info` indexes `cityrp.clans.clans[player._Clan]` with no nil guard | `clans/sv_init.lua` |

The `clanskinchanger` shared-timer collision and the `/clan model` nil index are
deliberately **not** listed — that command is being retired in Phase 1, so fixing
it first would be wasted work.

Phase 0 does not attempt to fix the architecture. It stops the bleeding.

## Phase 1a — Word filter and staff force-rename tool

Pulled out of Phase 1 and run first (or in parallel with Phase 1 Steps 1–3,
below). Two architecture decisions shape this plan and are not re-litigated
here: **Step 2 of Phase 1 builds `core.kick` as a vertical slice before the
rest of Core**, and **this word-filter/force-rename work is split into its own
Phase 1a** because it sits on the moderation-policy dependency that blocks
other people's work — pulling it forward unblocks their critical path, and
because it does not depend on any clans-specific schema or framework code,
there is no reason to make it wait on Phase 1's sequencing.

1. **`cityrp.wordfilter` gamemode library** (`gamemode/core/libraries/`, not
   under `clans/`). Multiple named categories (`reserved`, `slur`,
   `profanity`), each independently curated and independently
   enabled/disabled per call site. Normalisation pipeline: casefold, strip
   separators/punctuation, fold leetspeak digits (`4→a`, `3→e`, `0→o`,
   `1→i`/`l`), fold common homoglyphs. Two match modes: whole-field (for short
   fields like the abbreviation) and substring (for longer free-text). This is
   the first consumer-agnostic profanity/slur filter in the gamemode — no
   equivalent exists today anywhere, which is exactly why it is being built as
   a shared library instead of inline in `clans/`, matching the existing
   allowlist-drift lesson from [image hosts](../../image-hosts.md) (AGENTS.md
   footgun #9 — this is the same failure shape: one allowlist copied into
   several call sites and drifting apart).
   List *contents* are owned by moderation; the category-to-field policy
   matrix is a product decision made per-consumer (clans' matrix is in
   [core.md](core.md#prohibited-content)) — the library itself ships with
   empty or seed lists and does not hardcode either.
2. **Staff force-rename / force-retag tool.** Registered via
   `cityrp.acommands.AddCommand` — this is a staff tool and belongs on `!`,
   never on `/` with a restricted access flag (AGENTS.md footgun #14). Needs a
   category, a syntax string, and a tip per the acommands contract. Scope:
   rename and re-tag (abbreviation) a clan without deleting or refunding it,
   bypassing the normal `core.edit_identity` gate and the collision/word-filter
   screens that would otherwise apply to the *offending* value (the new value
   staff choose still goes through validation and the word filter — only the
   requirement that the *acting player* hold `core.edit_identity` is bypassed).
   Logged via `cityrp.logs.add()` as an admin action, independent of the audit
   trail conventions Bank uses for money (footgun #8 — don't conflate the two
   logging APIs).
3. **No clan-specific work lands here.** This phase produces a library and a
   staff tool usable by any future feature, not clan schema or clan commands —
   Phase 1 Step 4 (below) is Core's *consumer* of this library, wired in once
   both are ready.

Dependency: Phase 1 Step 4 (identity field validation) cannot ship until this
phase's library exists — that is the one point where Phase 1 waits on Phase
1a. Everything else in Phase 1 is independent of it.

## Phase 1 — Core (Module 1)

Core **is** the framework. The module registration API and the base clan
feature set ship together — building the framework as a separate deliverable
with no modules attached would validate nothing. Per the architecture review,
the framework is proven against the smallest real permission check
(`core.kick`) before the rest of Core is built against imagination.

### Step 1 — Minimal framework skeleton

Just enough to register a module and declare a permission — not the full
membership/rank feature set.

- Module registration API: `id`, `pcall`-wrapped `init`, collision checks on
  both the module id prefix (`bank.withdraw`, never a bare `can_kick`) and any
  declared table prefix (`clan_bank_*`). Second registration of the same
  module id is rejected or no-ops — hot-reload duplicate registration is a
  recurring bug class here (AGENTS.md footgun #7), and the framework doc is
  explicit that "declarations replace, side effects guard" are *opposite*
  behaviours, not one rule.
- Permission registry: declaration format (`id`, `module`, `label`, `kind`,
  `default`, `unit`), the three `kind`s (`BOOLEAN`, `THRESHOLD`,
  `NUMERIC_LIMIT`), and the resolution order (stored value → declared default
  → fail-closed `NULL` with a `cityrp.logging` warning if nothing registers
  the id).
- Schema for this step only: `clan_ranks.rank_order` (`UNIQUE (clan,
  rank_order)`) alongside the existing `rankid`, and
  `clan_rank_permissions(clan, rankid, permission_id, value)` with **`value
  INT NULL`** — not `VARCHAR`. This is the direct fix for the `QueryParams`
  landmine: `DB:QueryParams` binds every parameter as a quoted string
  (`db.lua:239`), so a `VARCHAR` value column would compare lexicographically
  and invert threshold checks above rank 9 — live clans already have up to 28
  ranks, so this is reachable today, not a hypothetical.
- Core accessors (read-only copies/views, never live table references) for
  rank ordinals — the only thing `core.kick` needs to read.
- Nothing consumes any of this yet.

### Step 2 — Vertical slice: `core.kick`

Build one permission end to end before building the rest of Core. `core.kick`
is chosen because it is the smallest complete exercise of the full stack: a
`THRESHOLD` permission registry read, ordinal resolution
(`ord_target`/`ord_thresh`/`ord_actor`), one atomic SQL statement, and the
Core accessor layer — with no dependency on identity fields, radio, MOTD, or
the UI.

- Register `core.kick` (`THRESHOLD`) against the Step-1 registry.
- Implement the threshold formula server-side as a pure function: `allowed =
  defined ∧ (ord_target ≥ ord_thresh) ∧ (ord_target > ord_actor)`. The
  formula's boundary cases are enumerated in
  [acceptance-criteria.md](acceptance-criteria.md#threshold-formula) as a
  manual reference for reviewing the implementation — automated coverage is
  out of scope for this plan (GLuaTest is unconfigured in this repo; fixing
  that is tracked separately and not scheduled here).
- Implement the kick action as a single parameterised statement carrying the
  permission check in its `WHERE`/`EXISTS` clause (per
  [design.md](design.md#the-authorisation-boundary-is-the-sql-statement)) —
  not a Lua read-then-decide-then-write. Affected-row count is the only
  success signal; 0 rows means denied for any reason.
- On a 0-row result, run the separate **non-authoritative diagnostic `SELECT`**
  to produce a specific rejection message. The `UPDATE`/`DELETE` remains the
  only thing that grants.
- Re-validate `IsValid(ply)` **and** `ply._Initialized` *inside* the async DB
  callback, not before it (AGENTS.md footgun #2) — this is also the direct
  regression fix for defect 2, which returned from inside the callback and
  silently dropped the live-state update.
- The membership row deletion happens regardless of whether the kicked
  player's notification can be delivered; only the notification is
  conditional on `IsValid`.
- Landmine check specific to this slice: `clan_rank_permissions.value` must
  already be `INT` (from Step 1) before this statement is written, or the
  ordinal comparison silently inverts per the `QueryParams` landmine above —
  this is the concrete case that motivated the schema decision. Verify by hand
  against a clan with 10+ ranks before sign-off (mirrors acceptance criterion
  PERM-SQL1) — the bug is in how the ordinal reaches MySQL, not in the formula
  itself, so eyeballing the formula alone will not catch it.
- No UI in this step. Exercised via a direct call/console command for
  validation; the in-game menu's Roster `[Kick]` button wires into the same
  function in Step 5.

This step is the framework validation gate: if `core.kick` requires
reshaping the registration API, the accessor contract, or the statement
pattern, that reshaping happens here, once, before Step 3 builds nine more
actions against the same shape.

### Step 3 — Rest of membership lifecycle and rank management

Built against the now-validated Step 2 shape. Covers: invite, cancel invite,
accept (re-validated at accept time), leave (including the sole-leader
rejection), leadership transfer, `setrank`, rank CRUD (create, rename,
reorder, delete with optional `migrate_to`), and clan deletion (`core.delete_clan`,
cascading members and invites — Bank's distribution step is Phase 2, but the
cascade and the $25,000 refund path belong here).

- **Leadership transfer must be a single atomic statement**, not demote-then-
  promote — `db.lua` has no transaction API, so the only way to avoid a
  zero-or-two-leader race window is one statement that swaps both rows'
  `rank_order` (or reassigns membership to `rank_order = 1`) in one query. Two
  separate statements reopen exactly the window this rule exists to close.
- Rank deletion with `migrate_to`: reassign holders and remove the rank in one
  statement for the same reason — no transaction API to fall back on if a
  partial failure needs rolling back.
- `INV-4a`/rank-1-inalienable-permission enforcement: the write path for
  `clan_rank_permissions` rejects any attempt to set `core.manage_ranks` false
  on rank 1, checked in the same statement or as a hard precondition before
  it — never a check-then-write gap.
- Rank-order renumbering on delete/reorder, and the "no threshold may resolve
  to a rank at or above its owner" sweep (invariant 4) run inline on every
  structural rank change, not only in a periodic job.
- Seed data for a new clan's ranks is a **deep copy** of the template
  (invariant 9) — this is the direct fix for defect 6 (ranks assigned by
  reference). Verify by creating two clans and confirming a mutation to one's
  ranks does not appear on the other before sign-off.
- `clan_members` re-key to `(clan, steamid)` (see Migration hazards below)
  must be live before this step's invite/accept pre-check ships, since the
  pre-check and the constraint are meant to work together as primary and
  defence-in-depth.

### Step 4 — Identity, radio, MOTD, administration

Name, abbreviation, motto, description, MOTD — full validation per
[core.md](core.md#identity-field-validation) (character vs. byte counting,
charset, trim/collapse, reserved-word and prohibited-content screening),
clan radio, MOTD administration.

- **Depends on Phase 1a.** The reserved-word and prohibited-content screens
  call `cityrp.wordfilter` with the field-specific category matrix from
  [core.md](core.md#prohibited-content) — this step cannot start until Phase
  1a's library exists.
- Validation must be identical at creation and at every edit path (ID-10) —
  implement as one shared validator function called from both, not two
  hand-copied checks.
- `abbreviation varchar(7)` is a new column, not a repurposing of `short`
  (`varchar(2000)`) — check what live data in `clans.short` holds before
  deciding whether to preserve or drop it (this is a data-preservation check
  at migration time, not a design constraint — see core.md).
- Charset: join-key columns (`clan_members.steamid`, `clan_invites.steamid`)
  migrate to `latin1` to match `players._SteamID`; text columns (name, motto,
  description, MOTD) are `utf8mb4`. This is also where defect 8's underlying
  cross-charset join gets fixed properly, not just the `clan_member` →
  `clan_members` typo — fixing only the typo leaves a `latin1`/`utf8` join
  behind it.
- `self._Clan` vs `self.cityrp._Clan`: Core's public API/accessors must not
  expose either raw field. Anything touching the old `_Clan` reads during this
  port needs to be read in context and routed through a named accessor.

### Step 5 — In-game menu

Replaces the `"Coming soon..."` stub (`cityrp_Clan`), per [ui.md](ui.md).
Sections: Roster / Ranks / Invites / Identity, landing on Roster. **A Bank
section placeholder ships in this step's tab bar but stays hidden or disabled
until Phase 2** — see [open question](#open-questions-flagged-during-planning)
below on menu sequencing. Everything scales through `cityrp.ui`
(`Scale`, `CreateScaledFont`, `OnScaleChanged`) — do not follow
`player_settings/cl_panel.lua`'s opt-out (AGENTS.md footgun #15).

- Roster wires directly into Step 2's `core.kick` and Step 3's `setrank`/
  transfer-leadership functions. `[Kick]`/`[Rank ▾]` render only on rows the
  viewer's threshold reaches (never shown disabled).
- Ranks tab: master–detail ladder, permission editor built by iterating the
  permission registry and dispatching on `kind` — no hardcoded form, so a
  module registering a new permission (Bank, in Phase 2) needs no UI change.
  This is the concrete reason Step 1's registry-driven declaration format
  matters beyond Core itself.
- No-clan landing state, invites list, deposit-adjacent copy is **not** built
  here (Bank UI is Phase 2) but the Identity tab and creation flow ($50,000
  cost, confirmation) are.
- Progressive disclosure per [ui.md](ui.md#progressive-disclosure) table.

### Step 6 — Retire `/clan model`

Remove the command and the `cityrp.model.register` call in `loadclan`.
Fail-closed by construction: `cityrp.model`'s `access()` defaults to `false`
and the consumer at `metatables/sv_player.lua:1292` rejects any unregistered
model, so removing the registration makes clan models unavailable, not
unrestricted. Also apply the `sv_model.lua` `table.RemoveByValue`-on-a-
key-indexed-table fix from Phase 0 here if it has not already landed, since
this is the step that would otherwise next touch that code path. Announce to
players before it lands (open risk, tracked below).

### Schema work landing in Phase 1

`clans.abbreviation`, `clans.join_rankid`, `clans.next_rankid`,
`clan_ranks.rank_order` (`UNIQUE (clan, rank_order)`), `clan_rank_permissions`
(value column **`INT NULL`**), and charset normalisation of the clan tables to
match `players`. **`clans.bank`'s widening to `BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`
moves to Phase 2** — it is Bank's landmine to fix immediately before Bank
ships writing to it, not a Core concern, and there is no reason to widen a
column a full phase before anything writes meaningful amounts through it.

**Migration hazards specific to this fleet:**

- `GM:ConnectToDatabase` runs pending migrations on **every** server against
  one shared database, with nothing serialising them. Two servers restarting
  together both see a migration pending and both execute it. Make every clan
  migration idempotent and guarded (`WHERE rank_order IS NULL`, `ON DUPLICATE
  KEY UPDATE` on the tracking row), or take the fleet down for this migration.
  Applies to every schema change in this phase, not only the `clan_members`
  re-key below.
- `clan_members.clan` is currently `int NULL`, and **a `NULL` cannot
  participate in a primary key** — the re-key to `(clan, steamid)` fails
  outright on any such row, mid-migration, halting boot fleet-wide. **Delete
  any row with a `NULL` clan**: a membership record that names no clan is
  meaningless, not recoverable data. Then set the column `NOT NULL`, then
  re-key. Log the deleted rows.
- Split the `clan_members` audit and the re-key into **two migrations**, and
  sequence the re-key **last** in the phase, after Step 3's invite/accept
  pre-check is live and proven — the application pre-check is what actually
  rejects duplicate membership; the constraint is defence in depth and should
  land second.
- **Forward-only after first write.** `down()` exists per migration, but once
  leaders have configured `clan_rank_permissions`, dropping that table
  destroys their configuration. Take a verified backup immediately before,
  and document the restore procedure rather than implying `down()` is a
  safety net.

## Phase 2 — Bank (Module 2)

Per [bank.md](bank.md). Depends on Phase 1's permission registry and Core
accessors (Step 1), and specifically on Phase 1 Step 3's membership/rank
tables being fully migrated (the withdrawal statement joins `clan_members`
and `clan_rank_permissions` directly). Also depends on the `DB:RunChecked` /
`DB:QueryParamsChecked` affected-row change — see Step 0 below, which is
called out as its own step rather than folded into Step 3 because bank.md
flags it as needing explicit lead-programmer sign-off before implementation,
not just before this module ships.

### Step 0 — `DB:RunChecked` / `DB:QueryParamsChecked` affected-row count

Both currently discard the affected-row count for non-`INSERT` queries
(`db.lua:164`, `db.lua:257`). The atomic ledger-append pattern in Step 3 is
built entirely around branching on that count (1 row = accepted, 0 rows =
rejected, duplicate-key = retry), so this is a hard prerequisite, not
parallel work. **Flagged, not resolved, here** — see Open questions below;
this needs explicit lead-programmer agreement on the exact signature change
before Step 3 starts, per bank.md's own note.

### Step 1 — Schema

- `clans.bank` widened to **`BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`**. This is the direct
  fix for the landmine: the column is currently `int NULL`, a 32-bit ceiling,
  and `SET bank = bank + ?` against a `NULL` row silently yields `NULL` —
  voiding the deposit with no error. Backfill any existing `NULL` to `0` as
  part of the same migration, before the `NOT NULL` constraint is applied, or
  the migration fails on those rows.
- New table `clan_bank_ledger` (event stream): `clan`, `seq`, `steamid`,
  `action` (`deposit`/`withdraw`/`reclaim`/`dissolution_payout`/correction),
  `delta`, `balance_after`, `created_at`, plus audit fields (actor name,
  request id, originating surface) per [bank.md](bank.md#audit-ledger).
  **`UNIQUE (clan, seq)`** is the concurrency control for this entire module —
  see Step 3.
- `clans.bank_unlocked_at` — nullable timestamp, the one-way latch. Written
  once when `unlock_min_age`/`unlock_min_members` are first satisfied, never
  re-evaluated to `NULL` or recomputed on every action.
- Per-`(steamid, clan)` consent-tracking columns/table for the deposit consent
  prompt (last-interaction timestamp).
- Idempotency and one-row-per-server rules from Phase 1's migration hazards
  apply identically here — this table is new, so there is no backfill
  complexity, but the shared-DB/no-serialisation hazard still applies to the
  tracking row for this migration itself.

### Step 2 — Permission registration and pure functions

- Register `bank.deposit`, `bank.withdraw` (both `BOOLEAN`, not
  `NUMERIC_LIMIT` — there is no per-rank withdrawal cap, only a global
  `per_withdrawal_cap`, so keeping the SQL predicate a boolean is what keeps
  the per-transaction cap out of SQL entirely) against Phase 1's registry.
  No `bank.configure_limits` permission — the tuning knobs are server
  operator config with no in-game editing surface, so there is nothing for a
  permission to gate (see [bank.md](bank.md#rank-gating)).
- `validateBankAmount(amount)` — one pure function, called by deposit,
  withdrawal and reclaim. Rejects non-numeric, NaN, non-finite, non-integer,
  `≤ 0`, and `> MAX_TRANSACTION` ($100,000,000). Write and review this before
  Step 3, since both statements depend on it — the boundary cases are listed
  in [acceptance-criteria.md](acceptance-criteria.md#amount-validation) as a
  manual reference; automated coverage is out of scope for this plan (see
  Phase 1 Step 2 note on GLuaTest).
- Rolling-cap and reclaim-window arithmetic (the pure calculation only, not
  its atomic enforcement, which is Step 3/4).

### Step 3 — Atomic ledger append: deposit and withdrawal

The core of the module. One statement per action type; balance check,
permission check and ledger append happen in the same `INSERT ... SELECT`,
never a Lua read-then-decide-then-write — see the worked withdrawal statement
in [bank.md](bank.md#withdrawals-must-be-a-single-atomic-statement).

- **No transaction is used, and none is needed** — this is the direct answer
  to the `db.lua`-has-no-transaction-API landmine for this operation. The
  ledger insert *is* the sole authoritative write (event sourcing per
  [bank.md](bank.md#the-ledger-is-authoritative--event-sourcing)); the
  `clans.bank` cache update that follows is fire-and-forget and explicitly
  allowed to fail without rolling anything back. Consistency comes from doing
  the whole balance-check-permission-check-append as one MySQL statement
  (single-statement atomicity), not from a multi-statement transaction the
  codebase has no primitive for.
- `seq = COALESCE(MAX(seq), 0) + 1` computed inside the same `INSERT ...
  SELECT`, rejected by `UNIQUE (clan, seq)` on collision. On a duplicate-key
  error, **retry** — recompute against the now-current stream. This is what
  replaces the old cache-row lock as the serialisation point across
  processes; an in-process Lua lock protects nothing since multiple game
  servers and the (now-disabled) web app share one MySQL instance.
- Withdrawal's `EXISTS` clause uses `LEFT JOIN clan_rank_permissions` plus
  `COALESCE(p.value, ?)` bound to the registered default — an inner `JOIN`
  would wrongly deny a rank relying on the unmaterialised default (BA-3).
  Deposit's statement has no permission predicate (`bank.deposit` is
  universal) but does carry an `EXISTS` check against
  `clans.bank_unlocked_at IS NOT NULL` — deposits are blocked until the bank
  unlocks, same as withdrawals (see
  [bank.md](bank.md#deposits-are-gated-by-the-unlock-latch-too)). Still the
  simpler of the two statements — build it first as a warm-up before the
  withdrawal statement.
- `balance_after` computed and stored in the same statement — makes the
  current balance a single-row read and cache rebuilds cheap.
- Rate limiting: 10s cooldown per player, shared across deposit/withdraw/
  reclaim entry routes, enforced server-side at the entry point — not inside
  the retry path (BC-7/BC-8).
- Requires Step 0's affected-row fix to branch on 1-row/0-row/duplicate-key.

### Step 4 — Self-reclaim

Same atomic-`UPDATE` shape as withdrawal, distinct `action = 'reclaim'`, no
`bank.withdraw` predicate — eligibility is "this is your own deposit, within
`self_reclaim_window`," not a rank permission. Explicitly **not** counted
against `rolling_withdrawal_cap` (BR-5) — this needs its own predicate path
rather than reusing withdrawal's cap-check clause, since exempting it is
deliberate (closing the reclaim-starvation griefing vector), not an oversight
to fix later.

### Step 5 — Cache, reconciliation and dissolution distribution

- Fire-and-forget `clans.bank` cache update issued after the Step 3/4 ledger
  callback returns — never retried, never blocking, never a transaction
  failure. On any disagreement between cache and `SUM(delta)`, the ledger
  wins; rebuild the cache and log the mismatch at Error (observability
  signal, not a fault) on clan load and periodically.
- Dissolution distribution formula
  ([bank.md](bank.md#distribution-formula)) reads the ledger only, never the
  cache, and includes every SteamID that ever appears in the ledger — not
  only current members. Runs synchronously as part of `/clan delete`, no
  hold or countdown (see bank.md's arbitrage analysis for why a hold was
  rejected, not merely omitted — do not reintroduce one without re-solving
  that).
- Payout delivery: online recipients get `GiveMoney` then `SaveData`. Offline
  recipients get a **new** `remote` row type (not `pmoney`, which is
  moneypack-specific) — **claim the row before granting** (`UPDATE remote SET
  done = 1 WHERE id = ? AND done = 0`, proceed only if one row affected),
  never grant-then-mark. Require `IsValid(ply)` and `ply._Initialized` inside
  the handler. Target `server = 'all'` and rely on the claim-before-grant
  `UPDATE` for exactly-once delivery — this is deliberately the opposite
  shape from the `reloadclan`/cache-invalidation use of `remote` (Phase 1's
  landmine, "one row per server, never `server = 'all'`"): that case is
  fan-out (every server must see it), this case is single delivery (exactly
  one server must pay out), so the fix for one is not the fix for the other.
  Worth an explicit code comment at both call sites given how easy the two
  shapes are to conflate.
- On `cityrp.remote.noSave` servers (`build`, `beta`, `beta2`, `event`),
  return without `done()` so a real server picks up the payout instead.

### Step 6 — Rolling cap, unlock gate, consent prompt

- Clan-scoped rolling 24h withdrawal cap ($75,000 default), evaluated against
  the ledger (sum of withdrawals in the trailing 24h for the clan, not the
  actor) — closes promote→withdraw→demote cycling by construction, since the
  clock is per-clan, not per-person.
- Unlock latch: evaluate `age >= unlock_min_age AND members >=
  unlock_min_members` **only** to decide whether to write
  `clans.bank_unlocked_at` for the first time. Every subsequent gate check
  reads the stored flag, never re-evaluates the condition — this is the
  direct fix for the "obvious implementation relocks it" trap called out in
  bank.md.
- Deposit consent prompt: shown before deposit completes on first-ever
  deposit to this clan, or after `consent_reprompt_days` (30) since the
  player's last *deposit or withdrawal or reclaim* with this clan — passive
  viewing does not reset the clock. Stored per `(steamid, clan)`.
- `/clan undo` guard: reject with a balance-nonzero check regardless of
  whether the 3-day unlock gate structurally prevents the scenario today —
  defensive guard in case the gate is ever loosened (BU-2).

### Step 7 — Bank UI tab

Lights up the Step 5 placeholder from Phase 1. Balance, deposit (with consent
prompt), own reclaimable deposits — visible to everyone (`bank.deposit` is
universal). Full ledger — visible only to `bank.withdraw` holders. Deletion
confirmation gains the balance/distribution copy from
[ui.md](ui.md#clan-deletion). All amounts/labels through `cityrp.ui` per
Phase 1's scaling requirement, same as every other tab.

## Data migration

| Item | Action |
|---|---|
| Orphaned `clan_members` rows | Players may be silently in clans they believe they left, from failed joins. Audit and clean |
| Non-contiguous rank IDs (live data has `8`, `170`) | Backfill `rank_order` per clan by sorting on legacy `rankid`, preserving ties. Leave `rankid` untouched to preserve foreign keys |
| `clans.next_rankid` | Seed to `MAX(rankid) + 1` per clan |
| `clans.join_rankid` | Backfill to any rank at `MAX(rank_order)`; log the choice |
| `clans.short` (`varchar(2000)`) | Establish what it holds before the abbreviation migration — it may be worth keeping or safe to drop |
| Clans with zero members or no leader | Flag for manual review; do not auto-resolve silently |
| Dead tables (`clan`, `clan_has_players`, `clan_has_invite`) | Confirm unused, then drop |
| `clan_models`, `clans.model` | Dead once `/clan model` retires. Keep the rows until the model files themselves are decommissioned — they record which model belonged to which clan, which is the only remaining reference if a clan later asks |
| Rank/member caps (50 / 100) | Live maxima are 28 and 18, so nothing is currently over cap. Grandfather any that appear |

## Deferred

Not in this plan. Recorded so the framework can be sanity-checked against them.

| Item | Notes |
|---|---|
| **Web app** | Repository disabled. If it returns, it must share the authorisation boundary rather than reimplementing it — see [design.md](design.md#surfaces) |
| `/clan shift` (#1327) | A later Core rework. Essentially an additional gate on command execution, so it retrofits cleanly; no seam needs reserving now |
| Clan inventory (#1624) | Future module |
| Clan vehicles | Future module; `clan_vehicles` table already exists |

Clan models are **retired**, not deferred — see [design.md](design.md#retiring-clan-models).

## Open risks

| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| In-game becomes the only management surface | With the web app gone, anything the menu cannot do, nobody can do | Audit the web app's feature set against the planned menu before Phase 1 closes — rank creation and permission editing especially |
| `/clan model` retirement is player-facing | Any clan still using it loses the feature | Low impact — clan activity is minimal — but announce before it lands rather than after |
| Rank IDs are non-contiguous in live data | Rebuilt logic may assume contiguity | `rank_order` is the only column compared; verify the backfill on a copy first |
| Orphaned membership rows | Players silently in old clans | Audit during migration |
| Word list curation is a content decision | Engineering cannot pick the list | Needs whoever owns moderation policy, before Phase 1 ships |

## Open questions flagged during planning

Raised while adding step-level detail to Phases 1–2. Deliberately not resolved
here — each needs a decision from whoever owns that call before the relevant
step starts, not a default baked silently into the plan.

| # | Question | Where it bites | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Does the in-game menu ship in Phase 1 Step 5 with a hidden/disabled Bank tab placeholder, or does the whole menu wait for Phase 2 so Bank lands complete? | Phase 1 Step 5, Phase 2 Step 7 | This plan assumes the former (ship Roster/Ranks/Invites/Identity in Phase 1, light up Bank in Phase 2) because the menu is the only clan management surface and #1541 has been open since ~2017 — holding it hostage to Bank's separate scope seemed like the wrong trade-off to make silently. Flagging in case the product/design side disagrees. |
| 2 | Is `core.kick` in Phase 1 Step 2 backend-only (console command / direct call for validation), with the Roster `[Kick]` button wired up later in Step 5? | Phase 1 Step 2 vs Step 5 | Assumed yes, to keep the vertical slice minimal and UI-independent per the architecture review's stated purpose ("de-risk the framework shape"). If the intent was to validate the UI wiring too as part of the slice, Step 2's scope needs to grow. |
| 3 | Exact signature for the `DB:RunChecked` / `DB:QueryParamsChecked` affected-row-count change | Phase 2 Step 0 | bank.md explicitly calls this out as needing lead-programmer agreement before implementation, not just before Bank ships. This plan places it as a blocking Step 0, but the actual sign-off conversation still needs to happen — it is not resolved by being scheduled. |
| 4 | Whether Phase 2's schema/data work can start on a server before every server in the fleet has completed Phase 1's `clan_members` re-key migration | Phase 1 → Phase 2 boundary | The Bank withdrawal statement joins `clan_members` directly; if any server is mid-fleet-rollout on Phase 1's re-key, Phase 2's migrations landing on that same shared database could interact with rows in an inconsistent shape. This plan assumes Phase 1 is fully rolled out fleet-wide before Phase 2's Step 1 migration runs, but that is an assumption about rollout sequencing, not something derivable from the design docs alone. |

topics.title: Clans — In-Game Menu
topics.body:
# Clans — In-Game Menu

The in-game menu is the **only** clan management surface. Anything it cannot do,
nobody can do — the companion web app is out of scope and its repository is
disabled, and the legacy in-game panel is a `"Coming soon..."` stub.

> **Status**: Recommended route, not an implementation spec. Exact dimensions,
> colours and Derma control choices belong to whoever builds it.
> Companion to [core.md](core.md) and [bank.md](bank.md).

## Integration

`core/derma/cl_main.lua` already defines the F1 shell as a top tab bar
(`f1_categoriesToBeMade`), where each entry is a `Dock(FILL)` panel resolved by
class name. `cityrp_Clan` is already registered — it is the stub. Adding `"Clan"`
to that array is the whole shell-level integration cost.

Everything below happens inside that one panel. For sub-navigation the nearest
precedent is the Settings tab (`core/plugins/player_settings/cl_panel.lua`): a
persistent left sidebar, content on the right.

Sections: **Roster / Ranks / Bank / Invites / Identity**, landing on Roster.

**Do not copy Settings' opt-out of `cityrp.ui` scaling.** That panel uses fixed
sizes because it configures the scale slider itself — a bootstrapping problem
Clans does not have. Every font here goes through `cityrp.ui.CreateScaledFont`
and every dimension through `cityrp.ui.Scale`. The roster, rank list and
permission editor rebuild child controls when data changes, so they must also
hook `OnScaleChanged` to relayout — not merely rebuild fonts.

## No-clan state

A player without a clan still needs somewhere to land:

1. `"You're not in a clan."`
2. Pending invites — header `"You have X invites"` and a table, accept and
   decline per row. Omitted entirely when there are none.
3. A **Create a clan** button, stating the $50,000 cost before confirmation.

This is the only route to clan creation once chat commands are replaced, and the
only place invites are visible. The legacy implementation surfaced invites once
as a spawn notification — easy to miss, impossible to recall.

## Roster

```text
┌─ ROSTER ── 24 / 100 members ──────────[ Search ]─┐
│  ⬤ Nova         Leader                            │
│     Online · Joined 12 Jan 2025                   │
│  ⬤ Rusk         Officer      [Kick] [Rank ▾]      │
│     Online · Joined 03 Mar 2025                   │
│  ⚪ Priya        Lieutenant   [Kick] [Rank ▾]      │
│     Offline · Joined 02 Jul 2025                  │
│  …                                                 │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

- Sorted by rank, then online-first, then alphabetically.
- Online status is **icon and word**, never colour alone.
- **`[Kick]` and `[Rank ▾]` render only on rows the viewer's threshold actually
  reaches** — omitted entirely elsewhere, not shown disabled. At 100 members a
  greyed-out button on every unreachable row is noise.

That last point does real teaching work: the presence or absence of a Kick button
next to a specific person explains a threshold permission more clearly than any
abstract configuration screen.

## Ranks

Ranks are a strict ladder — one rank per position, most senior first. A plain
ordered list is correct.

**Master–detail**: the ladder on the left, the selected rank's identity and
permissions on the right. Member count is shown inline per rank, because deleting
a rank that members hold is rejected by default and the leader needs that number
before trying.

Rank 1 is **not** editable here beyond renaming. Reassigning who holds it is a
membership action tied to a person — Transfer Leadership, in Roster — not a
structural rank edit.

Reordering is drag-and-drop, but **every drag needs a non-drag equivalent** for
keyboard use: a per-row context menu with Move Up / Move Down / Rename / Delete /
**Duplicate permissions from…**

Duplication is a scale mitigation, not a convenience. Live clans reach 28 ranks
and the cap is 50; configuring each rank's permissions from blank is the real
"wall of controls" risk. Cloning an existing rank as a starting point is what
keeps it usable.

### Permission editor

**Built by iterating the permission registry and dispatching on `kind`, grouped
into a section per owning module.** Nothing here is a hardcoded form — that is
what makes module-declared permissions work in practice, and a new module's
permissions must appear with no UI change.

| Kind | Control | States |
|---|---|---|
| `BOOLEAN` | Toggle | On / Off |
| `THRESHOLD` | Rank picker plus a resolved sentence | None, or a specific rank |
| `NUMERIC_LIMIT` | Grant toggle → number field or Unlimited | Off / Limited / Unlimited |

Always render the module-declared `label` ("Withdraw from clan bank"), never the
raw id (`bank.withdraw`). Never show `-1` or `NULL` to a player — those are
storage sentinels, not vocabulary.

**Threshold permissions need a plain-language caption, not just a dropdown.**
"Kick = Lieutenant" does not self-evidently mean "may kick Lieutenant and
everyone below it". Pair the picker with a permanent sentence:

> *Grants authority over Lieutenant and everyone junior to it.*

The sentence is the floor — cheap, accessible, complete on its own. A clickable
mini-ladder that shades the covered range is a worthwhile enhancement on top, but
it needs a non-colour indicator per row, and it degrades to the sentence cleanly
if it does not fit the build.

**Filter the options to what the server would accept.** A rank's threshold picker
offers only ranks strictly junior to it (invariant 4). The same principle applies
throughout: never render a control whose action would be rejected.

> ⚠ `core.manage_ranks` also gates editing a rank's own permissions, including
> `core.delete_clan` — granting it to a non-leader rank is effectively clan
> co-ownership. Show a **persistent inline warning** under that toggle whenever
> it is enabled for any rank other than rank 1. Persistent, not a one-time toast:
> the consequence is standing, not momentary.

### Change Rank is the mirror case

Assigning a person to a rank resolves to one specific rank, and its options are
filtered to those satisfying the actor's `core.setrank` threshold — both the
target's current rank and the new rank must satisfy it.

`core/derma/cl_market.lua`'s category picker (`dropDown.CategoryTree`, built with
`AddSubMenu`) is the existing precedent for a grouped dropdown.

## Progressive disclosure

**Rule**: if a section has legitimate read-only value for every member, show it
read-only and gate the controls. If it is operationally private with no read-only
value, hide it entirely.

| Section | Visible to | Reasoning |
|---|---|---|
| Roster | Everyone | Baseline membership info |
| Ranks | Everyone, **read-only** without `core.manage_ranks` | A member knowing what an Officer can do — and therefore who to ask — costs nothing |
| Invites | `core.invite` or `core.manage_invites` holders | Who is being recruited is operationally sensitive with no read-only value to someone who cannot act |
| Bank — balance, deposit, own reclaimable deposits | Everyone | `bank.deposit` is universal; a player must see their own deposits to reclaim them |
| Bank — full ledger | `bank.withdraw` holders | Financial oversight rather than baseline transparency |
| Identity | Everyone views; **field-level** edit split — name, abbreviation, motto and description need `core.edit_identity`, MOTD needs `core.motd_edit` | Two permissions gate different fields in one tab, so control-level adaptation applies within a section, not only at the sidebar |

## Clan deletion

Deletion distributes the bank balance pro-rata to all historical net contributors
and cannot be undone.

1. **`[Delete Clan]` sits in a visually separated danger zone**, never beside
   frequent actions.
2. The confirmation states, in plain language rather than formulas:
   - "This will permanently delete **[Clan Name]**."
   - "Current bank balance: **$X**."
   - "This will be split among everyone who has ever contributed, in proportion
     to what they put in. Anyone who withdrew more than they deposited receives
     nothing."
   - "Your $25,000 creation deposit is refunded to you separately."
   - "This happens immediately and cannot be undone."
3. **Type the clan name to confirm.** The button stays disabled until it matches.
   This mirrors the existing confirmation-code convention while using something
   the leader already knows, so typing it is itself part of registering what is
   about to happen.

**Deletion is immediate — there is no hold, countdown or cancellation window.**
The typed confirmation is the only safeguard, which is the standard pattern for
irreversible destructive actions. Members learn of the dissolution from their
payout notification. See [bank.md](bank.md#why-there-is-no-deletion-hold) for why
a hold was rejected rather than merely omitted.

## Deposit consent prompt

Shown before a first deposit to a clan, and again after `consent_reprompt_days`
of no deposit or withdrawal. Four short lines, not a wall of text:

```text
┌─ Depositing to [Clan Name] ──────────────────┐
│  ⚠ You do not currently hold withdraw          │
│    permission in this clan.                    │
│    Only Leader and Officer can take money out. │
│                                                 │
│  • This money becomes clan property.           │
│  • You can reclaim THIS deposit yourself for   │
│    the next 10 minutes.                        │
│  • If the clan disbands, remaining funds are   │
│    split by how much each person put in.       │
│                                                 │
│        [ Cancel ]      [ Deposit $500 ]        │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

- The withdraw-status line is personalised and **always in the same position**,
  tonally adaptive — warning if they lack `bank.withdraw`, neutral if they hold
  it. Consistent placement matters because the prompt reappears later, possibly
  under different leadership.
- **No "don't show again" checkbox.** The re-prompt interval is a deliberate
  server-side safety mechanism; a client-side snooze would either do nothing or
  actively defeat it.
- The amount is entered before the prompt and carried into it.
- Escape maps to Cancel. The default action must never be the one that commits
  money.

## Accessibility

| Requirement | How |
|---|---|
| Keyboard only | Every drag interaction has a context-menu equivalent |
| Scales at all resolutions | Everything through `cityrp.ui`; `OnScaleChanged` relayout on data-driven panels |
| Not colour-only | Online/offline is icon + word; threshold range uses a per-row marker, not tint |
| No unwarned flashing | The deletion countdown is static or slow — never strobing |

Long-form fields have no per-line caps, so **the renderer must hard-wrap on
character boundaries** — a single unbroken 2000-byte MOTD is valid input. Panels
clip or scroll; they never expand.

> Outside this design's scope but worth raising: the outer F1 frame is currently
> fixed at 1008×825 and is not itself scaled. A correctly-scaled Clan panel inside
> an unscaled frame still will not grow with the player's HUD scale preference.

## Open decisions

| # | Decision | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|
| ~~1~~ | ~~Is the deletion hold cancellable?~~ | **Moot — the hold was dropped.** Deletion is immediate; the typed confirmation is the safeguard |
| ~~2~~ | ~~Should the UI block a leader removing `core.manage_ranks` from their own rank?~~ | **Resolved in the model, not the UI.** Rank 1 permanently holds `core.manage_ranks`; see [core.md](core.md#inalienable-permission). The editor renders it locked-on with an explanation rather than as an editable toggle that would be rejected |
| 3 | Should a `core.invite`-only holder see the pending list for invites they sent? | Default no for v1 — keep the Send control, hide the list |

topics.body:
# Docs layout migration: `src/docs/` → `docs/` + `tools/docs/`

Scope: repo layout, CI, tooling, link rewrites. No gamemode behaviour changes.

## Goal

1. Narrative docs live at `docs/` (today `src/docs/topics/`), so the repo reads like every other
   repo: `docs/modern-apis.md`, `docs/plugins.md`, `docs/clans/…`, `docs/design/…`.
2. `src/docs/` is deleted. Doc tooling is not "source"; it moves to `tools/docs/`.
3. Every LDoc remnant that is *tooling* goes. LDoc *tag handling* in `generate.py` stays, because
   ~hundreds of Lua files still carry `@tparam`/`@state`/`@warns` and the generator is what keeps
   them rendering until each is converted (see [doc-comments.md](../doc-comments.md)).

## Inventory (what is in `src/docs/` today — 48 tracked files)

| Path | What it is | Fate |
|---|---|---|
| `topics/*.md` (25 files) | Narrative docs, rendered to site + `api.json` | → `docs/*.md` |
| `topics/clans/*.md`, `topics/design/*.md` | Nested docs (api.json only, not HTML sidebar) | → `docs/clans/`, `docs/design/` |
| `generate.py`, `test_generate.py`, `fixtures/sample.json` | LuaLS JSON → HTML/api.json generator + tests | → `tools/docs/` |
| `requirements.txt` (`wenmode`) | Generator deps | → `tools/docs/requirements.txt` |
| `build.sh` | Installs node + sass + cssbeautify **globally via sudo**, compiles `ll.scss`, concatenates CSS | **delete** (see §3) |
| `style/ldoc-base.css` | Vendored LDoc layout CSS (`#navigation`/`#content`) | → `tools/docs/style/base.css` (rename; keep content, fix header comment) |
| `style/ll.scss` + `style/ll.css` | Theme, committed in *both* forms | keep `ll.css`, **delete** `ll.scss` |
| `style/glua.css` | Syntax colours | → `tools/docs/style/glua.css` |
| `.gitignore` (`build/`, `style.css`, `__pycache__/`) | Generated outputs | → `tools/docs/.gitignore`, drop `style.css` entry once build.sh is gone |
| `mcp/` (server, tests, Dockerfile, compose, README, requirements) | `cityrp-docs` MCP server | → `tools/docs-mcp/` |

Nothing outside this tree imports the Python modules; the only consumers are the two CI workflows.

## Why `tools/docs/` and not `docs/_build/` or similar

`generate.py:load_topics()` globs `topics_dir/*.md` for the HTML sidebar and `rglob("*.md")` for
`api.json`. If tooling lived *inside* `docs/`, its `README.md`/`mcp/README.md` would be swept into
the published topic index. Keeping tooling outside the content root means `--topics docs` needs no
exclusion list. (`src/` keeps its other build helpers — `setmodel`, `visprot`, `enums.py` — so
`tools/` is a new top-level dir; if that is unwanted, `src/docs-tooling/` works identically.)

## Reference map (every place that hard-codes `src/docs`)

Counts are occurrences of the literal `src/docs`.

| Area | Files | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| CI (mirrored) | `.github/workflows/docs.yml` (11), `.gitea/workflows/docs.yml` (10), `.gitea/workflows/docs-mcp.yml` (4) | Paths filters, `--doc_out_path`, `--topics`, `--style`, publish dir, docker `context` |
| Lint gate (mirrored) | `.github/scripts/standards-diff.py` (17), `.gitea/scripts/standards-diff.py` (17) | Human-facing "(see src/docs/topics/x.md)" strings in rule messages |
| Agent guidance | `AGENTS.md` (21), `.github/copilot-instructions.md` (8), `.cursor/rules/*.mdc` (13 across 6 files), `.claude/agents/garrysmod-specialist.md` (4), `.claude/docs/technical-preferences.md` (3) | Plain link rewrites |
| Contributor docs | `CONTRIBUTING.md` (6), `.github/GOVERNANCE.md` (1), `.github/CODEOWNERS` (2) | CODEOWNERS path pattern must change or ownership silently lapses |
| Inside the docs | `topics/doc-comments.md` (7), `topics/luacats.md` (6), `mcp/README.md` (11) | Plus **22 `../` relative links** in topics (`casino.md`, `clans/bank.md`, `coding-standards.md`, …) that assume depth 3 — each loses two `../` |
| Lua source comments | `gamemode/sh_init.lua:113`, `entities/cityrp_laboratory/shared.lua:86` (`@see`), `plugins/pcasino/sv_init.lua:42` | Comment-only; the `@see` renders on the docs site, so it must be right |
| Plugin READMEs / notes | `perma_ents/README_3D_SIGNS.md`, `README_BILLBOARDS.md`, `problems/04-…`, `improvements/05-…` | Plain link rewrites |
| Generator itself | `generate.py` header comment (2) | Comment only |

`docs/` does not currently exist, so there are no collisions. `.claude/docs/` is unrelated (Claude
agent preferences) and stays.

## Plan — one PR, five commits, in this order

Use `git mv` so history follows. Note that for Lua files a rename un-grandfathers the standards gate,
but no Lua files are renamed here — only `.md`/`.py`/`.css`, which the gate ignores.

### 1. `chore(docs): move topics to docs/`
```bash
git mv src/docs/topics docs
```
Then fix the 22 `../` links (depth 3 → depth 1: `../../../x` → `../x`, `../../x` → `x`). Verify with:
```bash
grep -rn "](\.\./" docs
```
Each remaining hit should resolve: `cd docs && for f in $(grep -rho "](\.\./[^)#]*" . | sed 's/](//' | sort -u); do [ -e "$f" ] || echo MISSING $f; done`.

### 2. `chore(docs): move generator and MCP server to tools/`
```bash
git mv src/docs/generate.py src/docs/test_generate.py src/docs/fixtures src/docs/requirements.txt src/docs/.gitignore tools/docs/
git mv src/docs/style tools/docs/style
git mv src/docs/mcp tools/docs-mcp
git rm src/docs/build.sh src/docs/style/ll.scss   # see §3
git mv tools/docs/style/ldoc-base.css tools/docs/style/base.css
```
`src/docs/` is now empty and gone.

### 3. `chore(docs): drop LDoc build tooling`
- `build.sh` existed to compile SCSS and concatenate CSS, installing node/sass/cssbeautify globally with
  `sudo` on the runner. `ll.css` is already committed next to `ll.scss` (and has drifted — last
  touched in different commits). Replace the whole script with a ~10-line `--style-dir` in
  `generate.py` that concatenates `base.css` → `glua.css` → `ll.css` into `build/style.css` itself.
  Keeps `--style <file>` working for anyone passing a prebuilt file.
- Rename `ldoc-base.css` → `base.css`; rewrite its header comment to say it's the site's base layout
  (originally captured from LDoc output) rather than implying LDoc is still upstream.
- **Keep** `parse_ldoc_tags()` and `ParseLdocTagsTests` in `generate.py` — they are the shim that
  renders the legacy `@state/@warns/@bugs/@deprecated` tags still present in Lua. Rename to
  `parse_legacy_tags` if you want the word gone; behaviour unchanged.
- **Keep** the `luacats-ldoc-tags` rule in `standards-diff.py` — it's the guard that stops new LDoc
  tags, which is exactly what you want once the tooling is gone.
- The three topic files that mention LDoc (`coding-standards.md`, `doc-comments.md`, `luacats.md`)
  and `AGENTS.md` ("LDoc is gone; `src/docs/config.ld` no longer exists") already describe it as
  dead; just update their paths.

### 4. `ci(docs): point workflows at docs/ and tools/docs/`
Both `.github/` and `.gitea/` copies — they are deliberately mirrored (self-hosted vs ubuntu, gh-pages
vs codeberg pages action), so edit both, not one.

`docs.yml` (×2):
- `paths:` → `'docs/**'`, `'tools/docs/**'`, and the workflow's own path.
- drop the "Build CSS" step.
- `pip install -r tools/docs/requirements.txt`
- `--doc_out_path=tools/docs/out` (anything gitignored; don't write `doc.json` next to source).
- `python3 tools/docs/generate.py --json tools/docs/out/doc.json --output tools/docs/build --style-dir tools/docs/style --topics docs`
- upload/publish dir → `tools/docs/build/`.
- **Add** a step `python3 -m unittest tools/docs/test_generate.py` — nothing runs it today.

`docs-mcp.yml` (gitea only):
- `paths:` → `'tools/docs-mcp/**'`; `requirements`, `unittest -s`, and docker `context` → `tools/docs-mcp`.

`CODEOWNERS` (both references): `src/docs/` → `docs/` **and** `tools/docs/` + `tools/docs-mcp/`, otherwise review ownership for the tooling silently disappears.

### 5. `docs: rewrite src/docs links across the repo`
Mechanical. From the repo root (Git Bash; these files are LF/ASCII-safe but confirm with `git diff --stat` that only intended files changed — several repo files are CRLF and `sed -i` will flip them; use the Edit tool or a Python byte-replace for any CRLF file):
```bash
grep -rIl --exclude-dir=.git --exclude-dir=node_modules "src/docs" . 
```
Replacement rules, applied in this order:
1. `src/docs/topics/` → `docs/`
2. `src/docs/mcp/` → `tools/docs-mcp/`
3. `src/docs/generate.py` → `tools/docs/generate.py`
4. any remaining `src/docs/` → `tools/docs/`

Then rerun the grep — it must return nothing. Spot-check the three Lua comments and the
`standards-diff.py` rule messages by eye (they're what contributors see in CI failures).

## Verification checklist

- [ ] `grep -rI "src/docs" .` → empty (excluding `.git`).
- [ ] `python3 -m unittest tools/docs/test_generate.py` passes.
- [ ] Local site build: install LuaLS, run the two commands from §4 by hand, open `tools/docs/build/index.html` — sidebar lists every top-level `docs/*.md`, topic pages render, `api.json` contains `clans/…` and `design/…` ids.
- [ ] `tools/docs-mcp` tests: `python -m unittest discover -s tools/docs-mcp -p 'test_*.py'`.
- [ ] Both lint gates clean on the branch (they only look at Lua under the gamemode, so expect no findings — but the `@see` comment edit in `cityrp_laboratory/shared.lua` is a Lua diff and will be checked).
- [ ] After merge: `docs.yml` green on master, site at docs.limelightgaming.info updated; `docs-mcp.yml` green, `cityrp-docs` MCP `list_topics` still returns the full topic set (the server reads `api.json` from the deployed site, so it's a follow-on check, not a PR gate).
- [ ] Contributor-facing MCP setup path in `CONTRIBUTING.md` / `tools/docs-mcp/README.md` matches the new location.

## Things deliberately *not* in scope

- Converting the remaining LDoc-tagged Lua comments (`@tparam`, `@treturn`, `@usage`, …). That is
  per-file work governed by the standards gate; the generator shim stays until it's done.
- Renaming `@namespace` or changing how `generate.py` parses anything.
- Moving `problems/`, `improvements/`, `todo/`, `CONTEXT.md`, `SECURITY-REVIEW-2026-08.md` under
  `docs/`. They're working notes, not published docs, and pulling them in would put them on the
  public site (`rglob` feeds `api.json`). If they should become docs, that is a separate decision
  per file.
- `.claude/docs/` — not docs in this sense; leave it.

topics.body:
# Design Docs

Plans and proposals, kept apart from the technical topics because they describe work rather than
document behaviour. A design doc argues for a change — what it would touch, in what order, and what
it deliberately leaves alone. For how the gamemode actually works today, use the topics list
instead.

Open each doc with front matter; the table below is built from it, so a doc that omits a field
leaves a hole in the index rather than going unlisted:

```yaml
---
title: Docs layout migration          # sidebar and index label; falls back to the first heading
status: Proposed                      # Proposed / Accepted / Landed / Implemented / Abandoned
date: 2026-08-22                      # when it was written, not when it landed
description: One line on what it changes.
pinned: true                          # optional; lifts it to the top of this list
---
```

A body of work large enough to need several docs gets its own folder below, with one of them marked
`index: true` to serve as its landing page.
