topics.body:
# Design: Class-Based Item Registration (`ITEM:New`)

> **Code**: `core/libraries/sh_itemcore.lua` (the `ITEM` class), `core/libraries/sh_item.lua` (`cityrp.item.new`, `cityrp.item.register`, the registry)
> **History**: metatable-based item library introduced 2019-08-21 (`efcf7cb22`); `ITEM` split out of `cityrp.item` into its own file 2020-05-02 (`d366624eb`)

This document was written after the fact. It records what the class-based registration route is, why it replaced `cityrp.item.register({})`, the decisions baked into it, and the sharp edges those decisions left behind. The usage guide is [items.md](../items/items.md); the action hooks are in [item-actions.md](../items/item-actions.md); metadata is in [item-metadata-schema.md](../items/item-metadata-schema.md). This page is about *why the route is shaped the way it is*.

## Problem

Before this route, every item was a plain table handed to `cityrp.item.register(tbl, baseID)`. Two problems drove the redesign:

1. **Inheritance required a registered parent.** `register(tbl, "base_x")` looks the base up in `cityrp.item.stored`, so the base had to be a registered — and therefore obtainable — item. Anything that wanted to share data (ten suits at the same price, a family of backpacks) had to either duplicate the fields or publish an abstract base that players could see in the market unless something explicitly hid it. This is [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) footgun #6.
2. **One item per file, lots of boilerplate.** Each variant was a full table with its own `name`, `cost`, `model`, `description`, `uniqueID` assignments. Families of near-identical cosmetic items (the bulk of the catalogue) were the worst case.

## Goals

- Share data between variants without registering the shared part.
- Define several related items in one file with minimal repetition.
- Keep the runtime contract (`cityrp.item.stored[id]`, the `canX`/`onX` hooks, `cityrp.item.get`) identical so every consumer — inventory, market, manufacturing, entities — keeps working unchanged.
- Coexist with the legacy route indefinitely. Migrating the legacy files was never in scope; today 368 files use `ITEM:New` and 250 still call `cityrp.item.register`.

### Non-goals

- Replacing the registry. `cityrp.item.stored` is still a flat `uniqueID -> table` map.
- Validating item definitions (required fields, model existence, category names). Registration still accepts whatever it is given.
- Changing the hook naming. The UpperCamelCase/lowerCamelCase split described at the top of `sh_itemcore.lua` (`SetCost` vs `canUse`) is deliberate: construction-time API vs runtime hooks.

## Design

### Two layers

| Layer | Where | Responsibility |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ITEM` class | `sh_itemcore.lua` | The global base table every item ultimately indexes into. Holds defaults (`size = 1`, `cost = 0`, `batch = 5`, `store = true`, `category = "Base"`, `model = "models/error.mdl"`), the fluent setters, `New`/`Clone`/`Merge`/`Register`, and the default `canX = true` hooks. |
| `cityrp.item` | `sh_item.lua` | The registry and its lookup/category helpers. `cityrp.item.new(base)` builds the metatable link; `cityrp.item.register(item)` post-processes and stores. |

`ITEM:Register(id)` is a thin wrapper: it sets `uniqueID` if given, then calls the **legacy** `cityrp.item.register(self)` with no base argument. The fluent route therefore reuses all the legacy normalisation (default `canX`, `replaced`/`outdated` handling, `.rep` to `.reps` fix-up, `GetMetaName`, the long-category warning) rather than duplicating it. There is exactly one registration code path.

### Inheritance is a metatable chain, not a copy

```
ITEM  <--__index--  stored["base_accessory"]  <--__index--  (unregistered local BASE)  <--__index--  stored["backpacknavy_2"]
```

- `ITEM:New("base_id")` → `cityrp.item.new("base_id")` → `setmetatable({base = id, BaseClass = stored[id]}, {__index = stored[id]})`.
- `ITEM:New()` with no base → `setmetatable({}, ITEM)` (`ITEM.__index = ITEM`).
- `item:Clone()` → `setmetatable({base = rawget(self, "uniqueID") or "tmp_base_<file>"}, {__index = self})`.

This is the decision that solves goal 1. A clone's parent is whatever table it was cloned from, registered or not, so an intermediate `BASE` can exist purely in the file's local scope. The chain terminates at a registered base (which in turn chains to `ITEM`), so every fluent setter and every default hook is reachable from the leaf.

Contrast with the legacy route, which does `table.Inherit(item, baseTab)` — a shallow *copy* of the base's fields onto the item at registration time — and sets the item's metatable to the base only as a fallback.

**Consequence (intended):** the shared part is never stored, so it can never be bought, spawned, or listed.

**Consequence (accepted):** fields are resolved lazily. Mutating a base after its children are registered changes the children too, because nothing was copied. `uponLoad` handlers, which run over every stored item after all item files have loaded, rely on this being safe.

### The fluent API

Setters return `self` so a whole item is one expression. Most setters are generated by `ITEM:AutoFunction(name, key)` from a `datas` table (`Cost`/`Price` → `cost`, `Description`/`Desc` → `description`, `Category`/`Cat` → `category`, `Team`, `Batch`, `Member` → `membershiplevel`, `REP`/`REPs` → `reps`, `CanUse`, `Size`, `LootName`, `LootPlural`). The aliases exist so call sites read naturally; they are not separate fields.

Hand-written setters exist where one call sets more than one field or has `true`-means-copy semantics:

- `SetName(name, plural)` also sets `plural` (default `name .. "s"`; `true` → same as name; `""` → `false`).
- `SetModel(model, skin, autoStore)` / `SetSkin(skin, autoStore)` / `SetStoreModel` / `SetStoreSkin` — `true` copies from the other side (inventory ↔ store), `autoStore` pushes to the other side. This exists for cosmetic items whose inventory model and market preview differ.
- `SetStore(val)` — `false`/`0` hides from the market; a number both enables the store and sets `batch`.
- `SetColor` / `SetMaterial` — appearance overrides, consumed by `cityrp.item.applyAppearance`.
- `SetMetaSchema` / `AddMetaField` / `RemoveMetaField` / `SetMetaFieldOrder` — see [item-metadata-schema.md](../items/item-metadata-schema.md).
- `CanUse`/`OnUse`, `CanGive`/`OnGive`, … `CanPlace`/`onPlace` — one pair per action in [item-actions.md](../items/item-actions.md). `CanX(nil)` resets to the always-true default.
- `Replaced(by)` / `Replacement(new, old)` — mark an ID as superseded. `Replacement` builds a stub that inherits from the *new* item and registers it under the *old* ID with the replaced flag, so the legacy `onUse` override tells the player what to buy instead.

`SetData(key, value)` and `Merge(tbl)` are the escape hatches for fields with no setter. `ITEM:New` also accepts a data table in either argument position (`New("base", {...})`, `New({...}, "base")`, `New({...})`), which is how table-style definitions are bolted onto the fluent route without a rewrite.

### Load order

Registration order matters because `cityrp.item.new(base)` looks the base up *at call time*. `sh_init.lua` enforces it:

1. `core/items/<folder>` in a fixed list, with `base` first, then ammunition, cars, clothing, …, collectables.
2. `cityrp.plugin.LoadSubResourceItems` — plugin-owned `items/` folders, after core so they can inherit from core bases.
3. `item:uponLoad()` on every stored item.
4. `CityRP.Core.PostItemLoad`.

Within a folder, files load in `file.Find` order. A base defined in the same folder as its children is only safe if it sorts first — which is why the real bases live in `core/items/base/`.

## Alternatives considered

These are reconstructed from the shape of the code rather than from a record of the original discussion.

- **Keep `register(tbl, base)` but add a `hidden` flag to bases.** Rejected in effect: it still pollutes the registry, still needs every consumer (market, `/giveitem`, loot tables, `cityrp.item.get` fuzzy matching) to honour the flag, and doesn't reduce boilerplate. `store = false` already exists and is exactly this half-measure; it hides from the market only.
- **Copy-on-register for the fluent route too (`table.Inherit`).** Would make registration-order mistakes fail loudly (the base is fully materialised) and remove the late-mutation hazard, but breaks `uponLoad`-style post-processing of bases and costs memory across a catalogue of several hundred items. Lazy chaining was kept.
- **A separate new registry.** Rejected; dual registries would have forced every consumer to check both. Reusing `cityrp.item.register` for post-processing is why the fluent route got the legacy fix-ups for free.

## Known sharp edges

Things the design leaves open, documented so they are not rediscovered as bugs. None of these are new; they are consequences of the decisions above.

| Edge | Cause | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Misspelled or not-yet-loaded base is silent.** | `cityrp.item.new(base)` falls through to `setmetatable({}, ITEM)` when `stored[base]` is nil. | `ITEM:New("base_accesory")` registers a working item with `ITEM` defaults (`models/error.mdl`, category `Base`) and no error. Same outcome if the base's file loads later. |
| **Legacy bases do not expose `ITEM` methods.** | A table registered via `cityrp.item.register` with no base has no metatable, so a chain rooted at it never reaches `ITEM`. | `ITEM:New("legacy_base")` returns a table on which `:SetCost` is nil. `cityrp.item.applyAppearance` is a plain function rather than a method for this reason. Fluent items must inherit from fluent or `ITEM`-rooted bases. |
| **Setters called on the global `ITEM` change every item.** | All setters write to `self`; nothing stops `self` being `ITEM` itself. | Always start a chain with `New` or `Clone`. |
| **Clone base IDs are synthetic.** | `Clone()` names an unregistered parent `tmp_base_<file>`. | `item.base` is not guaranteed to be a registered ID; consumers that walk `base` must use `BaseClass`/the metatable, not `stored[item.base]`. |
| **Registration re-runs on hot reload.** | `stored[id]` is overwritten, not guarded. | Re-including an item file replaces the table; anything holding a reference to the old table keeps the stale one. Consistent with [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) footgun #7. |
| **`onPlace` setter is lowercase.** | Preserved for compatibility. | `item:onPlace(fn)` sets the hook; `item:OnPlace` is nil. |
| **No validation at `Register`.** | By design (non-goal). | A missing `name` errors inside `register`'s log-string concatenation rather than with a useful message; a missing `uniqueID` stores the item under `nil`. |

## Consequences for contributors

- New items use `ITEM:New(<real base>)` and chain setters; never `cityrp.item.register` for new code ([modern-apis.md](../modern-apis.md)).
- Shared data between variants goes on an unregistered `local BASE = ITEM:New(...)`, and each variant is `BASE:Clone():...:Register(id)`.
- Do not create a registered item whose only job is inheritance. If a real base is missing, add it under `core/items/base/` so the load order protects it.
- `:Register(id)` must be the last call in the chain; the post-processing in `cityrp.item.register` runs once and does not see later direct mutations (only lazily-chained ones, see above).
- When touching a legacy file, converting it to this route is welcome but must preserve its `uniqueID`s — those are persisted in player inventories.

topics.title: Writing Doc Comments
topics.body:
# Writing Doc Comments

This site is built by [`generate.py`](https://github.com/limelight-development/cityrp2/blob/master/tools/docs/generate.py) from two independent sources, so a doc comment lives or dies depending on which one actually reads it:

1. **`lua-language-server`'s `--doc` JSON export.** LuaLS parses the codebase and exports every doc comment it understands — that means real [LuaCATS](https://luals.github.io/wiki/annotations/) annotations (`--- @param`, `--- @return`, `--- @class`, ...) attached **immediately above** a declaration, with no blank line in between. A blank line between the comment and the code it describes means LuaLS never associates the two, and the comment is silently dropped from the JSON entirely.
2. **`generate.py`'s own raw-source scan**, used only for each file's *leading header comment* (description, `@namespace`, etc). This one tolerates a blank line before the code that follows. Write headers as `---` lines.

Everything else in this page is about what each of those two paths actually understands. For the
annotations themselves — every tag, its fields, the full type syntax, and the Garry's Mod-specific
conventions — see [LuaCATS Annotations](luacats.md).

## Pipeline

```bash
# 1. LuaLS walks the gamemode and exports its own understanding of every doc comment.
lua-language-server --doc=gamemodes/cityrp_2_by_limelightgaming/gamemode \
                     --doc_out_path=tools/docs/out

# 2. generate.py turns that JSON (plus docs/**/*.md) into this site.
python3 tools/docs/generate.py --json tools/docs/out/doc.json \
                                --output tools/docs/build \
                                --style-dir tools/docs/style \
                                --topics docs
```

Files under `core/server`, `core/autogen`, `core/plugins/antihack`, `core/plugins/screengrab`, and every `core/items/<category>` subfolder are excluded from the export entirely — no doc comment in those paths will ever appear on the site.

### Seeing every feature at once

[`tools/docs/fixtures/stubs.lua`](https://github.com/limelight-development/cityrp2/blob/master/tools/docs/fixtures/stubs.lua) is a stub file using every tag, realm, callout, type and section the site renders. It is never loaded, and it sits outside the gamemode so its fake symbols can never reach the published site. Build just that file when changing `generate.py` or the stylesheet — it is far quicker than hunting for a real function that happens to use the feature you touched:

```bash
lua-language-server --doc=tools/docs/fixtures --doc_out_path=tools/docs/stub-out \
                    --configpath=tools/docs/luarc-docs.json
python3 tools/docs/generate.py --json tools/docs/stub-out/doc.json \
                              --output tools/docs/stub-build \
                              --style-dir tools/docs/style --topics docs \
                              --source tools/docs/fixtures
```

That produces two pages: `stubs` for the library-style symbols and `StubEntity` for the metatable ones. `test_generate.py` fails if the stub stops covering a callout kind, a realm, or the example/section/alias tags, so it cannot quietly fall behind the generator.

## Topic files and folders

Every markdown file under `docs/` is published, and the folder it sits in decides where. Top-level files are listed directly under the sidebar's **Topics** heading. A subfolder becomes a single collapsed entry at the bottom of that same list, linking to the folder's index page — `docs/design/x.md` publishes to `topics/design/x.html`, reachable from the **Design Docs** entry. The folder's pages only unfold in the sidebar while you're on one of them, so the Topics list is the same length from everywhere else and a body of design docs doesn't crowd out the technical topics.

Folders nest to any depth. `docs/design/car-boosting/hotwiring.md` sits under **Car Boosting** inside **Design Docs**, and opening it unfolds both — every ancestor of the page you're on, and nothing else. A folder is labelled by its own leaf name; the parent it sits under supplies the rest of the context. Each level of the tree also gets its own index page, and a parent's index links down into its children under a **Sections** heading, so nothing is reachable only from an already-expanded sidebar.

There is no per-folder config; creating the folder is the whole step. Add an `index.md` to give the folder a name and an intro — its `title` becomes the sidebar label. The list of what's in the folder is always generated, never hand-maintained.

`topics/` mirrors `docs/`, so a relative link between two topic files stays correct on the site as well as on GitHub — `generate.py` only swaps the `.md` for `.html`, and leaves any link that doesn't resolve to a topic (`../AGENTS.md`, absolute URLs) alone. That mirroring cuts both ways: **moving a doc into a folder changes its depth, so its own `../` links and everyone else's links to it need updating in the same change.** Headings get GitHub's own anchor slugs, so `plugins.md#keys` works in both places too.

A relative link that points *above* `docs/` — `../AGENTS.md`, `../../gamemodes/…/db.lua` — has no
page to land on, because only `docs/` is published. Those are rewritten to the repo browser rather
than left to 404. `test_generate.py` runs the whole `docs/` tree through the generator and fails on a
link or heading anchor that doesn't resolve, which is the only thing that reliably catches a doc
being moved between folders.

Topic pages with more than two `##` headings get a **Contents** block in the sidebar, and the sidebar
search box covers every topic, module and symbol — it reads `search.json`, fetched on first use.

A page's opening `<h1>` is dropped from the rendered HTML — the title already sits in the header bar above it, so keeping both would print it twice. Keep writing the heading; it's what makes the file readable on GitHub, and it's the fallback when there's no front-matter `title`. Only the first one goes, and only if the page opens with it.

### Front matter

Any topic may open with a `---` block. It's flat `key: value` lines, not real YAML — the docs build has no YAML dependency, and a block that isn't in that shape is left in the page as ordinary markdown rather than silently swallowed.

| Key | Effect |
| :--- | :--- |
| `title` | Sidebar label, page header, and index row. Overrides the first heading, which is otherwise what the title comes from. |
| `status` | Index column. Free text — `Proposed`, `Landed`, `Implemented`, whatever the folder uses. |
| `date` | Index column. |
| `description` | Index column. One line on what the doc covers. |
| `pinned` | `true`/`yes`/`1` lifts the doc to the top of its list, marked with a pin. Anything else, including omitting it, leaves the doc in filename order. |
| `featured` | `true`/`yes`/`1` adds the doc to the **Important Topics** list on the site's front page, regardless of where it lives in the tree. Independent of `pinned` — pinning only affects sidebar order, this is what puts it on the homepage. |
| `index` | `true` promotes the doc to be its folder's landing page. See below. |

A folder index tabulates only the columns some page in that folder actually sets, so a folder using none of them stays a plain list of links. Every field, including ones not listed above, is carried into `api.json` under the topic's `meta` for the `cityrp-docs` MCP server.

### Promoting a page to be the folder index

A folder whose landing page should be one of its own docs — rather than a summary written for the purpose — marks that doc `index: true`. `docs/design/clans/design.md` does this: it already explains what clans are, so the **Clans** sidebar entry points straight at it.

A doc **named after the folder it sits in** is promoted the same way without needing the flag, since that naming almost always means "this is the overview". `docs/design/car-boosting/car-boosting.md` is the **Car Boosting and Ringing** entry for its folder on that basis alone. The name has to match in full: `car-boosting-live-test-plan.md` is not a match.

Precedence, most deliberate first — `index: true`, then an `index.md`, then a folder-name match:

| Folder contains | Landing page |
| :--- | :--- |
| a doc with `index: true` | that doc, whatever it's called |
| `index.md` | `index.md`, with the generated listing below its prose |
| `<folder-name>.md` | that doc |
| none of the above | a generated page listing the folder |

A promoted page keeps its own URL (`topics/design/clans/design.html`, not `index.html`), so links written to it still resolve, and it's written once rather than existing at two addresses. It drops out of the folder's own list, since the folder entry above is now the way to reach it, and its content stands in for the generated listing rather than being prefixed to it. Links down into any *subfolders* are still appended, so promoting a page can't orphan a folder nested below it.

The folder's other pages are then reachable from the sidebar, which is unfolded whenever you're on any page in that folder — including the promoted one. If you want a listing as well as prose, use an `index.md` instead: that keeps the generated table and puts your text above it. Where two of the three mechanisms are present in one folder the table above decides, and the loser becomes an ordinary page in the list; that isn't an error, but it's worth not doing on purpose.

Pinning is scoped to the list the doc is already in — a pinned top-level doc rises within **Topics**, a pinned doc inside a folder rises within that folder's sidebar list and its index table. It doesn't lift a doc out of its folder, and folders themselves can't be pinned; they always sit below the loose files. Pinning several docs keeps them in filename order relative to each other.

## Function/variable-level: use real LuaCATS annotations

Write these as `--- @tag ...` directly above the `function`/assignment they describe, no blank line. `generate.py` reads the native `args`/`returns` LuaLS already resolved from the function signature itself (so types are accurate even if you never repeat them) and only borrows the tag's text for the human-readable description.

| Annotation | Syntax | Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `@param` | `--- @param <name> <type[?][|type...]> [description]` | Primary way to document a parameter. `?` suffix on the type marks it optional. |
| `@return` | `--- @return <type> [<name> [comment]]` | Primary way to document a return value. One `@return` line per return value, in order. |
| `@class` | `--- @class [(exact)] <name>[: <parent>...]` | Defines a struct/type, optionally with inheritance. |
| `@field` | `--- @field [scope] <name> <type[?]> [description]` | Documents a field of a `@class`. `scope` is `public`/`protected`/`private`/`package`. |
| `@type` | `--- @type <type>` | Declares the type of a variable, e.g. `--- @type string[]`. |
| `@generic` | `--- @generic <name> [:parent_type]` | Generic type placeholder for reusable code. |
| `@overload` | `--- @overload fun([param: type...]): [return_type]` | Documents an additional call signature. |
| `@alias` | `--- @alias <name> <type>` | Names a type (or enum) for reuse elsewhere. |
| `@enum` | `--- @enum [(key)] <name>` | Marks a table as an enum, usable at runtime. |
| `@cast` | `--- @cast <value_name> [+|-]<type|?>[, ...]` | Narrows/widens a variable's type from this point on. |
| `@deprecated` | `--- @deprecated` | Marks the item outdated (LuaLS strikes it through in editors). This is the LuaCATS spelling — see also the codebase's own `@deprecated` callout below, which the two share. |
| `@nodiscard` | `--- @nodiscard` | Warns if the return value is ignored at the call site. |
| `@async` | `--- @async` | Marks a function as asynchronous. |
| `@see` | `--- @see <symbol>` | Cross-reference to another documented symbol. |
| `@operator` | `--- @operator <op>[(param_type)]:<return_type>` | Documents an operator metamethod (`__add`, etc). |
| `@package` / `@private` / `@protected` | `--- @package` / `--- @private` / `--- @protected` | Restricts where the item is considered accessible. |
| `@version` | `--- @version [<|>]<version>` | Required Lua/LuaJIT version. |
| `@meta` | `--- @meta [name]` | Marks a whole file as definition-only (not real, executable code). |
| `@as` | `--[[@as <type>]]` | Inline cast forcing a type onto an expression. |
| `@diagnostic` | `--- @diagnostic <state>:<diagnostic>` | Suppresses/enables a specific LuaLS diagnostic. |

Two annotations are explicitly **not** used here, even though LuaLS supports them:

- **`@module`** — LuaLS reserves this for its own `require()`-return-type inference and silently drops any doc comment that uses it. Use the codebase's own [`@namespace`](#file-header-tags-this-codebases-own-set) tag instead (see below) — this is the single most common mistake when porting old LDoc comments.
- **`@vararg`** — deprecated by LuaLS itself in favor of `--- @param ... <type> [description]` for documenting varargs.

Only `@param` and `@return` currently have their *description* folded back into the rendered page by `generate.py` (by parameter name, and by return position, respectively) — the other annotations above are understood natively by LuaLS/your editor for hover/autocomplete/type-checking, but `generate.py` doesn't render most of them specially yet.

Minimal example:

```lua
--- Gets the value of an env-var.
--- @param name string The env-var to get
--- @return string The value found, nil otherwise
function ENV:Get(name)
	...
end
```

## Function/table-level: this codebase's own tags

These are custom to `generate.py`, not LuaCATS — but like `@param`/`@return`, they're written **directly above the function or table they describe**, with no blank line, since `generate.py` only reads the tags attached to that specific declaration's own doc comment.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Write these with a space after the dashes — `--- @state server`, not `---@state server`.
>
> LuaLS parses `---@tag` as an annotation and drops any tag it doesn't recognise, so the tag never reaches `generate.py` and the whole line vanishes with no error. `--- @tag` is description text as far as LuaLS is concerned, which is exactly how these survive into the export for `generate.py` to re-parse. The one `@usage` in the tree was written `---@usage` and had therefore never rendered anything.

The tags:

| Tag | Purpose |
| :--- | :--- |
| `@section <title>` | Starts a new named subsection on the module page. Every following item in the file (until the next `@section`) is grouped under it, so in practice it's usually only written once per group rather than on every function. The tag's own value is the heading, so write it as you want it read — `@section Rank Colours`. A one-word lowercase slug (`@section functions`, the older form) is title-cased into "Functions". |
| `@state <word>` | One of `client`, `server`, `menu`, `shared`, `global`, `clmenu` — drives the realm badge shown next to the item. If a function omits it, it falls back to whatever `@state` the file's header comment declared. |
| `@example <code>` | Renders an "Example" code block after the parameters and returns. Continuation lines are kept as lines, so a multi-line example stays multi-line. Not `@usage` — see below. |

### Callout tags

Seven tags render as callout boxes, in the manner of the [GMod wiki's note boxes](https://wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Structures). They come out as the same boxes a topic gets from `> [!WARNING]`, so the site has one visual language for "read this before you use it" rather than two, and each has its own colour.

They always appear in this order on an entry — whether you should be using this at all, then what is wrong with it, then advisories — regardless of the order they were written in:

| Tag | Box | Stock text when no text is given |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `@deprecated [text]` | Deprecated | "This function is deprecated and may be removed in a future version." |
| `@internal [text]` | Internal | "This function is internal. Whilst you can call it, you probably shouldn't." |
| `@bug <text>` | Bug | — |
| `@warning <text>` | Warning | — |
| `@ambig [text]` | Ambiguous | "This entry is unclear or incomplete." |
| `@validate [text]` | Validate | "This entry has not been checked against the code recently." |
| `@note <text>` | Note | — |

`@bugs`, `@warns`, `@notes` and `@ambiguous` are accepted as alternative spellings. Several spellings of the same tag on one function collapse into a single box rather than producing two. The text is rendered as markdown, so links and `code` work inside a callout.

Topics can use any of these as GFM alerts too — `> [!BUG]`, `> [!DEPRECATED]` — alongside the standard `[!NOTE]`, `[!TIP]`, `[!IMPORTANT]`, `[!WARNING]` and `[!CAUTION]`.

```lua
--- Old warrant lookup, kept for legacy callers.
--- @deprecated Use cityrp.warrants.issue instead.
--- @bug Does not account for expired warrants.
--- @state server
--- @example cityrp.warrants.legacyLookup(ply)
function cityrp.warrants.legacyLookup(ply)
	...
end
```

Not `@usage`: it is an LDoc tag, and `standards-diff.py` rejects it in CI. Supporting it here would mean the docs rendering something nobody is allowed to write.

## Constant families: `@alias` gathers the constants it names

A page that declares a long run of prefixed constants — the 87 `COL_*` colours, the 26 `TEAM_*`
jobs — would otherwise list every one of them as a top-level entry, interleaved alphabetically with
everything else the page declares. An `@alias` over those constants turns them into a section of
their own instead: the alias becomes the heading, its constants sit beneath it, and it gets its own
line in the page's **Contents**.

```lua
--- Every colour the gamemode ships as a constant.
--- @section Colours
--- @alias COL
---| `COL_WHITE`
---| `COL_BLACK`
---| `COL_UI_GREY`

--- @section Generic
COL_WHITE = Color(255)
COL_BLACK = Color(0)

--- @section Limelight UI Guidelines
COL_UI_GREY = Color(41, 41, 41, 230)
```

- The alias's description and `@section` are its own — `@section` names the heading (defaulting to
  the alias name, so `COL` without one), and the description renders as the section's intro.
- `@section` on the constants themselves subdivides the family, exactly as it groups functions
  elsewhere on the page.
- The constants must be documented on the same page as the alias. An alias whose members are string
  literals (`@alias WARRANT "bolo" | "search" | "arrest"`) or other types (`@alias Colour \`COL\` |
  \`Color\``) has no constants to gather, so it stays an ordinary entry — rendered as an **Accepted
  values** list rather than the raw code block LuaLS hands over.
- Two constants is the minimum; below that a heading costs more than it saves.

Deep links are unaffected: `#COL_WHITE` still lands on the constant, and `#COL` now lands on the
family heading it used to be an entry in.

## Class pages: `@namespace <ClassName>` gathers a class's members

A metatable class is re-opened all over the tree — `Player` in nine files, so that a library can hang
one helper on it without owning the whole metatable. Each member would otherwise land on the page of
whichever file happens to declare it, or, if that file claims no `@namespace` of its own, on a page
derived from a *different* file's path entirely.

Declaring `@namespace <ClassName>` on one of the class's files makes that the class's page, and every
`<ClassName>.member` follows it there, wherever it was written:

```lua
--- Shared Player Metafunctions.
--- @namespace Player          <-- claims the page

--- @class Player
local pMeta = FindMetaTable("Player")
```

```lua
--- Access and Flags - Server.
--- @namespace cityrp.access   <-- this file's own page

--- @class Player
--- @field BlacklistTime fun(self: Player, access: string): integer|string
local pMeta = FindMetaTable("Player")
```

`ply:BlacklistTime()` renders on **Player**; `cityrp.access.hasAccess` stays on **cityrp.access**.
Both are declared in the second file.

This is opt-in, and deliberately so. `Player`, `GM`, `PLUGIN`, `ITEM`, `CONSOLE` and
`WEIGHTED_RANDOM` claim a page this way. A `@class` that exists to describe a library's own table —
`Pass`, `Logger`, `RankData` — declares no such namespace, so its fields stay on that library's page
next to the thing they describe, which is where they belong.

The page's own intro comes from a file that *claims* the namespace, not from whichever contributor
file sorts first, so the Player page does not introduce itself as "Access and flags - server.".

### Metatables and panels get their own sidebar sections

Two groups are split out of the flat **Modules** list, both classified by where the code lives rather
than by a tag every file has to remember:

- **Metatables** — a `@class` declared in `gamemode/core/metatables/`. `Player`, `Entity` and
  `Vehicle`. These claim a page the same way a `@namespace` class does *without* needing to declare
  one: `Player` already did, but `Entity` and `Vehicle` declare only `@class`, so their members were
  scattering onto whichever library page LuaLS listed first — exactly the problem the `@namespace`
  opt-in exists to solve, never applied to them.
- **Panels** — a module whose members all come from a `derma/` folder. "All", not "some", so a
  library that happens to define one panel helper stays under Modules.

Neither needs anything added to a Lua file. A section with nothing in it is omitted, so the Panels
heading only appears once derma files are documented — today almost none are, since a panel's methods
hang off a file-local `PANEL` table that LuaLS can't attribute to anything.

## File-header tags: this codebase's own set

The very first comment in a file (`---` line comments, blank line before the code is fine) is scanned separately for these tags — they are **not** LuaCATS and LuaLS doesn't know about them:

| Tag | Purpose |
| :--- | :--- |
| `@namespace <name>` | **Not `@module`.** Groups every doc'd item in this file onto one page named `<name>`, merging with any other file that declares the same namespace (e.g. a `cl_*.lua`/`sv_*.lua` pair). Without it, the page falls back to the file's own dotted path (`core.libraries.sv_foo`). Must not contain `..`. Only makes sense here — write it once, on the file header. |
| `@state <word>` | Same word list as the function-level tag above. Written on the file header, this becomes the *default* realm badge for every item in the file that doesn't declare its own `@state`. |
| `@copyright`, `@release`, `@author` | Accepted and parsed, but **not currently rendered anywhere** on the generated site — keep them for humans reading the source, don't rely on them showing up on the page. |

Write the file header as a run of `---` lines:

```lua
--- One-line description.
--- @copyright 2015-2026 Limelight Gaming
--- @author Someone
--- @namespace some.namespace
```

## Putting it together

```lua
--- Player-facing warrant helpers.
--- @namespace cityrp.warrants

--- Issue a warrant against a player.
--- @param ply Player The player to warrant.
--- @param reason string Why the warrant was issued.
--- @return boolean Whether the warrant was successfully issued.
--- @state server
function cityrp.warrants.issue(ply, reason)
	...
end
```

topics.title: Vehicle Emergency Lighting (ELS)
topics.body:
# Vehicle Emergency Lighting (ELS)

Civilian-installable emergency lighting is handled by the `Vehicles` plugin
(`core/plugins/vehicles/sh_init.lua` / `sv_init.lua`). A player uses one of four items on a
vehicle they own, and the plugin swaps in a Photon lighting preset for that model.

## Groups

| Constant  | Item (`uniqueID`) | Photon flag | Gate |
| :-------- | :----------------- | :--- | :--- |
| `POLICE`  | `veh_pwl` | `CityRP_IsPoliceELS` | LEO pass/`orange`, Presidential pass/`red`, `IsLawenforcement()`, `IsPresident()`, or `IsRescue()` (ERT) |
| `WARNING` | `veh_awl` | `CityRP_IsAmbers` | None (amber warning lights) |
| `ARROWS`  | `veh_arrows` | `CityRP_IsArrowboard` | None (amber + directional arrowboard) |
| `MEDICAL` | `veh_mwl` | `CityRP_IsMedicalELS` | `IsDoctor()` or `IsRescue()` (ERT; covers Paramedic and Fire Chief) |

Gates live in `onVehicleLightsUsed` in `sv_init.lua`. Each item's `onUse` just calls
`onVehicleLightsUsed(ply, <GROUP>)`. The Photon flag column is the field a preset sets to claim the
group for itself — see [Self-registering from a Photon file](#self-registering-from-a-photon-file).

## `carLighting` — model to Photon preset

`carLighting[string.lower(model)][GROUP]` maps a vehicle model to the *name* a Photon preset was
registered under (`list.Set("Vehicles", name, V)` — the key, which is conventionally also
`V.Name`). `onVehicleLightsUsed` looks the preset up with `list.Get("Vehicles")[loadout]` and
merges it onto the vehicle's `VehicleTable`.

Most entries are hand-written at the top of `sh_init.lua`:

```lua
carLighting["models/metrohd/audi_a6.mdl"] = {"AudiA6_RB", "AudiA6_AW"}
-- array-style: index 1 = POLICE, 2 = WARNING, 3 = ARROWS (matches the constants below)
carLighting["models/tdmcars/trucks/gmc_c5500.mdl"] = {[WARNING] = "GMCC5500_AW"}
-- or explicit group keys when a model only supports some groups
```

## Self-registering from a Photon file

A Photon vehicle registration (an `addons/vehicles_emvu/lua/autorun/*.lua` file, or any other
`list.Set("Vehicles", name, V)` call) can set its group's flag from the [Groups](#groups) table to
claim itself as that group's preset, instead of requiring a hand-written `carLighting` entry:

```lua
local V = {
	Name = name,
	Model = "models/metrohd/audi_a6.mdl",
	-- ...
	CityRP_IsPoliceELS = true,
}
list.Set("Vehicles", V.Name, V)
```

`mergeSelfRegisteredLighting()` (in `sh_init.lua`, runs once from the `CityRP.Core.PostItemLoad`
hook) scans every registered Photon vehicle and fills in any `carLighting[model][group]` slot that
isn't already set. **A hand-written entry always wins** — self-registration only fills gaps, it
never overwrites a hand-authored mapping.

Either kind of clash is dropped instead of silently picking one, and logged via
`PLUGIN.logger:Warning(...)` (`cityrp.logging`, namespace `plugin.Vehicles`; see
[logging.md](logging.md)) so it shows up in console/DB without being confused for an audit event:

- A self-registered preset tries to claim a group another self-registered preset already claimed
  for that model.
- A self-registered preset tries to claim a group a hand-written `carLighting` entry already set
  for that model.

Use self-registration for new Photon presets going forward — it keeps the "which vehicle supports
which lighting" fact next to the preset that answers it, instead of requiring a second edit in
`sh_init.lua` that's easy to forget. The hand-written table isn't being migrated off; it stays for
existing entries and as an override when you need one preset for a model to win over another's
self-registration.

topics.title: Environment (Env-vars)
topics.body:
# Environment (Env-vars)

The CityRP env.lua (`ENV`) provides a wrapper for ``gmsv_environ``, giving access to the runtime (Docker) environment variables.

## API

### Get environment variable

**`ENV:Get("name")`**

Returns string or nil when environment variable was not found.

Example:

```lua
local password = ENV:Get("MY_PASS")
```

## HowTo: Setup environment variables (panel)

In order to pass environment variables to the runtime, you will have to register them via the Gamepanel first.

> [!NOTE]
> If you are not a panel admin, please ask one to register the variables for you.

1. Login to the admin interface: [https://panel.limelightgaming.net/admin](https://panel.limelightgaming.net/admin)
2. Click on "Nests" on the sidebar at the bottom left
3. Select the Egg Group "Limelight"
4. Open the Egg "Garrys Mod - CityRP" and click on "Variables"
5. Now you can add environment variables and decide whether panel users shall view+edit them etc...


## HowTo: Edit exisiting environments variables for a server

1. Just select a server in the panel and click on the "Startup" menu.

2. In the startup menu you can edit environment variables for that server.

> [!NOTE]
> This only works when the admin has given view/edit permissions for these environment variables.
> If not, only an admin can edit them in the admin panel startup menu for that server.

topics.title: Image Hosts
topics.body:
# Image Hosts

Players can point several systems at an image URL and have the server or every other client
fetch it. Each of those systems used to carry its own copy of the "safe hosts" list, and the
copies drifted — the billboard UI advertised a host the validator rejected, and the 3D sign
editor accepted a host the Material URL tool had already dropped.

There is now one list, in
`gamemode/core/libraries/sh_imagehosts.lua`, exposed as `cityrp.imageHosts`. It is shared
(client and server), loads with the core libraries, and is the only place a host name should
appear.

## Maintaining the list

Edit `cityrp.imageHosts.definitions`:

```lua
cityrp.imageHosts.definitions = {
	{host = "cdn.limelightgaming.net", enabled = true, reason = "Limelight's own CDN."},
	{host = "i.ibb.co", enabled = true, reason = "ImgBB direct image host."},
	{host = "i.postimg.cc", enabled = true, reason = "Postimages direct image host."},
	{host = "i.imgur.com", enabled = false, reason = "UK age verification broke server-side and client-side downloads."}
}
```

- Set `enabled = false` rather than deleting an entry, so the reason a host was dropped stays
  on record. Disabled entries are invisible to every consumer.
- Give the *exact* hostname players will link to. Matching is exact and case-insensitive;
  subdomains are not implied, so `i.ibb.co` does not permit `evil.i.ibb.co`.
- Prefer hosts that serve the raw image bytes. `imgur.com/abc` returns an HTML page;
  `i.imgur.com/abc.png` returns the image.

Accepted file extensions live alongside it in `cityrp.imageHosts.extensions`.

The UIs that list approved hosts read them from here, so no UI text needs updating when the
list changes. Player-facing prose goes through `getHostList()` / `getExtensionList()`, which
use `FormatList` so the wording matches the rest of the gamemode; UI that lays the hostnames
out itself (one per line, bullet-separated) uses `getHosts()` and does its own formatting.

## Using the list

Validate whole URLs with `cityrp.imageHosts.validate`, which normalises the input and returns
a player-facing reason on rejection:

```lua
local url, reason = cityrp.imageHosts.validate(input, true) -- true = also require png/jpg/jpeg

if not url then
	ply:Notify(reason, NOTIFY_ERROR)
	return
end
```

Other entry points:

| Function | Purpose |
| :--- | :--- |
| `cityrp.imageHosts.validate(url, requireExtension)` | Normalise and check a URL. Returns the normalised URL, or `nil` plus a reason. |
| `cityrp.imageHosts.isAllowed(url)` | Boolean check of a full URL. |
| `cityrp.imageHosts.isAllowedHost(host)` | Boolean check of a bare hostname. |
| `cityrp.imageHosts.normalise(url)` | Lowercase the scheme, assume `https://` when none is given, strip trailing slashes, reject anything that is not http or https. Does not check the allowlist. |
| `cityrp.imageHosts.getHost(url)` | Parse the hostname out of a URL. |
| `cityrp.imageHosts.hasAllowedExtension(url)` | Check the file extension only. |
| `cityrp.imageHosts.getHosts()` | Copy of the enabled hostnames, for UI that lays them out itself. |
| `cityrp.imageHosts.getHostList(conjunction)` | The enabled hostnames as prose, via `FormatList` — "a, b or c". |
| `cityrp.imageHosts.getExtensionList(conjunction)` | The accepted extensions as prose, the same way. |

### Schemes

Both `http` and `https` are accepted, and a URL with no scheme is assumed to be `https`.

Plain http means the image bytes can be tampered with in transit by anything sitting between
the server and the host. That is a deliberate, accepted trade-off rather than an oversight: the
host is still allowlisted, the response is only ever decoded as an image, and enough approved
links arrive as http that rejecting them broke more than it protected. Anything that is neither
http nor https — `ftp://`, `javascript:`, `data:`, a protocol-relative `//host/path` — is
rejected.

A URL carrying userinfo (`user@host`) or an explicit port is also rejected outright rather than
parsed. That is not new hardening — the per-system pattern matches this library replaced
already rejected both, because they required `/` or end-of-string straight after the hostname.
It is called out here because parsing the authority instead of pattern-matching it is exactly
where that property gets dropped by accident, and dropping it would let a crafted authority
read as one host to the validator and another to whatever fetches the URL.

## Current consumers

| System | Where it validates |
| :--- | :--- |
| Billboards (`plugins/billboards`) | `sh/zad_url_validation.lua` wraps the library; the config UI lists the hosts from it. |
| Material URL tool (`addons/material_url_2559426779`) | `lua/autorun/materialurl_whitelist.lua` bridges `MatURL.checkURL` onto the library. |
| 3D signs (`addons/3dsign`, `entities/cityrp_3d_sign`) | The editor validates as you type; the apply net messages re-check server-side. |

The Material URL bridge runs from `lua/autorun`, which loads **before** the gamemode. It
therefore resolves `cityrp.imageHosts` at call time and denies the URL if the library is not
loaded yet, rather than caching a snapshot. Any addon-side consumer added later needs to do
the same.

## What this does not cover

rRadio keeps its own allowlist of audio stream hosts (`rRadio.config.AllowedHosts`). Those are
stream endpoints with different rules — plain `http` is normal for them, and the list is
maintained against the station packs — so they are deliberately not merged into
`cityrp.imageHosts`.

topics.title: Item Actions
topics.body:
# Item Actions

Every item action (Use, Give, Remove, Drop, Destroy, Pickup, Sell, Place — the same set the inventory panel uses to generate its buttons) follows the same two-hook pattern: a `canX` check that decides whether the action is allowed at all, and an `onX` handler that performs the action's effect and can veto the library's default follow-up behaviour.

## `canX` — is this allowed?

`canX(ply, ...)` is checked before the action runs. It returns a boolean, and optionally a reason string to show the player if it returns `false`.

```lua
function ITEM:canDrop(ply, pos, amt)
	return false, "You cannot drop this car."
end
```

If `canX` returns `false`, the action is stopped immediately — `onX` is never called, and no server-side state (inventory, money) changes.

## `onX` — do the thing, optionally overriding the default effect

`onX(ply, ...)` is called once `canX` has passed. Most actions have a default effect that runs immediately afterwards — deducting the item from the player's inventory, giving money, spawning an entity, and so on. `onX` can suppress that default effect by explicitly returning `false` (optionally with a message string, shown to the player the same way `canX`'s does). Any other return value — including no return at all — lets the default effect proceed.

| Action | Default effect if `onX` doesn't return `false` |
| --- | --- |
| `onUse` | Item removed from inventory |
| `onGive` | Item transferred to the recipient, money/logs recorded |
| `onDrop` | Item removed from inventory, entity spawned in the world |
| `onPlace` | Item removed from inventory, entity spawned in the world |
| `onDestroy` | Item removed from inventory |
| `onSell` | Item removed from inventory, money given to the player |
| `onPickup` | The owned vehicle entity is removed |
| `onRemove` | None — `onRemove` *is* the effect (e.g. unequipping a worn item); there's nothing further to suppress |

This mirrors the way DOM event handlers work: `canX` is like checking whether an event is cancellable in advance, and returning `false` from `onX` is like calling `preventDefault()` — the handler still ran, it just declined the library's default follow-up.

## Worked example

The `bmwm3gtr46` vehicle item is untradeable and undroppable. It uses `canGive`/`canDrop` to refuse the action outright with a player-facing reason, and — as defence in depth, in case a caller ever bypasses the `can` gate — also has `onGive`/`onDrop` return `false` with the same message:

```lua
function ITEM:canDrop(ply, pos) return false, "You cannot drop this car." end
function ITEM:canGive(ply, to, amt) return false, "You cannot trade this car." end

function ITEM:onGive(ply, amt, to) return false, "You cannot trade this car." end
function ITEM:onDrop(ply, pos) return false, "You cannot drop this car." end
```

In practice, `canX` alone is enough to block a normal action — use it when you simply want to disallow something. Reach for the `onX` override when the handler needs to run custom logic first and only conditionally allow the default effect afterwards (for example, consuming an item only if using it succeeded).

topics.title: Item Metadata Schema
topics.body:
# Item Metadata Schema

This document describes the schema-based item metadata system.

## Why this exists

Legacy metadata was stored as opaque strings (for example `plate=ABC-123`) and parsed manually in many files. That made refactors brittle and made field removal unsafe.

The schema system allows items or bases to declare supported metadata fields and silently ignore removed/unknown fields.

## Core APIs

Shared library: `core/libraries/sh_itemmeta.lua`

- `cityrp.itemmeta.GetSchema(itemOrID)`
- `cityrp.itemmeta.GetEditableFields(itemOrID)`
- `cityrp.itemmeta.Encode(data)`
- `cityrp.itemmeta.Normalize(itemOrID, rawMeta)`
- `cityrp.itemmeta.NormalizeKey(itemOrID, rawMeta)`
- `cityrp.itemmeta.Decode(itemOrID, rawMeta)`
- `cityrp.itemmeta.GetField(itemOrID, rawMeta, field, default)`
- `cityrp.itemmeta.SetField(itemOrID, rawMeta, field, value)`
- `cityrp.itemmeta.RemoveField(itemOrID, rawMeta, field)`
- `cityrp.itemmeta.NewContext(itemOrID, rawMeta)`
- `cityrp.itemmeta.Commit(ply, itemID, amount, oldMeta, context)`
- `cityrp.itemmeta.FormatName(itemOrID, baseName, rawMeta)`
- `cityrp.itemmeta.FormatDetails(itemOrID, rawMeta)`
- `cityrp.itemmeta.NormalizeDisplayKey(itemOrID, rawMeta)`
- `cityrp.itemmeta.GetMatchingStacks(itemOrID, stacks, inputMeta)`
- `cityrp.itemmeta.ResolveInventoryKey(itemOrID, stacks, inputMeta)`

Item hooks receive `(..., meta, metaContext)` — raw meta string first, then the mutable context. Dirty context is committed automatically from `onUse` when the item is kept (`return false`) and from `onGive` before the inventory transfer. Paths that remove the item (`destroy`/`sell`/`drop`/`place`) do not commit because the stack is leaving inventory.

## Declaring schema on items

Use item metatable helpers:

- `ITEM:SetMetaSchema(schema)`
- `ITEM:AddMetaField(name, definition)`
- `ITEM:RemoveMetaField(name)`
- `ITEM:SetMetaFieldOrder(order)`
- `ITEM:MetaContext(meta)`

Schema shape:

```lua
:SetMetaSchema({
	fields = {
		plate = {
			type = "string",
			label = "Plate"
		},
		turbo = {
			type = "boolean",
			title = false
		}
	},
	order = {"plate", "turbo"}
})
```

Fields are optional by default: a missing value is omitted unless `default` is set.

## Hidden fields

Mark field definitions with `hidden = true` to keep them in the storage/stacking key while excluding them from F1 names, F1 detail text, and display-key grouping:

```lua
appearance = {
	type = "string",
	hidden = true
}
```

Storage still uses the full canonical key (`NormalizeKey`). UI and fuzzy matching use the visible subset (`NormalizeDisplayKey`).

## Title vs details

Mark a field with `title = false` to keep it in F1 details / display keys while omitting it from the short inventory title:

```lua
springs = {
	type = "number",
	label = "Springs",
	title = false
}
```

Example with `base_vehicle` (`plate` in title, `springs`/`turbo` details-only):

- title: `2013 Government Taurus (TEST)`
- details: `Plate: TEST, Springs: 3, Turbo: On`

`springs` and `turbo` are applied at spawn through `cityrp.vehicleparams` (see
[vehicle-params.md](../vehicle-params.md)). Additional upgrade fields should register modifiers
there rather than patching `SpawnVehicle` directly.

## Fuzzy inventory matching

`GetMatchingStacks` and `ResolveInventoryKey` support:

- exact canonical keys
- legacy raw keys before normalization
- partial visible-field matches (for example `plate=ABC-123`)
- bare values for single visible-field items (for example `ABC-123` on license plates)

When multiple hidden variants share the same visible metadata, binds that only specify visible fields resolve to the first stack for single-quantity `use`/`pickup`/`remove` commands. Multi-quantity or trade commands require a specific stack or the F1 menu.

## Testing metadata (including multi-field)

`/giveitem` accepts a `meta:` argument immediately after the amount. Multiple fields are separated with `;` (also `&` / `|`):

```text
/giveitem <player> Policecar 1 meta:plate=TEST;springs=3;turbo=1 testing multi meta
/giveitem <player> license_plate 1 meta:plate=ABC123 testing plate item
```

`base_vehicle` already declares `plate`, `springs`, and `turbo`, so any vehicle item is a convenient multi-meta test target. After giving, F1 should show:

- title: `2013 Government Taurus (TEST)` (`springs`/`turbo` use `title = false`)
- details line: `Plate: TEST, Springs: 3, Turbo: On`

Boolean fields accept `1` / `0` / `true` / `false`. Do not put spaces inside the `meta:` token (argument parsing splits on spaces).

### Building the metadata in a menu instead

Running `/giveitem` or `/takeitem` with no arguments at all opens a picker (the `itemgrantmenu` plugin) instead of the usage error. It builds one input per schema field from `GetEditableFields`, so the field names, types, enums, `min`/`max` and defaults come straight from the item rather than having to be remembered — a `boolean` or `enum` field gets a drop-down, a `number` field an entry that coerces and clamps to its declared range, and a `string` field free text.

The metadata section only appears for items that declare a schema. There is no free-text passthrough for items that don't: a value with no field to hold it and no type to check it against is exactly what the schema exists to prevent. Taking a stack that already carries schemaless metadata still works — the stored value is passed back untouched — it just cannot be typed in by hand. Use the `meta:` token for that.

A field that declares no `label` is captioned from its own key (`serial_number` becomes "Serial number"), which is also the fallback `FormatDetails` uses, so the menu and the F1 detail line caption a field the same way.

The menu submits through the ordinary command handler, so every check, notification and log entry is identical to typing the command. It is not restricted by the token's space rule, though: because the arguments are already split when they reach the handler, a value with a space in it (`BAD C0P`) can be entered in the menu even though it cannot be typed as `meta:plate=BAD C0P`.

In take mode the item list starts on the target's actual stacks, showing each one's quantity and its formatted detail text, so an item held under several metadata variants can be picked apart precisely.

## Silent field removal

Mark field definitions with `removed = true` (or use `ITEM:RemoveMetaField("field")`).

When metadata is normalized:

- removed fields are dropped silently
- unknown fields are dropped silently for schema-based items
- invalid values are dropped silently (or clamped when min/max is set)

## Migration file

Inventory meta is normalized by migration `0006_normalize_item_meta_schema`:

- empty/`NULL` meta values become the canonical empty key `"0"`
- stacks that would collide on `(steamid, item, meta)` after that rewrite are merged (quantities summed) before the update
- plate values are left unchanged — spaces in plates are intentional (e.g. `BAD C0P` ≠ `BADC0P`)

It runs automatically via the migrations runner (`core/libraries/sv_migrations.lua`).

meta.description: What items are, the three categories they fall into, and how to define one.

topics.body:
Items are one of the most simple parts to CityRP 2, yet one of the widest ranging, due to their use within every sector of the gamemode, and constant development.

## Types of Items

Items currently fall into 3 distinct categories.

| Item Type | Status |
| --- | --- |
| Table | Deprecated, Majority of Items |
| Parented Table | Deprecated, Mostly Vehicles |
| Item Class | Active, Development |

> [!WARNING]
> `cityrp.item.register({})` (Table Items and Table Items with Inherence, below) is deprecated. **New items must use the Class-Based Items pattern** (`ITEM:New(...)`) described at the end of this page. The two table-based patterns are documented here only because they still make up most existing items.

### Table Items

Table items are the simplest, being mearly a table and a call to item.register.

```lua
local ITEM = {}
ITEM.name = "My Special Item"
ITEM.cost = 999
ITEM.description = [[Stuff and things are done by my super cool item.]]
ITEM.uniqueID = "specialitem"

cityrp.item.register(ITEM)
```

Whilst the simplest, these are also often the largest, if code is repeated, due to the fact that elements must be duplicated in their entirety. For example, for the suit items, even though there may be 10 or more suits with the same price, they must be repeated each time.

### Table Items with Inherence
Similar to the table items, these items simple pass a table to cityrp.item.register. However, passing a second argument to register will cause it to take that already-registered item, and use it as a parent.

```lua
if not cityrp.plugin.get("vehicles") then return end

local ITEM = {}
ITEM.name = "1981 Ford F150"
ITEM.cost = 160000
ITEM.model = "models/talonvehicles/tal_f150_1981.mdl"
ITEM.uniqueID = "81fordf150"

cityrp.item.register(ITEM, "base_vehicle")
```

This means that utility functions and shared information can stay on the base, reducing the duplication between files.

However, this has the downside of requiring that each base item is registered, and thus may accidentally become available to end users.

### Class-Based Items.
To combat this, the alternative is class-based items. These use a completely different style to tabular items, can contain multiple items in the same file with ease, and can base themselves without registration.

```lua
local BASE = ITEM:New("base_accessory")
	:SetCost(10000)
	:SetModel("models/modified/backpack_2.mdl", 1, true)
	:SetCategory("Accessories")
	:SetDescription([[A modern camping backpack to carry all your gear.]])
	:SetOffEmote("takes off their backpack.")

BASE:Clone()
	:SetName("Navy and Tangerine Camping Backpack")
	:SetOnEmote("puts on their navy and tangerine camping backpack.")
	:Register("backpacknavy_2")

BASE:Clone()
	:SetName("Olive and Blue Camping Backpack")
	:SetSkin(2, true)
	:SetOnEmote("puts on their olive and blue camping backpack.")
	:Register("backpackolive_2")

BASE:Clone()
	:SetName("Red, White and Green Camping Backpack")
	:SetSkin(3, true)
	:SetOnEmote("puts on their red, white and green camping backpack.")
	:Register("backpackred_2")
```

In the above example, the base item is the accessory base, but the camping backpacks have data which is shared between each element, which is also put into the base. The base is then cloned, data updated, and then only then is it registered.

For the rationale behind this route — why inheritance is a lazy metatable chain, how load order protects bases, and the known sharp edges — see [design/items-registration.md](../design/items-registration.md).

## Related

- [Item Actions](item-actions.md) — the `canX`/`onX` hook pair behind Use, Give, Drop and the rest
- [Item Metadata Schema](item-metadata-schema.md) — per-instance metadata fields and their types

topics.title: Console Logging Library
topics.body:
# Console Logging Library

The CityRP console logging library (`cityrp.logging`) provides a robust, namespaced, level-filterable logging facility for developer diagnostics and runtime troubleshooting.

## Overview

**Purpose**: Provide structured logging with configurable levels for core systems and plugins.

**Key Features**:
- Hierarchical namespaced loggers with inheritance
- Configurable log levels (DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR, CRITICAL, FATAL)
- Special levels (ALWAYS, NEVER, INHERIT, DEFAULT)
- Colored console output via `MsgC`
- Automatic persistence to `cityrp.logs` for WARNING+ messages
- Runtime configuration via console commands
- Safe handling of unvalidated input
- Performance-optimized with lazy evaluation and caching
- Extensible sink API for custom log destinations

**Important**: This library is for **developer diagnostics only**. For audit logging (player actions, admin actions, transactions), continue using `cityrp.logs.add()` directly.

## Log Levels

### Numeric Mapping

| Level      | Numeric Value | Description                                      |
|------------|---------------|--------------------------------------------------|
| `INHERIT`  | -1            | Recursively inherit from parent (default for non-root loggers) |
| `ALWAYS`   | 0             | Bypass logger-level filtering (sinks may still filter) |
| `DEBUG`    | 20            | Low-level diagnostic info                        |
| `INFO`     | 30            | Routine operational logs                         |
| `WARNING`  | 40            | Unexpected but non-breaking situations           |
| `DEFAULT`  | 40            | Alias for WARNING (default for root logger)      |
| `ERROR`    | 50            | Errors requiring investigation                   |
| `CRITICAL` | 60            | Serious failures                                 |
| `FATAL`    | 70            | Highest severity; immediate attention required   |
| `NEVER`    | 100           | Suppress all output from this logger             |

### Level Constants

Access level constants via `cityrp.logging.levels`:

```lua
cityrp.logging.levels.INHERIT   -- -1
cityrp.logging.levels.ALWAYS    -- 0
cityrp.logging.levels.DEBUG     -- 20
cityrp.logging.levels.INFO      -- 30
cityrp.logging.levels.WARNING   -- 40
cityrp.logging.levels.DEFAULT   -- 40 (alias)
cityrp.logging.levels.ERROR     -- 50
cityrp.logging.levels.CRITICAL  -- 60
cityrp.logging.levels.FATAL     -- 70
cityrp.logging.levels.NEVER     -- 100
```

### Level Semantics

- **INHERIT (-1)**: Logger does not define its own level; resolve effective level by recursively checking parent. This is the implicit default for all non-root loggers until explicitly set.
- **ALWAYS (0)**: Bypasses the logger's effective level check. Entry is always dispatched to sinks (subject to sink-level filtering). Useful for critical output that must not be suppressed.
- **NEVER (100)**: Suppresses all log output from this logger. No sinks are called.
- **DEFAULT (40)**: Alias for WARNING. Used as the default level for the root logger.

## Logger API

### Acquiring Loggers

**`cityrp.logging.GetLogger(namespace)`**

Returns a logger instance for the given dot-notated namespace string.

```lua
local log = cityrp.logging.GetLogger("banking")
local childLog = cityrp.logging.GetLogger("banking.sql")
local rootLog = cityrp.logging.GetLogger("") -- or GetLogger(nil)
```

- Namespaces are hierarchical: `"banking.sql.query"` → parent is `"banking.sql"` → parent is `"banking"` → parent is root
- Root logger namespace is the empty string `""`. Calling `GetLogger(nil)` or `GetLogger("")` returns the root logger
- Loggers are singletons per namespace; repeated calls return the same instance

### Logger Instance Methods

All logging methods are **chainable** (return the logger instance).

#### Core Logging Methods

```lua
logger:Debug(msg_parts..., meta?)
logger:Info(msg_parts..., meta?)
logger:Warning(msg_parts..., meta?)
logger:Error(msg_parts..., meta?)
logger:Critical(msg_parts..., meta?)
logger:Fatal(msg_parts..., meta?)
```

Accept varargs for message parts. Final table argument is treated as metadata.

#### Bypass Method

```lua
logger:Raw(level, msg_parts..., meta?)
```

Bypasses the logger's effective level check. Always dispatches to sinks (subject to sink filtering). `level` is a numeric level (or level constant).

#### Configuration Methods

```lua
logger:SetLevel(level)           -- Set explicit level (chainable)
logger:GetLevel()                -- Get explicit level (may be nil if inheriting)
logger:GetEffectiveLevel()       -- Get resolved effective level (after inheritance)
```

#### Hierarchy Navigation

```lua
logger:GetName()                 -- Returns namespace string (e.g., "banking.sql"; root returns "")
logger:GetDisplayName()          -- Returns display name ("root" for root logger)
logger:GetParent()               -- Returns immediate parent logger instance
logger:GetChild(child_segment)   -- Returns child logger for given segment
logger:GetChildren()             -- Returns array of direct child logger instances
logger:IsRoot()                  -- Returns true if this is the root logger
```

#### Field Binding

```lua
logger:WithFields(fields_table)
```

Returns a wrapper logger that merges `fields_table` into metadata on every log call. Useful for binding common context (e.g., request ID, user ID).

## Basic Usage

### Simple Logging

```lua
local log = cityrp.logging.GetLogger("banking")
log:Info("Banking plugin initialized", {version = "1.2.0"})
log:Debug("Player balance lookup", {player = ply:SteamID64(), balance = 5000})
```

### Colored Output

```lua
local log = cityrp.logging.GetLogger("auth")
log:Info(Color(0, 255, 0), "Login success: ", Color(255, 255, 255), ply:Name())
```

### Using Sanitization Helpers

```lua
local log = cityrp.logging.GetLogger("chat")
log:Info(cityrp.logging.sanitizePlayer(ply), " said: ", msg)
-- Output: [2025-12-14 13:22:10][chat][INFO] PlayerName (STEAM_0:1:12345) said: hello
```

### Lazy Messages

Defer expensive computation until the log level check passes:

```lua
local log = cityrp.logging.GetLogger("expensive")
log:Debug(function()
	return "Heavy computation result: " .. compute_expensive()
end)
-- compute_expensive() is only called if DEBUG level is enabled
```

### WithFields (Bound Context)

Bind common metadata to all log entries:

```lua
local log = cityrp.logging.GetLogger("http")
local req_log = log:WithFields({request_id = "abc123", endpoint = "/api/balance"})
req_log:Info("Request started")
req_log:Info("Request completed", {status = 200})
-- Both entries include request_id and endpoint in metadata
```

### Chainable Calls

```lua
cityrp.logging.GetLogger("startup")
	:Info("Initializing subsystems")
	:Debug("Loading config")
	:Info("Startup complete")
```

### Bypass Level Filtering (Raw)

```lua
local log = cityrp.logging.GetLogger("console")
log:Raw(cityrp.logging.levels.INFO, "Command executed: ", cmd)
-- Always logs regardless of logger's effective level
```

## Message Parts (varargs API)

Message parts may include:

- **Strings**: literal text
- **Color objects**: `Color(r, g, b, a)` — used by console sink for colored output via `MsgC`; stripped by non-color sinks
- **Entities/Players**: game objects; sinks are responsible for serialization (e.g., console shows name+steamid; DB stores steamid64)
- **Functions**: lazy evaluation — function returning string to defer expensive computation

**Metadata table** (optional final argument):

- Plain Lua table containing structured key-value pairs for additional context
- Metadata is available to sinks for filtering, formatting, and persistence
- Any trailing table argument without metatable is treated as metadata

**Example:**

```lua
logger:Info("Player ", ply, " connected from ", ip, {country = "US", new_player = true})
```

## Logger Hierarchy and Inheritance

### Dot-Notated Namespaces

Namespaces are dot-separated: `"banking"`, `"banking.sql"`, `"banking.sql.query"`.

Parent-child relationships are implicit from the namespace structure.

Root logger namespace is `""` (empty string); displayed as `"root"` in output.

### Inheritance Rules

- **Level inheritance**: If a logger's explicit level is `nil` (or `INHERIT`), the effective level is resolved by recursively checking the nearest ancestor with an explicit level, or the global default
- **Explicit overrides**: Calling `SetLevel(level)` on a logger sets an explicit level that overrides inheritance
- **Caching and invalidation**: Effective levels are cached. When a logger's level changes, it synchronously notifies its children to invalidate their caches

### Example

```lua
local parent = cityrp.logging.GetLogger("banking")
parent:SetLevel(cityrp.logging.levels.DEBUG)

local child = cityrp.logging.GetLogger("banking.sql")
-- child inherits DEBUG from parent

child:Info("Query executed")  -- dispatched because INFO >= DEBUG

child:SetLevel(cityrp.logging.levels.ERROR)
child:Info("Query executed")  -- suppressed because INFO < ERROR
```

## Runtime Configuration

### Console Commands (Server-only, RCON/Console)

**`cityrp_log_set <namespace> <level>`**

Set the log level for a namespace.

```
cityrp_log_set banking DEBUG
cityrp_log_set banking.sql 20
cityrp_log_set root INFO
```

- `<namespace>`: dot-notated string (e.g., `"banking.sql"`) or `"root"` for root logger
- `<level>`: numeric value or string token (e.g., `"DEBUG"`, `20`, `"INHERIT"`)
- Immediately updates the logger and invalidates child caches
- Writes updated configuration to `data/cityrp/log_levels.json`

**`cityrp_log_get <namespace>`**

Get the explicit and effective log level for a namespace.

```
cityrp_log_get banking
```

**`cityrp_log_list`**

List all configured namespaces and their explicit levels.

```
cityrp_log_list
```

### Persistence

- All namespace → level mappings are stored in `data/cityrp/log_levels.json` (single JSON file)
- File is loaded at gamemode initialization
- File is written immediately (atomic write) when a level is changed via concommand

**Format:**

```json
{
	"": 40,
	"banking": 20,
	"banking.sql": 10
}
```

### Client vs Server State

- Client and server logging state are independent
- Configuration (concommands, persistence) is server-only
- Client-side loggers respect client-side defaults but do not write to DB or forward to server

## Sinks

### Default Sinks

**Console sink** (`"console"`):

- Registered by default
- Uses `MsgC` for colored output on both server and client
- Colorizes output by level:
  - DEBUG: grey `Color(128, 128, 128)`
  - INFO: cyan `Color(0, 255, 255)`
  - WARNING: yellow `Color(255, 215, 0)`
  - ERROR: dark red `Color(128, 0, 0)`
  - CRITICAL: red `Color(192, 0, 0)`
  - FATAL: bright red `Color(255, 0, 0)`
- Format example: `[2025-12-14 13:22:10][banking.sql][INFO] Message text {metadata}`
- When running as a multiplayer listen server, adds a CLIENT/SERVER realm indicator

**cityrp.logs sink** (`"cityrp_logs"`):

- Registered by default (server-only)
- Forwards entries at or above WARNING to `cityrp.logs.add` for database persistence
- Stores:
  - `timestamp` (UNIX int)
  - `namespace` (string)
  - `level` (numeric)
  - `message` (resolved final string)
  - `meta` (JSON-encoded table)
- Client-side logger state never writes to DB

### Extensible Sink API

Register custom sinks via:

```lua
cityrp.logging.RegisterSink(name, sink_table)
```

**Sink table structure:**

```lua
{
	Write = function(entry)
		-- entry.timestamp (os.time())
		-- entry.namespace (string)
		-- entry.level (numeric)
		-- entry.message_parts (array of strings, Color objects, entities, players)
		-- entry.meta (table or nil)
	end
}
```

Sinks are responsible for:

- Formatting: Convert message_parts to final output (handle Color objects, serialize entities/players)
- Sanitization and escaping: Loggers may contain unvalidated user input; sinks must protect against injection/exploits
- Filtering: Sinks may filter entries by level, namespace, or any other criteria independent of logger-level filtering

## Plugin Integration

### Automatic Logger Creation

When a plugin is registered, the core plugin system automatically creates a logger for the plugin:

```lua
plugin.logger = cityrp.logging.GetLogger("plugin.<plugin_id>")
```

`<plugin_id>` is the plugin **key** — the folder name, or a file plugin's name without its scope
prefix — not `PLUGIN.name`. That matters here because `cityrp_log_set` splits its arguments on
whitespace, so a namespace derived from a display name like `"Area Manager"` could never be passed
to it. See [plugins.md](plugins.md#keys).

Plugin objects expose:

- `plugin.logger` — the plugin's logger instance

Plugins may call `plugin.logger:Info(...)`, `plugin.logger:Debug(...)`, etc.

### Lifecycle Event Logging

Core plugin system logs lifecycle events at DEBUG level using the plugin's logger:

- Plugin loaded: `plugin.logger:Debug("Plugin loaded")`

### Plugin Log Configuration

Per-plugin log level configuration is done via the same namespace-based concommand system:

```
cityrp_log_set plugin.my_plugin DEBUG
```

No separate per-plugin convars.

## Sanitization Helpers

### `cityrp.logging.sanitizePlayer(ply)`

Returns an array for use in message parts:

```lua
{Color(r, g, b), "PlayerName (STEAM_X:Y:Z)", Color(255, 255, 255)}
```

- Player color priority: rank color if available, else team color, else white
- White reset color at end

### `cityrp.logging.sanitizeEntity(ent)`

Returns an array:

```lua
{Color(0, 255, 255), "EntityClass [123]", Color(255, 255, 255)}
```

- Entity color: cyan/green
- Format: class and entindex

## Performance and Optimization

### Best Practices

1. **Use DEBUG sparingly in production**: Prefer INFO or higher
2. **Use lazy message functions for expensive debug messages**:
   ```lua
   logger:Debug(function() return expensive_trace() end)
   ```
3. **Bind common metadata with `WithFields`** to avoid repeated allocations:
   ```lua
   local req_log = logger:WithFields({request_id = id})
   req_log:Info("Request started")
   ```
4. **Limit metadata size**: Library enforces safe limits (max 50 keys, strings truncated at 1024 chars by sinks)

### Optimization Strategies

- **Fast level checks**: Early-return before formatting or metadata serialization if level filtered out
- **Lazy message formatting**: Support message parts as functions to defer expensive string construction
- **Effective level caching**: Cache resolved effective levels; invalidate synchronously when parent/ancestor levels change
- **Minimal allocations**: Reuse buffers where safe; avoid churn in hot paths

## Security and Safety

### Safety Guarantees

- **Never errors**: Logging calls never throw errors, even with nil or malformed input
- **Safe serialization**: Metadata serializer is bounded and non-recursive; handles circular refs gracefully
- **Sanitization**: Sinks are responsible for sanitizing and escaping metadata and message content for their output target (console, DB, network)

### Security Notes

- **Unvalidated user input**: Loggers may receive unvalidated player-supplied input (e.g., chat messages, entity names). Sinks MUST sanitize and escape data to prevent injection attacks or exploits
- **Client logs**: Client-side logs remain on the client. No client-to-server forwarding in any circumstance (no net messages, no admin-request mechanism)
- **DB sink**: Server-only. Clients cannot write to DB directly or indirectly
- **Concommand permissions**: Concommands are server console or RCON only; no player-executable commands

## Migration from Legacy Logging

### Do NOT Replace cityrp.logs for Audit Events

- `cityrp.logs` remains the canonical system for persistent game-audit events (player actions, admin actions, transactions)
- `cityrp.logging` is for developer diagnostics and runtime troubleshooting
- Use `cityrp.logs.add` for events that must be queryable and persistent for moderation/audit
- Use `cityrp.logging` for debug output, performance traces, and operational monitoring

### Replacing Legacy Prints

Replace developer-facing `print()`, `ServerLog()`, `MsgN()` calls with `cityrp.logging`:

**Old:**

```lua
print("Banking: Player " .. ply:Name() .. " balance: " .. bal)
```

**New:**

```lua
local log = cityrp.logging.GetLogger("banking")
log:Debug("Player balance: ", bal, {player = ply, balance = bal})
```

## Examples

### Basic Logging

```lua
local log = cityrp.logging.GetLogger("banking")
log:Info("Banking plugin initialized", {version = "1.2.0"})
log:Debug("Player balance lookup", {player = ply:SteamID64(), balance = 5000})
```

### Using Player/Entity Sanitization

```lua
local log = cityrp.logging.GetLogger("chat")
log:Info(cityrp.logging.sanitizePlayer(ply), " said: ", msg)
```

### Lazy Evaluation

```lua
local log = cityrp.logging.GetLogger("expensive")
log:Debug(function()
	return "Heavy computation result: " .. compute_expensive()
end)
```

### Bound Context with WithFields

```lua
local log = cityrp.logging.GetLogger("http")
local req_log = log:WithFields({request_id = "abc123", endpoint = "/api/balance"})
req_log:Info("Request started")
req_log:Info("Request completed", {status = 200})
```

### Chainable Logging

```lua
cityrp.logging.GetLogger("startup")
	:Info("Initializing subsystems")
	:Debug("Loading config")
	:Info("Startup complete")
```

### Hierarchical Configuration

```lua
-- Set parent to DEBUG
cityrp.logging.GetLogger("banking"):SetLevel(cityrp.logging.levels.DEBUG)

-- Child inherits DEBUG
local child = cityrp.logging.GetLogger("banking.sql")
child:Info("Query executed")  -- dispatched

-- Override child to ERROR
child:SetLevel(cityrp.logging.levels.ERROR)
child:Info("Query executed")  -- suppressed
```

## API Reference

### Global API

```lua
-- Level management
cityrp.logging.SetDefaultLevel(level)
cityrp.logging.GetDefaultLevel()

-- Logger factory
cityrp.logging.GetLogger(namespace)

-- Sink management
cityrp.logging.RegisterSink(name, sink_table)
cityrp.logging.UnregisterSink(name)

-- Sanitization helpers
cityrp.logging.sanitizePlayer(ply)
cityrp.logging.sanitizeEntity(ent)

-- Level constants
cityrp.logging.levels.INHERIT
cityrp.logging.levels.ALWAYS
cityrp.logging.levels.DEBUG
cityrp.logging.levels.INFO
cityrp.logging.levels.WARNING
cityrp.logging.levels.DEFAULT
cityrp.logging.levels.ERROR
cityrp.logging.levels.CRITICAL
cityrp.logging.levels.FATAL
cityrp.logging.levels.NEVER
```

### Logger Instance Methods

```lua
-- Logging methods
logger:Debug(...)
logger:Info(...)
logger:Warning(...)
logger:Error(...)
logger:Critical(...)
logger:Fatal(...)
logger:Raw(level, ...)

-- Configuration
logger:SetLevel(level)
logger:GetLevel()
logger:GetEffectiveLevel()

-- Hierarchy
logger:GetName()
logger:GetDisplayName()
logger:GetParent()
logger:GetChild(segment)
logger:GetChildren()
logger:IsRoot()

-- Context binding
logger:WithFields(fields_table)
```

### Console Commands (Server-only)

```
cityrp_log_set <namespace> <level>
cityrp_log_get <namespace>
cityrp_log_list
```

topics.title: LuaCATS Annotations
topics.body:
# LuaCATS Annotations

The complete annotation reference for this codebase — what every tag means, what its fields are, and
which ones look correct but are silently ignored here.

[LuaCATS](https://luals.github.io/wiki/annotations/) ("Lua Comment And Type System") is the
annotation dialect understood by [lua-language-server](https://github.com/LuaLS/lua-language-server)
(LuaLS). It is the **mandatory** documentation format for this repository: every function must carry
one. Annotations do three jobs at once:

1. **Type checking and editor intelligence** — hover text, autocomplete, go-to-definition, and
   wrong-argument warnings, in any editor with the LuaLS extension installed.
2. **The public docs site** — CI runs LuaLS `--doc` over the gamemode and feeds the resulting JSON to
   `tools/docs/generate.py`. If LuaLS doesn't understand your comment, the docs site never sees it.
   See [Writing Doc Comments](doc-comments.md) for the pipeline itself.
3. **Machine-readable intent** — the annotations are frequently the only statement of what a
   function is *supposed* to accept and return, in a codebase with no runtime type system.

Related reading: [Writing Doc Comments](doc-comments.md) (how the docs pipeline consumes these),
