[Modern APIs](modern-apis.md) (which APIs to annotate against),
[Coding Standards](coding-standards.md) (checklist + CI reject criteria).

## The rules that decide whether an annotation counts

Everything below is conditional on these four. Break any one of them and the annotation still
"looks" fine in the diff, still passes lint, and is silently dropped:

1. **Three dashes, always.** `--- @param` counts, `-- @param` does not. A two-dash comment is a plain
   comment to LuaLS regardless of what it contains.
2. **Directly above the declaration, with no blank line.** LuaLS attaches a doc comment to whatever
   declaration immediately follows it. One blank line between the comment and the `function`, and the
   two are never associated — the annotation is dropped from the doc JSON entirely and no hover text
   appears in editors.
3. **Description first, tags after.** The human-readable description lines come before the `@` tags,
   not interleaved with them.
4. **Names must match the real signature.** `--- @param ply Player` only binds if the function
   actually has a parameter called `ply`. A renamed parameter with a stale annotation is a
   `undefined-doc-param` warning at best, wrong docs at worst.

**Enforcement note:** `standards-diff.py` fails a changed line that introduces `--- @module`
(use `--- @namespace` on file headers), an LDoc tag, `--- @vararg`, a two-dash `-- @tag`, or a
`---`-prefixed inline cast. It also fails a **file-level** `function` declaration your diff adds
with no doc comment directly above it, and one whose doc comment a blank line has detached.
Declarations nested inside another function — panel callbacks such as `function combo:OnSelect(...)`
and local helpers — are out of CI's reach but still a review requirement; do not ship undocumented
functions.

House style in this repo:

* Write `--- @tag` with a space after the dashes. Both `--- @param` and `---@param` parse identically,
  but the spaced form is what the overwhelming majority of the codebase uses — match it.
* Indent with tabs, like all other Lua here.
* Descriptions start with a capital letter and end with a full stop.
* Descriptions may span multiple lines; each line needs its own `---`.

```lua
--- Issues a warrant against a player.
--- Fails silently if a live warrant of the same type already exists.
--- @param ply Player The player to warrant.
--- @param reason string Why the warrant was issued.
--- @return boolean issued Whether a new warrant was created.
--- @state server
function cityrp.warrants.issue(ply, reason)
	...
end
```

## Documenting functions

### `@param`

```
--- @param <name> <type>[?][|<type>...] [description]
```

One per parameter, in declaration order. The **name comes first**, then the type — the reverse of
LDoc's `@tparam`, which is the single most common porting mistake.

The `?` goes on the **type**, as a nullable suffix, and marks the parameter as optional (callers may
omit it or pass `nil`):

```lua
--- Formats a number of seconds into a human-readable string.
--- @param time number The number of seconds to format.
--- @param showMins boolean? Whether to include minutes in the output.
--- @return string formatted The formatted time string.
function cityrp.formattime(time, showMins)
	...
end
```

`showMins boolean?` and `showMins boolean|nil` mean the same thing — `?` is shorthand for `|nil`
appended to the type. For a union, the `?` goes on the end of the whole union:
`base string|table?` reads as "`string|table`, or nil".

Varargs are documented as a parameter literally named `...`:

```lua
--- Prints each supplied name.
--- @param ... string The names to print.
function PrintNames(...)
	...
end
```

### `@return`

```
--- @return <type> [<name>] [description]
```

**One `@return` line per returned value, in order.** LuaLS does accept
`--- @return boolean, string` on a single line, but this codebase writes them one per line — it is
the only form where each value gets its own name and description.

```lua
--- Attempts to unlock a door for a player.
--- @return boolean success Whether the door was unlocked.
--- @return string? reason Why the unlock failed, or nil on success.
function cityrp.door.tryUnlock(ply, door)
	...
end
```

Naming the return value is optional but strongly preferred: `@return boolean success` reads far
better in hover text and on the docs site than a bare `@return boolean`.

### `@overload`

```
--- @overload fun([<name>: <type>, ...]): [<return type>[, ...]]
```

Declares an *additional* call signature beyond the one described by `@param`/`@return`. Use it for
functions that genuinely branch on arity or argument type, rather than widening every `@param` to a
union:

```lua
--- Resolves a player from a name, SteamID, or the player itself.
--- @overload fun(ply: Player): Player
--- @param identifier string A name fragment or SteamID.
--- @return Player? ply The matched player, or nil if no unique match.
function cityrp.util.findPlayer(identifier)
	...
end
```

### `@generic`

```
--- @generic <name>[: <parent type>][, <name2>[: <parent type>]]
```

Introduces a type variable so the return type can be tied to an argument type, instead of collapsing
to `any`:

```lua
--- Returns the value unchanged.
--- @generic T
--- @param value T The value to return.
--- @return T value The same value.
function Identity(value)
	return value
end
```

Genuinely useful for table/collection helpers (`table.Copy`-alikes, `pick`, `filter`) where `any`
would throw away every downstream type.

### `@nodiscard`

Warns at the call site if the return value is thrown away. Correct for pure getters and predicates
(`IsAdmin`, `CanAfford`, `GetInventoryItems`), wrong for anything whose side effect is the point.

```lua
--- @return boolean isAdmin Whether the player is an admin.
--- @nodiscard
function pMeta:IsAdmin()
	...
end
```

### `@async`

Marks a function that does not complete before it returns. In this codebase that means anything
built on `DB_MAIN:Run`, `HTTP`, `timer.Simple`, or a `net` round trip. It is a documentation signal
to the caller, not a language feature — and it pairs with the async footgun in
[AGENTS.md](https://github.com/limelight-development/cityrp2/blob/master/AGENTS.md): **the callback
must re-validate entities itself**, because the player may have disconnected before it fires.

```lua
--- Loads a player's bank balance from the database.
--- @async
--- @param ply Player The player to load for.
--- @param callback fun(balance: number) Invoked with the loaded balance.
function cityrp.banking.loadBalance(ply, callback)
	...
end
```

## Describing shapes: classes, fields, and types

### `@class`

```
--- @class [(exact)] <name>[: <parent>[, <parent2>...]]
```

Defines a named type. Attach it to the table it describes (the declaration on the line below), or use
it standalone as a pure type definition. `(exact)` forbids fields that weren't declared — useful for
config tables where a typo'd key should be an error rather than silently ignored. Inheritance is
`: Parent`, and multiple parents are comma-separated.

```lua
--- A single entry in the image-host allowlist.
--- @class ImageHostDefinition
--- @field host string The hostname players link to, matched exactly and case-insensitively.
--- @field enabled boolean Whether the host is currently accepted.
--- @field reason string Why the host is trusted, or why it is currently disabled.

--- A vehicle owned by a player.
--- @class Vehicle : Entity
--- @field _Owner Player The owning player.
--- @field _Petrol number Fuel level, 0-100.
```

### `@field`

```
--- @field [<scope>] <name> <type>[?] [description]
--- @field [<key type>] <value type> [description]
```

Declares one member of the `@class` it belongs to. The rules that matter:

* **`@field` lines must sit in the same contiguous comment block as their `@class`**, immediately
  after it. A blank line, or an unrelated tag block in between, orphans them.
* **`?` marks an optional field** and goes on the type, as a nullable suffix: `--- @field reason string?`.
  An optional field may be absent entirely; `string|nil` says the same thing spelled out.
* **`<scope>` is optional** and is one of `public` (the default), `protected`, `private`, or
  `package`. It controls where LuaLS considers the field accessible — `private` to the defining
  class, `protected` to it and its subclasses, `package` to the same file.
* **A bracketed key type declares an index signature** rather than a named field — the shape of
  *arbitrary* keys. `--- @field [string] number` means "any string key maps to a number", and
  `--- @field [integer] Player` means "integer-indexed, holding players".

```lua
--- A logging sink.
--- @class Logger
--- @field namespace string The namespace this logger reports under.
--- @field private level number The minimum level this logger emits at.
--- @field sinks Sink[] Sinks this logger writes to.
--- @field parent Logger? The logger this one inherits configuration from.
--- @field [string] any Arbitrary caller-attached metadata.
```

`@field` also documents members of a table you're describing in place, and is the right tool
whenever a function takes or returns a "config table" — declare the table's shape as a `@class` once,
then reference that class by name in `@param`, instead of typing the parameter as a bare `table`:

```lua
--- @class WarrantOptions
--- @field reason string Why the warrant is being issued.
--- @field expires number? Unix timestamp the warrant lapses at.
--- @field silent boolean? Suppress the player-facing notification.

--- Issues a warrant.
--- @param ply Player The player to warrant.
--- @param opts WarrantOptions Warrant configuration.
function cityrp.warrants.issue(ply, opts)
	...
end
```

### `@type`

```
--- @type <type>
```

Declares the type of a variable or table where LuaLS can't infer it — most often an empty table that
gets populated later.

```lua
--- @type table<string, Player>
local playersBySteamID = {}

--- @type {[PASS]: Pass}
local passes = {}
```

`@type` on a *function* is wrong — use `@param`/`@return`.

### `@alias`

```
--- @alias <name> <type>
--- @alias <name>
--- | <literal> [# description]
```

Names a type for reuse. The single-line form is a straight synonym; the multi-line `---|` form
enumerates the permitted values, which is what gives autocomplete a fixed list to offer:

```lua
--- @alias TeamID number

--- @alias NotifyKind
--- | "generic" # Neutral information.
--- | "error" # Something went wrong.
--- | "hint" # Contextual tip.
```

### `@enum`

```
--- @enum [(key)] <name>
```

Attaches directly to a **real, runtime table** of constants, and makes the type usable as a
type-checked set of that table's values. `(key)` switches it to using the table's *keys* rather than
its values.

```lua
--- Notification kinds accepted by ply:Notify().
--- @enum NotifyType
local NOTIFY = {
	GENERIC = 0,
	ERROR = 1,
	UNDO = 2,
	HINT = 3,
}
```

The difference from `@alias`: `@alias` is a type that exists only in annotations, `@enum` describes a
table that exists at runtime. Use `@enum` for the `CAPITALIZED_WITH_UNDERSCORES` constant tables this
codebase already has; use `@alias` when there is no backing table.

### `@operator`

```
--- @operator <operator>[(<param type>)]: <return type>
```

Documents a metamethod so LuaLS knows `a + b` is legal on your class:

```lua
--- @class Money
--- @operator add(Money): Money
--- @operator unm: Money
```

## Visibility, lifecycle, and cross-references

| Tag | Syntax | What it does |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `@deprecated` | `--- @deprecated [text]` | Marks the item outdated. LuaLS strikes it through at call sites; `generate.py` renders it as a "Deprecated" callout on the docs site. Always say what to use instead. |
| `@private` | `--- @private` | Accessible only within the defining class. |
| `@protected` | `--- @protected` | Accessible within the defining class and its subclasses. |
| `@package` | `--- @package` | Accessible only within the same file. |
| `@see` | `--- @see <symbol>` | Cross-reference to another documented symbol. |
| `@version` | `--- @version [<\|>]<version>` | Required Lua/LuaJIT version. Rarely needed — the whole server is LuaJIT. |
| `@source` | `--- @source <path>[:<line>]` | Points at the real definition when the code LuaLS sees is a stub. |

```lua
--- Old warrant lookup, kept for legacy callers.
--- @deprecated Use cityrp.warrants.issue instead.
--- @see cityrp.warrants.issue
--- @param ply Player The player to look up.
function cityrp.warrants.legacyLookup(ply)
	...
end
```

Note that `@deprecated` does double duty: it is both the LuaCATS tag (editor strikethrough) and one
of `generate.py`'s own callout tags (docs-site banner). The one line drives both.

## Narrowing and escape hatches

### `@cast`

```
--- @cast <variable> [+|-]<type>[, ...]
```

Re-types an existing variable **from that line onward**. `+` adds a type to the union, `-` removes
one. The most common legitimate use here is stripping `nil` after a guard LuaLS can't follow:

```lua
local ent = ply:GetEyeTrace().Entity
if not IsValid(ent) then return end
--- @cast ent Entity
```

### `@as`

```lua
local ent = ents.FindByClass("prop_vehicle_jeep")[1] --[[@as Vehicle]]
```

An inline, expression-level cast. Note the syntax carefully: it is a **block comment containing only
`@as <type>`** — `--[[@as Vehicle]]`. It is *not* written with the `---` prefix that every other
annotation uses, and `--[[--- @as Vehicle]]` does not work.

### `@diagnostic`

```
--- @diagnostic <state>:<diagnostic name>
```

`<state>` is `disable`, `enable`, `disable-line`, or `disable-next-line`. Suppress the narrowest
scope that solves the problem, and only when the diagnostic is genuinely wrong — a file-wide
`disable` hides real errors from everyone who touches the file afterwards.

```lua
--- @diagnostic disable-next-line: undefined-global
local plugin = PLUGIN
```

### `@meta`

```
--- @meta [name]
```

Marks an entire file as **definition-only** — types and signatures with no executable body. Correct
for a hand-written stub file describing an external API; wrong for any file that actually runs.

## Type syntax

Types are written the same way everywhere — in `@param`, `@return`, `@field`, `@type`, and `@alias`.

| Form | Example | Meaning |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Primitive | `number`, `string`, `boolean`, `nil`, `table`, `function`, `integer`, `any` | Stock Lua types. `integer` is a narrower `number`. |
| Engine class | `Player`, `Entity`, `Vector`, `Angle`, `Color`, `Panel` | Any `@class` name, including Garry's Mod's own. |
| Union | `string\|number` | Either type. |
| Optional | `string?` | Shorthand for `string\|nil`. |
| Array | `string[]`, `Player[]` | Sequential table of that type. |
| Dictionary | `table<string, number>` | Keys of the first type, values of the second. |
| Table literal | `{ x: number, y: number }` | Inline anonymous shape. |
| Function | `fun(ply: Player, amount: number): boolean` | Callable with those parameters and return. |
| Function, varargs | `fun(...: string): number` | Callable taking varargs. |
| Literal | `"red"\|"green"\|"blue"` | Only those exact values. |
| Parenthesised | `("red"\|"blue")[]` | Needed to array-ify or optional-ify a union. |

```lua
--- @param teams table<number, TeamID> Map of team indices to team IDs.
--- @param predicate fun(ply: Player): boolean Called per player; return true to keep.
--- @param bounds { min: Vector, max: Vector } The region to search.
--- @param colours ("red"|"blue"|"green")[] Allowed colours, in priority order.
```

Prefer the most specific type that is actually true. `table` and `any` are legal and sometimes
unavoidable, but each one is a place where the annotation stopped being useful — if the table has a
known shape, give it a `@class` and reference that instead.

## Garry's Mod and CityRP specifics

* **Use the engine class names, not `table`.** `Player`, `Entity`, `Weapon`, `Vehicle`, `NPC`,
  `Vector`, `Angle`, `Color`, `IMaterial`, `Panel`, `ConVar`, `PhysObj`, `CUserCmd`, `CMoveData`,
  `VMatrix`, `File`, `IGModAudioChannel`, `CTakeDamageInfo`. `Player` is a subtype of `Entity`, so a
  function that accepts any entity should say `Entity`, not `Player`.
* **`Player` does not imply valid.** An annotation is documentation, not a runtime guarantee — every
  entity argument still needs its `IsValid()` check, and every async callback needs that check
  *inside* the callback. Annotating a parameter `Player` never removes the guard.
* **Metatable methods.** Methods added via `FindMetaTable("Player")` extend the existing `Player`
  class; document the method with `@param`/`@return` as normal, and add new fields you attach to
  players with a `@class Player` + `@field` block rather than leaving them undeclared.

  ```lua
  --- @class Player
  --- @field _Money number The player's current wallet balance.
  --- @field _LocalPlyVars table<string, any> Per-player variables networked only to that player.
  local pMeta = FindMetaTable("Player")

  --- Checks whether the player holds an access flag.
  --- @param flag string The access flag to test, e.g. "a" for admin.
  --- @return boolean hasAccess Whether the player holds the flag.
  --- @nodiscard
  function pMeta:HasAccess(flag)
  	return cityrp.access.hasAccess(self, flag)
  end
  ```

* **Plugin and item tables.** `PLUGIN` and `ITEM` methods are documented exactly like any other
  function. Callbacks registered through `hook.Add` are usually best documented on the `PLUGIN`
  method they delegate to, since that is the thing with a real signature.
* **Realms.** LuaCATS has no concept of client/server. That is what this codebase's own `@state` tag
  is for — see below.

## Tags that are not LuaCATS but live in the same comment

These are `generate.py`'s, not LuaLS's. They are written in the same `---` block, and LuaLS ignores
them harmlessly. Full detail in [Writing Doc Comments](doc-comments.md):

| Tag | Where | Purpose |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `@namespace <name>` | File header | Groups the file's items onto one docs page. **Use this instead of `@module`.** Naming it after a `@class` also makes that the [class's page](doc-comments.md#class-pages-namespace-classname-gathers-a-classs-members), gathering members declared in other files. |
| `@state <realm>` | File header or item | `client`, `server`, `shared`, `menu`, `global`, `clmenu` — drives the realm badge. On the file header it is the default for every item in the file. |
| `@section <title>` | Item | Starts a named subsection on the module page; the tag's value is the heading. On an `@alias` over a run of constants, it names the [constant family](doc-comments.md#constant-families-alias-gathers-the-constants-it-names) those constants are gathered under. |
| `@uniqueid <id>` | Item | The registration ID a documented class is stored under, rendered as a "Registration ID" chip. See [Registration IDs](#registration-ids) below. |
| `@warns <text>` | Item | Renders a "Warnings" callout. |
| `@bugs <text>` | Item | Renders a "Known Issues" callout. |
| `@internal [text]` | Item | Renders an "Internal" callout. |
| `@copyright`, `@release`, `@author` | File header | Required by the style guide; parsed but not currently rendered. |

### Registration IDs

A class whose name does not contain the string it is registered under needs `@uniqueid`, or nobody
can find it. `ITEM.ModelBodygroup` is registered as `base_modelbg`; without the tag, searching the
docs or the `cityrp-docs` MCP for `base_modelbg` returns nothing at all.

```lua
--- The bodygroup modifier item base. Contains helpers for setting model bodygroups.
--- @uniqueid base_modelbg
--- @class ITEM.ModelBodygroup : ITEM
local ITEM = ITEM:New()
```

The ID is what `search_api` matches on (an exact hit outranks everything else), what `get_symbol`
prints as **Registration ID**, and what the module page renders as a chip. Repeat the tag once per
ID if one declaration registers several.

Two constraints, both of which fail silently:

- **The tag needs a class of its own.** LuaLS only exports a declaration it can name. A plain
  documented `local`, or one annotated `@type ITEM`, exports nothing, and the tag disappears with
  it. Re-opening a shared class (`@class ITEM` in fifteen different files) is worse than useless:
  LuaLS merges the declarations and every one of them reports the *first* file's description, so
  fourteen files' tags are silently discarded. Give the thing its own `@class X : Parent`.
- **Keep it adjacent.** A blank line between the description and `@class` drops the description —
  and the tag with it — from the docs export, with no warning anywhere.

## Annotations that look right and are not

| Written | Problem | Write instead |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `--- @module "cityrp.util"` | **LuaLS reserves `@module` for its own `require()` return-type inference and silently drops the whole doc comment.** The most common porting mistake in this repo. | `--- @namespace cityrp.util` |
| `--- @vararg string` | Deprecated by LuaLS itself. | `--- @param ... string` |
| `--- @usage foo()` | LDoc, not LuaCATS. LuaLS does not understand it and `generate.py` does not render it — the line is dead weight. There are still a few in the tree. | Put the example in the description, in a fenced block. |
| `--- @tparam Player ply` | LDoc. | `--- @param ply Player` |
| `--- @treturn bool` | LDoc — and `bool` is not a Lua type. | `--- @return boolean` |
| `--- @classmod ENV` | LDoc. | `--- @class ENV` (plus `--- @namespace ENV` on the file header) |
| `--- @number x` / `--- @string s` / `--- @bool b` | LDoc typed-parameter shorthand. | `--- @param x number` etc. |
| `--- @function` / `--- @local` | LDoc. | Omit; use `@private`/`@package` for visibility. |
| `-- @param ply Player` | Two dashes — a plain comment. | `--- @param ply Player` |
| `--- @param Player ply` | Type and name the wrong way round. | `--- @param ply Player` |
| `--- @param ply Player?` where `ply` is required | `?` on a mandatory parameter. | `--- @param ply Player` |
| `--- @param ply? Player` | `?` on the name instead of the type. | `--- @param ply Player?` |
| `--[[--- @as Entity]]` | Inline casts take no `---`. | `--[[@as Entity]]` |
| `--[[-- Description. @namespace x --]]--` as a file header | Legacy pre-LuaCATS syntax, not real LuaCATS — LuaLS gives it no hover/autocomplete/type-checking. Only `generate.py`'s raw-source scan tolerates it, and only to keep old files rendering on the docs site. | A run of `---` lines (see [Writing Doc Comments](doc-comments.md)). |
| `--- @class Player` as the last line of a **file header** | The header *is* the comment attached to the class, so the file's description, `@copyright` and `@author` all become the class's description — and because LuaLS merges every re-opening of a class, that one header then describes the class everywhere it appears. `Player` was documented sitewide as "Serverside Inventory Metatable." this way. | End the header at `@namespace`, and put `--- @class Player` on its own directly above `local pMeta = FindMetaTable("Player")`. |
| `--- @alias meta` above `local meta = FindMetaTable("Entity")` | LDoc's `@alias`, meaning "this local is the module table". LuaCATS reads it as a type alias with no definition — it declares a junk type and documents nothing. | Delete it. |
| Blank line between the comment and the `function` | LuaLS never associates them; the annotation vanishes from the docs and from hover. | Delete the blank line. |

LDoc was this project's previous documentation format and its tags are still scattered through older
files. They are not a style to match — when you touch a function carrying LDoc tags, convert them.

## Worked example

```lua
--- Player-facing warrant helpers.
--- @copyright 2015-2026 Limelight Gaming
--- @release CityRP 2
--- @author Someone
--- @namespace cityrp.warrants
--- @state server

cityrp.warrants = cityrp.warrants or {}

--- The kinds of warrant that can be issued.
--- @enum WarrantType
local WARRANT = {
	ARREST = 0,
	SEARCH = 1,
	WANTED = 2,
}

--- A live warrant against a player.
--- @class Warrant
--- @field target Player The player the warrant is against.
--- @field issuer Player The officer who issued it.
--- @field kind WarrantType What the warrant authorises.
--- @field reason string Why the warrant was issued.
--- @field expires number? Unix timestamp the warrant lapses at, nil if indefinite.

--- @type table<string, Warrant>
local activeWarrants = {}

--- Issues a warrant against a player.
--- Fails if the player already has a live warrant of the same kind.
--- @param ply Player The player to warrant.
--- @param issuer Player The officer issuing the warrant.
--- @param kind WarrantType What the warrant authorises.
--- @param reason string Why the warrant was issued.
--- @return boolean issued Whether a new warrant was created.
--- @return string? failure Why issuing failed, or nil on success.
--- @section warrants
function cityrp.warrants.issue(ply, issuer, kind, reason)
	if not IsValid(ply) then return false, "Invalid player." end
	...
end

--- Returns every live warrant against a player.
--- @param ply Player The player to look up.
--- @return Warrant[] warrants The player's live warrants, empty if none.
--- @nodiscard
function cityrp.warrants.getFor(ply)
	...
end

--- Old warrant lookup, kept for legacy callers.
--- @deprecated Use cityrp.warrants.getFor instead.
--- @param ply Player The player to look up.
--- @return table warrants The player's live warrants.
--- @bugs Does not filter out expired warrants.
function cityrp.warrants.legacyLookup(ply)
	...
end
```

## Checklist

Before considering an annotated change done:

- [ ] Every function you added or touched has a description ending in a full stop, plus a `@param`
      per parameter and a `@return` per returned value.
- [ ] No blank line anywhere between a doc comment and the declaration it documents.
- [ ] Every `@param` name matches the real parameter name, in order.
- [ ] No LDoc tags (`@tparam`, `@treturn`, `@classmod`, `@usage`, `@number`, `@local`) introduced.
- [ ] No `@module` — file headers use `@namespace`.
- [ ] Table parameters with a known shape are typed as a `@class`, not as bare `table`.
- [ ] Optional parameters and fields carry `?` on the type, as a nullable suffix.
- [ ] File header has `@namespace`, `@state`, `@copyright`, `@release`, and `@author`.
- [ ] `glualint` passes on the file — see
      [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/limelight-development/cityrp2/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#linting).

To verify the docs pipeline actually picked your annotations up, reproduce what CI does — if a
function you annotated is missing from the JSON, the cause is almost always rule 1 or rule 2 above:

```bash
lua-language-server --doc=gamemodes/cityrp_2_by_limelightgaming/gamemode \
                    --doc_out_path=tools/docs/out
python3 tools/docs/generate.py --json tools/docs/out/doc.json \
                               --output tools/docs/build \
                               --style-dir tools/docs/style \
                               --topics docs
```

CI pins LuaLS 3.18.2 (`.github/workflows/docs.yml`); annotations added after that release may parse
locally and not in CI.

topics.title: Maintenance Work System
topics.body:
# Maintenance Work System

The Maintenance Work System adds periodic maintenance tasks to entities around the city, providing a new avenue for income and making the server feel more alive. Entities randomly break down and require player intervention to repair.

## Overview

The maintenance system works by:
1. Scanning the map for entities that support maintenance
2. Randomly selecting entities to trigger maintenance events on
3. Displaying active maintenance jobs to players via HUD
4. Allowing players to fix maintenance issues for a reward

## Configuration

The maintenance plugin can be configured in `sh_init.lua`:

```lua
PLUGIN.config["Maintenance Timer"] = 300       -- Delay in seconds between triggering new maintenance events
PLUGIN.config["Max Maintenance Jobs"] = 3      -- Maximum number of active maintenance jobs at once
PLUGIN.config["Reward Fee"] = 1000             -- Amount to pay player for fixing maintenance issues
PLUGIN.config["Fix Distance"] = 200            -- Maximum distance in units to fix a maintenance issue
PLUGIN.config["Fix Cooldown"] = 300            -- Cooldown in seconds before an entity can break again after being fixed
```

## Maintenance Event Types

The system supports several maintenance event types:

| Type | Status | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Electronic | **Active** | Electronics fault with sparking visual effects |
| Water | **Active** | Water leak with visual spray effects (area-based) |
| Petrol | **Active** | Petrol leak with visual drip effects (area-based) |
| Gas | **Active** | Gas leak with visual cloud effects (area-based) |
| Restock | Not Used | Entity needs restocking (deprecated) |
| Destock | **Active** | Vending machine expired stock; dispose trash bag for payout |

### Electronic Maintenance

Entities with electronic faults display sparking effects and become non-functional until repaired.

**Supported Entities:**
- Phonebooths (`cityrp_phonebooth`)
- Vending Machines (`cityrp_nommachine`)
- Tesla Superchargers (`cityrp_tesla_supercharger`)
- Lift electrical boxes (map buttons)

### Water Maintenance

Area-based water leaks that display water spray effects. Created by admins at specific map locations.

**Status:** Active (area-based)

### Petrol Maintenance

Area-based petrol leaks that display drip effects. Created by admins at specific map locations.

**Status:** Active (area-based)

### Gas Maintenance

Area-based gas leaks that display cloud effects. Created by admins at specific map locations.

**Status:** Active (area-based)

### Destock Maintenance

Vending machines occasionally need expired products removed. Destocking is a two-step job:

1. A maintenance worker uses the machine (`+use`) to clear the maintenance flag and spawn a `cityrp_trashbag`
2. The trash bag must be placed in a `cityrp_rubbish_bin` to claim the reward payout

Clearing the machine restores normal use immediately — the worker does not need to finish the disposal step for the machine to work again. Payment is only granted when the bag is deposited. If a trash bag is abandoned, any player can pick it up and dispose of it for the reward.

**Supported Entities:**
- Vending Machines (`cityrp_nommachine`) — randomly Electric or Destock when a job triggers

**Testing:** `maintforce destock`

## Area-Based Maintenance Points

Water, Petrol, and Gas maintenance are area-based and require admin setup. These are positions on the map where leaks can randomly occur.

### Admin Commands

**Add a maintenance point:**
```
/maintpoint add <type>
```
Types: water, petrol, gas

Looks at where you're aiming and adds a maintenance point of the specified type.

**Remove nearby maintenance points:**
```
/maintpoint remove
```
Removes all maintenance points within 256 units of where you're aiming.

**List maintenance points:**
```
/maintpoint list
```
Shows total count and breakdown by type for the current map.

**Save maintenance points:**
```
/maintpoint save
```
Saves all maintenance points to the data folder. Points are automatically loaded on map start.

### Maintenance Point Storage

Points are saved per-map in:
```
garrysmod/data/cityrp/plugins/maintenance/<mapname>.txt
```

The file is automatically created when you save points.

## Adding Maintenance Support to Entities

To add maintenance support to a new entity:

### 1. Register the Entity Class

Add the entity class to `maintenanceEntClasses` in `sh_init.lua`:

```lua
PLUGIN.tab.maintenanceEntClasses = {
    ["ent_phonebooth"] = "Electronic",
    ["cityrp_nommachine"] = "Restock",
    ["your_entity_class"] = "Electronic", -- Your new entity
}
```

### 2. Initialize Maintenance in Entity

In your entity's `Initialize` function (server-side):

```lua
function ENT:Initialize()
    -- ... your existing initialization code ...
    
    local maintenancePlugin = cityrp.plugin.get("maintenance")
    if maintenancePlugin then
        self.maintenance = maintenancePlugin.electric  -- or .restock
        self.maintenance.disabled = false  -- for electric
        -- OR
        self.maintenance.needsRestock = false  -- for restock
    end
end
```

### 3. Check Maintenance Status in Use Function

In your entity's `Use` function (server-side):

```lua
function ENT:Use(activator, caller)
    -- Check if entity needs maintenance
    if self.maintenance and self.maintenance.disabled then
        activator:Notify("This entity is broken! Perhaps a mechanic could fix it?", NOTIFY_ERROR)
        return
    end
    
    -- OR for restock type:
    if self.maintenance and self.maintenance.needsRestock then
        activator:Notify("This entity needs restocking!", NOTIFY_ERROR)
        return
    end
    
    -- ... rest of your use logic ...
end
```

### 4. Add Client-Side Hints (Optional)

In your entity's `DrawTargetHUD` function (client-side):

```lua
function ENT:DrawTargetHUD(x, y, alpha)
    y = GAMEMODE:DrawInformation(self.PrintName, FONT_TARGETID_HEAD, x, y, COL_BRAND, alpha)
    
    if self.maintenance and self.maintenance.disabled then
        if cityrp.hints:Get("maintenance_work") then
            y = GAMEMODE:DrawInformation("This entity is broken. Use ␂maintfix␃ to repair it.", FONT_TARGETID, x, y, Color(255, 150, 0, alpha), alpha)
        else
            y = GAMEMODE:DrawInformation("This entity is broken.", FONT_TARGETID, x, y, Color(255, 150, 0, alpha), alpha)
        end
    elseif cityrp.hints:Get("entities") then
        y = GAMEMODE:DrawInformation("Press ␂+use␃ to interact.", FONT_TARGETID, x, y, COL_GUIDE, alpha)
    end
end
```

## Creating New Maintenance Types

To create a new maintenance type:

1. Create a new file in the maintenance plugin directory (e.g., `sh_water.lua`)
2. Define the maintenance type behavior:

```lua
---@state shared
local PLUGIN = PLUGIN_SHARED

PLUGIN.water = {}

---Trigger water maintenance on an entity
---@param e Entity The entity to trigger maintenance on
function PLUGIN.water:triggerMaintenance(e)
    self.leaking = true
    
    -- Add visual effects here (e.g., water spray particle effect)
end

---Fix water maintenance on an entity
---@param e Entity The entity to fix
---@param ply Player The player fixing the entity
function PLUGIN.water:fixMaintenance(e, ply)
    self.leaking = false
    
    ply:Notify("You fixed the water leak and earned $" .. string.Comma(PLUGIN.config["Reward Fee"]) .. "!", NOTIFY_HINT)
    ply:GiveMoney(PLUGIN.config["Reward Fee"])
    
    PLUGIN.tab.activeJobs[e] = nil
end
```

3. Include the file in `sv_init.lua`:

```lua
include("sh_water.lua")
AddCSLuaFile("sh_water.lua")
```

4. Update entity classes to use the new type in `sh_init.lua`:

```lua
PLUGIN.tab.maintenanceEntClasses = {
    ["your_entity"] = "Water",
}
```

## Player Commands

Players use the **Mechanic Wrench** SWEP to fix maintenance issues. Simply equip the wrench and left-click while aiming at a broken entity or standing near an area-based leak.

## User Interface

### Active Jobs HUD

Active maintenance jobs are displayed in the top-right corner of the screen, showing:
- A header "Maintenance Jobs"
- List of entities that need maintenance

### Entity Hints

When looking at an entity that needs maintenance:
- Entity displays its broken status
- If hints are enabled, shows the command to fix it (`maintfix`)

## Hints System Integration

The maintenance system integrates with CityRP's hints system under the "Maintenance Work" category. Players can toggle maintenance hints in **Options > Limelight > Hints**.

## System Behavior

1. **Entity Indexing**: On server start, the system indexes all entities on the map that support maintenance
2. **Point Loading**: Area-based maintenance points are loaded from the data folder for the current map
3. **Periodic Triggering**: Every 300 seconds (configurable), the system checks if new maintenance events should be triggered
4. **Max Jobs**: The system maintains up to 3 active maintenance jobs at once (configurable), combining both entity-based and area-based jobs
5. **Job Selection**: Jobs are randomly selected from both entity and area-based pools. Vending machines randomly choose Electric or Destock.
6. **Cooldowns**: After an entity is fixed, it goes on a 5-minute cooldown (configurable) before it can break again
7. **Client Sync**: Active jobs are synchronized to all clients for HUD display
8. **Distance Check**: Players must be within 200 units (configurable) of an entity or leak to fix it

## Future Enhancements

Planned features for future releases:
- Job-restricted maintenance (require specific jobs to fix certain types)
- Specialized tools or equipment requirements
- Difficulty-based rewards
- Integration with vehicle systems
- Damage effects for gas leaks

topics.title: MESKA
topics.body:
# MESKA

MESKA is CityRP's Metrics, Skills and Achievements framework. It stores player
activity as metrics, derives skill experience and levels from those metrics,
and evaluates achievements against persistent skill statistics.

## Startup lifecycle

`core/libraries/meska/init.lua` loads MESKA in this order:

1. Shared constants and helpers.
2. Database and cache providers.
3. Configuration and timers.
4. Daily bonus, custom bonus, metrics, skills and achievements.
5. MESKA's Garry's Mod hooks.

After CityRP reports `DBConnected`, MESKA:

1. loads achievement definitions;
2. loads daily bonuses;
3. synchronizes configured metrics;
4. emits `MESKA::ACHIEVEMENTS::READY`; and
5. emits `MESKA::INTEGRATIONS::SETUP` for add-on skills.

New skills must register on `MESKA::INTEGRATIONS::SETUP`. Registering earlier can
race the database connection, while registering later can omit the skill from a
player's first metrics provisioning pass.

## Skill configuration

`meska.skills.setup(name, config)` adds four configuration sections:

- `metrics`: named counters and products;
- `defaults`: minimum and maximum level;
- `perks`: level-gated benefits; and
- `guides`: Skills-page guide entries.

It also registers the supplied achievements and synchronizes the metric
configuration to the database.

Every metric includes:

```lua
{
	lvl = 1,
	exp = 1,
	highlight = false,
	requirements = {},
	excludeFromProductEligibility = true
}
```

`exp` is the amount of skill XP granted per tracked unit. Metrics used only as
achievement counters should use `exp = 0`.

## Persistence

MESKA uses these configured tables:

| Table | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `meska_metrics` | Per-skill metric definitions, defaults, perks and guides |
| `meska_metrics_user` | Player metrics and skill stats stored as JSON |
| `meska_achievements` | Achievement definitions |
| `meska_achievements_requirements` | Achievement requirements |
| `meska_achievements_rewards` | Achievement rewards |
| `meska_achievements_user` | Awarded achievements |
| `meska_dailybonus` | Global skill bonuses |
| `meska_custombonus` | Player-specific skill bonuses |

The database schema also uses `meska_skills.name` as the parent registry for
skill names. `meska_metrics.skill` has a foreign key to that registry. A new
skill must therefore create its `meska_skills` row before MESKA inserts metric
configuration or skill-scoped achievements.

Player data in `meska_metrics_user` has two JSON documents:

- `metrics.<skill>.<metric>` stores metric counters; and
- `stats.<skill>.exp` and `stats.<skill>.lvl` store experience and level.

`meska.metrics.initFor` inserts missing JSON paths for a player.
`meska.skills.loadFor` reads those paths into `ply.meska.skills` and mirrors the
result to the client `skills` network variable.

## Tracking and levels

Call:

```lua
meska.metrics.track(ply, "skill_name", "metric_name", "+1")
```

MESKA multiplies the tracked amount by the metric's `exp`, applies active daily
and custom bonuses, updates the player's metric and stats JSON, then calculates:

```text
level = floor((experience ^ (1 / 3)) / 1.4)
```

The configured minimum and maximum are applied when skills load. A level
increase emits `MESKA::SKILLS::LEVELUP`.

## Achievements

Achievement requirements are evaluated by
`MESKA::Achievements::MeetsRequirements`. The important requirement types are:

- `stats`: compare `skills[skill .. "_lvl"]` or another skill statistic; and
- `metrics`: compare `skills[skill][metric]`.

MESKA scans connected players every five minutes. Systems may also call
`meska.achievements.award(ply)` after a metric update when immediate feedback is
important.

Requirement evaluation must treat a missing skill table as unmet. It must not
index through a missing skill, because players connected during a hot reload can
temporarily have an older MESKA cache.

## Reset and debugging

MESKA does not currently register a chat or console command that resets player
achievements, skill XP or metrics. The Car Boosting
`!boosting debug refresh|status|complete|fail` actions exercise active Boosting
contracts; they do not revoke MESKA awards or clear persistent MESKA data.

Awarded achievements are rows in `meska_achievements_user`, while skill metrics
and stats are JSON fields in `meska_metrics_user`. A development reset therefore
needs a deliberately scoped database operation for one SteamID and the affected
skill or achievement, followed by a reconnect or explicit cache reload. This
should not be exposed as an unrestricted live-server command.

## Boosting Skill

Car Boosting registers `boosting` as its own skill. The Skills web page formats
that registry entry as **Boosting Skill** and groups Boosting achievements under
it.

The integration first ensures this parent row exists:

```sql
INSERT IGNORE INTO `meska_skills` (`name`) VALUES ('boosting');
```

Only after that query succeeds does it register metrics and achievements. It
then re-provisions any connected player whose cache predates the new skill.

This order prevents:

```text
meska_metrics_meska_skills_name_fk
```

from rejecting the `meska_metrics` insert. MESKA's metric-requirement hook also
checks the intermediate skill table, preventing the later nil access previously
reported at `hooks.lua:194`.

## Adding another skill

1. Pick a lowercase stable skill identifier.
2. Insert or migrate its `meska_skills` registry row.
3. Register on `MESKA::INTEGRATIONS::SETUP`.
4. Give counter-only metrics `exp = 0`.
5. Use unique achievement aliases.
6. Re-provision connected players if hot reload is supported.
7. Confirm the skill, guides and achievements appear on the Skills page.
8. Reconnect and confirm metrics, XP, levels and awards persist.
9. Test with a player cache that does not yet contain the new skill.

topics.title: Modern APIs

meta.description: The authoritative list of which API to use for each category, and what it replaces.

topics.body:
# Modern APIs CityRP is a mature codebase containing many legacy patterns and deprecated systems. The table below is the authoritative, up-to-date list of which API to use for each category. Legacy alternatives remain in the codebase — because they predate the migration, not because they're still correct — and must not be used in new or refactored code. Agents also see a condensed always-on copy of this table in [`.cursor/rules/agent-musts.mdc`](../.cursor/rules/agent-musts.mdc). When you add or change a row here, update that MUST card in the same change. The checklist and CI reject criteria for forbidden patterns are in [Coding Standards](coding-standards.md). | Category | ✅ Modern API (MANDATORY) | ❌ Legacy / Standard GMod (FORBIDDEN) | Why? | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Audit Logging** (player/admin actions, transactions) | `cityrp.logs.add(nick, steamid, ...)` | `print()`
`ServerLog()` | Logs to database and admin interfaces for moderation/audit; `print` is invisible to admins. | | **Diagnostic Logging** (developer debugging, traces) | `cityrp.logging.GetLogger(namespace):Debug/Info/Error(...)` | `print()`
`ServerLog()` | Namespaced, level-filterable developer diagnostics. Does not replace `cityrp.logs.add()` for audit events. See [logging.md](logging.md). | | **Items** | `ITEM:New("base_id")` (Fluent), or `ITEM:New()` for no base | `cityrp.item.register({})` | Metatable-based fluent API with better inheritance and cleaner code, and it doesn't require a spawnable/purchasable base item to be registered just to be inherited from. See [items.md](items/items.md). | | **Networking** | See tiers below | `umsg.*`, `SendLua()`, `BroadcastLua()` (banned) | Pick the highest tier that fits; `cityrp.network` exists as a library but isn't mandatory yet, so legacy networking (NSVar/LocalPlayerVar) remains the correct default; never use the banned tier. | | **Color Constants** | `COL_WHITE`, `COL_BLACK`, `COL_RED`, `COL_GREEN`, `COL_BLUE`, `COL_GREY` (from `sh_enumerations.lua`) | `color_white`, `color_black` (GMod globals) | Consistency, easier global theming later, reduces reliance on GMod globals. Custom one-off colors are still fine as inline `Color(...)` calls. | | **Running a CityRP command from code** | `ply:ConCommand("cityrp ")` (clientside UI)
`cityrp.command.consoleCommand(ply, cmd, argsTable)` (serverside) | `ply:ConCommand("say / ")` | Both end up in `cityrp.command.consoleCommand`; `say /` only adds the chat pipeline in front of it, where a `PlayerSay` hook can swallow the message, `cityrp.replacecodes` rewrites `%`/`$q` codes inside the arguments, >452 characters are dropped silently, and the arguments are re-quoted by a naive scanner. See [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md) footgun #13. | | **"Is this plugin here?"** (guarding a cross-plugin call) | `cityrp.plugin.IsAvailable("")` | `cityrp.plugin.get("") ~= nil`; unguarded cross-plugin calls | `get` only sees plugins that called `register`, and ~27 loaded plugins never do — so it reports them missing. `IsAvailable` reads the loader's bookkeeping, is realm-accurate, and answers `false` for every reason a plugin can be absent. Use `cityrp.plugin.GetDependencyStatus(key)` when you need to know *which* reason; it is for diagnostics, not for guards. See [plugins.md](plugins.md#guarding-a-cross-plugin-call). | | **Plugin lookup** (you need the plugin's table) | `cityrp.plugin.get("")` — the folder key, as used by `.meta.lua` and load order. Inside a plugin, `cityrp.plugin.get(PLUGIN.key)` | `cityrp.plugin.get("Display Name")`; indexing `cityrp.plugin.stored` directly | `cityrp.plugin.stored` is keyed by the plugin key. A display name still resolves through `cityrp.plugin.names` and costs the same, but warns once per name — the two identities are not derivable from each other (`area` registers as `"Area Manager"`). Existing display-name call sites work; convert one when you are already editing that code. See [plugins.md](plugins.md) and [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md) footgun #22. | | **Console Entity** | `CONSOLE` | `console` (lowercase) | `console` is a deprecated alias kept only for backwards compatibility with external plugins — see `admin/sv_init.lua`. | | **Player chat commands** (`/` prefix; aka normal / slash-commands) | `cityrp.command.add(name, access, minArgs, callback, category, syntax, tip[, emgr])` | Raw `PlayerSay` / `concommand` parsers for gamemode commands; staff tools registered as `/` | Non-privileged player RP/job tools only — generally available to all players. **Always** pass category (key from `categoryAliases`), syntax (`""` if none; shown on invalid-syntax errors), and a short tip description for the F1 commands menu. Callback is `(ply, arguments)` table. See [commands.md](commands.md) and [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md) footgun #14. | | **Staff chat commands** (`!` prefix; aka privileged / admin / staff commands) | `cityrp.acommands.AddCommand(name, func, minArgs, access, emgr, category, syntax, tip)` | Staff tools on `/` (even with a restricted access flag); ad-hoc `PlayerSay` handlers for `!` | **Always** use this if the command requires staff privileges of any kind — including RP Assistant. Same mandatory category/syntax/tip metadata as player commands. Callback is `(ply, ...)` varargs. When moving a staff tool from `/` to `!`, leave `cityrp.command.redirectToAcommand(oldName)` so `/old` only notifies to use `!old`. Prefer `cityrp.player.resolveTarget` and `cityrp.command.parseMoney` over copy-pasted lookup/money parsing. See [commands.md](commands.md) and [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md) footgun #14. | | **UI Scaling** (Derma panels, entity menus, HUD overlays, custom `Paint`) | `cityrp.ui.Scale()`, `cityrp.ui.GetScaleFactor()`, `cityrp.ui.CreateScaledFont()`, `cityrp.ui.OnScaleChanged()` | Ad-hoc `ScrW() / 1920` scaling; calling `LimelightHUD.GetScaleFactor()` directly; fixed `surface.CreateFont` sizes; hardcoded pixel dimensions that never rebuild on scale change | One resolution- and preference-aware scale for all UI; fonts and layout stay in sync when `cl_llhud_scale` or screen size changes. See [ui-scaling.md](ui-scaling.md) and [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md) footgun #15. | If existing code conflicts with this table, follow this table — usage of a legacy pattern elsewhere in the codebase is not evidence it's the correct approach, only that it predates this list. ## Networking tiers Networking isn't a simple modern/legacy split — use the **highest tier that fits the use case**, don't default to a lower one out of habit. 1. **Top tier: Entity Networking (DTVars).** `Entity:NetworkVar(...)` / DataTables (`SetupDataTables`). Use for anything that's naturally a property of a **Lua-authored** entity (a SENT or SWEP you define yourself) — it's predicted, delta-compressed, and needs no manual send/receive code. **This does not work for GMod's engine-defined vehicle base classes** (`prop_vehicle_jeep`, `prop_vehicle_prisoner_pod`, etc.) — they don't run `SetupDataTables` the way a Lua SENT does, so DTVars aren't an option for vehicle state. See tier 4. 2. **`cityrp.network`.** `cityrp.network.Register(...)` (`core/libraries/sh_network.lua`, see [networking.md](networking.md)). Covers anything tier 1 doesn't: non-player entity state (doors, vehicles, signs), Global-scope values, LocalPlayer-private state, or any value that needs recipient filtering (`:Filter()`, `:SendPVS()`/`:SendPAS()`), a change hook, or pull-on-visible resync. **Not yet mandatory** — see *Migration status* below before reaching for this tier over tier 3. See [networking.md](networking.md) for the full builder-chain reference. 3. **Legacy networking.** For events/actions, use `net.*` directly. For player state that isn't a natural entity property: - `ply:SetNSVar(name, value)` / `ply:GetNSVar(name, default)` — for state every client needs to know about that player (broadcast to all clients via `net.Broadcast()`). - `cityrp.player.setLocalPlayerVariable(ply, CLASS_TYPE, "_Name", value)` — for state only the owning client needs (sent privately via `net.Send(ply)`). - Both require the variable name to be pre-registered (see `networking/sh_init.lua`) — setting an unregistered name fails **silently**, with only a `print()` to console, not an error. Register the name first. - **Both are Player-metatable-only** (`FindMetaTable("Player")`) — they don't generalize to vehicles or other non-player entities. For non-player entity state, `net.*` directly is the current option (tier 2 isn't mandatory yet — see below). - Not deprecated: this tier works, is still reasonably efficient, and is the correct default today. It just sits below `cityrp.network` once that tier becomes mandatory. 4. **Avoided: low-tier networking.** `SetNWInt`/`SetNW2Int`/etc. (NW/NW2 vars). Avoid for player data — don't use it in new or refactored code, see [problems/03](../problems/03-deprecated-network-vars.md) and [improvements/01](../improvements/01-deprecated-networked-variables.md). **Exception**: vehicles currently use this tier for real (`sv_vehicle.lua`'s `locked`/`engine_on`/`HP` state) precisely because neither tier 1 (DTVars — engine entity, no `SetupDataTables`) nor tier 3 (NSVar/LocalPlayerVar — Player-only) apply to them, and they haven't been migrated to tier 2 yet. Until that migration lands, this is the practically justified option for vehicles, not just legacy inertia. 5. **Banned.** `umsg.*` (pre-`net` legacy usermessage library — no structure or size guarantees `net` provides), `SendLua()`, `BroadcastLua()` (execute arbitrary Lua source on the client — a code-injection vector if the string is ever built from anything less than a fully trusted, static literal, and pure legacy debt even when it isn't). Never use these. ### Migration status `cityrp.network` has landed as a library only — no call site has been migrated, and it is **not yet mandatory** for new or refactored code. `SetNSVar`/`GetNSVar`, `cityrp.player.setLocalPlayerVariable`/`Player:SetLPlyVar`, and `SetNW*` for vehicles all remain the correct APIs to use until a separate, later change flips this note and starts requiring `cityrp.network` for the call sites described in tier 2. Do not start converting call sites to `cityrp.network` off this note alone. See [issue #3207](https://github.com/limelight-development/cityrp2/issues/3207) for the full migration plan.

topics.title: Networking Library
topics.body:
# Networking Library

`cityrp.network` (`gamemode/core/libraries/sh_network.lua` and `core/libraries/network/`) is the
unified replacement for three overlapping systems: engine `SetNW*`/`GetNW*`, NSVars, and
LocalPlayerVars (`core/plugins/networking`). See [issue #3207](https://github.com/limelight-development/cityrp2/issues/3207)
for the full rationale.

**Status: migration in progress.** `cityrp.network` is its own tier — above legacy networking
(NSVar/LocalPlayerVar/`SetNW*`) and below nothing except DTVars — but it is **not yet mandatory**;
see [Networking tiers](modern-apis.md#networking-tiers). The library is live and the first call sites
have moved onto it (`gamemode/core/libraries/sh_network_vars.lua`), but `core/plugins/networking` is
still fully live too, and `SetNSVar` / `GetNSVar` / `SetLPlyVar` / `SetNW*` remain the correct APIs to
use for now — not deprecated, just a lower tier that hasn't been superseded yet. Move a call site as
a deliberate change, with its legacy registration removed in the same commit — not opportunistically
off this topic alone.

## Why a new library

- **NSVars are player-only.** Non-player entities (doors, vehicles, signs) still have no option but
  the deprecated `SetNW*`/`GetNW*` tier — see [problems/03](../problems/03-deprecated-network-vars.md).
- **No recipient filtering.** NSVars are `net.Broadcast()` or nothing; LocalPlayerVars are
  owner-only or nothing. Nothing in between — no faction-private, gang-private, or police-private
  state without hand-rolling a new `net.*` message.
- **The registration ID is a positional wire contract.** NSVars assign IDs by call order
  (`#registered + 1`); any load-order divergence between the client and server realm shifts every
  ID and silently corrupts every value, with no error.
- **Recycled indices leak state.** The client keys NSVar state by raw entity index
  (`PLUGIN.NSVars[entIndex]`) and never clears an entry on disconnect, so a new player who receives a
  recycled index inherits whatever the previous occupant left behind.
- **Broadcast while out of PVS is lost.** There is no pull-on-visible path — a value set while a
  client is out of range never reaches it unless something else happens to resend it later.

## Core concepts

A **network var** is registered once, in shared code, with a builder chain:

```lua
cityrp.network.Register("cityrp_VehicleLocked")
	:SetEntity()
	:Bool()
	:SendPVS()
	:SetHook("CityRP.VehicleLockChanged")
	:Accessor("VehicleLocked")
```

Registration must happen before the registry **seals**, which occurs automatically on the
`Initialize` hook (both realms). Registering afterward is a logged error and the var is never
networked — register vars at file scope or from an early hook, not lazily on first use.

### Scope

Exactly one scope per var, set with one of these (default: `:SetEntity()`):

| Method | Storage | Default recipients |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `:SetEntity()` | On the entity (`ent.__netvars`) | Broadcast |
| `:SetPlayer()` | Same as Entity — a player is an entity. Routes `:Accessor()` to `FindMetaTable("Player")` — see *Accessor targets* below. | Broadcast |
| `:SetVehicle()` | Same as Entity. Routes `:Accessor()` to `FindMetaTable("Vehicle")`. | Broadcast |
| `:SetWeapon()` | Same as Entity. Routes `:Accessor()` to `FindMetaTable("Weapon")`. | Broadcast |
| `:SetLocalPlayer()` | On the owning player | That player only, always — recipient methods below don't apply |
| `:SetGlobal()` | In the library, no owning entity | Broadcast |

`:SetEntity()`, `:SetPlayer()`, `:SetVehicle()`, and `:SetWeapon()` are identical in storage and wire
framing — `cityrp.network.IsEntityScope(scope)` is `true` for all four. The only thing that differs
between them is which metatable `:Accessor()` attaches its generated methods to. `:SetLocalPlayer()`
also routes to `FindMetaTable("Player")`, despite differing in storage/recipients from the other four.

### Codecs

Call one codec method per var (default is `:Auto()` if none is called):

| Method | Wire shape |
| :--- | :--- |
| `:Bool()` | 1 byte via `net.WriteBool` |
| `:Bit()` | Raw bit via `net.WriteBit`/`net.ReadBit`, returns `0`/`1` rather than a boolean |
| `:Nibble()` / `:UNibble()` | 4-bit signed/unsigned |
| `:Byte()` / `:UByte()` | 8-bit signed/unsigned |
| `:Short()` / `:UShort()` | 16-bit signed/unsigned |
| `:Int()` / `:UInt()` | 32-bit signed/unsigned |
| `:Integer(bits)` / `:UInteger(bits)` | Explicit 1-32 bit width |
| `:Float()` | 32-bit IEEE float |
| `:Double()` | 64-bit IEEE double |
| `:Long()` | Alias of `:Double()` — see *Integer widths* below |
| `:String()` | `net.WriteString` — null-terminated, so the writer decides the length |
| `:String(maxLen)` | Length-prefixed: a fixed-width count, then that many bytes. Variable length, hard ceiling, no padding — see *Bounded strings* below |
| `:Vector()` | Three signed components, each auto-choosing float vs. compact integer |
| `:Normal()` | Compact vector encoding for components that stay within ±1 |
| `:Angle()` | Same per-component encoding as `:Vector()` |
| `:Color()` | RGB plus an optional alpha byte (only sent if alpha isn't 255) |
| `:Entity()` | `net.WriteEntity`/`net.ReadEntity` |
| `:Player()` | `net.WritePlayer`/`net.ReadPlayer` — narrower than `:Entity()`, sized off `MAX_PLAYER_BITS` instead of `MAX_EDICT_BITS`. `:Auto()` picks this over `:Entity()` on its own whenever the value is a player. |
| `:Table()` | Recursive, self-describing — each key/value goes through `:Auto()` |
| `:Data(maxLen)` | Fixed-length byte string via `net.WriteData`/`net.ReadData` |
| `:Auto()` | Self-describing: a small type tag, then the value. What NSVars do today. |
| `:Write(fn, opt)` / `:Read(fn, opt)` | Custom codec — see *Custom codecs* below |
| `:Enum(list)` | Fixed set of legal values — see *Enums* below |

#### Integer widths

`net.WriteInt`/`net.WriteUInt` only accept 1-32 bits. NSVars' `NETTYPE_LONG` (64) and
`NETTYPE_XLONG` (128) passed 64/128 to those functions and could never actually work. Separately,
GLua numbers are IEEE doubles, so no integer above 2^53 can round-trip through Lua regardless of how
it's framed on the wire. `:Long()` is therefore an alias of `:Double()` — the widest integer GLua can
actually represent exactly — not a wider integer codec. There is no `:XLong()`; nothing in Lua can
hold the value, so the name would only reproduce the old illusion.

#### Bounded strings

`:String()` reads with `net.ReadString()`, which runs to a null the *sender* places — the length is
whatever arrives, capped only by the 64 KB `net` limit. `:String(maxLen)` instead writes a length
prefix and reads exactly that many bytes, so the ceiling comes from the registration and never from
the wire.

The prefix is a **fixed** width (`CODEC_ARG_BITS`), not one derived from `maxLen`. Deriving it cost a
day on beta: `math.floor(math.log(64, 2)) + 1` answers 6 or 7 depending on whether the expression was
interpreted or JIT-compiled, so the two realms sized the same prefix differently and the payload
arrived shifted by one bit — with the length still decoding correctly, because the extra bit happened
to be zero. Every bit width in this library is now either a constant, written to the wire beside its
value, or carried in the manifest. None is recomputed independently on both realms and assumed to
match.

That distinction is what makes it the only string form `:ClientOwned()` accepts. `:Data(maxLen)` is
equally safe to read — its length also comes from the registration — but it is *fixed* width, not
up-to-width: it pads short values with `\0` and costs `maxLen` bytes regardless, which is right for a
fixed-shape token and wrong for text.

Nothing is ever truncated silently, and the three ways it can happen are not the same severity:

| Where | What it means | What happens |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| A value longer than `maxLen` is written | A bug — data is being lost | Logged as an error naming both lengths, then truncated, exactly as `:Integer()`/`:Data()` report being called wrong |
| A decoded length prefix exceeds `maxLen` | Not truncation — a malformed or hostile message | The read is clamped for safety and **the rest of the message is abandoned**, the same contract `DecodeEntry` already has for an unknown var id |

The second row is the one worth understanding: the byte stream is desynced the moment the prefix
lies, so clamping and carrying on would corrupt every sibling var batched behind it rather than just
the offending one.

`maxLen` counts **bytes**, so a truncation can split a multi-byte character. That only happens on a
path that has already logged an error, but it is why the limit should be set from the byte length you
actually mean to allow.

#### Custom codecs

`:Write(fn, opt)` / `:Read(fn, opt)` bypass the built-in codec table entirely. Because the manifest
(below) can't describe an arbitrary function, a custom-codec var is always sent **alone in its own
message**, never batched alongside other vars — an undecodable custom value can then only ever
corrupt its own message, not a whole batch riding with it. Both realms must register the same var
with matching `:Write`/`:Read` calls; a client that never called `:Read()` for a name the manifest
describes as Custom-coded logs an error and drops that message when one arrives.

#### Enums

`:Enum(list)` declares a var's legal values as `list`, a sequential (`ipairs`-ordered) array, and
picks between two wire strategies by comparing their actual bit cost:

- **Direct value** (batchable) — if `list` is entirely integers, the value itself goes on the wire,
  sized to its min/max via `:Integer`/`:UInteger` (signed only if the set dips below zero). No offset
  from the minimum is applied even when every value shares a large common magnitude (e.g. `{100,
  101}`) — an offset would itself need a per-var `:Write()`/`:Read()` closure, i.e. `CODEC_CUSTOM`,
  which is exactly the cost this path exists to avoid. Order carries no wire meaning here.
- **Mapped index** (not batchable) — the value's *index* in `list` goes on the wire instead, via an
  auto-generated `:Write()`/`:Read()` pair sized to `#list`. `CODEC_CUSTOM` under the hood (see
  *Custom codecs* above), so a resync entry using it never shares a message with sibling vars on the
  same entity — its own `WriteIndexHeader` plus framing, and its own resync-queue slot. Order **does**
  matter here: it's the wire index, so both realms must register the same var with the same list in
  the same order.

For an all-integer `list`, the mapped index is only chosen if it beats the direct-value bit cost by
more than `cityrp.network.RESYNC_GROUP_OVERHEAD_BITS` (24), the approximate resync-framing cost of
escaping batching. A `list` containing anything non-integer (strings, mixed types) always uses the
mapped index; there's no numeric value to size a direct encoding from.

Either way, `Set`ting a value that isn't in `list` is rejected — logged and dropped, never stored or
sent — rather than silently encoding as something adjacent or vanishing into no enum value at all.
`nil` (clearing the var) always bypasses this check.

```lua
-- Direct value: dense, low-magnitude set — 3 bits, batchable.
cityrp.network.Register("cityrp_Rank"):SetPlayer():Enum({1, 2, 3, 4}):Accessor("Rank")

-- Mapped index: small set, but string-valued (no direct encoding available) — 3 bits, not batchable.
cityrp.network.Register("pass"):Enum({"grey", "green", "blue", "orange", "red"}):Accessor("Pass")
```

### Recipients

Only meaningful for Entity/Player/Vehicle/Weapon/Global scope — LocalPlayer scope is always
owner-only regardless.

| Method | Behaviour |
| :--- | :--- |
| `:Broadcast()` | Default. Sends to everyone. |
| `:SendPVS()` | `net.SendPVS(ent:GetPos())` — everyone who can potentially see the position. |
| `:SendPAS()` | `net.SendPAS(ent:GetPos())` — everyone who can potentially hear it. |
| `:SendOmit(fn)` | `fn(ent, value)` returns who to exclude; everyone else gets it. |
| `:Filter(fn)` | `fn(ent, value)` returns who receives it — a `Player`, a `Player[]`, or a `CRecipientFilter`. |

**`:Filter()` is the only secrecy boundary.** PVS, PAS, and Omit are treated as **bandwidth**
optimizations, not authorization: resync and the join bootstrap (below) always include a PVS/PAS/Omit
var's current value for a player who's asking, because pull-on-visible only fires once the client is
already in a position to receive it anyway. If a value must never reach a player at all — faction,
gang, or police-private data — use `:Filter()`, not `:SendOmit()`. `:Filter()`'s callback doubles as
that authorization check: the same function that decides who gets a *live* update also decides who's
allowed to pull it via resync, so there's exactly one predicate to keep correct, not two that can
drift apart. Keep `:Filter()` callbacks cheap and free of side effects — they can run once per set
and again per resync candidate.

### Behaviour

| Method | Effect |
| :--- | :--- |
| `:SetHook(name)` | Runs `hook.Run(name, ent, newValue, oldValue, predicted)` on both realms when the value changes. `predicted` is `true` only for a client-side local apply the server hasn't confirmed — see below. |
| `:AutoHook()` | Shorthand for `:SetHook("CityRP.Network.<name>.Changed")` — use when you don't care what the hook is called. |
| `:Accessor(name)` | Generates `Get<Name>()` (both realms) and `Set<Name>()` (server only, unless `:Predictable()`) — see *Accessor targets* below for which metatable. |
| `:Predictable()` | Also generates a client-side `Set<Name>()` for local prediction — see below. Only valid on `:SetLocalPlayer()`. |
| `:ClientOwned()` | Lets the client set this var on its own player and have the server accept it — see *Client-owned vars* below. Requires `:SetPlayer()`/`:SetLocalPlayer()`, a bounded codec, and a `:Debounce()`. |
| `:Debounce(seconds[, ceiling])` | Coalesces sets to at most one change per `seconds` — see *Debouncing* below. `ceiling` reserves the shape for adaptive backoff; omit it and the interval never moves. |
| `:SetNoSync()` | Excludes the var from the join bootstrap and resync — push-only. A client that was out of PVS during a push never gets it. |
| `:SetDefault(value)` | What `Entity:GetNetVar`/`cityrp.network.GetGlobal` return before anything is set. |

#### Client-side prediction

`:Set<Name>()` is normally server-only — setting is server-authoritative, and the underlying
`SetNetVar`/`SetGlobal` don't exist on the client realm at all (`sv_send.lua` is a server-only file).
`:Predictable()` opts a `:SetLocalPlayer()` var out of that: the client gets its own `Set<Name>()`
too, which applies the value locally (storage + the `:SetHook()` hook, with `predicted = true` — never
a network send, the client has no authority to send anything) instead of calling into the
server-only machinery. `:ClientOwned()` below is the other way out of that rule, and the one that
does send.

This is for the standard prediction-and-reconciliation shape: client-side code that runs under
`IsFirstTimePredicted()` calls `Set<Name>()` immediately for instant feedback, while the server keeps
computing and pushing the authoritative value exactly as it always did. When that confirmed value
arrives back at the client through the normal decode path, it overwrites whatever was predicted
locally — correcting any drift the same way it always corrected a live update, no special-case
reconciliation code needed. If the client's prediction already matched, the delta guard in
`ApplyValue` means nothing observable happens; if it didn't, the value snaps to the server's.

Only valid for `:SetLocalPlayer()` — a client predicting some other entity's state has no
server-authoritative copy of *that* entity's future value to reconcile against, so the scope doesn't
make sense there. Using `:Predictable()` on any other scope logs an error at accessor-generation time
and simply doesn't generate the client-side setter, rather than producing a footgun that looks like
it works.

```lua
cityrp.network.Register("_Stamina"):SetLocalPlayer():UByte():Accessor("Stamina"):Predictable()

-- In shared code, guarded the same way any other predicted mutation is:
if SERVER or IsFirstTimePredicted() then
	ply:SetStamina(newValue) -- works on both realms now
end
```

#### Client-owned vars

`:ClientOwned()` is the only supported client→server write path. The generated `Set<Name>()` becomes
available on the client, where it applies the value locally and then sends it; the server validates
the sender, decodes it, and hands it to `ply:SetNetVar()` — the ordinary server-side setter.

```lua
cityrp.network.Register("cityrp_F1Open"):SetPlayer():Bool():Accessor("F1Open")
	:ClientOwned():Debounce(1):SetDefault(false)

-- Client, wherever the menu opens and closes:
LocalPlayer():SetF1Open(true)
```

Because the receiver hands off to `SetNetVar`, **everything else composes for free**: the var's
`:Enum()` validator, its delta guard, its `:Debounce()` and its recipient mode all behave exactly as
they would for a server-set value. A client-owned var is *not* implicitly a broadcast one. `:Filter()`
is the interesting combination, since its callback doubles as the resync authorization check — "only
my faction sees this claim" is a supported shape — and `:SetLocalPlayer()` is coherent too: the claim
reaches nobody but the sender, with a server-side `:SetHook()` doing the work.

**The value is a claim, not a fact.** The library relays it faithfully and never second-guesses it,
so it carries exactly the authority the sender has: none. Never gate permissions, economy or
anti-cheat on one. The worst a liar can do to `cityrp_F1Open` is produce fake overhead text — that is
the bar a new client-owned var has to clear.

Constraints, all checked when the registry seals, each a logged error that clears the flag rather
than a silently-generated hole:

- **`:SetPlayer()` or `:SetLocalPlayer()` scope.** The message carries no entity index — the server
  applies it to whoever sent it — so a client cannot address another entity. That is structural, not
  a check to remember.
- **A bounded codec.** The test is not "is it small" but "who decides how much the server reads".
  Fixed-width codecs, `:Enum()`, `:Data(maxLen)` and `:String(maxLen)` all read a width fixed by the
  registration. `:Auto()` (a wire-supplied type tag), unbounded `:String()` and `:Table()` all let the
  sender decide, and are refused. A hand-written `:Write()`/`:Read()` pair is refused for the same
  reason; `:Enum()`'s generated one is admitted, because its read is a fixed-width index.
- **A `:Debounce()`.** Accepting unthrottled client-authored state isn't supported.

Chaining `:Predictable()` as well is redundant — client-owned already applies locally first — and
warns rather than erroring.

Sets made before the manifest arrives are **buffered and flushed once it lands**, latest-wins per
var. Accessors exist from `Initialize`, but the client's var IDs come from the manifest, which
arrives after `InitPostEntity`; without the buffer, a var pushed once at startup ("my setting is X")
would be silently lost. The local apply still happens immediately — only the send waits.

##### Claims are not adjudicated

Whether a claim is currently *meaningful* — the player is alive, awake, not spectating, in range, on
the right job — is decided by whatever **consumes** it, never at the point of claim. There is
deliberately no server-side accept predicate and no server-side clear.

A rejecting predicate would strand state. Player opens F1 while alive, is killed, closes F1 — the
predicate refuses the close because they're dead, and "In Inventory" sits over their head for the
rest of the round. Every fix for that is machinery that exists only to undo damage the predicate
caused.

The condition also belongs at the consumer anyway, where it is *shared*: the overhead renderer
already needs a liveness test, and one test there covers `cityrp_Typing`, `cityrp_F1Open` and every
claim added later, rather than each var repeating the same three checks.

The check does not disappear, though — it **moves**, and is now the consumer's to write.

#### Debouncing

`:Debounce(seconds)` caps how often a var may actually change. It is not client-only — any
high-churn var can opt into it — but `:ClientOwned()` requires one.

- A set during a quiet period applies and dispatches **immediately**. No artificial latency on the
  common case.
- A set inside the window overwrites a **single pending slot**, latest wins, no accumulation.
- The pending value is applied when the window closes.

Coalescing rather than a token bucket, because these are **state, not events**. A bucket *drops*
updates, and a dropped "F1 closed" leaves everyone seeing stale overhead text until that player opens
and closes F1 again at a politer rate. Coalescing can't do that — the last value always lands, it
just lands late.

Most of the saving comes from the delta guard rather than the throttling: a rapid
`true → false → true → false` burst settles on a value that usually equals what is already stored, so
the flush reports no change and **nothing goes on the wire at all**. Pathological spam costs one
inbound decode per message and zero outbound messages.

The debounce covers the **apply**, not only the send, so there stays exactly one notion of a var's
current value. The cost, and the one surprising consequence: a server-side `GetNetVar` lags a
`SetNetVar` by up to the interval, so the two no longer round-trip within a frame.

`ceiling` reserves the shape for adaptive backoff — escalate on sustained *dispatches*, reset to the
floor after a full quiet window. It is inert today: omitting it sets `ceiling == seconds`, so the
interval never moves. Escalation counts dispatches rather than inbound messages deliberately, since a
burst that coalesces back to its original value costs the server nothing and must not be throttled
for it.

Pending and escalated pairs are drained on `Think` against a weak-keyed set, the same shape the
resync queues use, rather than a timer per player per var.

#### Accessor targets

`:Accessor(name)` attaches to `FindMetaTable("Entity")` for Entity/Global scope, `FindMetaTable("Player")`
for Player/LocalPlayer scope, and `FindMetaTable("Vehicle")`/`FindMetaTable("Weapon")` for those.
Calling `Entity:GetNetVar`/`SetNetVar` itself would already work identically regardless — GMod
resolves a method not found on a more specific metatable by falling through to Entity's — but the one
case that fallthrough doesn't cover is a same-named method the *more specific* metatable already
defines natively: it would shadow an Entity-attached `Get<Name>`/`Set<Name>` for every entity of that
type, silently calling the native method instead of yours. Attaching directly to the matching
metatable instead puts your accessor closer than Entity's in the lookup chain, so it wins.

This is a real, present-day risk, not a hypothetical one: `sv_vehicle.lua`'s `locked`, `engine_on`,
and `HP` state — the values [modern-apis.md](modern-apis.md) names as the reason vehicles still use
the otherwise-avoided `SetNW*` tier — are exactly the kind of vehicle-specific accessor a scope 2
migration would want to name `Locked`/`EngineOn`/`HP`, and `FindMetaTable("Vehicle")` is already
extended in this codebase (`core/metatables/sh_vehicle.lua`).

### Reading and writing

```lua
-- Server only
ent:SetNetVar("cityrp_VehicleLocked", true)
cityrp.network.SetGlobal("WeatherState", 2)

-- Both realms
local locked = ent:GetNetVar("cityrp_VehicleLocked", false)
local weather = cityrp.network.GetGlobal("WeatherState", 0)

-- Server only; runs fn(ply) once ply's handshake completes, or immediately if it already has
cityrp.network.WaitForPlayer(ply, function(ply)
	ply:SetNetVar("cityrp_Job", "Citizen")
end)

-- Client only, and only for a :ClientOwned() var. Equivalent to its generated Set<Name>(); use it
-- directly for a var registered without :Accessor().
cityrp.network.ClientSet("cityrp_F1Open", true)
```

`Entity:SetNetVar`/`SetGlobal` on an unregistered name, the wrong scope's accessor (e.g.
`Entity:SetNetVar` for a Global-scoped var), or `:SetNetVar` for a LocalPlayer-scoped var on a
non-player entity are all logged errors, not silent no-ops or thrown exceptions.

## Wire protocol

Four net strings, two used in both directions:

| Message | cl → sv | sv → cl |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `cityrp.network.Sync` | Client's net channel is ready | The manifest, then the join bootstrap |
| `cityrp.network.Resync` | Batched entity indices to resync | Batched per-entity/global var groups |
| `cityrp.network.Update` | — | A single live var change |
| `cityrp.network.ClientSet` | One `:ClientOwned()` var, for the sending player | — |

`ClientSet` carries a bare var entry and **no entity index**: the server applies it to whoever sent
it, so there is nowhere in the message to name another entity. One var per message, never batched, so
a desynced entry can only ever cost that one var. The entry's wire shape is written and read by the
same `WriteVarEntry`/`DecodeEntry` pair the server's own paths use — both live in `sh_store.lua`
rather than one per realm, because a matched pair split across two files is exactly what AGENTS.md
footgun #11 is about.

**The manifest is what fixes the positional-wire-contract bug.** The server seals the registry
(sorted var names → sequential IDs) and sends every client `id → name, scope, codec, arg`, with the
ID bit-width itself in the header. The client never assigns its own IDs — it waits for this message
and matches entries by name. A load-order difference between realms can no longer desync anything: at
worst, a var one realm doesn't have registered locally gets a synthetic entry built straight from the
manifest, logged once, and keeps working via `GetNetVar`/`SetNetVar`.

A joining player's `Sync` announce is retried every 2 seconds (up to 5 attempts) until the manifest
arrives. The server does not send `Update`/`Resync` traffic to a player until their handshake
completes — an update sent before the manifest would be undecodable, and because sets are
delta-guarded, that value would then be lost for good.

## Storage and the recycled-index bug

Entity/Player-scoped values live directly on the entity's own Lua table (`ent.__netvars`), the same
way Photon SimpleNet stores state, on both realms. This is what retires NSVars' recycled-index bug:
GMod hands a freshly-created entity a new Lua table regardless of which index it reuses, so there is
nothing left over to clean up and nothing that can leak between occupants of the same index.

## Resync
