Modeled on Photon SimpleNet's pull-on-visible design:

1. **Client** requests a resync when an entity is created over the network (`GM:NetworkEntityCreated`)
   or re-enters this client's PVS (`GM:NotifyShouldTransmit`). Requests debounce to at most one
   batched message per frame.
2. **Server** queues the requested entities per player and drains the queues from `Think`, subject to
   two ConVars:

   | ConVar | Default | Meaning |
   | :--- | :--- | :--- |
   | `cityrp_network_resync_rate` | 32 | Entities resynced per frame, server-wide. |
   | `cityrp_network_resync_rate_player` | 8 | Max entities resynced per frame for any one player. |

   Draining is round-robin across players with a persistent cursor, so a player with a large queue
   cannot starve everyone else — every player with a non-empty queue gets served within a bounded
   number of frames regardless of how full anyone else's queue is.
3. Each player's queue is a **weak-keyed set** of entities (`{[Entity] = true}`, `__mode = "k"`), not
   an ordered array. Both a disconnecting player's whole queue and an individual removed entity clean
   themselves out of every queue automatically; `PlayerDisconnected`/`EntityRemoved` hooks additionally
   purge eagerly rather than waiting on the next GC pass.
4. The **join bootstrap** reuses this same path: on handshake, every currently-known networked entity
   is queued for the new player exactly as if it had just re-entered their PVS, so a join gets the
   same per-frame rate limiting as any other resync rather than a separate bulk-send path to reason
   about. Global values and the joining player's own LocalPlayer-scoped values — neither tied to any
   entity's visibility — are sent once, directly, alongside the manifest.

`cityrp_network_sync_bytes` (default 8192) is the flush threshold, in bytes, for a batched `Resync`
message — checked between entity groups, so a message can exceed it by up to one group's worth of
vars. That default leaves roughly 57 KB of headroom under the 65536-byte `net` message cap.

## Diagnostics

`cityrp_network_dump` — server console/RCON only (same guard as `cityrp_log_set`). Prints the sealed
registry (id, name, scope, codec, plus `clientOwned` and `debounce=floor..ceiling` where they apply),
per connected player their handshake status and resync queue depth, and every (owner, var) pair
currently mid-window or escalated off its debounce floor. That last block matters because an
escalated interval is otherwise invisible — it presents only as "this player's indicator is laggy".

`cityrp_network_clientset_rate` (default 30) is the inbound backstop: `ClientSet` messages one player
may send per second before the rest of that second is ignored and a warning logged. It is a floodgate,
not the throttle that makes client-owned vars viable — `:Debounce()` is that, and it already flattens
every legitimate burst — which is why it can sit well above any real usage.

Verbose per-message logging goes through the existing logging library, not a dedicated ConVar:

```
cityrp_log_set network DEBUG
```

## What this library does not do

- **Most call sites have not been migrated.** `SetNSVar`/`GetNSVar`/`SetLPlyVar`/`SetNW*` remain
  correct for everything still on them — see [issue #3207](https://github.com/limelight-development/cityrp2/issues/3207)
  for the full plan (compatibility shims for `damagelog`, `prone_mod`, `vape_swep`, `mapaddons.lua`
  and the Discord relay's fake `MT:GetNSVar` stub, then deletion of `core/plugins/networking`).
  `core/plugins/networking` is still fully live.
- **No client authority over anything but the sending player.** `:ClientOwned()` is
  `:SetPlayer()`/`:SetLocalPlayer()` only; there is no client-driven Global or Entity scope, and no
  way for a client to write another entity's state.
- **No server-side adjudication of a claim.** No accept predicate, no server-side clear — see
  *Claims are not adjudicated* above for why both are deliberate omissions rather than gaps.

topics.title: New Map Checklist
topics.body:
# New Map Checklist

This document outlines the steps and configurations required when adding a new map to CityRP. Use this as a comprehensive checklist to ensure all map-specific features are properly set up.

## Server Configuration

### LLServer Value

The server's LLServer value determines which map-specific configuration is loaded. This is automatically derived from the hostname tags and map name.

- [ ] Update changelog `gm_starts` fields
- [ ] Configure `sv_remote` changelog notifier

## Permanent Entities

The permanent entities system spawns static entities when the map loads. These are defined in `gamemode/core/plugins/perma_ents/maps/{mapname}.lua`.

### World Props to Remove

- [ ] Identify and register world props to remove via `DeleteMapEntity(mapCreationID)`

### Vending Machines

- [ ] Spawn `cityrp_nommachine` entities at appropriate locations

### Tesla Chargers

- [ ] Spawn Tesla EV charging stations at designated parking areas

### Phone Booths

- [ ] Spawn `ent_phonebooth` entities throughout the map

### ID Terminals

- [ ] Spawn `cityrp_idterminal` entities at government buildings

### Government Lockers

- [ ] Spawn `cityrp_govlocker` entities in police stations and government buildings

### Resupply Boxes

- [ ] Place resupply boxes for emergency services

### Sales NPCs

Configure NPC merchants for various job systems:

- [ ] **Weed** - Drug dealer NPC (`cityrp_drugsdealer`)
- [ ] **Meth** - Meth man NPC (`cityrp_methman`) - Configure random spawn locations in `methSpawns` table
- [ ] **Lumberjack** - Lumberjack supplies NPC
- [ ] **Construction** - Construction supplies NPC
- [ ] **Trashman** - Trashman job NPC

### Lootables

Configure harvestable resources:

- [ ] **Trees** - Harvestable tree locations
- [ ] **Rocks** - Mining ore locations (`cityrp_coalore`, `cityrp_metalore`)
- [ ] **Bins** - Trash bins (`cityrp_rubbish_bin`)

### Fuel Station Hint Entities

- [ ] Spawn `cityrp_hint_trig_fuel` at fuel stations

## Areas

The area system defines named regions on the map. Areas are stored in `data/cityrp/plugins/areas/{mapname}.txt`.

- [ ] Define all major areas using `/addarea`, `/addareapos`, or `/addareasky` commands
- [ ] Ensure fire alarm areas are properly mapped
- [ ] Test vehicle location reporting

## Doors

Door configuration is critical for the property system.

### Unownable Doors

Configure doors that cannot be purchased via the unownable plugin:

- [ ] Mark public access doors as unownable via `/unownable <name>`
- [ ] Mark abandoned buildings with `/unownable Abandoned`
- [ ] Save via data files at `data/cityrp/plugins/unownable/{mapname}.txt`

### Property System

Properties are stored in the database and link multiple doors together:

- [ ] Create properties using `/property create <name>`
- [ ] Add doors with `/property add`
- [ ] Set rent with `/property rent <amount>`
- [ ] Save properties to database

### Peepholes

Players fit their own peepholes to doors they own, but staff can fit permanent ones that survive
restarts (government buildings, landmark doors, anywhere a peephole should always exist):

- [ ] Fit permanent peepholes with `/peephole`, aiming at the face of the door
- [ ] Remove them with `/peephole remove`
- [ ] Shot-out lenses are repaired with `/peephole repair`, or by using a peephole item on the door.
      Permanent ones can be repaired by anyone, since they belong to the map rather than to a player
- [ ] Saved automatically to `data/cityrp/plugins/Peepholes/{mapname}/peepholes.txt`, where
      `{mapname}` is always lowercased, whatever case the map file itself uses
- [ ] The side you are standing on when fitting becomes the interior — fit from inside the property

### Government Door Access

Configure secure doors that require government team access:

- [ ] Set up government-only doors
- [ ] Configure keypad access for secure areas

## Jail Points

Jail points determine where arrested players are teleported:

- [ ] Add jail points using `/jailpoint add` at cell locations
- [ ] Save jail points via `/jailpoint save`
- [ ] Stored at `data/cityrp/plugins/jailpoints/{mapname}.txt`

## Map Web Service

The HTML map overlay system requires map data:

- [ ] Register map with web service at `limelightgaming.net/services/map/`
- [ ] Provide map bounds and coordinates

## PoliceDB Allowed Areas

Define areas where the police database terminal can be accessed:

- [ ] Configure `IsInsideBox()` checks in `policedb/sv_init.lua` for:
  - Police station
  - Town hall
  - Jail areas

## Spawnpoints

Team-specific spawn locations:

- [ ] Add spawnpoints for each team using `/spawnpoint add <team>`
- [ ] Save spawnpoints via `/spawnpoint save`
- [ ] Stored at `data/cityrp/plugins/spawnpoints/{mapname}.txt`

## Worldprops

Persistent decorative props that survive map restarts:

- [ ] Add world props via `/worldprops add`
- [ ] Save via `/worldprops save`
- [ ] Stored as per-map data files

## Map Addons

Configure third-party addon integrations:

### KFC

- [ ] Set up KFC restaurant locations

### Fishing

- [ ] Configure fishing spots and zones

### Refuel

- [ ] Register fuel station locations

### Repair

- [ ] Set up vehicle repair locations

### Car Parking

- [ ] Configure parking lot boundaries and slots

---

## Additional Map Features

### Car Paint Shops

Location defined in `plugins/carpaint/` - Configure spray booth locations per map.

- [ ] Define paint shop coordinates in `carpaint/sv_init.lua` and `carpaint/cl_init.lua`

### UniSec Keypads

Government security keypad system for restricted doors:

- [ ] Configure secure door keypads via the unisec-keypads plugin
- [ ] Map name should use hyphens instead of underscores for storage

### HTML Map Integration

The map plugin provides an in-game HTML map interface:

- [ ] Ensure map is registered with the web service URL format: `https://limelightgaming.net/services/map/index.html?map={mapname}`

### Perma Ents Map File

Create a dedicated Lua file for permanent entities:

- [ ] Create `gamemode/core/plugins/perma_ents/maps/{mapname}.lua`
- [ ] Use `SetDefaultMap("{mapname}")` at the start
- [ ] Register entities with `RegisterPermanentEntity(class, pos, ang)`
- [ ] Register deletions with `DeleteMapEntity(mapCreationID)`

### Permanent Billboards

Map-owned `zad_adsign*` signs persist via `perma_ents` (not `!worldprops` or `data/zadkit`):

- [ ] Place and configure billboards in-game
- [ ] Dump with `!billboard_save` / `!billboard_save_all` and paste into the map file
- [ ] Or migrate a legacy `data/zadkit/{mapname}_advertsigns.txt` with `!billboard_migrate`
- [ ] See `gamemode/core/plugins/perma_ents/README_BILLBOARDS.md`

### Server Configuration Files

Map-specific server configuration may be required:

- [ ] Check if `gamemode/core/server/{llserver_value}.lua` exists or needs creation
- [ ] Configure map-specific ConVars or settings

### Auto Restart Configuration

If using the auto-restart plugin, ensure map is properly handled:

- [ ] Verify changelevel command targets the correct map

---

## Reference Notes

### Codebase Patterns

1. **Data Storage Convention**: Most map-specific data is stored in `data/cityrp/plugins/{feature}/{mapname}.txt` using `util.KeyValuesToTable`/`util.TableToKeyValues` format.

2. **Map Name Handling**: The map name is typically retrieved via `game.GetMap()` and may be lowercase normalized. Some systems use hyphens instead of underscores.

3. **Entity Optimization**: Permanent entities can be flagged as "dumb" (no think function) via the `isDumb` table in `perma_ents/sv_init.lua` to improve server performance.

4. **Map Copy Feature**: The `CopyMap(source, dest)` function in perma_ents allows copying all entity configurations from one map to another (useful for map variants like `rp_rockford_v1b` and `rp_rockford_v2b`).

### Recommendations

1. **Test on Build Server First**: Use the build server (`LLServer == "build"`) to test map configurations before deploying to live servers.

2. **Document Custom Entity Positions**: When adding permanent entities, consider documenting the Vector positions with comments describing the location (e.g., "Fish Avenue Docks", "Town Hall").

3. **Coordinate with Map Variants**: If the map has variants (e.g., `_v1b`, `_v2b`, `_fl2`), consider whether configurations should be shared or distinct.

4. **PoliceDB Area Checks**: The PoliceDB allowed areas use bounding box checks - ensure boxes encompass all floors and don't accidentally include unintended areas.

5. **Backup Configuration**: Before making changes, consider backing up existing data files from the data folder.

### Currently Supported Maps

The following maps have existing `perma_ents` configurations:

- `rp_evocity_v33x`
- `rp_evocity_v4b1`
- `rp_evocity_v4b1_fl2`
- `rp_evocity_v17x`
- `rp_evocity2_v2p`
- `rp_evocity2_v5p`
- `rp_rockford_v1b`
- `rp_rockford_v2b`
- `rp_florida`
- `rp_florida_v2`
- `rp_truenorth_v1a`
- `rp_southside_day`

topics.title: Plugins
topics.body:
# Plugins

Plugins live in `gamemode/core/plugins/` and are the unit CityRP features are built in — "new features should be plugins when possible" ([CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/limelight-development/cityrp2/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)). There are two formats. Both are discovered and ordered by `cityrp.plugin.Resolve` (`gamemode/core/libraries/sh_plugin.lua`) and executed by the loop in `gamemode/sh_init.lua`.

## Choosing a format

| | Folder plugin | File plugin |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Layout | `core/plugins/<key>/sv_init.lua`, `cl_init.lua`, `sh_init.lua` | `core/plugins/<scope>_<key>.lua` |
| Realms | Any combination | Exactly one file, on the realms its scope prefix implies |
| Extra files | Yes — include them yourself from `sv_init`/`cl_init` | No |
| Shared state across realms | Via the `PLUGIN_SHARED` handshake | Not applicable — there is only one file |

Use a **file plugin** when the whole feature is one file. Use a **folder plugin** when it needs more than one file, genuinely different code per realm, or [sub-resources](#sub-resources-entities-weapons-items-derma) such as entities, weapons, items, or derma panels.

Do not convert existing folder plugins wholesale. Convert one opportunistically when you are already editing it and it qualifies.

## File plugins

A file plugin is a single `.lua` file sitting directly in `core/plugins/`, named `<scope>_<key>.lua`:

| File | Server does | Client does |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `sv_<key>.lua` | `include()` | nothing — the file is never sent |
| `cl_<key>.lua` | `AddCSLuaFile()` | `include()` |
| `sh_<key>.lua` | `AddCSLuaFile()` + `include()` | `include()` |

```lua
--- Kicks players who idle past the AFK limit.
--- @copyright 2015-2026 Limelight Gaming
--- @release CityRP 2
--- @author You
--- @namespace AutoKick
--- @state server

local PLUGIN = {}
PLUGIN.name = "Auto Kick"
PLUGIN.author = "You"

hook.Add("Think", "AutoKickThink", function() end)

cityrp.plugin.register(PLUGIN)
```

`core/plugins/sv_auto_restart.lua` is a real example.

### `sh_` is not the folder format's `sh_init.lua`

This is the one place the two formats genuinely differ, and getting it wrong is easy.

The loader **never includes** a folder plugin's `sh_init.lua`. It only `AddCSLuaFile`s it; each folder plugin includes its own shared file and hands its table across through the `PLUGIN_SHARED` global.

A file plugin has no second file to hand a table to, so `sh_<key>.lua` simply means "included on both realms". **Never read or write `PLUGIN_SHARED` from a file plugin.** Folder plugins assign it as a global and never clear it, so a file plugin that reads it picks up whichever folder plugin happened to run last. Use `SERVER`/`CLIENT` guards inside the file instead — or, if the realms need to diverge more than that reads cleanly, use a folder plugin.

## Folder plugins

```
core/plugins/<key>/
    sv_init.lua    included on the server
    cl_init.lua    sent to the client, included there
    sh_init.lua    sent to the client; included by sv_init/cl_init, never by the loader
```

The `PLUGIN_SHARED` handshake, as used by `core/plugins/flashlight/`:

```lua
-- sv_init.lua and cl_init.lua both do this
local PLUGIN = {}
PLUGIN_SHARED = PLUGIN
include("sh_init.lua")

-- sh_init.lua reads it back
local PLUGIN = PLUGIN_SHARED
PLUGIN.name = "Flashlight"
```

Class-style plugins can skip the global entirely by returning the table instead, as `core/plugins/cpr/` does:

```lua
-- sh_init.lua
local PLUGIN = PLUGIN:New("CPR", "Taylor")
return PLUGIN

-- cl_init.lua
local PLUGIN = include("sh_init.lua")
PLUGIN:Register()
```

Any file beyond those three is the plugin's own responsibility to `include`/`AddCSLuaFile`.

## Sub-resources: entities, weapons, items, derma

A **folder** plugin can own entities, weapons, items, and derma panels directly, so "plugin disabled/absent ⇒ its content doesn't load" is automatic instead of per-file gating. File plugins never get sub-resources.

```
core/plugins/<key>/
    entities/<class>/ or entities/<class>.lua   (ENT, engine-style layout)
    weapons/<class>/  or weapons/<class>.lua    (SWEP, engine-style layout)
    items/*.lua                                  (same conventions as core/items)
    derma/{sv,sh,cl}_*.lua                       (same conventions as core/derma)
```

`entities/`/`weapons/` follow the engine's own folder convention, matched exactly so migration is a pure file move: each realm includes one entry file — `init.lua` on the server, `cl_init.lua` on the client, falling back to `shared.lua` — and `shared.lua` is otherwise only included by those files themselves, as existing `init.lua` files already do. The loader (`cityrp.plugin.LoadSubResourceEntities` in `sh_plugin.lua`) also mirrors what the engine pre-sets on the global before including: `SWEP.Primary`/`SWEP.Secondary` as empty tables, `SWEP.Base = "weapon_base"`, and `Folder` on both kinds — so weapon files that write `SWEP.Primary.Damage = ...` without creating the table keep working unchanged. It then calls `scripted_ents.Register`/`weapons.Register` and clears the global — the same shape as `core/plugins/animations/animationsapi/mocap_controller.lua`'s manual registration. Class names are lowercased, like plugin keys, because the client's download cache lowercases paths.

One deliberate superset of engine semantics: the loader always `AddCSLuaFile`s `shared.lua` and `cl_init.lua` itself. Under the engine those files are only sent because `init.lua` manually sends them (entity folders are not on the engine's auto-send list), which is the classic forgotten-boilerplate footgun — the entity works on a listen server and breaks for connecting clients. In a plugin entity folder that boilerplate is therefore optional: existing `AddCSLuaFile` lines in migrated files are harmless duplicates, and new files can omit them. The include side is unchanged — the client still only includes its one entry file.

Loading happens in this order, once per map load, in plugin load order:

1. **Plugin phase** — every plugin's `sv_/cl_/sh_init.lua` runs. A plugin cannot see its own sub-resources yet, but every plugin has initialised by the time any sub-resource loads.
2. **Entity/weapon phase** — immediately after. Each loaded plugin's `entities/` and `weapons/` classes register.
3. **Item phase** — after `core/items/*`, so plugin items can inherit from bases registered there. `cityrp.item.stored`'s `uponLoad` sweep runs after this and covers plugin items automatically.
4. **Derma phase** — after `core/derma`, same prefix rules (server sends every file, includes only `sh_`; client includes everything).

Only a **loaded** plugin's sub-resources are loaded — a plugin that failed to resolve ([dependencies and load order](#dependencies-and-load-order)) or is disabled contributes nothing here, silently.

### Class name collisions

Two plugins declaring the same class is logged as an `ERROR` on the server at load, naming both claimants. The gamemode's own `entities/`/`weapons/` tree is a separate case: the engine scans it *after* gamemode Lua finishes, so a same-named class there silently overwrites the plugin's registration — the loader catches that with an `InitPostEntity` sweep that verifies every plugin-registered class survived, and logs an `ERROR` naming the overwritten class. Neither is ever fatal: GMod's registries have last-registration-wins semantics regardless of what the loader does, so treat the logs as the guard rail, not a safety net.

### Migration status

Only `weapons/cityrp_breathalyser/` has been migrated, from the gamemode-level `entities/weapons/` tree into `core/plugins/breathalyser/weapons/`, as the pilot for this system. Migrating other plugin-dependent entities/items is follow-up work, done opportunistically per plugin — do not bulk-migrate.

## Registration

Either form works in either format:

- `local PLUGIN = {}` … `cityrp.plugin.register(PLUGIN)` — the legacy form, used by most plugins.
- `local PLUGIN = PLUGIN:New(name, author)` … `PLUGIN:Register()` — the class form (`sh_plugincore.lua`), which adds `PLUGIN:AddHook`, enable/disable, and per-plugin data/map file helpers.

**`cityrp.plugin.stored` is keyed by the plugin key**, the same identity `.meta.lua` and load order use — so a lookup is `cityrp.plugin.get("area")`. `cityrp.plugin.get` still accepts the display name (`cityrp.plugin.get("Area Manager")`) and resolves it through `cityrp.plugin.names`, but warns once per name: the two identities are not derivable from one another, so nothing can bridge them automatically. Hundreds of call sites still pass display names; they work, and converting one is worth doing when you are already editing that code. Both forms cost the same — the key is simply the identity everything else already uses.

Registration also stamps the resolved key onto the plugin as `PLUGIN.key`, creates a per-plugin logger at `plugin.<key>`, and exposes it as `PLUGIN.logger`. Use `PLUGIN.key` rather than repeating the key as a literal when a plugin needs to look itself up.

## Keys

A plugin's **key** is its identity for everything the loader does. It is the folder name, or a file plugin's name with the scope prefix and `.lua` stripped:

| On disk | Key |
| :--- | :--- |
| `core/plugins/stamina/` | `stamina` |
| `core/plugins/sv_auto_restart.lua` | `auto_restart` |
| `core/plugins/sh_billboards.lua` | `billboards` |

Keys are lowercased, so file names should be all lowercase. Folders and files share one key space — a folder and a file cannot both claim the same key.

`*.meta.lua` holds a plugin's [dependency metadata](#dependencies-and-load-order) and is never loaded as a plugin.

## Disabling a plugin

A plugin declares itself off in its own `.meta.lua`:

```lua
return {
	-- Superseded by the admin plugin; kept for reference.
	disabled = true,
}
```

`disabled` is a boolean expression, not just a literal — `licenseplates/.meta.lua` computes it from
`cityrp.configuration["Plate Plugin"]`, the same config other code already reads that flag from. It
lives in the same table as [dependencies and load order](#dependencies-and-load-order) and
[availability conditions](#availability-conditions) — a plugin can declare all three. A disabled
plugin is skipped on both realms, contributes no sub-resources, and its client files are never
sent; any dependent sees it as `disabled`, not `not installed`.

The *why* belongs as a comment above the field, not a separate `disabledReason` key.

There is no loader-side override list. For "off on some servers or maps," use
[availability conditions](#availability-conditions) instead — a file-scope
`if LLServer == "build" then return end` is no longer a supported way to not-exist.

## Key conflicts

Two things claiming one key is a conflict. It is logged as an `ERROR` on the server and is **never fatal** — the highest-precedence candidate loads and the rest are ignored:

| Precedence | Candidate |
| :--- | :--- |
| 1 (highest) | folder |
| 2 | `sh_<key>.lua` |
| 3 | `sv_<key>.lua` |
| 4 (lowest) | `cl_<key>.lua` |

The trap worth naming: **`sv_foo.lua` + `cl_foo.lua` is a conflict, not a two-realm plugin.** It is the shape of the folder format, so it is the natural mistake, and its consequence is that the client half silently never loads. Use a folder plugin for a server/client pair.

The losing candidate is never `AddCSLuaFile`d, so the client only ever receives the winner.

A `.lua` file in `core/plugins/` with no recognised scope prefix logs a `WARNING` and is skipped. Non-Lua files are ignored silently.

## Dependencies and load order

Plugins load in alphabetical order by key, folders and files interleaved, unless something says otherwise. A plugin says otherwise in an optional `.meta.lua` beside it:

| Format | Metadata file |
| :--- | :--- |
| Folder plugin | `core/plugins/<key>/.meta.lua` |
| File plugin | `core/plugins/<key>.meta.lua` |

It returns a plain table and must have no side effects — it is read before any plugin code runs, on both realms. The same table also carries [availability conditions](#availability-conditions):

```lua
return {
	dependencies = {"police"},
	optional_dependencies = {"banking"},
	after = {"excusenlr"},
	before = {},

	not_servers = {"build"}
}
```

Every dependency/ordering value is a **plugin key** — the folder name, or a file plugin's name without its scope prefix. Not `PLUGIN.name`. Matching is exact and keys are lowercase, so write them lowercase.

A plugin with no `.meta.lua` declares nothing and keeps its alphabetical slot. That is the normal case and is silent.

### Depending versus ordering

These answer two different questions, and picking the wrong one is the easy mistake:

| Field | Means | If the target is absent |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `dependencies` | I cannot work without this | **This plugin does not load.** `ERROR` |
| `optional_dependencies` | I use this when it is here | Loads anyway. `WARNING`, server only |
| `after` | I must run later than this | Loads anyway, no message |
| `before` | I must run earlier than this | Loads anyway, no message |

`after` and `before` are ordering only. They never fail a plugin and never claim it needs anything, so use them when you only care about sequence. `core/plugins/networking/.meta.lua` is `after = {"*"}` — the plugin used to be named `zz_networking` purely to sort last; the wildcard is what that name was really trying to say, and the folder no longer needs the trick.

`"*"` means every other plugin: `after = {"*"}` is "load last", `before = {"*"}` is "load first". It is only meaningful in those two fields; a `"*"` in either dependency list is rejected with a `WARNING`, since requiring every plugin would make any single absence fatal.

### What the loader does with it

Order is a topological sort, tie-broken alphabetically: of the plugins whose dependencies are already satisfied, the alphabetically first goes next. A plugin therefore keeps its usual slot unless something genuinely has to come before it.

| Situation | Result |
| :--- | :--- |
| Required dependency missing or disabled | Dependent does not load. `ERROR` |
| A plugin that something requires fails | That dependent does not load either, transitively. `ERROR` |
| Required dependency cycle | Every plugin in the cycle fails, and the `ERROR` names the path |
| Optional dependency missing | Loads without it. `WARNING`, server only |
| Any soft rule that would create a cycle | That one ordering rule is dropped, never the plugin |

Nothing here is fatal to the server or to any other plugin. A failed plugin's client files are still sent, because the client resolves the same graph independently and may reach a different answer.

### The realm trap

**A dependency must exist on every realm its dependent loads on.** There is no realm tagging: a plugin that is not on this realm is simply missing here.

32 of the 116 plugins are server-only — a folder with neither a `cl_init.lua` nor an `sh_init.lua`, or an `sv_` file plugin — so they do not exist clientside at all. A plugin that loads on both realms declaring `dependencies = {"clans"}` loads perfectly on the server and then fails on every client, because `clans` is server-only. Depend on a server-only plugin only from another server-only plugin; otherwise use `optional_dependencies`, or guard the call site instead.

### Reading another plugin

Declaring a dependency fixes the load order; it does not make a file-scope lookup good practice. `core/plugins/hud/cl_init.lua` calls `cityrp.plugin.get("Excuse NLR")` at file scope and works only because `excusenlr` sorts before `hud`. Do the lookup inside a hook or at run time instead, and guard it:

```lua
hook.Add("InitPostEntity", "MyPluginSetup", function()
	local other = cityrp.plugin.get("excusenlr")
	if not other then return end
end)
```

Pass the plugin key, the same value the metadata uses. A display name still resolves, but warns.

Items load after every plugin, so item files may gate on a plugin at file scope — `core/items/ammunition/sh_ammo_pistol.lua` opens with `if not cityrp.plugin.get("generic") then return end`.

### Guarding a cross-plugin call

When you only need to know *whether* a plugin is there, not to call into its table, use `cityrp.plugin.IsAvailable(key)`:

```lua
if cityrp.plugin.IsAvailable("banking") then
	-- safe to call into the banking plugin here
end
```

Any plugin can be removed from the repo at any time, and nothing stops another plugin's code from assuming it still exists — so an unguarded cross-plugin reference is a live bug, not a hypothetical one. There is deliberately no structural safety net: nothing proxies cross-plugin calls into silent no-ops, because that would turn "plugin removed" into a quietly degraded feature instead of a loud, findable one. Call sites guard themselves.

`IsAvailable` is not the same as `cityrp.plugin.get(key) ~= nil`, and the difference bites. It reads the loader's own bookkeeping rather than `cityrp.plugin.stored`, so it is true for the ~27 plugins that load without ever calling `register`, and for `xp-bar`, which returns early without registering when MESKA is absent. `get` would call all of those missing.

It is also realm-accurate in both directions. A server-only plugin is never discovered clientside, so `IsAvailable` is correctly `false` there — the query-side counterpart of [the realm trap](#the-realm-trap) above. A plugin with no realm files of its own but with [sub-resources](#sub-resources-entities-weapons-items-derma) does materialise clientside and reads `true`.

Every reason a plugin might be absent — never installed, removed, `disabled = true`, excluded by `servers`/`maps`, a missing required dependency, a required dependency cycle — returns the same `false`, because from a caller's side they are the same thing. When the difference matters, `cityrp.plugin.GetDependencyStatus(key)` returns the outcome (`status`, `reason`, `missing`, `missingOptional`, `cycle`, `order`) or nil if nothing by that key was discovered here. That one is for diagnostics and error messages — do not guard with it; its shape is an implementation detail and may gain fields.

## Availability conditions

A plugin can declare in its `.meta.lua` which servers and maps it is allowed to exist on. Four optional keys, all lists of lowercase strings, matched exactly against `LLServer` and `string.lower(game.GetMap())`:

```lua
return {
	servers = {"v2d", "usv2d"},   -- allowlist of server codes; absent = every server
	not_servers = {"build"},      -- blocklist; wins over servers
	maps = {"rp_evocity_v33x"},   -- allowlist of map names; absent = every map
	not_maps = {"rp_florida_v2"}  -- blocklist; wins over maps
}
```

They live in the same table as [dependencies and load order](#dependencies-and-load-order) — a plugin can declare both.

Rules:

- Within an axis (server or map), the blocklist beats the allowlist: `not_servers` is checked before `servers`, `not_maps` before `maps`.
- Both axes apply — a plugin declaring both `servers` and `maps` must satisfy both.
- All four absent is today's behaviour: available everywhere. Every plugin without a `.meta.lua`, and every `.meta.lua` that only declares dependencies, is unaffected.

A plugin excluded this way is treated **exactly like a plugin declaring `disabled = true`**: it never enters the discovered set, so it contributes no sub-resources and is never `AddCSLuaFile`'d, and any dependent sees it as `disabled` — not `not installed` — with the usual cascading `ERROR`. A `DEBUG` log line names the reason, e.g. `Skipping 'flashlight': excluded on server 'build'.`, so a gated plugin does not read as hand-disabled when you go looking for it.

### Server codes, not server names

Match against `LLServer` (`v2d`, `usv2d`, `v4b1_fl2`, `southside`, `build`, `event`, `beta`, `staging`, …) — the same value the [realm trap](#the-realm-trap) uses — not what the team calls a server out loud. `build` and `event` are Live, not Development; Live versus Development is not the axis this gates on.

The trap: **`"beta2"` is a server name, not a server code.** Both beta servers report `LLServer == "beta"`; only `LLServerChatID` tells them apart. `servers = {"beta2"}` silently never matches anything. The server logs a `WARNING` for a `servers`/`not_servers` entry that names no file under `core/server/` — server only, since the client is only ever sent the one file matching its own `LLServer` and has no way to see the rest of the list.

Map names are not validated against a known list — there isn't one to check against.

### Migration

An in-file early return is no longer a supported way to not-exist. `if LLServer == "build" then return end` at the top of a plugin's `sv_init.lua`/`sh_init.lua`/`cl_init.lua` compiles and works for the code in that one file, but it does nothing about the plugin's sub-resources or its `AddCSLuaFile`s — replace it with `not_servers = {"build"}` in a sibling `.meta.lua` instead.

## Troubleshooting

The loader logs to the `plugins` namespace at `DEBUG`, which is below the default level. On the **server**:

```
cityrp_log_set plugins DEBUG
```

Levels persist server-side and are re-read at gamemode init, and plugins load at map load — so set the level, then restart or change level, then read the output.

The same command on a client does not persist, so client-side load-time `DEBUG` output is effectively unobservable. Verify the client by effect instead:

```
lua_run_cl print(cityrp.plugin.get("auto_restart") ~= nil)
lua_run_cl PrintTable(select(1, file.Find(GMFOLDER .. "/gamemode/core/plugins/*", "LUA")))
```

The second line lists the file plugins the client actually received, which is the quickest way to confirm an `AddCSLuaFile` did or did not happen.

Conflict `ERROR`s and unrecognised-file `WARNING`s are logged on the server only — the client cannot see a losing candidate, and both levels would otherwise print into every player's console.

Dependency *failures* are the exception: they are logged on **whichever realm they happen on**, because the two realms resolve independently and the server cannot tell that a client failed. A dependency `ERROR` appearing only in player consoles is the [realm trap](#the-realm-trap), and the message says so. A missing *optional* dependency is not a failure and is reported on the server only — the server sees the whole disk, so clientside that message would mostly mean "this one is server-only", which is the case optional dependencies exist for.

## Related topics

- [Coding Standards](coding-standards.md)
- [Modern APIs](modern-apis.md)
- [Console Logging Library](logging.md)
- [LuaCATS Annotations](luacats.md)

topics.title: UI Scaling
topics.body:
# UI Scaling

The `cityrp.ui` library (`gamemode/core/libraries/cl_ui.lua`) is the mandatory way to scale client UI — Derma panels, entity menus, HUD overlays, and any other screen-space layout or drawing. It combines automatic resolution scaling (1920×1080 reference) with the player's `cl_llhud_scale` preference and keeps every consumer in sync when either input changes.

## When to use it

Use `cityrp.ui` for **any** client-side UI dimension that should track screen size or the player's scale setting:

- Panel sizes, margins, padding, and positions
- Font sizes
- Icon and button dimensions
- `draw.*` coordinates in custom `Paint` functions

Do **not** roll your own scale factor. Ad-hoc `ScrW() / 1920` math, calling `LimelightHUD.GetScaleFactor()` directly, or hardcoded pixel values that never rebuild on scale change are legacy patterns — they drift from the HUD, ignore `cl_llhud_scale`, and break when resolution changes mid-session.

**Enforcement:** new or modified lines that introduce `ScrW() / 1920`, `ScrH() / 1080`, or
`LimelightHUD.GetScaleFactor()` fail `standards-diff.py` in CI (legacy `core/derma/cl_hud_*.lua`
panels are grandfathered until migrated). See [Coding Standards](coding-standards.md).

## Core API

| Function | Purpose |
| :--- | :--- |
| `cityrp.ui.Scale(value)` | Scale a single pixel measurement to the nearest whole pixel. Use for widths, heights, margins, positions, and any other screen-space dimension. |
| `cityrp.ui.GetScaleFactor()` | Return the raw, unrounded scale multiplier. Use only when you need the factor itself (e.g. proportional math before a single final round), not for individual pixel measurements — prefer `Scale()` for those. |
| `cityrp.ui.CreateScaledFont(name, baseFont, baseSize[, weight])` | Create a font at the current scale. `baseSize` is the size at 1920×1080. |
| `cityrp.ui.OnScaleChanged(id, callback)` | Register a debounced callback that fires when `cl_llhud_scale` or screen resolution changes. Use to rebuild fonts and relayout panels. |
| `cityrp.ui.Shade(colour, amount)` | Lighten or darken a colour for hover/pressed states. Cache the result at style time, not inside `Paint`. |
| `cityrp.ui.ScaleCheckBox(checkbox, font)` | Apply a scaled font to a `DCheckBoxLabel` and grow its tick box to match. |
| `cityrp.ui.AddTitleBarCloseButton(frame, titleBarHeight, onClose)` | Add the shared text-only close button used on CityRP menu title bars. |

## Standard patterns

### Scale dimensions

```lua
local pad = cityrp.ui.Scale(10)
frame:SetSize(cityrp.ui.Scale(400), cityrp.ui.Scale(300))
button:DockMargin(pad, pad, pad, pad)
```

### Scaled fonts

Build fonts once at load and rebuild them when the scale changes:

```lua
local function createMyMenuFonts()
	cityrp.ui.CreateScaledFont("MyMenuTitle", "Roboto", 17, 500)
	cityrp.ui.CreateScaledFont("MyMenuBody", "Roboto", 13, 400)
end

createMyMenuFonts()
cityrp.ui.OnScaleChanged("mymenu", createMyMenuFonts)
```

### Relayout on scale change

If a panel's geometry depends on scaled values, rebuild or relayout inside the `OnScaleChanged` callback — not only the fonts. Menus that watched only `cl_llhud_scale` but not resolution kept the sizes they were built with when the screen size changed underneath them; `OnScaleChanged` watches both.

## What not to do

| ❌ Forbidden | ✅ Use instead |
| :--- | :--- |
| `ScrW() / 1920` (or similar resolution ratios) | `cityrp.ui.Scale()` / `cityrp.ui.GetScaleFactor()` |
| `LimelightHUD.GetScaleFactor()` in new code | `cityrp.ui.GetScaleFactor()` |
| `surface.CreateFont` with a fixed `size` for UI text | `cityrp.ui.CreateScaledFont` |
| Hardcoded pixel sizes with no scale rebuild | `cityrp.ui.Scale()` + `cityrp.ui.OnScaleChanged` |
| `cvars.AddChangeCallback("cl_llhud_scale", ...)` alone | `cityrp.ui.OnScaleChanged` (also watches resolution) |

Existing HUD derma under `gamemode/core/derma/cl_hud_*.lua` still calls `LimelightHUD.GetScaleFactor()` directly — that predates `cityrp.ui`. New or refactored UI code must go through the library.

topics.title: Update Checklist
topics.body:
# Update Checklist

This document outlines the checklist of required items for publishing updates to the master branch. Some items may not be relevant for each update.

### Definition

An "update" refers to any change with gamemode impact. Minor documentation changes, code style fixes, or other non-gameplay changes do not require the full checklist.

## All Updates

The checklist of required items for publishing any update to master.

- [ ] **Testing**: Updates must be tested before being merged.
- [ ] **Review**: Updates must be reviewed before being merged, unless written by dev management or gamemasters.
- [ ] **Security Review**: Validate that changes do not introduce SQL injection, XSS, or other security vulnerabilities. This should be conducted during development and by the reviewer.
- [ ] **Performance Check**: Ensure changes do not introduce performance regressions, especially in hot paths (think hooks, networking). This is informal as we don't have the framework in place to do full testing.
- [ ] **Maintainability**: Ensure code is readable, well-structured, and follows established patterns to facilitate future maintenance and updates.
- [ ] **Backwards Compatibility**: Verify that changes do not break existing save data, inventory items, or player progress.

### Documentation

- [ ] **Internal Documentation**: Update internal API references, documentation topics and developer guides as needed.
- [ ] **Public Documentation**: Assist the event/assistant team in creating guides, familiarisation materials, and tutorials for new systems.

## Named Updates

The checklist of required items for publishing a named (major) update. Some items may not be relevant for each update.

### Approval

Creating and releasing an update as a named update must be pre-approved by development management, as it often requires cross-team coordination (e.g., media for graphics, writing). An update qualifies as a named update if it meets **any one** of the following criteria:

- Affects two or more areas of the gamemode, OR
- Introduces entirely new mechanics that would benefit from describing, detailing and showcasing, OR
- Combines two or more suggestions to make a pack update, OR
- Overhauls important parts of the gameplay experience.

Exceptions to these guidelines can be authorised by development management.

### Ingame

- [ ] **Hints**: Add hints to the hints system.

### Code

- [ ] **Comments**: Ensure functions and libraries are commented appropriately.
- [ ] **Guidelines**: Ensure guidelines are met.
  - If updating old code, the code can be left on old standards.
- [ ] **Database Migrations**: If database schema changes are required, ensure migrations are tested and documented.

### Server Content

- [ ] **Team Briefing**: If new content is required, ensure team is briefed for a full restart of main.
  - Ideally, upload model content in advance for a clean release.

### Testing

- [ ] **Content Variation**: Test in line with content variation.
  - If non-staff are affected, test with non-staff.

### Release

- [ ] **Media Content**: Prepare media content, screenshots, video if applicable.
  - Liaise with media in advance to prepare content.
  - Ensure a written version of the thread is available for graphics-based threads.
- [ ] **Release Thread**: Collaborate with media team to prepare the release thread.
- [ ] **RP Assistants**: Brief RP assistants, allow them to pre-write guides and tutorials.
- [ ] **Staff Briefing**: Brief staff if staff-relevant changes occur (can be put in a HR ticket).
- [ ] **Welcome Menu**: Update Welcome Menu.
- [ ] **Homepage Banner**: Add banner to homepage.
- [ ] **Steam Group**: Steam Group Message.
- [ ] **Scope Limitations**: Document any known scope limitations in the GitHub PR or GitHub Issue. Systems should not be releasing with known bugs, but may release with known and accepted scope limitations.

### Economy Balance Release Schedule

- [ ] **Timed Release**: If there will be time-restricted economy-affecting changes (limited stock), pre-post the update thread with a set release time (e.g., 7pm GMT).

topics.title: Vehicle Params & Script Editor
topics.body:
# Vehicle Params & Script Editor

Runtime helpers for reading and writing Source vehicle physics (`VehicleParams`), plus a
developer in-game editor for iterating on vehicle scripts. This is also the foundation future
vehicle-modification plugins should build on (item-meta upgrades such as springs, turbo, engine
kits, etc.).

## Why this exists

CityRP cars get their handling from Valve KeyValues scripts under `scripts/vehicles/**/*.txt`,
applied with `SetKeyValue("vehiclescript", ...)` **before** `Spawn`/`Activate`. Editing those files
and restarting is slow when overhauling content.

GMod exposes `Vehicle:GetVehicleParams` / `Vehicle:SetVehicleParams` for live tuning after spawn.
Those APIs are the right place for:

1. A build/dev editor that applies changes immediately and exports a `.txt` script body
2. Item-meta modifiers that stack on top of the script baseline at spawn time

## Core library

Shared library: `core/libraries/sh_vehicleparams.lua` → `cityrp.vehicleparams`

| API | Purpose |
| :--- | :--- |
| `IsTunableVehicle(ent)` | `prop_vehicle_jeep` guard |
| `GetEditableParams(veh)` | `GetVehicleParams` with speed fields converted to **MPH** |
| `SetEditableParams(veh, params)` | Converts those MPH speeds back to HU/s, then `SetVehicleParams` |
| `CaptureBaseline(veh)` / `RestoreBaseline(veh)` | Snapshot / restore script defaults on the entity |
| `RegisterModifier(id, apply, priority?)` | Register a named runtime modifier |
| `ResolveModifiers(entries)` | Turn `{id, data}` requests into an ordered apply list |
| `ApplyModifiers(veh, modifiers, context?)` | Re-apply from baseline + modifier list |
| `CollectModifiersFromMeta(item, meta, veh?)` | Built-in meta → entries, plus collect hook |
| `ApplyFromItemMeta(veh, item, meta)` | Spawn-time entry point |
| `SerializeKeyValues(params, header?)` | Export a `"Vehicle"` KeyValues block for scripts |
| `BuildEditorSections(params)` / `ApplyEditorValues(...)` | Schema-driven editor helpers |

### MPH vs HU/s

`GetVehicleParams` returns `engine.maxSpeed` / `maxRevSpeed` / `boostMaxSpeed` in hammer units per
second. Since 2021, `SetVehicleParams` uses **the same units** (HU/s), not miles per hour — the
older wiki note that Set expects MPH is stale, and passing MPH numbers back in makes a car crawl
and bounce. Vehicle `.txt` scripts still store those fields in MPH.

The library always works in MPH on the editable side (`GetEditableParams` / modifiers / editor /
export). `SetEditableParams` converts back to HU/s before writing. Conversion factor: **17.6 HU/s
per MPH**.

### Spawn integration

`Vehicles` plugin `SpawnVehicle` captures a baseline immediately after `Activate`, then calls
`ApplyFromItemMeta`. Re-applying modifiers always starts from that baseline so stacking stays
deterministic.

## In-game editor

Plugin: `core/plugins/vehiclescript_editor/`

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Command | `!vehiclescript` |
| Access | Developer only (`/` flag / `IsDeveloperOnly`) |
| Target | Vehicle you are sitting in, otherwise the jeep under your crosshair |

Actions:

- **Apply** — write the form values to the live entity via `SetVehicleParams`
- **Reset** — restore the captured script baseline
- **Export** — serialize a `"Vehicle"` KeyValues block to `data/cityrp/vehicle_scripts/<name>.txt` and copy it to the clipboard

Sounds (`"Vehicle_Sounds"`) are not edited here; paste the exported `"Vehicle"` block into the
existing script file and keep the sounds section as-is.

## Item-meta modifiers (foundation)

`base_vehicle` already declares `springs` and `turbo`. Those fields are no longer display-only:
spawn applies them through the modifier registry.

| Meta field | Modifier id | Effect (intentionally mild) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `springs` (−10…10) | `springs` | Scales axle spring constant / max body force (~±50% at extremes) |
| `turbo` (bool) | `turbo` | Enables torque boost and raises boost force / duration / max speed |

### Adding a future upgrade

```lua
cityrp.vehicleparams.RegisterModifier("engine_upgrade", function(params, context)
	local tier = tonumber(context.data) or 1
	params.engine.horsepower = (params.engine.horsepower or 0) * (1 + 0.1 * tier)
	params.engine.maxSpeed = (params.engine.maxSpeed or 0) * (1 + 0.05 * tier)
end, 70)

hook.Add("CityRP.VehicleParams.CollectModifiers", "my_vehicle_mods", function(entries, item, meta, veh)
	local tier = cityrp.itemmeta.GetField(item, meta, "engine_upgrade")
	if tier then
		table.insert(entries, {id = "engine_upgrade", data = tier})
	end
end)
```

Prefer a dedicated plugin for player-facing upgrade shops/items. Keep the apply math in
`RegisterModifier` so the editor, spawn path, and future systems share one code path.

### Collect hook

`CityRP.VehicleParams.CollectModifiers(entries, item, meta, veh)` — append `{id=..., data=...}`
tables to `entries`. Unknown ids are skipped with a debug log line.

## Testing

On the build/dev server as a developer:

1. Spawn a car, look at it, run `!vehiclescript`
2. Raise `HorsePower` / `MaxSpeed`, **Apply**, drive
3. **Reset**, confirm script feel returns
4. **Export**, confirm clipboard + `data/cityrp/vehicle_scripts/`
5. `/giveitem <you> <car> 1 meta:springs=5;turbo=1` — spawn and confirm stiffer suspension / boost

## Related

- [Item Metadata Schema](items/item-metadata-schema.md) — `springs` / `turbo` on `base_vehicle`
- [Modern APIs](modern-apis.md) — vehicle networking caveats
- [Hotwiring](design/car-boosting/hotwiring.md) — engine start flow (independent of physics params)

topics.title: Waypoints
topics.body:
# Waypoints

The Waypoints plugin provides server-authoritative world navigation with a VMF-scaled minimap, hosted F1 map, compact compass and a through-wall marker. Saved locations, dynamic nearest-entity destinations and system destinations all use the same selection path.

## Player commands

```text
/waypoint <location>
/waypoint goto <location>
/waypoint clear
/waypoint end
/waypoint stop
/waypoints list
```

`/waypoints list` prints every currently available public destination, its
category and the matching `/waypoint` command to the player's console. The
former `/waypoints` Derma menu remains removed.

The F1 **Map** interface is searchable and grouped by category. It includes saved map locations, dynamic **Nearest** destinations and locations registered by another system. It deliberately excludes the legacy `/place` coordinate table from ordinary player navigation.

## VMF map projection

The HUD minimap and F1 Map use the same exported map artwork and reversible Source-world transform. The `rp_evocity_v4b1_fl2` definition currently uses:

```text
HUD image: rp_evocity_v4b1_fl2_gmod.png
Image size: 3896 x 4096
World X: -16368 to 12944
World Y: -15446 to 15376
Y axis: image top is maximum world Y
```

World positions are converted into normalized texture coordinates:

```text
u = (worldX - minX) / (maxX - minX)
v = (maxY - worldY) / (maxY - minY)
```

`WorldToMapUV` and `MapUVToWorld` expose both directions of the transform. The HUD minimap, F1 player marker, active waypoint marker and positioned map pins therefore share one coordinate system rather than separate manually tuned percentages.

## Map material cache

The client downloads the 3896×4096 in-game derivative from the configured beta
map path, validates its PNG signature and stores it under:

```text
data/cityrp/waypoints/maps/<map>_<version>.png
```

The cached file is loaded as the native HUD material. The hosted F1 page uses
the same optimized `3896×4096` derivative and exact canvas ratio as the HUD.
This avoids decoding a roughly 1.1 GB RGBA source texture, eliminates
letterbox drift between pins and artwork, and cuts the map download from
roughly 1.5 MB to 125 KB. A version change in the shared map definition
produces a new HUD cache filename. The F1 page uses a versioned service-worker
cache for its map, scripts, styles and pin images.

## HUD minimap

The GTA-inspired minimap uses the same background and outline colours as the
TEAM/ALL radio panel. Its default width matches the 294-pixel Limelight citizen
HUD panel.

The map remains centred on the player and rotates to keep the navigation heading
at the top. On foot, the minimap, compass, full-map marker and F1 player arrow
use camera yaw. While seated, they use the player model's vehicle-aligned render
yaw, so free-looking cannot skew navigation away from the direction of travel.
The redundant north pointer is hidden because the integrated compass provides
cardinal orientation.
The minimap shows the active destination as an edge-clamped marker when it is
outside the visible crop, without repeating its name or distance under the map.
The north-up F1 map uses the same white four-point player arrow and rotates it
to the current model-facing heading.

The minimap is enabled by default and remains fixed at the top right. Hold `C`
and open **HUD Options → Toggle Minimap** to toggle it, choose **Default Size**
or **Small Size**, and independently toggle its compass section. The former
`/minimap` command and alternate screen anchors have been removed.

The `−`, reset and `+` controls in the minimap's upper-right corner use the
hosted F1 map styling at a smaller HUD scale and change its crop zoom. They
accept mouse input while the player holds `C`. Visibility, size, compass and
zoom preferences are archived client-side. Areas beyond the map image are
filled with `#1a1a1a`.

When a waypoint is active, the minimap draws the server-calculated route along
the exported road surfaces. The `#0D47A1` road stroke uses rounded corners and
caps. Its `#546E7A` off-road sections identify the connection from an off-road
player or destination back to the nearest recognized road. The destination
remains edge-clamped when it is outside the visible crop.

## Hosted F1 city map

Pressing `M` opens the F1 menu directly on the Map tab. The console command `cityrp_open_map` exposes the same behaviour for custom binds.

The F1 panel hosts the beta service-map interface so its category controls,
location cards and full pin artwork remain identical to the browser map. It
supports:

- mouse-wheel zoom;
- left-drag panning;
- a reset control;
- active-navigation state; and
- interactive server-authoritative location pins.

Clicking a pin selects it and centres its anchor in the current map view. The
location list remains searchable and filterable by the category controls at
the top. Clicking either a row or its **Set Waypoint** button focuses the same
pin before selecting the destination.

Static locations use their saved world coordinates. Registered system destinations use their resolver coordinates. Dynamic destinations are refreshed from the current matching entity's `WorldSpaceCenter()`.

The server sends those locations to the client through
`CityRP.Waypoints.MapData`. The client converts Source world positions through
`WorldToMapUV` and injects a JSON payload into the already-loaded DHTML page with
`CityRPMapSetLocations`. This data exists only in that player's in-memory page:

- the game server does not POST coordinates to the website;
- the website does not receive database credentials;
- no public JSON file is modified on server startup; and
- a fresh server response replaces stale browser-map positions.

This is preferable for the in-game F1 map because live and nearest resolvers can
change. `!waypointexport` remains the controlled workflow for updating the
standalone public map.

## Nearest map category

The hosted F1 map includes a **Nearest** category. Its entries are list-only:

- they are visible in the category and location list;
- they do not create map pins;
- clicking the entire location row sets the waypoint; and
- the existing **Set Waypoint** button performs the same action.

Nearest destinations resolve to the closest currently valid entity each time they are selected:

| Identifier | Destination |
| --- | --- |
| `locker` | Government Locker |
| `weed` | Drug Dealer |
| `meth` | Meth Dealer |
| `coal` | Coal Mine |
| `metal` | Metal Mine |
| `tree` | Pine Tree |
| `bin` | Rubbish Bin |
| `trash` | Trash Collector |
| `wood` | Wood Chopper |
| `rocks` | Construction Worker |
| `terminal` | ID Terminal |
| `vending_machine` | Vending Machine |
| `tesla_supercharger` | Tesla Supercharger |
| `fuel_station` | Fuel Station |
| `phonebooth` | Phonebooth |

## Persistent map locations

Roleplay Assistants and higher staff can save locations to the current map while looking at the required position:

```text
!waypointset <name> [hidden|visible]
!waypointsetcategory <location> <category>
!waypointdelete <name>
```

New locations begin in **General**.

All privileged functions use documented acommands:

| Example | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `!waypointset "Industrial Road" visible` | Save or update the aimed position |
| `!waypointcategory add "Fuel Stations" red diamond` | Create, edit, list or remove categories |
| `!waypointsetcategory "Inner City BP" "Fuel Stations"` | Move a saved location |
| `!waypointhide "Staff Garage"` | Hide a saved pin |
| `!waypointshow "Staff Garage"` | Restore a saved pin |
| `!waypointdelete "Old Location"` | Delete a saved location |
| `!waypointplayer Vadar "Inner City BP"` | Assign or clear another player's route |
| `!waypointexport` | Print the current map JSON |
| `!waypointdebug roads` | Inspect the road graph and route |

The same examples and descriptions appear in the F1 Commands page for
authorized staff.

Locations are stored under:

```text
data/cityrp/plugins/waypoints/<map>.json
```

Repository-managed configurations may be placed under:

```text
gamemode/core/plugins/waypoints/maps/<map>.json
```

The server imports a changed packaged configuration once and records its checksum under `data/cityrp/plugins/waypoints/imports/`. Later in-game edits are therefore not overwritten on every restart.

Staff can print the complete current map configuration to their client console:

```text
!waypointexport
```

The export is the correct source for a reviewed public-map update. An automatic
server-to-website upload would require an authenticated write endpoint, replay
protection, map/version validation and deployment rollback. Runtime DHTML
injection avoids that operational and security surface for the in-game map.

## Hidden locations

A saved location can remain addressable without appearing in the F1 location list:

```text
!waypointhide <name>
!waypointshow <name>
!waypointset <name> hidden
```

Hidden locations remain usable through direct selection, staff assignment and system integrations.

Nearest entries are different from hidden saved points: they remain visible in the F1 list but are marked as list-only so the map does not draw a pin.

## Categories

```text
!waypointcategory add <name> [colour] [shape]
!waypointcategory set <name> [colour] [shape]
!waypointcategory remove <name>
!waypointcategory list
```

`create` aliases `add`, `edit` aliases `set`, and `delete` aliases `remove`. Removing a category moves its saved locations to **General**.

Supported colours are `blue`, `green`, `orange`, `red`, `yellow`, `purple` and `white`. Supported shapes are `diamond`, `circle`, `square` and `triangle`.

Multi-word category names use an underscore identifier, such as `City Services` becoming `city_services`.

## Buildings and road routing

The map PNG is visual artwork only. Buildings, water and terrain may change
without changing navigation. Road routing uses the packaged
`rp_evocity_v4b1_fl2_roads.json`, which contains world-coordinate road polygons
and holes exported from the VMF.

On server startup, the plugin samples that geometry into a connected 256-unit
road grid. A waypoint projects the player and destination onto their nearest
road nodes, runs A* with diagonal corner protection, and simplifies the result
only where the straight segment remains within the exported road surface. The
server sends the resulting world-coordinate route with the waypoint. It
recalculates only when the player moves more than three grid cells from the
active route.

The route geometry is independent from the PNG and therefore cannot mistake a
building colour for a road. The current graph is bidirectional because the
source data describes surfaces rather than lane direction. One-way support
would require directed lane or edge metadata in a future export.

Roleplay Assistants and higher staff can inspect the routing system with:

```text
!waypointdebug roads
!waypointdebug route
!waypointdebug status
!waypointdebug off
```

The `roads` mode draws every recognized road-grid node in green over the base
map, draws active route points in yellow and leaves the calculated path in its
normal on-road and off-road colours.
The minimap also displays the road-node and route-point counts. `route` and
`status` print the graph load state, source path and active route coordinates to
the console. This distinguishes a missing graph from a route-calculation or
HUD-rendering problem.

## Staff directions

```text
!waypointplayer <player> <location>
!waypointplayer <player> clear
!waypointplayer <player> end
!waypointplayer <player>
```

The player argument accepts a partial or full name, server UserID or legacy SteamID through CityRP's normal lookup. Without a destination, the waypoint uses the staff member's aimed position.

Staff assignment may resolve the existing `/place` and `/warp` tables for compatibility. Those legacy coordinates are not exposed in the ordinary player menu.

## Server API

```lua
local waypoints = cityrp.plugin.get("waypoints")

waypoints:SetWaypoint(
	ply,
	"Delivery",
	Vector(100, 200, 300),
	260,
	"example",
	false,
	"orange",
	"triangle",
	"deliveries"
)

waypoints:ClearWaypoint(ply, "example")

waypoints:RegisterDestination(
	"example",
	"Example Destination",
	Vector(100, 200, 300),
	260,
	"green",
	"circle",
	"services"
)
```

Source identifiers allow systems to clear only their own navigation without removing a staff or unrelated system waypoint.

## Car Boosting

When Waypoints is loaded, Car Boosting replaces another active destination with a silent `Chop Shop` waypoint when delivery begins. It clears when delivery completes, fails or the player enters the destination radius.

Without Waypoints, the Boosting objective HUD retains its own delivery bearing and distance.

## Runtime checks

1. Clear the map material cache and confirm the PNG downloads and renders in both HUD and F1.
2. Verify both minimap sizes, visibility and compass toggles from the `C` menu.
3. Hold `C` and verify `+` and `−` change the minimap crop zoom.
4. Walk and drive between known landmarks and verify world movement matches the minimap.
5. Set distant waypoints and verify the blue route follows roads and reroutes after leaving them.
6. Rotate on foot and in a vehicle, then look independently, and verify the expected heading remains correct.
7. Press `M` and confirm F1 opens directly on the hosted Map panel.
8. Verify F1 zoom, pan, reset, player position and active navigation marker.
9. Compare saved pins against their corresponding doors, properties and service entities.
10. Confirm Nearest entries draw no pins and both row/button actions resolve the closest live entity.
11. Test saved categories, hidden points, staff assignment and automatic clearing inside the arrival radius.
